summary: Pre-built per-gene covariate matrices for TCGA-MESO (Malignant mesothelioma, overwhelmingly pleural in TCGA (51 of 87 cases pleura NOS, 11 thorax NOS, 5 abdominal/peritoneal; 52 epithelioid, 21 biphasic). GTEx has no mesothelium or pleura tissue, so MESO had no GTEx mapping: the proposed mapping key MESO takes Lung (the organ the visceral pleura covers, representative column) and Adipose_Visceral_Omentum (the peritoneal surface tissue GTEx samples), both organ-level proxies in which mesothelial cells are a minor fraction -- read the GTEx block as tissue context, not cell of origin. Expression is tumor-only: all 87 TCGA-MESO RNA-seq files are primary tumors, no normals. TCGA ATAC-seq covered (Corces et al. 2018; the tarball's bigWigs are named MESO_..., read from its first member). roadmap null: Roadmap's 127 epigenomes include no mesothelial, pleural or peritoneal sample (adipose E025/E063 and lung E096 are the wrong cell). encode_chromatin: DNase-seq of NCI-H226, the only mesothelioma line in ENCODE (Cellosaurus CVCL_1544: pleural epithelioid mesothelioma, originally described as lung squamous carcinoma; ENCODE health status 'squamous cell carcinoma; mesothelioma'), no histone ChIP exists for it; 2025 pipeline replicate-1 file. NCI-H2052, NCI-H28, NCI-H2452, MSTO-211H, Met-5A and LP-9 return no ENCODE experiments. summary: TEMPLATE-DIRECTED MASS FABRICATION OF BIOMEDICAL MICRO/NANOROBOTS AT THE LIMIT is a 770-page, high-density English research monograph on scaling template replication without losing dimensional fidelity, surface integrity, functional consistency or scientific traceability. The book treats the template as a stateful manufacturing ancestor rather than a passive tool. Every cavity and replication cycle is registered so that template wear, release-coating decay, demolding force, replica bias, particle residue, spatial defect clustering and functional outcomes can be linked across the full template life. Its central falsifiable claim asks whether lifetime-aware monitoring can predict rising defect probability before damage spreads. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates cover cavity filling, squeeze flow, material relaxation, cure conversion, shrinkage, residual stress, adhesion, demolding, fracture, Archard wear, coating survival, hidden wear states, geometry transfer, Hausdorff error, spatial point processes, defect ancestry, survival hazards, change points, capability, conservative yield, hierarchical variance and qualified-part cost. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the monograph develops replication physics, release mechanics, template wear, spatial defect genealogy, adaptive process control, functional qualification, lifecycle economics and independent transfer. Two hundred Research Gates define blind challenges, strong comparators, evidence packages, hard stops and successor forks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos present genuinely different witnesses, challenge artifacts, estimators, controllers, economic falsifiers, release keys and handoff kits. The work is explicitly nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim a completed manufacturing campaign, human treatment, autonomous in-body efficacy or regulatory approval. Its release rule is conjunctive: wear, demolding force, geometry, defect clustering, unselected yield, task function and traceability must pass together over the complete template life. Author: Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXIV / Flagship 09 Edition: Research Working Edition v1.0 / October 2026

summary: A Turing machine carries a computation forward through successive configurations, but continuation beyond infinitely many steps requires a rule assigning the configuration from which the next instruction can proceed. The Quantum Γ-Turing machine considered here retains a finite-dimensional register’s trace-norm limit when it exists, preserving the coherence needed by subsequent operations. Averaging a history that never settles permits another continuation, although registers independent at every finite stage can then acquire correlations through their shared timing. We characterise when an assigned state can replace its history without changing a later joint calculation. For assignments compatible with every fixed quantum operation, the largest composition error equals the mean trace-norm distance from the assigned state, and a partner carrying classical labels can approach that value. Independent composition with every partner holds precisely when temporal variance under the chosen mean vanishes. Requiring this under every shift-invariant mean gives uniform vanishing of average squared fluctuations, a condition that permits sparse excursions despite failure of ordinary convergence. For a programme repeatedly applying one fixed channel, independent composition is instead equivalent to ordinary convergence, with the exact error determined by its surviving nonstationary spectral component. Algebraically specified channels and initial states admit a finite decision procedure and certified bounds, while bounded repetitions of states preserve the stronger averaging condition and transfer its certificates to a simulation. These results connect transfinite continuation to finite verification for specified programmes and provide composition certificates that can be carried through a controlled simulation.
title: Independent Composition and Quantum Limits in Transfinite Γ-Turing Machines

summary: Per distruggere la Rotta dei Chersoneso, venne fatta la Battaglia di Cheronea https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_di_Cheronea_(87_a.C.) Per distruggere i commerci con Etruschi e Cartaginesi, venne fatta la Battaglia di Alalia https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_del_Mare_Sardo Per distruggere i rapporti con la Facies Sarda dei Bessi di Perperikon, venne fatta la battaglia del Monte Emo:   La battaglia del Monte Emo (o Haemus ) è storicamente legata a due momenti distinti dell'antichità che videro scontrarsi gli eserciti invasori con le tribù tracie, in particolare i Bessi , e il cui contesto geografico e spirituale è strettamente connesso al celebre sito monumentale di Perperikon , situato nelle montagne dei Rodopi in Bulgaria. [ 1 , 2 ] Ecco come si collegano questi tre elementi:   1. La prima battaglia del Monte Emo (335 a.C.) Prima di lanciare la sua campagna contro i Persiani, Alessandro Magno guidò una spedizione nei Balcani per rendere sicuri i confini settentrionali del suo regno. Sul Monte Emo (l'attuale catena dei Monti Balcani) affrontò i Traci Liberi e altre tribù locali. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] La tattica dei carri: I Traci si erano posizionati sulla vetta e intendevano far rotolare dei pesanti carri giù dai ripidi pendii per rompere la falange macedone. [ 1 , 2 ] La contromossa di Alessandro: Il re macedone ordinò ai suoi soldati di aprire i ranghi per far passare i carri oppure di sdraiarsi a terra coprendosi con gli scudi intersecati (creando una sorta di testuggine). La tattica funzionò alla perfezione: i carri rimbalzarono sugli scudi senza causare vittime tra i Macedoni. Le truppe di Alessandro caricarono poi la vetta, sbaragliando i difensori. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   2. Lo scontro dei Bessi con Roma (72 a.C.) In epoca successiva, il nome della battaglia del Monte Emo si associa alla sottomissione definitiva dei Bessi , una delle tribù tracie più bellicose e fanaticamente dedite al culto religioso. Il proconsole romano Marco Licinio Lucullo affrontò i Bessi proprio nei pressi della catena del Monte Emo, sconfiggendoli duramente in una grande battaglia campale, conquistando il loro centro principale ( Uscudama ) e aprendo la strada alla successiva egemonia romana nella regione. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   3. Il legame con Perperikon La tribù dei Bessi era storicamente la custode del famosissimo Santuario e Oracolo di Dioniso , situato proprio sulla maestosa roccia sacra di Perperikon . Questo luogo ha un valore storico eccezionale per due importanti profezie collegate ai protagonisti di queste guerre: [ 1 , 2 ] La profezia di Alessandro Magno: Secondo le fonti antiche, prima di iniziare la sua spedizione in Asia (subito dopo aver pacificato la Tracia), Alessandro visitò l'oracolo di Dioniso a Perperikon. Il vino versato sull'altare creò una fiammata altissima fino al cielo, un segno divino che i sacerdoti interpretarono come il presagio che avrebbe conquistato il mondo intero. [ 1 ] La profezia di Ottaviano Augusto: Anni dopo, anche il padre di Augusto (Gaio Ottavio) ricevette nello stesso santuario dei Bessi la medesima profezia sul futuro dominio globale di suo figlio. [ 1 ] In sintesi, la resistenza dei Traci sul Monte Emo rappresenta lo scontro militare per il controllo dei Balcani, mentre Perperikon costituisce il cuore spirituale, politico e identitario della tribù dei Bessi che contro quegli imperi tentò invano di difendere la propria indipendenza. [ 1 , 2 ]   Attenzione: questo documento è stato appena pensato: si tratta di una bozza iniziale basata sul Paradigma Sardo Corso Atlantideo di Luigi Usai. summary: Deepwave provides wave propagation modules for PyTorch, for applications such as seismic imaging and inversion. It performs forward modelling and backpropagation, so it can simulate wave propagation to generate synthetic data, or invert for the scattering potential (reverse-time migration, RTM, or its least-squares counterpart, LSRTM), other model parameters (full-waveform inversion, FWI), initial wavefields, or source wavelets. It can also be used inside a larger chain of operations, with forward and backpropagation flowing through the whole chain end to end. You can use your own objective functions, or functions that generate the propagator's inputs, and PyTorch's automatic differentiation calculates how to backpropagate through them. New to seismic/wave-equation terminology? The glossary defines the terms (PML, CFL, Born, FWI, and more) used throughout this README and the rest of the documentation. Deepwave requires Python 3.9 or later and PyTorch 2.4 or later. First install PyTorch for your CPU or CUDA device using the instructions on the PyTorch website . Then install Deepwave: pip install deepwave   macOS wheels support Apple Silicon. Intel Mac wheels are no longer provided: PyTorch 2.4 and newer do not publish wheels for that platform. Prebuilt x86 wheels require AVX2. Older CPUs need a source build; see installation troubleshooting . PyTorch is Deepwave's only dependency. The example scripts under docs/ additionally import matplotlib (to draw their figures) and, in some cases, numpy , scipy (smoothing and filter design), torchaudio (applying those filters), torchvision and geomloss , but those are needed only to run the examples, never by Deepwave itself. To install all of them: pip install 'deepwave[examples]'   The documentation contains examples and instructions on how to install and use Deepwave. You might also like to watch a video summary of Deepwave . Not every propagator supports every option (dimensionality, backend, boundary faces, batching, second-order differentiation, callbacks, ...). See the capability matrix (declared in the code and checked by conformance tests) before assuming a combination works. Why Deepwave Computationally efficient. Deepwave's compiled kernels use a hand-derived adjoint for better performance and lower memory requirements than pure PyTorch implementations. See what Deepwave calculates . Second derivatives are supported, not just first. The scalar, acoustic, and elastic propagators can compute Hessian-vector products (derivatives of gradients); see the Hessian example . Born (linearised) modelling. Model scattered waves from perturbations to a background medium for linearised inversion and imaging. See the torch.func example . Deepwave fits into an ordinary PyTorch workflow. Because propagation is a normal PyTorch autograd Function , it works directly with PyTorch optimisers, DistributedDataParallel over shots, torch.func transforms, and any PyTorch loss function or neural-network model of the input parameters. See the capability matrix for exactly what each propagator supports. Deepwave does not try to be a general symbolic PDE solver, a multi-node HPC code, or a non-differentiable simulation toolkit — see Devito , SPECFEM , and k-Wave respectively for those needs. If you are choosing between wave-propagation packages, see the comparison guide . (Note: the DeepWave-KAUST GitHub organisation, home of the SWEEP package, is unrelated to this project.) Features Supports the 1D, 2D, and 3D constant density acoustic / scalar wave equation (regular and Born modelling), variable density acoustic, elastic, viscoacoustic (single-mechanism SLS attenuation), elastic VTI (anisotropic), and pseudo-acoustic VTI ( deepwave.acoustic_vti , the Duveneck et al. 2008 V_S=0 reduction) wave equations Runs on CPUs and appropriate GPUs The gradient of all outputs (final wavefields and receiver data) can be calculated with respect to the model parameters (wavespeed, scattering potential, etc
title: Deepwave

summary: Data and R code that reproduce all tables and figures of the article "Dependence on China, Export Volatility and Relationship Persistence: Shipment-Level Evidence from Peruvian Copper Ore, 2006–2025", of its Appendix A and of its Supplementary Material.   Version 1.1.0 accompanies the revised manuscript (first review round). It keeps all data, code and outputs of version 1.0.0, which are reproduced identically, and adds the scripts, data and outputs of the analyses carried out in the revision: Cox models stratified by firm, with shared frailty and with a firm random effect, and without Chinese-owned firms; a firm-level (granular) and a Shapley decomposition of aggregate export volatility; a destination counterfactual; seasonality checks; regime-specific concentration coefficients; destination concentration by net weight; sensitivity analyses and a shift-share instrument for the firm–year panel; mirror statistics from UN Comtrade (imports of HS 2603 reported by China and the Republic of Korea); and a comparison of the extract with SUNAT's published statistics (Tables G8 and G9).   The package contains the shipment-level extract of Peruvian exports of copper ores and concentrates (HS 2603.00.00.00) from PromPerú's Infotrade platform, based on SUNAT export customs declarations, January 2006 – December 2025, validated month by month against PromPerú's official totals (23,106 shipments; 22,582 commercial shipments by 200 firms to 44 destinations, USD 219.3 billion FOB, in the analysis), together with the auxiliary data, the processed datasets and all outputs. A single script (run_all.R) runs the whole pipeline.   Exporters who are natural persons (18 of 266 RUCs; 90 shipments) are pseudonymized; the replacement is one-to-one and does not change any result. The firm–destination–month dataset obtained from SUNAT through an access-to-information request, used only for cross-validation, is not redistributed. See README.md for details.
title: Data and R code for: Dependence on China, Export Volatility and Relationship Persistence: Shipment-Level Evidence from Peruvian Copper Ore, 2006–2025

summary: Öz   Bu çalışmanın amacı, genç erkek basketbolcularda Fonksiyonel Hareket Tarama (FMS) toplam ve alt test puanları ile alt ekstremite denge asimetrisi arasındaki ilişkileri ve bu puanların asimetriyi yordama düzeyini incelemektir. Kesitsel ve ilişkisel tarama modelinde tasarlanan araştırmaya, yaş ortalaması 18,90 ± 1,21 yıl ve spor yaşı ortalaması 7,83 ± 1,77 yıl olan 52 gönüllü lisanslı erkek basketbolcu katılmıştır. Fonksiyonel hareketler yedi alt testten oluşan FMS ile değerlendirilmiştir. Alt testler 0–3 arasında puanlanmış ve toplam puan 21 puan üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Dinamik denge, anterior, posteromedial ve posterolateral uzanma yönlerini içeren Y-Denge Testi (YBT) ile ölçülmüştür. Her iki alt ekstremiteden elde edilen uzanma mesafeleri kullanılarak taraflara ait bileşik puanlar hesaplanmış ve denge asimetri yüzdesi analiz edilmiştir. Verilerin analizinde betimsel istatistikler, Pearson korelasyon analizi ve çoklu doğrusal regresyon analizi kullanılmıştır. FMS toplam puanı ile asimetri yüzdesi (r = −0,059), dominant bileşik puan (r = −0,031) ve non-dominant bileşik puan (r = −0,013) arasında anlamlı ilişki bulunmamıştır (p > 0,05). Asimetri yüzdesi ile dominant bileşik puan arasında çok güçlü pozitif ilişki saptanmıştır (r = 0,921; p < 0,01). FMS toplam ve alt test puanlarını içeren regresyon modeli genel olarak anlamlı değildir (R² = 0,256; düzeltilmiş R² = 0,117; p = 0,094). Modelde gövde stabilitesi şınavının (TSPU) katsayısı negatif (β = −0,399; p = 0,015), omuz mobilitesinin (SM) katsayısı ise pozitif yönde anlamlı bulunmuştur (β = 0,342; p = 0,049). Diğer alt testlerin ve toplam puanın katsayıları anlamlı değildir (p > 0,05). Sonuç olarak, FMS toplam puanı bu örneklemde denge asimetrisiyle anlamlı bir ilişki göstermemiştir. Bulgular, basketbolcuların değerlendirilmesinde yalnızca toplam FMS puanına odaklanılmaması gerektiğini; alt test sonuçlarının ve taraflara özgü dinamik denge ölçümlerinin birlikte ele alınması gerektiğini göstermektedir.   Anahtar Kelimeler: Basketbol, Fonksiyonel Hareket Taraması, Dinamik Denge, Ekstremiteler Arası Asimetri, Gövde Stabilitesi   Abstract The relationship between the Functional Movement Screen (FMS) total and individual test scores and the asymmetry of balance of the lower extremities, as well as the predictive effect on young male basketball players, was analysed in this study. This was a cross-sectional correlational study that consisted of 52 licensed male basketball players volunteering for the study at the age of 18.90 ± 1.21 years and having a sport experience of 7.83 ± 1.77 years. The assessment of functional movement was carried out through the seven FMS tests. These tests were individually scored in range of 0 to 3 points with a maximal total of 21 points. Reach distances for both lower extremities were used to calculate limb-specific composite scores, and balance asymmetry percentage was analyzed. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were used. FMS total score was not significantly correlated with asymmetry percentage (r = −0.059), dominant composite score (r = −0.031), or non-dominant composite score (r = −0.013; all p > 0.05). summary: Replication package for the paper "Risk, not sunshine: financing costs drive the price of reliable solar-plus-storage electricity in the Middle East and North Africa" (Younas Khan and Štefan Bojnec). summary: SimilCode Benchmark is a curated dataset of 120 short source-code snippets in C# and Java, organised into 60 test-case pairs per language across four ground-truth similarity categories (identical, functional, structural, and different) with fifteen reference groups per language. Every pair was independently classified by two raters blind to the original labels, with near-perfect inter-rater agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.989). All code was authored specifically for this study or drawn from the public domain; no student-submitted code is included. The dataset was used to benchmark four contemporary commercial large language models as similarity analysts — claude-opus-5 , gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 , gemini-3.1-pro-preview and deepseek-v4-pro — with three independent replicates per case–model combination, yielding 1,440 evaluations. The same 120 pairs were also processed with three established classical detectors drawn from three distinct algorithmic families: Moss (winnowing fingerprints), JPlag v6.3.0 (token-string matching) and Dolos v2.9.3 (tree-sitter syntax trees). The record further includes a separate corpus for validating algorithmic-complexity (Big O) estimation: 40 canonical algorithms and 8 adversarial cases designed to defeat surface cues such as misleading identifiers, unreachable code and memoisation. Raw model responses, classical-detector outputs, the standardised prompt with its SHA-256 checksum, the ground-truth tables and the analysis scripts are published together for reproducibility.
title: SimilCode Benchmark: A Dual-Language Source-Code Similarity Dataset for the Evaluation of AI-Based Detectors

summary: This record archives version 0.3.0 of takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg, research software for classifying prepared electrocardiogram (ECG) images as takotsubo syndrome or acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The default inference input is an already prepared 480 x 480 pixel image. Supported single-frame formats are PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF and WebP; the loader converts images to RGB. Paper-default test-time augmentation (TTA) uses 24 views with magnitude 1 for ViT, one unchanged view (no TTA) for ConvNeXtV2, and 32 views with magnitude 3 for MLP-Mixer. summary: Objectives. Autoimmune hypothyroidism is associated with disturbances in lipid metabolism. This study assessed lipid profiles and cardiovascular risk markers in patients with overt (OH) and subclinical hypothyroidism (SH) compared with healthy controls, and examined lipid changes during levothyroxine treatment. Methods. This observational case–control study included 129 adults: 65 patients with autoimmune hypothyroidism (35 OH, 30 SH) and 64 controls. All patients had complete lipid, TSH, and fT4 measurements at baseline, 8 weeks, and 16 weeks. Lipid indices included LDL cholesterol (LDL-c), HDL cholesterol (HDL-c), non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-c), and the total cholesterol/HDL-c ratio. Between-group comparisons and paired longitudinal tests were performed; longitudinal p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Results. Baseline LDL-c was higher in patients than controls (3.96 ± 1.67 vs 3.39 ± 0.76 mmol/L; p = 0.015). Non-HDL-c was higher in OH than SH (5.31 ± 2.19 vs 3.64 ± 0.96 mmol/L), and the total cholesterol/HDL-c ratio was higher in patients than controls (4.16 ± 1.59 vs 3.42 ± 0.75; p = 0.001). At 16 weeks, mean LDL-c decreased from 3.96 ± 1.67 to 3.28 ± 1.00 mmol/L (p = 0.001), and non-HDL-c from 4.54 ± 1.92 to 3.68 ± 1.17 mmol/L (p < 0.001). HDL-c did not improve significantly. At week 16, TSH was within the reference interval in 42 of 65 patients (64.6%). Conclusions. Overt autoimmune hypothyroidism was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile than SH or euthyroid status. During levothyroxine treatment, LDL-c and non-HDL-c improved, particularly in OH, while HDL-c did not. These observational findings do not establish a causal treatment effect or a reduction in cardiovascular events.
title: LIPID PROFILE AND CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTORS IN PATIENTS WITH AUTOIMMUNE HYPOTHYROIDISM

summary: When formal proofs or deductive verifications exceed human cognitive surveyability, does epistemic justification require an agent-accessible chain of reasoning, or must epistemology shift from internalist warrant to structural-systemic reliability? Since the seventeenth-century rationalist and empiricist programs of Descartes and Locke, Western epistemology has rested upon the axiom of epistemic transparency: for an epistemic agent S to possess genuine a priori demonstrative knowledge of a theorem phi, S must be capable of cognitively surveying the inferential chain connecting primitive axioms Gamma to phi. Even when Bolzano, Frege, and Russell purged psychologism and spatio-temporal intuition from deductive logic, they treated formalization as a vehicle for rendering every inferential transition perspicuous to rational inspection. However, automated theorem provers, Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers, and interactive proof assistants routinely generate formal derivations that are deductively sound yet impossible for any finite biological mind to survey in full—violating the Wittgensteinian criterion of cognitive surveyability (Übersichtlichkeit). This paper provides a systematic formal and historical analysis of this problem across eight sections: (1) Section 1 reconstructs the classical transparency paradigm across Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, and Kant, isolating the working-memory and temporal synthesis bounds built into classical deductio; (2) Section 2 demonstrates how the Bolzanian-Fregean-Hilbertian quest for local step-wise gaplessness (Lückenlosigkeit) triggered an inverse scaling law that dialectically destroyed global proof surveyability; (3) Section 3 analyzes the Wittgensteinian critique of un-surveyable derivations, formalizing the distinction between a normative grammatical criterion and an empirical physical experiment; (4) Section 4 proves via Gödelian speed-up, Gentzen cut-elimination, and propositional proof complexity lower bounds that trans-surveyable derivations (||D|| >> kappa(S)) are an inescapable metamathematical feature of formal systems rather than an artifact of unoptimized proof search; (5) Section 5 introduces Bounded Justification Logic (BJL_kappa), formally deriving the inconsistency of the Classical Surveyability Trilemma; (6) Section 6 evaluates the Tymoczko–Burge–Kripke debate on computer-assisted proofs, refuting both quasi-empiricist hardware inductivism and ungrounded testimonial transmission; (7) Section 7 constructs a positive theory of Structural-Systemic Warrant (SSW), demonstrating how de Bruijn meta-kernel soundness compression and substrate-invariant equivalence preserve derivative a priori warrant while bifurcating demonstrative warrant (Dass-Wissen) from explanatory illumination (Warum-Wissen); (8) Section 8 addresses foundational objections from rule-following skepticism, Gödelian second-incompleteness limits, and zero-knowledge probabilistic verification (ZKPs and PCPs), synthesizing the general epistemological conclusions.
title: Epistemic Justification Beyond Cognitive Surveyability: A Formal and Historical Account of Deductive Warrant under Trans-Cognitive Verification

summary: The book as a PDF, in the shape it is printed: read it in the browser at https://h0ffmann.github.io/closed-source/paper.pdf , or download it from the newest release at https://github.com/h0ffmann/closed-source/releases/latest/download/closed-source.pdf . The files of this record are the source that builds that PDF. A position paper arguing that closed source has failed as a protection, for science first. It reads the case through Robert M. Pirsig's Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance (1974), the book it stands on: the number of rational hypotheses that can explain a phenomenon is infinite, so science never closes, and a method that only its owner can open is one that nobody else can test. Large language models now decompile binaries into re-executable source; black-box queries extract parts of production models; distillation copies capabilities at industrial scale; and the largest 2026 trade-secret dispute in artificial intelligence, Apple's suit against OpenAI, turns on people, laptops and recruiting rather than on code that stayed secret. Against this background the paper revisits Linus Torvalds' Linux and Git as evidence that openness scales, and the author's closed undergraduate thesis as evidence of what secrecy costs a researcher. It argues that the ethical answer to universal reverse engineering is professional citation, proposes three rules for AI agents (borrow, cite, propagate), and describes Paper Fabric, the open pipeline in the Ouroboric style that produced it. This record is a book. It has not been peer reviewed. It holds the source of the book at the release tag: the Markdown text, the build and the agent configuration. The rendered PDFs are attached to the GitHub release of the same tag. The writer develops in the open. His three other works each have a permanent DOI, and this record cites all three: marola, an open, non-profit platform for sea conditions and bathing-water quality, written with five other people ( 10.5281/zenodo.23224155 ); WW3 GPU Lab, a bit-for-bit GPU port of WAVEWATCH III ( 10.5281/zenodo.23221351 ); and picasso, Nix flakes for scientific and agentic toolchains, which builds this book ( 10.5281/zenodo.23311208 ). The book is made in the Ouroboric style, and the Ouroboric ideas are Bruno Valério's ( https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/ouroboric ); Ouroboric has no DOI yet, so this record cites it by its address.
title: Closed Source: The God that Failed

summary: This deposit contains the data, code, and figures underlying a study of owned dog and cat populations in Ecuador, reconstructed from the 2022 Population and Housing Census (Censo de Población y Vivienda, CPV 2022) of the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INEC). It includes: (i) indicator tables of dog and cat ownership at the province, canton, and parish levels (CSV), with derived indicators such as the percentage of households keeping pets, pets per capita, and the dog-to-cat ratio; (ii) geospatial layers (GeoPackage) joining these indicators to canton and parish boundaries, plus the local spatial-cluster (LISA) classification; (iii) the full analysis pipeline (Python) that builds the indicators from the primary census tabulations, harmonizes place names and geometries, runs the spatial analysis, and generates the figures; (iv) the five manuscript figures (TIFF, 300 dpi); and (v) a documented log of figures on companion-animal populations circulated in Ecuadorian media and official communications, compared with the values reconstructed here. At the national level, the census records 7,601,269 owned dogs and cats (5,211,037 dogs and 2,390,232 cats), with 58.3% of households keeping at least one. Ownership is markedly higher in rural areas and strongly clustered across the central-southern Sierra (global Moran's I = 0.57). Raw inputs are not all redistributed here for licensing reasons; see the README and SOURCES file for provenance, licensing, and instructions to reproduce the analysis. summary: EXTERNAL QIGONG AND HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION PATTERNS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating whether thermographic differences observed during culturally defined qigong and matched neutral tasks can be distinguished from ordinary human thermoregulation, environmental exchange and measurement bias. The governing three-coupling is infrared thermal imaging x physiological regulation x heat-transfer models. The research treats “external qi” as a cultural and experimental task label, not an established physical energy carrier. The scientific core separates raw infrared radiance from inferred skin temperature and estimated heat flux. It develops emissivity and reflected-wall correction, blackbody calibration, spectral detector response, conduction and perfusion bioheat models, convection, evaporation, respiration-related temperature patterns, posture and muscular activity. The original candidate bulk heat equation is explicitly refined by separating volumetric tissue transport from surface heat-transfer boundary conditions. The principal proposed test uses concealed task assignments, matched breathing/movement/clothing, phantom references, negative-control regions and conventional physics-first rivals. Thirty physically distinct mathematical plates document governing relationships, units, assumptions, identifiability, masked falsifiers and chapter links. Eighty-two independent research chapters contain 410 single-page investigations. The true center of the monograph is its 200 one-page Research Gates, each posing a falsifiable question in bold deep-navy typography and asking what an independent successor must measure, challenge, disprove or preserve. Thirty-three differentiated Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, error-correction artifacts, negative-result protocols and reproducibility tools. The DOI registry separates three STARLI author mother volumes from eleven externally published methodological or conventional-science references on infrared thermography, emissivity, classical bioheat and research design. Bibliographic sources constrain methods; they do not validate extraordinary qigong mechanisms. Every integrated experiment is prospective. The book presents no completed human intervention, clinically established effect, new physical particle or evidence of treatment efficacy. Ethical authorization and independent scientific review would be required before future human-observation research. Author: 33 | STARLI White Rainbow Epoch Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXIII | Flagship 38 of 90

summary: Human observers can encounter representations of the same relational contribution history yet form different beliefs about its significance and trustworthiness. This third paper in a coordinated research programme investigates cognitive processes between the structural availability of evidence and an observer’s assessment of a person, claim, or contribution. Its proposed analytic objects are selective attention, evidence encoding, reconstructive memory, attribution, interpretive schemas, belief revision, epistemic vigilance, and behavioral reliance. The inquiry distinguishes evidentiary accessibility from cognitive encounter, subjective confidence from justified assessment, and expressed trust from risk-bearing cooperation. Prior work in attention, working memory, judgment under uncertainty, epistemic vigilance, and trust in automation motivates a provisional sequential-kernel architecture; that architecture remains a research proposal rather than a validated general cognitive model. AI-mediated information environments supply a historically relevant application, without defining the paper’s full scope. This working draft contains all ten planned sections, covering cognitive interfaces, selective attention, memory-based trajectory reconstruction, contribution attribution, proposition-specific belief revision, testimony evaluation, behavioral reliance, empirical designs with explicit identification boundaries, and a synthesis of conditional theoretical findings. It reports no original empirical results.
title: Cognitive Mediation of Relational Evidence: An Investigation of Epistemic Judgment and Reliance
