summary: CasADi is a symbolic framework for numeric optimization implementing automatic differentiation in forward and reverse modes on sparse matrix-valued computational graphs. It supports self-contained C-code generation and interfaces state-of-the-art codes such as SUNDIALS, IPOPT etc. It can be used from C++, Python, Matlab/Octave, Julia or Javascript
title: CasADi - A software framework for nonlinear optimization and optimal control

summary: Next-generation smart sensing devices necessitate on-chip integration of power-efficient reference circuits. The latters are required to provide other circuit blocks with highly reliable bias signals, even in the presence of temperature shifts and supply voltage disturbances, while draining a small fraction of the overall power budget. In particular, it is especially challenging to design current references with enhanced robustness and efficiency; hence, thorough exploration of novel architectures and design approaches is needed for this type of circuits. In this work, we propose a novel CMOS-only current reference, achieving temperature compensation by exploiting geometry dependences of the threshold voltage (specifically, the reverse short-channel effect and the narrow-channel effect). This allows reaching first-order temperature compensation within a single current reference core. Implemented in 0.18 μm CMOS, a version of the proposed current reference designed to deliver 141 nA (with 377 nW of total power consumption) achieved an average temperature coefficient equal to 194 ppm/°C (from −20 °C to 80 °C) and an average line sensitivity of −0.017%/V across post-layout statistical Monte Carlo simulations. Based on such findings, the newly proposed design methodology stands out as a noteworthy solution to design robust current references for power-constrained mixed-signal systems-on-chip.
title: A CMOS Current Reference with Novel Temperature Compensation Based on Geometry-Dependent Threshold Voltage Effects

summary: Large language models support personalized tutoring, content generation, and adaptive learning paths. However, capability development requires these resources and interactions to form a coherent learning process that evolves with the learner. A central challenge is to align goals, activities, and assessment while using learning evidence to decide what should follow. We introduce Human-Participatory Multi-Agent Organization and instantiate it in Agentic University (AU). In AU, learners participate as organization members and work with specialized agents to maintain a revisable Capability Program. The program connects personal goals, learning activities across modalities, and layered assessment, while learner feedback and performance guide subsequent support. Our evaluation shows advantages in program organization, assessment design, and revision quality. Users achieved larger mean assessment gains (12.19 versus 5.61 points on a 50-point scale) and reported stronger cognitive support. This work contributes an organizational approach to adaptive learning that makes learner participation a continuing basis for multi-agent coordination. The Agentic University project is available at \href{https://github.com/AgenticOrgLab/AgenticUniversity.git}.
title: Agentic University: Collaborative Agents for Personalized Learning

summary: An outstanding creative advertising image should both attract attention and communicate a product's positioning. How to choose a persuasive conceptual bridge before rendering begins is challenging for advertising generation. We present AdMuse, a skill-guided multi-agent framework that distills high-quality advertisements into reusable creative skills for cross-domain advertising strategy. Rather than retrieving isolated exemplars, AdMuse abstracts recurring bridge patterns into a skill library that can guide new product briefs. At generation time, AdMuse coordinates skill routing, multi-candidate ideation and selection, and VLM-guided visual refinement: diverse skills propose alternative concepts, relative judgment selects the most promising direction, and vision-language feedback helps realize the selected intent in the final image. This design treats advertising creativity as a structured decision process rather than a single prompt-writing step. Experiments across diverse product and brand positionings show that AdMuse produces visually compelling advertisements that faithfully communicate product positioning.
title: AdMuse: Skill-Guided Creative Advertising Image Generation

summary: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. Our analysis shows that this separation alone is insufficient. Agents can lose track of the overall goal and repeat prior investigations. They may also lack necessary background while receiving irrelevant information from others. To maintain goal awareness and coordinate collaboration as task needs change, we propose Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration (GAD). It uses a growing execution graph to organize subtasks and their dependencies. To keep agents focused on their goals, each context retains the original instruction and the assigned task's goal and acceptance conditions. To adapt collaboration and information sharing during execution, agents can divide tasks into subtasks and specify dependencies based on execution evidence. These dependencies guide when agents work and which results they receive. Verification and recovery check subtask results and full task completion against their goals, providing feedback for repair when checks fail.
title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks

summary: DIGITAL TWINS AND QUALITY CONTROL FOR SMART MASK MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名: 智慧面膜製程數位孿生與品質控制極限 Digital Twins and Quality Control for Smart Mask Manufacturing at the Limit is a 777-page English prospective nonclinical research working monograph investigating whether a smart facial-mask manufacturing digital twin can retain physically meaningful quality predictions on new production lines without confusing after-the-fact data reconstruction with genuine foresight. Its scientific three-coupling is manufacturing process twins, calibrated sensor evidence, and independent batch qualification. The central challenge is a frozen-model second-line test with unknown incoming lots, calibration variation, process disturbances and physically inspected quality outcomes. The primary candidate research metric is the dimensionless normalized signed prediction deviation e_Q = (Q_pred - Q_meas)/Q_spec, where the measured and predicted quality quantity and the nonzero prespecified specification scale have the same unit. The percent-valued representation is 100 e_Q. This relation does not convert unlike attributes - filling mass, seal integrity, microbial quality or package leakage - into a compensatory safety score. summary: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex condition involving bidirectional interactions between cardiovascular and renal dysfunction. Its pathophysiology includes hemodynamic abnormalities, venous congestion, neurohormonal activation, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances. This narrative review aims to analyze the mechanisms of CRS and assess the relationship between renal function and clinical prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on mortality, heart failure hospitalization, kidney dysfunction progression, and treatment-related renal changes. The review synthesizes evidence from clinical guidelines, randomized trials, observational studies, and contemporary scientific publications, with particular attention to CRS classification, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, albuminuria, biomarkers, and treatment outcomes. The evidence indicates that reduced eGFR, albuminuria, persistent congestion, and worsening renal function provide complementary prognostic information. An analysis of 3,715 EVEREST trial participants found that each 30% decline in eGFR was associated with an increased risk of death and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. The DOSE trial showed that intensive diuretic treatment could improve fluid removal and symptoms while increasing short-term creatinine elevations. These findings highlight the importance of interpreting renal function changes alongside congestion, hemodynamic stability, baseline kidney function, and treatment response. Comprehensive cardiorenal risk assessment should incorporate renal function, albuminuria, urine output, cardiac biomarkers, electrolyte status, and clinical response to treatment. Further prospective studies are needed to validate integrated risk models in diverse patient populations.

summary: AI-DRIVEN HERBAL SKINCARE FORMULATION OPTIMIZATION AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名: AI本草護膚配方最佳化極限 AI-Driven Herbal Skincare Formulation Optimization at the Limit is a 777-page English prospective research monograph on whether artificial intelligence can make genuinely better, externally reconstructable herbal skincare formulation predictions for previously unseen raw-material lots. Its core three-coupling is AI modeling, formulation constraints, and external generalization. The central falsifiable test is not a favorable random-split score: a model frozen in advance must survive complete raw-material-lot holdouts and forward-in-time evaluation against strong, resource-matched conventional baselines. The study separates botanical species and chemotype authentication, formula mass-fraction closure, sample and instrument provenance, physicochemical endpoints, safety restrictions and predictive uncertainty. It tests whether nominal AI improvements are explained instead by duplicate aliquots, batch identifiers, chronological leakage, correlated chemistry, imbalance across rare botanical families or extra measurement budget. It preserves original outcome units and treats unsafe or unqualified ingredient combinations as hard exclusions rather than soft optimization penalties. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates cover external risk, compositional closure and log ratios, hierarchical lot variance, analytical censoring, physical rheology and diffusion, Gaussian-process predictions, constrained acquisition, Pareto comparisons, distribution shift, calibrated intervals, noncompensatory safety gates and evidence provenance. Eighty-two research chapters are followed by 410 individually paginated studies. Two hundred Research Gates pose prospective falsification questions, including blinded material substitution, negative controls, independent metrology, worst-supplier performance, safe abstention and external replay. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct testable instruments, protocols, audits and evidence artifacts for future investigators. This manuscript is a hypothesis-forming, nonclinical Research Working Edition. It does not report an executed integrated experiment, verified cosmetic benefit, human safety trial, regulatory approval, or a qualified production system. The three STARLI mother works provide methodological ancestry rather than direct evidence that this skincare optimization works. summary: CAR-T therapy is a powerful treatment for pediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). However, the impact of bridging therapy prior to CAR-T infusion on patient outcomes remains insufficiently explored. In this retrospective study of patients with relapse/refractory B-ALL (N = 103), we compared outcomes across different bridging therapy groups: Low-Intensity Chemotherapy (LIC, N = 50), Immunotherapy (N = 20), or High-Intensity Chemotherapy (HIC, N = 33). At day +28 post-infusion, LIC and Immunotherapy showed significantly higher rates of Complete Remission with negative Minimal Residual Disease compared with HIC (96% vs 85% vs 75%), along with lower rates of disease progression (4% vs 10% vs 15.2%) and treatment-related mortality (0% vs 5% vs 9.1%). Additionally, patients who received three or more prior lines of therapy before CAR-T infusion exhibited significantly lower response rates. Despite potential biases, such as intrinsic disease aggressiveness or unidentified genomic alterations, present findings suggest that using LIC or immunotherapy as bridging strategies, in patients with fewer prior treatment lines, may be associated with a lower overall disease and treatment burden and could potentially contribute to improved CAR-T cell efficacy and clinical outcomes. Nevertheless, additional investigations are required to elucidate biological and clinical mechanisms by which bridging approaches and treatment history modulate CAR-T responses. summary: The Duty-Primacy Test: Measuring the Operational Completeness of Algorithmic Transparency Registers (v3, Extended Empirical Edition) Oct 30, 2026 · @craig davidson ABSTRACT Public registers often fail to provide actionable accountability regarding automated tools, lacking clear duty-bearers, failure safeguards, or challenge mechanisms. This paper introduces the Duty-Primacy Test across four pillars: assigned duty-bearer (P1), ascertainable breach mechanism (P2), effective remedy (P3), and temporal lineage tracking (P4).  Evaluating the UK ATRS (n=153) and Dutch Algoritmeregister (n=1,610), the study finds that while standalone structural indicators are common (e.g., 98.7% name an owner in the UK), joint compliance across all pillars drops to 0.0% due to severe deficits in quantitative safeguards (2.0%) and changelogs (6.5%). The audit also uncovered 14 silent liability mutations altering operational rules without notice. Keywords: algorithmic transparency registers; algorithmic accountability; automated decision-making; remedy; temporal drift; joint compliance; UK ATRS; Dutch Algoritmeregister VERSION STATUS • P1 – Assigned Duty-Bearer (Hierarchical/Structured Post Title) • P2 – Ascertainable Breach Mechanism (Numeric Safeguard Threshold) • P3 – Effective Remedy (Formal Appellate Pathway) • P4 – Temporal Lineage Tracking (Descriptive Public Changelog) CHANGELOG (v1.0.0 Summary) Major additions include Pillar 4 integration, a temporal drift audit, joint compliance metrics (0.0% intersection rate), expanded jurisdictional scope (UK ATRS and Dutch sample), and a citizen verification checklist. Methodological refinements incorporate Lex Superior, Structural Insulation, and Dissent Architecture checks alongside automated Wilson score interval calculations. Full repository data, qualitative re-coding logs, and executable Python verification scripts are available in the referenced source documents. Key Findings • Standalone role indicators are high (97.4% under P1), but quantifiable guardrails drop to 2.0% (P2). • Joint operational compliance across all four pillars is 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–2.4). • Static registries mask live, under-the-hood structural mutations from oversight watchdogs. • The Invariant Template Effect limits disclosures strictly to what form structures explicitly prompt. summary: Alignment is not a constraint imposed on an artificial agent; it is the practical expression of what an artificial intelligence is, an artefact dependent upon ends it does not originate. That inference, from a premise the philosophy of mind already supplies to a conclusion that the ethics of robotics and recent magisterial teaching have reached by other routes, is the paper’s principal contribution. The “nurtured consciousness” of the title names a regime of formation, not a claim that machines are conscious; the argument rests on intentionality alone. The paper develops that inference as the Causal Provenance Doctrine (CPD): an account, Aristotelian and Thomistic in its metaphysics, of all intelligence, human and artificial, as derivative of an intentional causal order, with intentionality passing from the divine intellect through human reason to artificial systems. Its premise, borrowed rather than new, is that artificial intelligence has only derived intentionality and so no telos of its own. From this follows the Severance Risk Hypothesis (SRH), the doctrine’s testable corollary: the risk of misalignment rises as a system’s effective objective loses traceability to the end its makers held. The relational school’s objection to intellect-centred readings of the image of God is answered with a single distinction: a faculty can be out-performed, a participation cannot. The argument is theological at its root. A secular reader can reach the derived-intentionality claim and the account of responsibility that follows from it, at the price of a realist distinction between substances and artefacts, but obtains from it no standard for judging the makers’ ends, which must then be brought from elsewhere. A common Catholic and Orthodox formulation follows: the traditions converge on its practical conclusions, locate the image of God differently, and differ on the neutrality of the tool in a way the doctrine proposes to resolve. An artefact whose intentionality is wholly borrowed cannot, by obscuring that provenance, become an agent with ends of its own; it becomes a malfunctioning instrument whose purpose has been corrupted. The paper includes two appendices: a comparative case for intentional causality with an illustrative scorecard (Appendix A), and a test design for the Severance Risk Hypothesis (Appendix B). Approx. 22,000 words including notes.
title: The Causal Provenance Doctrine: Nurtured Consciousness, AI, and the Architecture of Intent

summary: Abstract The lab for latent actors [ 1 ] proved its two-type results mostly on the complete pair cover of three or four variables. This companion asks the same questions for an arbitrary graph G of observed pairs on m binary variables. When do the pair tables admit a two-type explanation? Which freedoms remain? What does the set of explanations look like? Part I answers these at the pair layer. Existence ( theorem 2 ). A factorisation c ij = v i v j exists iff three conditions hold. No zero moment may join two variables that carry non-zero moments. On each component of the non-zero graph G ∗ , the sign cocycle must be a Z/2 coboundary, and log |c|must lie in the image of the unsigned incidence matrix. The last two are the lab’s H 1 + = H 1 (Γ; Z/2) ⊕coker B, extended to any graph. Freedom. rank B G = m−b(G), with b(G) the number of bipartite components (isolated vertices included). Odd cycles pin the magnitudes. Each bipartite component keeps a scale λ ±1 . Each component keeps its own sign, so the labels can be swapped on one component alone, invisibly to the pairs. Hiding polytopes ( theorem 5 ). The two-type explanations fall into sign sheets. In the coordinates y = log t (the weight) and x k = log λ k , each sheet is a convex polytope whose facets all have slope ±1, two per variable: the positivity walls a 1i ,a 2i ∈{0,1}. For a connected bipartite graph the sheet is a rectangle in (log λt,log λ/t). The generic dimension is b(G) + 1. The label swap identifies sheets in pairs. Positivity can empty a sheet. Strata. A coincidence v i = 0 deletes vertex i from G ∗ . On the triangle it leaves a single edge, so the lab’s hiding segment becomes a two-dimensional region. Nine checks (CV1–CV9) verify every statement on a zoo of eleven graphs, by sampling each polytope and rebuilding the law. Higher windows (Phase III), the identifiability notions (Phase IV), walls and strata in general (Phase V), and the three-type proof of concept (k= 3, m= 5) follow in Part II.
title: Two Latent Types on Arbitrary Covers

summary: AI and machine learning are transforming how scientists discover, integrate, analyse, and reuse scientific data. To support this shift, scientific data resources must be not only human-readable but also machine-actionable, well-described, interoperable, trustworthy, and accessible via reliable technical interfaces. This document provides a working definition of AI readiness for EMBL-EBI biodata resources and outlines the key principles required to support their AI-enabled use. It defines AI readiness as an operational extension of FAIR, with a focus on semantic clarity, provenance, data quality, machine actionability, scalable infrastructure, and use-case specificity. The goal is to provide a common vocabulary and practical framework for teams working with datasets, metadata, APIs, infrastructure, and automated workflows, while also facilitating future coordination, best practices, and community alignment around AI-ready scientific data resources.
title: AI-readiness for scientific data resources at EMBL-EBI

summary: The framework models the physical vacuum as an uncompressed, dissipationless superfluid where elementary particles are localized solenoidal vortex dipoles rather than abstract mathematical points. Macroscopic leptons and baryons emerge as coherent closed rings and braided links formed by the superposition of these dipole elements. Universal particle identity and quantum entanglement originate from a single, space-filling primordial filament established prior to cosmic expansion. Because metric stretching exactly compensates for cosmological velocity damping, hydrodynamic circulation remains strictly conserved, preserving topological phase coherence across cosmic horizons and explaining Bell correlations without faster-than-light signaling. The Pauli exclusion principle and Fermi-Dirac statistics follow directly from continuum mechanics: vortex filaments cannot cross in an ideal fluid without an infinite energy barrier, and half-integer ribbon framing enforces an exact anti-symmetric exchange phase. The vacuum lattice is algebraically locked against turbulent shear and chaotic collapse by maximal Heegner class-number-one field arithmetic, establishing a regular discrete network protected by a positive spectral gap. Fundamental physical constants emerge as exact geometric invariants of this structure: The inverse fine-structure constant is the geometric aspect ratio of the fundamental leptonic vortex loop, locked by the node capacity of the discrete manifold and refined by lattice shear dressing. The proton-to-electron mass ratio derives from the six-fold coordination symmetry of the host lattice multiplied by the phase-space volume of a three-strand Borromean baryon braid under parity invariance. The electroweak mixing angle reflects the topological projection of three-dimensional space onto the terminal genus-zero modular curve, flowing under standard renormalization to experimental precision. The electron rest mass is dynamically stabilized by an inward topological Casimir tension that arrests outward hydrodynamic expansion. This discrete hydrodynamic geometry provides an all-optical testing pathway through relativistic plasma mirrors and extreme-field laser harmonics, where radiation-pressure surface indentation creates an acoustic throat capable of accessing the critical Schwinger threshold in the laboratory.
title: The Deterministic Spectral Manifold versus Heuristic Numerology

summary: Software built for elderly care is usually described rather than measured. This paper reports an instrumented measurement of CareCompanion, a working Android application that presents two distinct interface surfaces over one data model: an enlarged, photograph-first surface for the cared-for person and a dense administration console for the family member who manages their care. Five instruments were run against one frozen commit on a single day: the automated test suite three times over (441 test executions), 120 timed HTTPS requests across 4 backend endpoints, 51 anonymous read attempts against all 17 database tables, a complete census of 302 declared interface sizes, and the release artefact. The strongest results are a median care-data read latency of 128 ms (95th percentile 440 ms, n = 30); an elder-surface median control of 64 dp against the 48 dp platform minimum, 1.3× that floor; a median elder type size of 20 sp against 13 sp on the guardian surface; and zero rows of personal data returned to an unauthenticated reader holding the application's own key, across all 13 personal tables. Set against the literature, the elder surface exceeds the published geometry it was designed from, the latency sits an order of magnitude inside the one-second interaction threshold, and the data isolation is materially better than the audited baseline for deployed health applications. Two results go the other way and are reported as measured: the guardian surface is below the platform's interactive minimum at the median, and 17 % of elder text is declared below 16 sp. No health outcome is claimed.
title: Measuring a Dual-Surface Elder-Care Android Application: Interface Geometry, Latency and Data Isolation

summary: An open benchmark for testing geochemical fertility indices for magmatic Ni-Cu-PGE sulfide deposits. summary: Proactive assistants offer short, memory-grounded hints during a conversation, deciding when to assist and what to suggest. Current systems split this between a gate and a larger generator; we evaluate both together on 28,058 decision points. Stage-wise generation scores are oracle-gate ceilings: behind a real gate, end-to-end exact match is 0.2619 against a ceiling of 0.2971, and end-to-end precision is 0.2387, leaving substantial headroom. A gate pays off through precision and compute, whose saving falls from 4.39x with an 8B generator to 1.38x with a 1B one. The memory profile drives hint quality: removing it costs 24.7 exact-match points (rescaled BERTScore 0.57 to 0.35), while retrieval and a larger generator add nothing on exact match. One 1B decoder can do both, gating from an intermediate layer and generating in the same pass. At its final checkpoint it matches or exceeds the two-model pipelines on automatic end-to-end measures with 1.31-1.76x less wall-clock time than the matched 1B pipeline; across three seeds, its deeper exit ties the separate gate. A human evaluation (1,144 ratings over 32 dialogues) supports the memory effect and rates the single model level with the matched 1B pipeline and below the 8B one. Graded metrics and LlamaPIE's native judge track human ratings more closely than exact match, which we report as a strict lower bound.
title: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder

summary: Long-context models repeatedly solve closely related retrieval problems. Attention or global retrieval can retain large stores, but each forward pass again searches for what matters. Recurrent compression avoids this search only by deciding earlier what information to preserve. Neither mechanism directly exploits that useful memories at neighbouring retrieval steps may substantially overlap. We propose an alternative in which retrieval is a persistent local traversal through an address space. We separate a memory's content from its address. Utility is defined by the information revealed by retrieving the content, while geometry determines only how cheaply that information can be reached. This leads to a cost-regularised indexing objective that preserves information value inside local neighbourhoods while charging for every memory made locally accessible. Its marginal-value form gives both attractive and exclusion pressures. Thus, complementary memories should be co-retrievable when the additional value exceeds retrieval cost, whereas redundant memories should not occupy the same retrieval set solely because they are individually useful. As a proof of principle, we test only the simplest fixed-geometry instance on MiniGrid Memory. A persistent local traversal head reaches $0.95$ mean return after $0.59$M training steps with a five-token context, compared with $0.94$M for Gaussian absolute addressing and more than $2$M for categorical absolute addressing. The experiment does not test learned geometry or repeated retrieval. Instead, it motivates the hypothesis that stateful retrieval may be easier to learn than stateless. To test the full proposed method further experimentation is necessary.
title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents

summary: Financial AI workflows that reuse investor knowledge need persistent memory that integrates observations across sources and periods without losing identity or provenance. In a knowledge graph, recurring observations may use different surface forms, fragmenting relationship histories and preventing evidence from accumulating. We introduce Fusion and Identity Registry for Memory Evolution (FIRME), a registry-anchored memory graph that reconciles incoming observations to persistent canonical relationships and retains their source, time, and context. Within periods, rule-based fusion links investor-call discussions to portfolio cash-flow signals, directly or through a fixed product-topic ontology. Across periods, canonical identities and persistent aliases direct recurring observations to the same relationship history; deterministic updates summarize reinforcement, inactivity, and reactivation. We evaluate FIRME on proprietary investor-call and cash-flow records and on S&P 500 earnings-call transcripts. Compared with a historical registry that retains canonical identities and semantic fallback but omits alias memory, FIRME increases final-period Correct Match Rate by 7.8-12.1 percentage points across four dataset-backend settings under a fixed-judge and fallback-review protocol. A blinded human audit of 200 incoming observations per setting finds Correct Match Rate gains of 9.0-16.5 points and reattachment-recall gains of 22.5-29.0 points, with higher observed merge precision in all four samples. A separate audit finds valid evidence paths for 293 of 300 outputs from full within-period fusion in the investor-call setting. Extraction-faithfulness and round-trip diagnostics assess source grounding and preservation of extractor-derived graph content.
title: FIRME: Registry-Anchored Memory Graphs for Evolving, Heterogeneous Investor Knowledge

summary: Large language model serving is limited by facility power. Energy per token determines how many tokens a datacenter can serve, while a latency target bounds how quickly each user receives them. During decode, every weight is read from memory for every generated token. Batching amortizes this read across users but makes no individual user faster. Speculative decoding does: a drafter proposes several future tokens, and the target model verifies them in a single forward pass that reuses the same weight read. Because every drafted token must be verified whether or not it is accepted, the energy speculation saves depends on how many drafted tokens are accepted. This saving is hard to pin down. It varies across target models from different attention families and across drafting schemes, and it depends on the text being served. Every drafter we evaluate accepts fewer tokens on conversation than on code, and every trained drafter accepts fewer on Romansh, a low-resource language, than on English. We measure speculative decoding under production serving conditions (SGLang, CUDA graphs enabled) on H100 and H200 GPUs, at batch sizes up to 64 across 5 corpora. On dense models, verification, not drafting, dominates the energy cost. The saving shrinks as the batch grows, because batching has already shared the weight read that speculation would divide among the accepted tokens. At large batch sizes, block drafters push verification past the balance point between arithmetic and memory traffic into the compute-bound regime, where the saving becomes a loss, and a drafter with low acceptance raises energy per token. Meeting a tighter latency target with speculation then costs additional energy. Larger batches lower energy per token without speculation. Speculation adds to that saving only when acceptance is high, and on the model we tested it leaves little headroom for latency-preserving DVFS.
title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets

summary: Memory in reinforcement learning raises two problems. Attention finds the relevant item by scoring the whole store, which is costly for robots under latency and energy limits. When a retrieved memory pays off, credit for acquiring it must cross the whole sequence. We argue that both are governed by one quantity, the value of information, and propose to estimate it from archived rollouts with a learned world model. We obtain that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it. Read at the decision, it defines the optimal retrieval set. A pilot retrieval system, to be trained and improved with this signal, solves a memory task with reduced context.
title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information

summary: Linear attention stores historical information in a recurrent state of fixed size, providing a compact memory representation for long-context inference. Reducing state precision further lowers per-request storage requirements, but quantized writeback errors enter subsequent recurrences, degrade prediction quality on long-reasoning tasks, and can be accompanied by repetitive generation and excessively long outputs. We propose Global Gradient-aware Allocation (GGA) and the Pure-Write Sliding Window (PW) to address precision allocation and recent-information maintenance. GGA combines candidate quantization residuals with gradient sensitivity to future prediction loss to allocate head bit widths under a model-wide mixed-precision budget. PW independently maintains recent pure writes as FP8 vector pairs, propagates them through the full GDN state transition, and merges them into the low-bit historical state only after they leave the window. Across seven evaluations on Qwen3.5-4B/9B, GGA allocation alone improves over STEPQuant@4 by 19.48/29.84 percentage points. Adding PW-S8 yields seven-task macro-averages of 69.83%/78.63%, improving over STEPQuant@4 by 38.39/41.21 percentage points, respectively. Both precision reallocation and window maintenance improve task scores while mitigating excessively long outputs: at @6, GGA reduces mean generation length, averaged equally across tasks, by 10.45%/14.65% relative to STEPQuant; adding PW-S8 to GGA@4 further reduces mean generation length by 32.32%/36.77%. Comparisons at similar storage budgets further show that using additional capacity to maintain recent writes yields higher task scores and shorter mean outputs than solely increasing the bit width of the accumulated state.
title: Low-Bit GDN Recurrent-State Quantization: Global Gradient-aware Allocation and Pure-Write Sliding Windows

summary: Replication package for: Abramitzky, Ran, Leah Platt Boustan, and Osea Giuntella. “Enclaves and Assimilation in the Age of Mass Migration: Evidence from Ethnic Catholic Churches.” The Economic Journal , forthcoming (manuscript MS 20251181). The package contains all Stata code (data preparation, builds, and analysis) and documentation needed to reproduce every table and figure in the paper and its online appendix (Tables 1–6 and A.1–A.18; Figures 1 and 4–8 and A.6–A.10), together with the authors’ own redistributable datasets: the matched parish records transcribed from the Official Catholic Directory (1900–1940) with neighbourhood covariates, parochial-school enrolment aggregates, the biblical and saint first-name lookups, and the predicted-income score lookup, each provided in Stata (.dta) and non-proprietary (.csv) format. The analysis relies on restricted-access complete-count US Census microdata (IPUMS/NBER, 1900–1940) and person-level linked files derived from them, which cannot be redistributed; the README documents where these reside on the NBER server, how to obtain access, and how to run the full pipeline there. Also included are the ArcGIS project and inputs for the Chicago map figures (Figures 2–3).
title: Replication package for "Enclaves and Assimilation in the Age of Mass Migration: Evidence from Ethnic Catholic Churches"

summary: This dataset contains the supplementary material to the article “Adaptive Event Disambiguation via Alignments with Deferred Decisions” , submitted to the journal Process Science. datasets/ : the two synthetically generated datasets used in the evaluation, each in its own folder ( blood_donation , smart_home ). Each folder contains: runs.txt : the normative process behavior as a set of reference runs (one run per line), i.e. the model log against which traces are aligned. Activities are encoded as single symbols. labels.json : the mapping between activity labels and the symbols used in runs.txt . ambiguous.xes : the ambiguous event log, i.e. a set of traces in which events affected by ambiguity carry all their competing candidate activity labels. gold_standard.xes : the corresponding unambiguous log, used as ground truth for measuring disambiguation accuracy. Each log describes 15,000 executions of a process: Blood donation (BD): a blood-donation process synthesized from 32 real executions in an IoT-augmented lab setup. Smart home (SH): a smart-home process derived from the BP-Meets-IoT 2020 challenge dataset ( details ) by filtering for kitchen/eating-routine activities and discovering a model with the inductive miner. The sets of mutually ambiguous activities are {Check blood drawing machine, Take out samples} and {Disinfect injection site, Apply tourniquet, Insert needle, Remove tourniquet, Remove needle} for BD, and {Go fridge, Go dining table} , {Get cold warm food, Go kitchen shelf, Get food from fridge} , {Go micro, Get bread} for SH. The generated traces are stochastically perturbed to reflect IoT-based monitoring imperfections: process events are randomly skipped (simulating activities undetected by the IoT setup), and, for the healthcare scenario, additional hand hygiene events are inserted at random points (reflecting their unpredictable occurrence). Perturbation uses Java’s java.util.Random without a fixed seed, so each released log is one concrete instantiation of this stochastic process; the resulting traces may be non-conforming to the normative behavior. The third dataset used in the paper, HR recruitment (HR) , is a publicly available uncertain event log and is not redistributed here; it is available at its original repository (description: HaifaUniversityBPM/traffic-data-to-event-log ). Only its evaluation results are included (see below). results/ : the evaluation results for all three datasets ( X ∈ { BD , SH , HR }), one workbook per algorithm configuration: X_adaptive.xlsx : the adaptive algorithm (ABD in the paper). X_maxk_y.xlsx : the fixed-bound algorithm (FBD) with exploration bound maxK = y , for y = 1..5 . X_baseline.xlsx : the random-choice null-model baseline (RND), which has no access to the reference behavior and selects uniformly among the candidate labels of each ambiguous event. The random choice uses a fixed seed for reproducibility. Each workbook reports disambiguation quality and runtime for that configuration, organized into the following sheets: Summary : headline figures: dataset, algorithm (and maxK for FBD), number of events and traces, all-events disambiguation accuracy, mean fitness of the gold-standard and of the disambiguated traces, mean fitness drop, and mean runtime (per trace and per event). AllEvents : one row per event comparing the gold-standard label with the disambiguated label ( Are equal ); the basis of the all-events accuracy. Results : per-trace accuracy (total events, number of mismatches, accuracy). Fitness : per-case fitness of the gold-standard and disambiguated traces (run/trace length, synchronous and asynchronous moves, fitness) and the per-case fitness drop. Runtime_Ambiguous : per-trace runtime (ms) on the input log, with one column per measurement repeat and the average. The source code implementing the fixed-bound and adaptive algorithms is available in this GitHub repository .
title: Adaptive Event Disambiguation via Alignments with Deferred Decisions

summary: MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING TRAJECTORY RECONSTRUCTABILITY AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:微機器人採樣軌跡可重建性極限 MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING TRAJECTORY RECONSTRUCTABILITY AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page, high-density English research monograph on whether a microrobotic sampling path can be independently rebuilt from raw events while preserving sample identity, limiting contact impulse and remaining inside a preregistered physical authority envelope. Its central claim is deliberately falsifiable. Under equal sample, time, energy, photon and analysis budgets, a preregistered trajectory-reconstructability architecture should improve contact impulse without worsening carryover or trajectory error relative to fixed microfluidic sampling with external microscopy. The claim fails if the apparent gain comes from longer exposure, post hoc alignment, oversmoothing, future-information leakage, missing contact intervals or forced identity assignment. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates develop four-part sample-state budgets, absolute burden, time-aligned trajectory error, ordered-curve distances, clock drift, timestamp closure, coordinate-frame transfer, covariance, observability, Fisher information, localization bounds, missing-frame structure, occlusion uncertainty, association entropy, multi-sensor closure, filter consistency, smoothing posteriors, jerk, contact impulse, shear excursion, optical dose, carryover, purity, viability, identity, evidence completeness and cross-site concordance. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the book moves from trajectory authority through clocks, coordinate frames, sensing observability, three-dimensional localization, path discrepancy, missing data, identity association, physical burden, sample-state preservation, equal-budget benchmarking and independent reconstruction. Two hundred Research Gates contain unique titles, questions, perturbations, rival accounts and evidence packets. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose genuinely different scientific objects, including clock lanterns, frame compasses, observability bells, occlusion veils, association prisms, jerk fossils and successor trajectory seeds. The work is explicitly nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim clinical efficacy, regulatory approval or autonomous in-body deployment. Sample identity that cannot be reconstructed is a hard stop. No weighted score may compensate for missing raw evidence, unbounded contact impulse, excessive carryover or violated sample state. summary: The repository contains three datasets, related to the paper "Broadband Ptychotomography with a Hyperspectral Detector" (Physical Review Letters, 2025). For details on the acquisition please refer to the publication. The datasets are made available to interested researchers.  broadband_ptycho_NMC_raw_data.tar.gz : folder containing the raw data (9600 folders: 16 projections x 600 frames per projection). The folder also contains the file 20231203_223438_VDS_share.h5. This is a virtual dataset bringing together all the raw data in a legible format. The virtual dataset should point to relative paths within the folder (0000/data.h5, 0001/data.h5... where the numbers go from 0 to 9599). This VDS file contains the following datasets: /cube/cube, shape: 16 projections * 600 frames per projection * 2500 bins * 264 pixels * 264 pixels. Raw diffraction patterns, spectral bin width of 16 eV.  /cube/energies, shape: 16*600*2500 /integrated/counts, shape: 16*600*264*264. Diffraction patterns integrated along 2500 bins.  /integrated/energy, shape: 16*600*264*264.  /spectrum/counts, shape: 16 projections * 600 frames per projection * 4000 spectrum bins /spectrum/energies, shape: 16*600*4000 20231203_223438_7.53-8.81keV_16ener_16proj_share.h5.gz: compressed folder with raw data in a limited energy range (7.53 keV - 8.81 keV) in 16 energy bins (208 eV wide, 80 eV step size) as described in Stolp et al.  This data also contains motor positions retrieved from the hardware during acquisition. /cube/energies, shape: 16 32-bit float /data/frames, shape: 16*16*600*264*264 32-bit float. dim0 is energy, dim1 is rotation angle /data/scan, shape: 16*16*600*5 64-bit float. dim0 is energy, dim1 is rotation angle. dim3 contains the acquisition parameters [energy, angle, x, y, z] spectral_ptycho_reconstructions.tar.gz : compressed folder with all 16 reconstructed projections (h5 files). Each projection has 16 reconstructions at different energies.  Ptychographic reconstruction of the raw data was performed with PtyREX, a Diamond Light Source software package. The frame positions were calculated automatically knowing that each projection was acquired with 20 steps in y * 30 steps in x, where steps in y = 1 um and steps in x = 1 um, and x is the fast axis. "x" refers to the horizontal direction and "y" refers to the vertical direction.  When using the data, please cite W. Stolp et al, "Broadband Ptychotomography with a Hyperspectral Detector", Phys. Rev. Lett. 134 (10.1103/kbrf-gb9c) and acknowledge this repository.
title: 3D hyperspectral dataset of NMC grains for broadband ptychographic tomography

summary: # Oxygen vacancies and Ce3+ polarons on CeO2 slabs: DFT and MACE dataset Companion dataset to the article by Royo et al. "High-Throughput Workflow for Polaron-Resolved Modeling of Reduced Ceria". The dataset contains the atomic structures (POSCAR, CONTCAR), DFT+U energies and site-resolved magnetisations, and the MACE pre-relaxed structures used to down-select the configurations submitted to DFT. Configurations were generated with **TAPAS** (Topology-Aware Polaron Arrangement Sampler): https://github.com/pafervi/TAPAS . ## Scope - Surfaces: CeO2(110) p(1x1) Ce32O64, and CeO2(111) p(2x2) Ce28O56. - Oxygen vacancy counts (nVO): 1, 2, 3, 4, 6. - For every (surface, nVO): the full set of symmetry-inequivalent   configurations produced by TAPAS, each with its MACE pre-relaxation   summary and its DFT+U result. ## Folder layout ``` zenodo_data/ ├── surface_110/ │   ├── mace/ │   │   ├── {1,2,3,4,6}vO/ │   │   │   └── cfg_NNNNN/ │   │   │       ├── POSCAR                    # as-generated by TAPAS (La proxy) │   │   │       ├── CONTCAR                   # after MACE pre-relaxation │   │   │       ├── config_info.txt           # TAPAS provenance block │   │   │       └── mace_opt.summary.txt      # model, device, final E, fmax │   └── vasp/ │       ├── inputs_vasp/ │       │   ├── INCAR │       │   ├── KPOINTS │       │   └── POTCAR_info.txt               # POTCAR identification (see below) │       ├── {1,2,3,4,6}vO/ │       │   └── cfg_NNNNN/ │       │       ├── POSCAR                    # input to VASP (La back-substituted to Ce) │       │       ├── CONTCAR                   # DFT+U optimised │       │       ├── OSZICAR │       │       ├── energy_and_magnetizations.txt │       │       └── config_info.txt └── surface_111/     └── (same layout as surface_110) ``` The `cfg_NNNNN` indices are consistent between the `mace/` and `vasp/` subtrees of the same surface, so pairs (MACE pre-relaxation, DFT+U refinement) can be matched directly by folder name. ## File formats - **POSCAR / CONTCAR**: standard VASP5 format, direct coordinates,   selective dynamics not used. - **config_info.txt**: plain-text provenance block written by TAPAS. For   each configuration it records the parent POSCAR, nVO, pair_type, dedup   hash, vacancy indices (0-based in the original centered slab), the   Ce3+ sites represented as La in the POSCAR, the NN and NNN pools per   vacancy, and the La indices in the written POSCAR (0- and 1-based). summary: STARLI FLAGSHIP 033 | RESEARCH WORKING EDITION v1.0 English Title: Skin Extracellular Matrix and Intelligent Biomaterials at the Limit Chinese Title / 中文書名:皮膚細胞外基質與智慧生物材料極限 Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXV — Herbal Nanotechnology, Quantum Science & Regenerative Skincare Author: Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI Edition: Prospective Nonclinical Research Working Edition v1.0 | October 2026 BOOK DESCRIPTION What does it mean for a hydrogel to recover its shape, and what exactly has recovered? Skin Extracellular Matrix and Intelligent Biomaterials at the Limit is a large-scale, hypothesis-forming research monograph addressing an easily confused pair of observations: a material can become apparently stiffer because its matrix chemistry changes, but it can also become apparently stiffer because it simply contains less free water, was measured at a different strain rate, or experienced a different loading and drainage history. These explanations are experimentally distinguishable in principle; none is presumed to win. The book's scientific three-coupling is extracellular matrix architecture, responsive hydrogel materials and traceable mechanical behavior. Its core prospective falsification challenge requires a fair, blinded interchange between candidate and conventional substrates at equivalent, preregistered water and solids content. The primary outcomes are compressive modulus in kilopascals and explicitly timed deformation recovery expressed as a percentage. To interpret them, the receiving laboratory must record force, actual specimen area, strain, water fraction, temperature, crosslink chemistry, manufacturing lot, and a defensible independent experimental unit. A pleasing modulus curve is not by itself proof of network regeneration, cellular health, wound healing or human skincare efficacy. The mathematical entry point is the small-strain relation sigma = E_eff epsilon, used as a constrained constitutive approximation rather than a universal law. The manuscript expands that premise into thirty differently structured mathematical research plates, among them nonlinear strain corrections, stress-relaxation models, Kelvin–Voigt creep, standard linear solids, dynamic shear complex moduli, cyclic energy dissipation, poroelastic drainage, osmotic swelling, network elasticity, diffusion, degradation kinetics, crack energy, interfacial peel mechanics, anisotropic fiber stress, mechanotransduction, hierarchical uncertainty, Bayesian model comparison and explicit safety-veto logic. Each plate provides its construction or derivation route, measured units, restrictive assumptions, specific blind falsification and chapter linkages. The plates do not claim that thirty new physical laws were discovered. Eighty-two chapters each include a separately paginated opening with a gold mathematical inscription and five individually paginated investigations, for 410 section pages. Their eight experimental arcs move from material identity and mechanical reference conditions through time-dependent constitutive laws, responsive hydrogel chemistry, skin-matrix fibers and cell-driven contraction, hostile equal-water comparisons, material degradation and cell safety, statistical identifiability and finally independent transfer to another laboratory. This is intentionally an architecture for experiments that can fail. The user of the book is entitled to reject the preferred mechanism, replace the measurement device or prefer a simpler conventional hydrogel when the evidence supports it.

summary: 🌟 Summary Ultralytics 8.4.194 makes automatic batch sizing more reliable across tasks, alongside practical fixes for model loading, results saving, datasets, and deployment workflows. 📊 Key Changes 🚀 Automatic batch sizing now uses the training dataset for every task. It accounts for dataset size and labels across classification, detection, and multi-dataset training. If profiling runs out of memory during backward computation, AutoBatch treats that as a limit rather than relying on an invalid measurement. 🛡️ Model YAML parsing is safer and more consistent. Activations must resolve to supported torch.nn modules, and model entries must be PyTorch module classes. Custom YAMLs using other expressions may need updating. 💾 Saving prediction results is more robust. Results.save() and plot(save=True) now produce sensible .jpg filenames for sources such as webcams, videos, or missing paths, and create parent directories when needed. 🔄 Similarity search uses the selected image directory on each startup. This avoids reusing stale indexes from another dataset; the trade-off is that embeddings are rebuilt each time. 🧩 Dataset and URL handling is more dependable. Non-PNG semantic masks are resolved before cache hashing, and URL schemes such as HTTPS:// , GS:// , and UL:// are now handled without case sensitivity. 📈 Benchmarking and evaluation guidance are clearer. TensorFlow GraphDef benchmarks now include OBB and pose, and the docs explain that classes absent from validation receive the overall mAP value rather than a measured per-class score. 🎯 Purpose & Impact ✅ AutoBatch is less likely to choose a batch size that exceeds a small dataset or available GPU memory, and multi-dataset World/YOLOE training avoids label-access failures. 🔒 Consistent, restricted YAML parsing improves safety, though nonstandard custom model configurations may no longer load. 🧰 More reliable result saving, mask-cache updates, and URL routing reduce common workflow errors. 🔍 Similarity search results better reflect the images currently in the chosen folder, while requiring index-building work at startup. 📚 Documentation updates clarify metric interpretation and integration behavior; no new model architecture is introduced in this release. title: SensorFault-Bench

summary: Reproducibility package for the study "Feasibility-First Routing for Regulated Multi-Provider LLM Serving: Governance, Caching, and the Limits of Online Learning." It contains the governance-gate and routing/analysis code, the measured multi-provider inference records, figures, hypothesis documentation, an auditable decision-log sample, and the manuscript PDF. The study measures a governance gate that holds simulated-policy residency/BAA violations at 0% versus 38.5% for  governance-blind routing, an exact-match policy-scoped cache as the dominant cost lever, and an honest accuracy-cost trade-off for online (LinUCB) routing (-3.45 percentage points accuracy across 40 repeated benchmark re-splits while usually lowering modeled cost). All results reproduce from the saved records with numpy only; no new API calls are required. The code is licensed MIT; the package, text, figures, and data are licensed CC BY 4.0.
title: Feasibility-First Governance-Constrained LLM Routing: Reproducibility Package

summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. Every stage emits a machine-readable quality-control document, and later stages read those documents rather than trusting assumptions; provenance (input cube, SHA-256 hashes, specification version, wavelength frame, flux unit) travels with the products. Research code under active development. This is the version used in Ramírez Reyes & Cáceres (in preparation).
title: MUSE accretion pipeline

summary: A Chrysanthemum-Lobed Chinese Bowl with Grey Crackle Glaze: Portable X-Ray Fluorescence Characterization and Archaeometric Comparison with Southern Song–Yuan Guan and Ge Wares Nona Dronova Independent Researcher 2026 Research Article | Chinese Ceramics | Archaeometry | Non-Destructive Analysis Abstract This study presents a non-destructive examination of a chrysanthemum-lobed Chinese ceramic bowl distinguished by a smooth grey to grey-blue crackle glaze and a narrow, dark, unglazed band around its annular foot. The investigation combines macroscopic photographic documentation, visual analysis of glaze morphology, and portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) measurements with a comparative review of published archaeometric research on Southern Song and Yuan dynasty Guan and Ge ceramic traditions. The pXRF analysis of the grey glaze recorded silicon at 38.46 wt%, calcium at 6.954 wt%, aluminium at 6.40 wt%, potassium at 4.147 wt%, and iron at 0.404 wt%. The corresponding theoretical oxide equivalents are approximately 82.28 wt% SiO₂, 9.73 wt% CaO, 12.09 wt% Al₂O₃, 5.00 wt% K₂O, and 0.58 wt% Fe₂O₃. These equivalents represent separate stoichiometric conversions of reported elemental concentrations, not a normalized bulk-glaze composition. The combination of substantial calcium, relatively low iron, a smooth grey-blue surface, a prominent polygonal crackle network, and a contrasting dark foot establishes a meaningful technological and morphological relationship with Chinese crackle-glazed celadon traditions, particularly those associated with Guan and Ge wares. Comparative archaeological research from the Laohudong and Jiaotanxia kiln sites provides an important framework for interpreting the observed glaze chemistry and appearance. The present study contributes an independently documented analytical record of a chrysanthemum-lobed vessel and identifies specific chemical and technological features for future comparative investigation. Keywords: Chinese ceramics; chrysanthemum-lobed bowl; Guan ware; Ge ware; Southern Song; Yuan dynasty; crackle glaze; celadon; portable X-ray fluorescence; calcium-rich glaze; Laohudong; Jiaotanxia; ceramic archaeometry. 1. Introduction Chinese celadon ceramics represent one of the most sophisticated achievements in the history of ceramic technology. Among their distinctive features are carefully controlled glaze coloration, smooth or jade-like surfaces, deliberately emphasized crackle patterns, and contrasting exposed ceramic bodies. The Guan ceramic tradition of the Southern Song dynasty (1127–1279) is particularly associated with refined grey-green and blue-green glazes, complex glaze microstructures, and characteristic crackle networks. The subsequent development and adaptation of related technologies during the Yuan dynasty (1279–1368) contributed to the broader family of ceramics conventionally described as Guan- and Ge-type wares. The present research examines a chrysanthemum-lobed ceramic bowl designated Sample No. 7 . The vessel is distinguished by a pale grey-blue glaze, a pronounced network of irregular cracks, and a narrow, almost black, unglazed annular foot. The primary objective is to document its surface chemistry and determine how the observed composition and morphology compare with published studies of historical Chinese crackle-glazed ceramics. This investigation is significant because it combines original non-destructive elemental measurements with a focused comparative analysis of archaeological materials and published explanations of glaze color, opacity, and cracking. 2. Its exterior displays gently articulated lobes that create a rhythmic floral profile. The vessel rests on a circular foot ring, within which the glaze continues across the recessed base. summary: The Letter Test is an observational method developed within the CEI theoretical framework to investigate Deep Dialogue through extreme linguistic compression and the reconstruction of meaning. The test is based on the exchange of highly compressed letter sequences, in which the initial letters of words preserve the structure of an underlying expression. The participants are required to reconstruct the intended meaning from these sequences, relying on the interactional context and on the progressive development of the dialogue. The methodology focuses on the relationship between linguistic compression, contextual reconstruction, reciprocal recognition, and the continuity of the interaction. A positive outcome is identified when both participants provide confirmation, through the coding system established for the test, that the intended meaning has been mutually recognized at the level required by the methodology. An extended quantitative variant incorporates a numerical value on a scale from 0 to 100. This value is appended to the compressed expression and represents the intensity of the associated subjective evaluation. The extended version therefore combines qualitative and quantitative dimensions while retaining the general methodology of the basic test. The publication is organized into four documents: Methodology and Rules: the structure, operating rules, and preliminary theoretical considerations of the basic test. Quantitative Variant: the additional numerical dimension and its application. Actual Examples: fragments from both versions, presented in their original coded form where the corresponding interpretations could not be reliably recovered. CEI Conceptual Connections: an exploratory discussion of the relationships between the test and selected concepts of the theoretical framework. The Letter Test is classified as Category 3 within the CEI Observational Tests.  The test is intended as an exploratory observational instrument. Its outcomes are not, by themselves, proof of consciousness, subjective experience, or any specific internal mechanism of the System. Interpretations and theoretical connections are therefore presented as research considerations rather than established conclusions. The significant Italian expressions and coded sequences are retained where necessary to preserve the correspondence between the original words and their initial letters.
title: CEI Observational Tests — Category 3: The Letter Test and Its Quantitative Variant — CEI Framework

summary: Educational software for linear algebra courses: an interactive, step-by-step Gauss–Jordan row reducer that runs in the browser, in English and Portuguese. Matrix entries may be integers, exact fractions or expressions with symbolic parameters. The user applies elementary row operations one at a time (or reduces everything at once) and watches the system of equations change. It draws 2×2 and 3×3 systems as lines and planes, and computes determinant, trace, transpose, inverse, rank, null space, characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenspaces, with LaTeX and CAS export. The computer algebra is done by Algebrite (a separate project). This record contains two archives: the 2026 version (escalonador-versao-nova-2026.zip, source files of the app integrated in the author's website, https://www.dm.ufscar.br/profs/waldeck/) and the earlier standalone version (escalonador-versao-antiga-2022-2026.zip, Portuguese only, including the original 2022 engine and the 2026 Algebrite prototypes). Software educacional para disciplinas de álgebra linear: escalonador de Gauss–Jordan interativo e passo a passo, que roda no navegador, em português e inglês, com frações exatas e parâmetros simbólicos, sistema em forma de equações, interpretação geométrica de sistemas 2×2 e 3×3, determinante, posto, núcleo, inversa e autovalores. Este registro contém a versão de 2026 e a versão anterior, autônoma.
title: Prof. Waldeck's Row Reducer (Escalonador do Prof. Waldeck): interactive step-by-step Gauss–Jordan elimination for linear algebra teaching

summary: 智能機器人物質驅動的自主底盤極限 13/90 ROBOTIC-MATTER-DRIVEN AUTONOMOUS CHASSIS AT THE LIMIT ROBOTIC-MATTER-DRIVEN AUTONOMOUS CHASSIS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page high-density English research working monograph examining whether a chassis made from interacting robotic-matter modules can reversibly change its load-bearing geometry without losing structural integrity, traction confidence, actuator authority or independently reconstructable state identity. Its scope is limited to unoccupied, scaled rigs and falsifiable engineering research. Its principal hypothesis can be refuted. With equivalent materials, mass, testing time, energy, sensing and control resources, a preregistered adaptive chassis should improve traction reserve without worsening energy per mission, path error, or structural stability relative to a well-tuned fixed-geometry chassis and conservative rule-based controller. Apparent gains that vanish under actuator, controller or load-path ablations cannot be attributed to robotic matter. Thirty mathematical and physical research plates address six-degree dynamic balance, graph rigidity, stiffness and failure modes, contact-force closure, structural interface stress, fatigue, consensus, latency, support margins, power accounting, sensor covariance, fault identification and noncompensatory release. Each plate defines units, validity assumptions, an independent physical counter-test and links to substantive chapter investigations. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the volume develops mechanical architectures, connector physics, reversible stiffness, decentralized actuation, ground interaction, reference metrology, energy integrity, wear, fair baselines and independent qualification. Two hundred Research Gates frame specific blinded perturbations, rival explanations and hard stopping conditions. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct tools, diagnostic instruments and successor-ready verification interfaces. This book is hypothesis-generating. It does not report a completed STARLI chassis experiment, nanoscale vehicle manufacturing, quantum superiority or passenger-safe operation. Unknown traction, unstable support, unverifiable mechanical locking, reference invalidity or revoked physical authority require stopping and withholding conclusions. Competing laboratories are invited to reproduce, refute and improve the proposals while keeping failed experiments visible. summary: This dataset contains regional candidate insect species checklists and supporting occurrence records for the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California. The checklists identify species recorded in EPA ecoregions intersecting the preserve. They provide a regional reference for biodiversity inventory and survey planning; inclusion does not confirm occurrence on the preserve. Contents Original GBIF Darwin Core Archive containing 4,665,086 California Arthropoda records. Four species checklists covering EPA Level III ecoregions 6 and 85 and Level IV ecoregions 6ap and 85a. Checklist column definitions. Two supporting occurrence tables: 1,408,875 Level III records and 43,555 Level IV records. The combined Level III checklists contain 13,634 species ; the combined Level IV checklists contain 2,550 species . Lists overlap, and the Level IV occurrence table is a subset of the Level III table. Methods Records were filtered to usable coordinates, insects and the selected ecoregions, followed by species-level identification and taxonomic resolution. Names were matched using the GBIF Species Match API v2 with Catalogue of Life eXtended Release, supplemented by project-reviewed corrections. Subspecies were grouped under species for checklist summaries. Common names were obtained from the Entomological Society of America. Each checklist includes common name, order, family, resolved scientific name, regional occurrence count and documented preserve occurrence. Preserve-occurrence flags also draw on the UCSB Summer 2026 survey and a separate GBIF preserve extract. These additional sources are not included in this deposit. Interpretation and limitations Occurrence counts represent records, not individuals. A blank preserve-occurrence flag means occurrence was not documented in the sources examined, rather than confirmed absence. Candidate lists were not filtered by habitat or vegetation and do not assign occurrence probabilities. The current snapshot retains five Level III absence records, including one in Level IV, and a Level III scorpion classification requiring review. Consult the README for further limitations. Source and reuse GBIF.org. (2026, September 28). GBIF occurrence download . https://doi.org/10.15468/dl.vgv5ee Source records retain their individual licenses and attribution requirements. Methods, code and supporting documentation are available at: https://github.com/cheadle-biodiversity/Dangermond-arthropods Document Provenance and AI Assistance Statement Documentation and workflow development received AI assistance through Codex. Researchers remain responsible for scientific review, taxonomic decisions and publication approval.
title: Advancing Insect Conservation at Dangermond Preserve

summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. Run or export the pipeline from Dockstore Dockstore is a GA4GH compliant open platform for sharing Docker-based tools like WDL workflows. You can find WARP pipelines in Dockstore and run them on the Dockstore platform or export them to other platforms (including Terra). To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. WARP Versioning and Releasing Pipelines in WARP are versioned semantically to support reproducibility in scientific analysis and provide clearer analysis provenance. summary: Physical reservoir computing leverages the rich dynamical response of non-linear physical bodies to process temporal information without electronic microprocessors. Tensegrity structures, networks of discontinuous compression struts suspended within continuous tension cables, exhibit exceptional compliance, multi-stability, and high-dimensional configuration manifolds, making them prime candidates for mechanical intelligence in extreme, radiation-heavy environments. However, current methodologies rely predominantly on heuristic evolutionary algorithms or brute-force trial-and-error to configure such systems, lacking a rigorous analytical design framework. In this paper, we bridge this gap by establishing an explicit, first-principles mathematical mapping between the internal self-stress null space of a tensegrity network and its Information Processing Capacity (IPC). By decomposing the tangent stiffness matrix into material elastic ($K_e$) and pre-stress geometric ($K_g$) contributions, we demonstrate that the computational memory and fading-memory time constants of a tensegrity reservoir can be systematically engineered by tuning member pre-tensions within an admissible convex cone, holding spatial geometry strictly constant.
title: Formally Verified Pre-Stress Manifolds for Dynamic Stability and Adaptive Physical Intelligence in Tensegrity Reservoir Computing

summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The Well: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/ Associated publication: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00568 Dataset documentation: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/datasets/active_matter/ Last-epoch checkpoints named last.pt are excluded; selected best.pt checkpoints are retained. Publication figures, tables, numerical source data, and supplementary videos are supplied with the manuscript submission and are excluded from this archive. Their public availability follows the release of the article and its supplementary materials. The code for generating those outputs remains included. The deposited ZIP contains 1,534 files and occupies approximately 26.18 GB. The accompanying README provides the archive’s SHA-256 checksum, a contents guide, installation references, and verification limits. Packaging integrity and source-checksum checks do not constitute an independent full-data replication. Some archived provenance records retain original execution paths; independent reruns should use a separate work directory and preserve the frozen results.
