summary: ENERGY DISTRIBUTION IN INTELLIGENT ROBOTIC MATTER AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:智能機器人物質能源分配極限 21/90 ENERGY DISTRIBUTION IN INTELLIGENT ROBOTIC MATTER AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition of STARLI's YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, asking whether twenty-four locally controlled robotic-matter modules can share a bounded energy supply for a fixed, verified vehicle-body reconfiguration task without concealing external work, structural risk or unsafe communication delays. The three-coupling is Energy Networks x Distributed Power Supply x Vehicle Reconfiguration. Tests are restricted to unoccupied, scaled hardware, traceable electrical rails and laboratory/hardware-in-the-loop environments; no completed roadworthy or nanorobotic supercar is claimed. The falsifiable hypothesis is that a pre-registered distributed allocator can reduce total mission joules at the same useful task, material mass, sensing quality, energy sources, cooling, computation, time and operator budget as a properly optimized wired centralized architecture, while not worsening critical command latency. A hidden unmetered driver, local thermal hotspot, power-rail partition, stale packets, reserve deficit or failure of physical stopping defeats the claim. The supplied consensus model, dx_i/dt = -sum_j a_ij(x_i-x_j)+w_i, is used to study local agreement; agreement alone cannot prove charge conservation, battery state of charge or safe power distribution. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates examine energy-balance and signed-work integration, nodal current conservation, converter and contact losses, motor work, SOC integration and transient terminal voltage, resistor networks, rated-edge loading, droop sharing, negative incremental impedance, spectral connectivity, packet age, deadline reliability, thermal RC and Joule heating, dependent hazards, stop-energy reserve, constrained dispatch, worst-node tail risk, covariance propagation and physical safe-stop latency. Each plate provides mathematical or physical construction, dimensional limits, an individually specified blind challenge and chapter references. Across eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations, the research program spans power-source custody, reconfigurable conductors, communication and consensus, electrothermal safety, fault isolation and independent qualification. Two hundred Research Gates pose distinct concealed-fault, equal-resource competitor and cross-interface problems with separate challenge, rival and stopping explanations. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose experimental meters, isolation benches, duty referees, communication-energy witnesses, thermal artifacts and second-laboratory transfer contracts. These are hypothesis-forming research proposals, not completed devices or demonstrated physical outcomes. The DOI ancestry preserves author-supplied parent identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 (metadata not independently confirmed). External component and methodology references include Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6), flying-swarm shape assembly (10.1038/s44172-026-00715-3), adaptive magnetic microrobots (10.1038/s41427-026-00682-3), changing-topology consensus (10.1109/TAC.2005.846556), distributed power sharing (10.1109/TPWRD.2012.2212919), energy-aware multi-robot allocation (10.1016/j.robot.2024.104762), and wireless robotic power transfer (10.1049/csy2.70065). These studies support limited component analogies and methods; none proves the integrated F21 vehicle-body architecture, passenger safety or nanoscale-to-macroscopic feasibility. summary: SAOS 6.0.0 This release brings tomographic control for MCAO, a redesigned deformable-mirror model, more accurate wavefront sensors and imaging, and a validation suite that compares every module with theory. From now on, a release to master requires the validation suite to pass. Highlights Tomographic reconstruction (Learn & Apply) with an atmospheric-profile estimator: Cn², r0, L0, wind, noise. Includes predictive L&A and joint reconstruction for several WFSs and DMs. Deformable mirrors with partition-of-unity influence functions , support for custom influence functions and DM dynamic models. Wavefront sensors: partially illuminated subapertures, with pupil amplitude and phase interpolation; continuous thresholded centre of gravity. Science camera: the PSF is computed by a matrix Fourier transform on the native pupil sampling, limited to its Nyquist band; no phase interpolation is involved; SAOS reports the resolution needed to cover the whole field. Validation suite and release gate: physics-based tests in tiers (fast, nightly), an HTML report and a GitHub check on a self-hosted runner that a pull request to master must pass. Solar images on Zenodo: downloaded on demand and verified by checksum. Git LFS is no longer needed. Documentation: every module page explains its theory and implementation, with equations and references. There is also a validation catalogue describing each test, its assumptions and tolerances. Control and reconstruction Learn & Apply tomography (standard and predictive), with a learning stage that estimates: the turbulence profile (fractional Cn², r0, L0) from the slope covariances, using analytical von Kármán covariances; the wind of each layer; the WFS noise. Reconstructors: Tikhonov-regularised reconstructors; joint interaction matrix for several WFSs and DMs, inverted as a single system; target residuals driven to zero by DM cooperation. Control laws: leaky integrator, generic state-space controller and pseudo-open-loop control (POLC). In per-DM POLC, the pseudo-open-loop slopes of each WFS include the contribution of every DM that it sees. Modal bases: zonal, Zernike, KL, Hadamard and Disk Harmonics. Piston-free bases have exactly nValidAct − 1 modes. Zernike signs follow Noll. Tip/tilt are removed from altitude DMs. Interaction matrices: DM identity is checked; IM files record their basis convention; files are never appended to: an existing file requires overwrite=True , and the write is atomic; check_output_file() validates the path before a long measurement; identical DMs and light paths reuse the same IM. Scalability: chunked reconstruction and tomography on the GPU, with automatic fallback to the CPU when the matrices do not fit; reduced VRAM use; a common thread pool to avoid CPU oversubscription. Deformable mirrors Partition-of-unity normalised RBF influence functions, and user-supplied influence functions. Misregistration (shift, rotation, radial scaling) applied at the actuator level through the influence functions, so it introduces no interpolation effects. Dynamic response: discrete state-space DM models. Validated against an independent Matlab simulation, including closed-loop timing. Also validated on the sensitivity function for a Tip disturbance of known PSD. Wavefront sensing and imaging Shack-Hartmann: partially illuminated subapertures, with pupil amplitude and normalised phase interpolation and a validity threshold; continuous thresholded centre of gravity; validated use_brightest . Correlating Shack-Hartmann: consistent units in rad or px; flux scaled with the field of view; lower VRAM use. Science camera: matrix Fourier transform on the native pupil sampling, band-limited to the Nyquist band (Whittaker–Shannon); frames produced at the end of each decimation window; long exposures always last at least the requested integration time; an option saves only the long exposure. summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. The book provides a systematic and rigorous introduction to mathematical reasoning, formal proof techniques, and the fundamental structure of the real number system. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. Chapter 1: Mathematical Language and Proof Techniques This chapter introduces propositional logic, logical connectives, truth tables, implications, equivalences, universal and existential quantifiers, and the negation of quantified statements. It develops the theory of sets, equivalence and order relations, injective, surjective, and bijective functions, images, preimages, composition, and inverse functions. Particular emphasis is placed on direct proof, proof by contraposition, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, and the construction of counterexamples. The chapter also examines rigorous mathematical writing, common logical errors, finite and infinite sets, countability, and the uncountability of the real numbers. Chapter 2: The Real Number System The second chapter develops the axiomatic structure of the real numbers through field axioms, order axioms, and the compatibility of algebraic operations with order. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. Pedagogical Approach The textbook integrates precise definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, complete mathematical proofs, explanatory examples, and carefully constructed counterexamples. It includes 120 fully solved exercises and 150 proposed exercises , organized according to the main topics of the two chapters. These activities reinforce theoretical understanding, logical reasoning, mathematical writing, and independent problem-solving skills. Intended Audience This publication is intended for undergraduate mathematics students, university instructors, mathematics educators, and independent learners seeking a rigorous foundation in real analysis. As the first volume of a six-volume academic collection, it establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for subsequent studies of sequences, numerical series, limits, continuity, metric spaces, compactness, differential calculus, Riemann integration, uniform convergence, and differential equations. summary: THERMAL MANAGEMENT OF MORPHING ROBOTIC VEHICLE BODIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形車體的熱管理極限 22/90 THERMAL MANAGEMENT OF MORPHING ROBOTIC VEHICLE BODIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in STARLI's YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, asking whether a scaled morphing robotic vehicle-body section can redistribute heat without hiding interface hotspots, temperature-induced material degradation or cooling-energy costs. Its three-coupling is Heat Conduction x Distributed Actuation x Thermal Safety. The program is restricted to 24-module unoccupied bench assemblies, coupons, sealed thermal chambers and hardware-in-the-loop control. It makes no claim of a road-ready vehicle, passenger protection or independently demonstrated nanoscale-to-macroscopic performance. The falsifiable candidate compares a frozen morphology-aware heat-management policy against equally resourced fixed passive and centralized wired thermal designs. Under matched mechanical tasks, material mass, source heat, cooling-work budget, sensing access and mission duration, the candidate should reduce the worst qualified local temperature without worsening safety-critical deadline-valid packet survival. The preassigned model rank([C;CA;...;CA^(n-1)])=n tests observability of an ideal local linear state representation; it does not itself prove physical temperature correctness. A hidden heat source, emissivity shift, detached thermal bridge, blocked coolant, over-temperature joint, unaccounted fan input, undercovered uncertainty or ineffective physical stop defeats release. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates address thermal control-volume energy conservation, Fourier and anisotropic conduction, pressure-dependent contact resistance, radiation, convection, dynamic heat storage, resistive heating, actuator dissipation, thermomechanical damage, strain-sensitive thermal conductivity, latent-heat buffering, thermal fatigue, forced cooling, heat-pipe and thermoelectric limits, observability, state-estimator innovation, correlated thermal uncertainty, inverse source ambiguity, physical stop latency, hazard dependence, extreme-tail qualification and Biot/Fourier scale arguments. Every plate specifies construction, dimensions, validity conditions, a separate blind falsification and chapter interfaces. Eighty-two research chapters contain 410 separate single-page investigations into physical heat source truth, changing morphology and thermal contacts, sparse sensor observability, cooling systems, thermally induced damage and second-site qualification. Two hundred Research Gates contain individually anchored hidden-fault, matched-comparator and cross-chapter questions with specific scientific notes and stopping criteria. Thirty-three distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos propose instruments, calorimeters, thermal-refusal cards, contact-heat probes, material aging tests and successor negative-case archives. These are prospective research designs, not completed results or operating vehicle hardware. Reference ancestry includes the author's supplied Flagship 13 identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 (metadata not independently confirmed). External peer-reviewed component literature includes Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6), thermally switchable polymers (10.1038/s41467-024-49354-2), thermally actuated soft robotics (10.1002/adma.202504683), conductive elastomer films (10.1039/D5NR03526K), responsive battery thermal regulation (10.1038/s41560-024-01535-5), phase-change/heat-pipe cooling (10.1016/j.enconman.2024.118506), and the supplied 2026 swarm/microrobot references (10.1038/s44172-026-00715-3; 10.1038/s41427-026-00682-3). Publications support component hypotheses and measurement methods; none independently verifies the integrated F22 concept. summary: Coarse flood maps support regional risk assessment but omit terrain detail relevant to local exposure. We present floodsr, a Python framework for reconstructing fine-grid flood depths using a trained residual U-Net (ResUNet) or the existing terrain-based CostGrow method. We trained the terrain-conditioned ResUNet on paired Canadian hydraulic simulations and evaluated it on withheld spatial tiles and independent simulations at two external sites. Wet-loss training improved reconstruction on five selected tiles, although internal validation favoured the deployed baseline. External depth errors decreased, but wet-depth errors and spatial agreement did not improve consistently. CPU benchmarks quantified runtime and memory for both methods, and repeatability and input-validation checks passed in the tested configurations. The framework supports comparison and reuse of reconstruction methods; application-specific validation remains necessary because finer grids do not guarantee more accurate flood maps.   Non-peer-reviewed preprint. Includes the manuscript and supplementary material. Software: https://github.com/cefect/floodsr . Documentation: https://floodsr.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ .
title: floodsr: A lightweight Python toolkit for terrain-conditioned flood map super-resolution

summary: v2.4.1 (2026-10-31) replaces the age-only standardization of v2.4.0 by indirect standardization over 16 sex-by-age strata (KDCA district-by-sex-by-age-band notifications and resident-registration population by district, sex and age band); all arms, threshold refits and figures were rerun and the credible set is unchanged (fiscal independence only). v2.4.0 (revision R1, 2026-10-31) adds revision_R1/: the additional analyses requested at peer review by JMIR Public Health and Surveillance (indirectly age-standardized expected counts as offset; every count or area covariate re-expressed as a share of district land area, a rate per 1000 residents or a density per km2, with log population density added; two uniform functional forms; parsimonious models; restricted spatial regression; zero-inflated negative binomial; residual Moran's I for every specification; 8 neighbourhood graphs; spatially varying coefficients for forest share and household wells; physicians per 1000 as ascertainment proxy; 2022-2024 only; repeated fits; reruns of the complete data pipeline under alternative screening thresholds and with linear interpolation), all outputs, the revised figures, and the inputs needed beyond the raw files. Under the revised principal model only fiscal independence remains credible (IRR 0.890, 95% CrI 0.819-0.966 per SD); the four other associations of the reviewed version survive age standardization alone but not rescaling, and forest share is credible under no revised specification. Three input corrections (Busanjin-gu and Cheonan-si land-use and well values; boundary-file area in place of the sewerage area field; Incheon Michuhol-gu/Namdong-gu polygon assignment) are documented; the reviewed specification refitted on the corrected inputs reproduces its 5 associations. The main script and results/ (v2.3.3, the reviewed analysis) are unchanged. Earlier history: Reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hepatitis A incidence in South Korea, 2020-2024 (negative binomial, Besag-York-Mollie convolution + RW1 + Knorr-Held Type I interaction, fitted with R-INLA; 219 districts, 1,095 district-years, 27 covariates). v2.1.0 is a DATA-REPAIR release that supersedes all earlier versions: an audit found that several administrative source files store unavailable values as 0 instead of missing and that some series were redefined in particular years, so that, under binary and quantile coding, covariates encoded data availability rather than their true level. These values are now recoded as missing and filled from the most recent earlier available year, and every change is logged (results/data_repair_log.csv). The v2.0.x associations for piped water-supply coverage and inpatient medical cost, and the v2.0.x claim of nine credible covariates, were artefacts of this defect and are withdrawn. The repaired analysis found four credible covariates (household groundwater wells, dairy-cattle farms, forest area, fiscal independence). A post hoc extreme-value screen then found aggregation errors (eg, a sex ratio near 50 males per 100 females, basic livelihood security recipients above 30%, mostly in cities with non-autonomous wards) affecting 17 district-years in 4 covariates; v2.2.0 adopts this screen as rule R7 of the principal analysis, which excludes 2 further districts (218 districts, 1,090 district-years) and adds sewer-pipe repair sites as a fifth credible covariate. Household groundwater wells and sewer-pipe repair sites are borderline (lost under some neighbourhood graphs, INLA settings or the alternative handling of extreme values), and only forest area is credible in every sensitivity analysis; dairy-cattle farms, sewer-pipe repair sites and fiscal independence are lost when 2020-2021 is excluded. The covariates take up only part of the spatial structure (residual Moran's I +0.22). The package contains a single R script (data repair, models, sensitivity and stability analyses), a figure script, a year-R2 data
title: Spatial Clustering of Hepatitis A in South Korea, 2020-2024: Nationwide Bayesian Analysis of Socioeconomic Gradients and Residual Clustering After Age Standardization (analysis code, data-repair log and compiled data, v2.4.1)

summary: TriadSense contains synchronised sensor recordings of nine groups of three people who assembled a puzzle together, with annotations of what every participant, every pair and the whole group did. Each participant wore an ear-worn device (OpenEarable 2.0) and a wrist-worn device (Xsens DOT); an optical motion-capture system (OptiTrack) recorded their positions. The record holds the raw recordings of the nine sessions, the annotations of three annotators (the final annotations, the original annotator's annotations before the review, and the reliability sample of 76 clips), the synchronised streams with the final labels on every sample, and the 5-second window table of the benchmark. Video and audio are not released. README.md describes every file and column. Access to the files requires accepting the terms of use (TERMS_OF_USE.md), which prohibit any attempt to re-identify the participants. The code that reproduces the processing and the benchmark: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/triadsense-pipeline-78DB/
title: TriadSense: body-worn and optical sensing of group activity in triads

summary: This record contains the supporting materials of the article “A trade-based Forest Club as a path to halting tropical deforestation”. It has two parts: a multi-regional input–output (MRIO) assessment of the deforestation embodied in agricultural trade and consumption, and the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model of the Forest Club . Every figure and table of the article, its Extended Data and its Supplementary Information is produced from the code, input data and results provided here. The Forest Club is a trade-based coalition. Its members hold their forest at its 2019 extent and are deemed compliant with the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). They charge the forest-risk commodities they import from non-members, either with a flat penalty or with a surcharge proportional to the deforestation embodied in each product. 1. MRIO impact assessment (folders 1. Data and 2. MRIO) The forest-to-cropland and forest-to-pasture transitions of HILDA+ v2.1 (2012–2019) are extracted from the netCDF files and assigned to countries. They are then allocated to the agricultural sectors of the GLORIA MRIO using FAOSTAT harvested areas and livestock numbers, smoothed with three-year moving averages; the FAO–GLORIA mapping and the hectares per head are in A-1_FAO_Cropland_mapping_GLORIA.xlsx and A-2_Head_per_ha.xlsx. Consumption-based accounting (CBA) attributes this agricultural deforestation to final consumers. Throughflow-based accounting (TBA, by hypothetical extraction) traces the share that transits through intermediary economies such as the EU, in detail for Brazil, Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The folders hold the Python script (CBA_TBA_script.py), the Alteryx workflows, the satellite accounts, the results and the visualisation files (Tableau, Sankey diagrams). These produce sections 2–4 of the Supplementary Information (Tables S1–S2, Figs S1–S4), which describe the deforestation the EUDR covers. 2. CGE model (synced from GitHub) The study simulates how the club forms, round by round, as each country compares its welfare inside and outside it. The model is GTAP-AEZ, a global CGE model with agro-ecological zones (42 regions, 35 sectors, 18 zones; GEMPACK). Every result is measured against a baseline that combines the EUDR with the business-as-usual clearing that DeDuCE v2.1 attributes to agriculture. The coalitions reached are tested for one-country deviations and for their sensitivity to the switching cost. 0_External_data: footprint intensities and border charges derived from DeDuCE v2.1, the EUDR import cut shares, the business-as-usual clearing by region and agro-ecological zone (HILDA+ v2.1 patterns; MapBiomas RAD 2025 for Brazil), and the productivity calibration of the cleared land. 1_Code: R scripts that calibrate and solve the two-stage baseline, run the membership game and the one-deviation stability tests, and calibrate the land-supply elasticities to Miranda et al. (2024). 2_Model: the GTAP-AEZ model files (TABLO code, command files, sets and aggregation). 3_Output and 4_DB: the text outputs of every solve and the result tables of every run, by region and round, for all membership processes and stability tests of the paper. 5_Figures: the Python pipeline that redraws all figures and tables from these results, with their source data. Data not included The GTAP Data Base (version 12, reference year 2019) is licensed by the Center for Global Trade Analysis, Purdue University. Solving the model requires a licensed copy in 2_Model/in/. Redrawing the figures and tables does not, because the extracted results are provided in 5_Figures/data. The GLORIA tables are distributed by the Global MRIO Lab. The README of the repository describes each step of the CGE pipeline. Code synced from the GitHub repository: https://github.com/etiennebert/forest_club/tree/main
title: A Trade-Based Forest Club as a Path to Halting Tropical Deforestation

summary: This article examines how customs authorities can shorten clearance times without reducing the detection of violations by redistributing fixed inspection capacity across risk lanes. The empirical basis is a declaration-level dataset from the Customs Committee of Uzbekistan, comprising 8,000 declarations lodged at 12 customs posts during 2023–2026. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model shows that assignment to the red lane multiplies expected clearance time by 2.97, while pre-arrival lodging reduces it by 29.7%. A linear programming model is proposed to rank declarations by the number of detected violations per hour of additional clearance time. With the same 1,820 inspections and 786 detected violations, the model reduces the 90th percentile of clearance time by 21.3 minutes and by 64.2 minutes when combined with an increased share of pre-arrival declarations.
title: TIME-AWARE ALLOCATION OF CUSTOMS INSPECTION RESOURCES ACROSS RISK LANES: DECLARATION-LEVEL EVIDENCE FROM UZBEKISTAN

summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.
tags: Ropelength filtration, compact Lie group, weak slope, metric criticality, isotropy, Lipschitz local section, symmetry-constrained minimax, Noether theorem
title: Lie group actions and metric criticality in ropelength-filtered knot spaces

summary: This repository provides the MATLAB source code and reproducibility resources associated with the manuscript entitled “Physics-Guided Reduced-Order Screening of Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames,” submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy (Manuscript No. HE-D-26-13275). The computational framework employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric, physics-guided reduced-order model to investigate the coupled effects of radiative heat loss, preferential diffusion, ammonia cracking, hydrogen enrichment, pressure, and strain on non-premixed ammonia/hydrogen diffusion flames. The MATLAB implementation supports the reproduction of the manuscript's numerical analyses, including baseline flame characteristics, reaction-zone localization, thermal response, relative NOₓ formation tendencies, scalar dissipation, extinction susceptibility, robustness indicators, mechanism-isolation studies, numerical convergence, closure sensitivity, uncertainty analyses, parametric sweeps, and Pareto-based screening. Repository contents and reproducibility The principal file, Master_NH3H2_ROM_Reproducibility.m , contains the model formulation, numerical procedures, analysis modules, and routines for generating supporting figures, numerical tables, and datasets. Executing the master function creates an organized output directory containing the enabled computational results. Model scope and limitations The framework is intended for comparative mechanism screening and prioritization of operating conditions for subsequent higher-fidelity investigations. It does not solve the full governing conservation equations or detailed chemical kinetics. The relative NOₓ formation-tendency index is not an absolute emission concentration, emission factor, or outlet flux. Similarly, the extinction and robustness indicators represent comparative screening metrics rather than experimentally validated stability limits. The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. Associated manuscript: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, HE-D-26-13275. Keywords: Ammonia/hydrogen combustion; reduced-order modeling; MATLAB; radiative heat loss; preferential diffusion; NOₓ formation tendency; extinction; uncertainty analysis; reproducibility.
title: Physics-Guided Reduced-Order MATLAB Framework for Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames: Code and Reproducibility Data

summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. Contents of this record Authority_at_Scale.pdf : the article (approx. 10,000 words, 21 pages). halden_schedule_check.py : reference implementation of the running case (Section 6.7). It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. The article generalizes the four service conditions developed for machine-mediated authority in Cott, N. (2026), The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority , Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23272655 .
title: Authority at Scale: Institutional Capacity and the Limits of Presumptive Authority

summary: Croft asked for the largest regular polygon that can be translated, rotated, and scaled inside another. For coprime side counts at least five, we prove the conjecture of Dilworth and Mane that an optimum occurs at one of two endpoint configurations. The endpoint values never tie, and every interior orientation in the fundamental interval is strictly suboptimal. Together with the published cases, this determines the exact optimum for every ordered pair of regular polygons. In the coprime case, the optimal placement is unique modulo the natural dihedral symmetries of the two polygons and has exactly four contacts between inner vertices and the relative interiors of outer sides. These form two reflected pairs. They lie in a common open half-plane whose boundary passes through the outer center exactly for (m, n) = (2k + 1, 2k), k ≥ 3; otherwise one lies in each open quadrant determined by the common symmetry axis and its perpendicular. The proof uses support constraints, balanced three-constraint certificates, and centered modular residues. Supplementary computations check identities and finite ranges without serving as proof premises. License scope: original scholarly text, figures, and project-generated mathematical data are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Identified original software is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The included file-scope maps and third-party notices specify exceptions; historical input archives retain their existing terms.
title: Optimal unrestricted containment of one regular polygon in another

summary: Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants. The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow

summary: Cross-border art transactions carry two kinds of legal uncertainty that reform proposals typically treat as one: incomplete verification of who owned, sold, or previously possessed a work, and divergent national rules about what follows once ownership and possession are established beyond dispute. Drawing on a nineteen-year restitution dispute in which the underlying facts were settled well before the litigation ended, this article shows that only the first kind of uncertainty yields to better documentation, tracing, or verification infrastructure; the second persists because national legal systems assign the risk of a stolen object's resale differently, a distributive choice that additional evidence does not change. Recent computational and blockchain-based compliance proposals close real gaps in beneficial-ownership tracing and anti-money-laundering enforcement. Applied to restitution litigation, the same proposals leave the underlying divergence untouched. Reclassifying the deficits identified in existing legal-architecture scholarship along this line separates the problems computational investment can solve from the one that needs a binding choice-of-law rule instead.
tags: art market regulation; provenance; choice of law; anti-money laundering; cultural property restitution; regulatory architecture.
title: A. TILLARD AND THE LEGAL QUESTIONS BEHIND THE GLOBAL ART MARKET

summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.
title: Experimental Artefacts for HARDIO: A Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator for Operational Data Quality in Instrumented Water Infrastructure

summary: Introduction: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) contribute to its pathogenesis, while musculoskeletal ultrasound provides valuable information about joint inflammatory activity. The aim of the study was to evaluate changes in IL-1β and IL-6 protein and gene expression and their correlations with clinical and ultrasonographic disease activity in RA patients before and after Tofacitinib treatment. Methods: Fourteen patients with RA were evaluated at baseline and after Tofacitinib treatment. Disease activity was assessed using the 28-joint Disease Activity Score (DAS28) and the seven joint Global Ultrasound Score (GUS7). Plasma cytokine concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA), and gene expression in peripheral blood cells was assessed by qPCR. Results: After six months, median DAS28 decreased from 5.80 to 3.31 (p<0.001), while GUS7 decreased from 20.0 to 11.0 (p=0.002). Plasma IL-6 concentrations decreased significantly from 7.83 to 0.06 pg/mL (p=0.020). No significant changes were observed in plasma IL-1β concentrations (p=0.445) or IL1-β and IL-6 gene expression (p=0.922 and p=1.0, respectively). DAS28 and GUS7 were positively correlated at baseline (ρ=0.890, p<0.001) and after treatment (r=0.689, p=0.006). Conclusion: Tofacitinib treatment was associated with improved clinical and ultrasonographic disease activity and reduced plasma IL-6 concentrations. The absence of significant changes in IL-1β concentrations and cytokine gene expression highlights the complexity of inflammatory regulation in RA. Combined clinical, imaging, and molecular assessments may provide complementary information on treatment response.
title: Beyond clinical improvement: a pilot study on cytokine and ultrasonographic changes following Tofacitinib treatment in Rheumatoid arthritis

summary: Background: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a popular age-linked ailment featured by prostatic enlargement and urinary obstruction. Dinoprostone (DINO) is prostaglandin E 2 having anti-proliferative and anti-inflammatory actions. Objective: This research attempted to assess the effect of DINO vs. finasteride (FINA) on testosterone (TEST)-induced BPH in rats. Methods: 40 adult male rats were haphazardly separated into 4 groups (n = 10); namely control, TEST, TEST + FINA, and TEST + DINO. BPH was induced with subcutaneous TEST (3 mg per kg per day) for 4 weeks. FINA (5 mg per kg) and DINO (7 mg per kg) were delivered orally. Results: TEST administration led to marked prostatic enlargement and hyperplasia, paralleled by remarkable elevations in PCNA, DHT, 5α-reductase, β-catenin, ERβ, pro-inflammatory IL-6, and pro-fibrotic TGF-β and VEGF mediators. FINA and DINO effectively attenuated these alterations, restoring prostate weight and histoarchitecture, downregulating β-catenin and ERβ, ameliorating PCNA expression, and suppressing DHT and 5α-reductase activity. Both drugs modified inflammatory and angiogenic mechanisms and corrected PPAR-γ expression and regulated BCL-2 levels, indicating diminished apoptosis. While FINA surpassed DINO in inhibiting DHT, IL-6, and β-catenin expression, both treatments were equally effective in terms of anti-hypertrophic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic actions. Conclusions: DINO demonstrated promising anti-BPH effects comparable to FINA, acting via EP receptor-mediated modulation of prostatic growth and inflammation. These findings are viewed as preliminary and warrant further investigations of DINO for BPH treatment.
title: Preventive effect of Dinoprostone (Prostaglandin E2) on testosterone-induced prostatic hyperplasia in a rat model

summary: The genus Hypocala Guenée, 1852 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae, Hypocalinae) was previously treated in the Fauna Sinica volume on Noctuidae, which recognised four species, based on external morphology from China: H. subsatura Guenée, 1852, H. deflorata (Fabricius, 1794) H. rostrata (Fabricius, 1794) and H. violacea Butler, 1879. A fifth species, H. andamana Wileman, 1923 is known from Taiwan, based on literature records, but was not available for examination in this study. In the present study, based on examination of available museum material, we provide updated diagnoses, descriptions and illustrations of adults and male genitalia for all four species, as well as female genitalia for two species where material was available. A taxonomic key to the Chinese species, updated synonymies and host plant records are also provided. This study establishes a comprehensive baseline for future taxonomic and pest-management research on Hypocala in China.
title: Review of the genus Hypocala Guenée (Lepidoptera, Erebidae, Hypocalinae) from Chinese fauna

summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: Device-Aware Weighted Gerchberg-Saxton and Flicker-Bounded Phase-Continuous Sequences for Holographic Optical Trap Arrays

summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model

The author-supplied falsifiable seed asks whether a frozen hybrid pipeline can reduce design energy without worsening its declared objective gap under equal material, electricity, computation, sensing, time and operator budgets. For a scientifically valid twin, this book additionally requires held-out physical forecast error, interval coverage, event identity and correct abstention under missing evidence. Classical physics-based state estimation, energy models and competitive ordinary optimizers are the primary predecessors; finite-element topology design alone is not a sufficient digital-twin baseline. Blinded interventions include a hidden missing load path, shifted clock, stale authenticated telemetry, shared sensor drift, thermal model mismatch, unlogged auxiliary power and material-batch substitution. A system loses its claim whenever digital agreement conceals unsafe physical truth. The volume contains 82 chapters and 410 independently paginated investigations organized around structural chronology, indoor environment and power, metrological state inference, communication and authority, fault challenges, quantum-classical method comparison and second-laboratory succession. summary: Analysis code accompanying the paper "When Fidelity Becomes Disclosure: Privacy Risk of Synthetic Data Generated from Very Small Rehabilitation Trials in Parkinson's Disease" (submitted to ACDSA 2027). The code trains four tabular generators (Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN) and a differentially private generator (AIM) on a pilot trial of serious games versus physiotherapy in Parkinson's disease (n = 22; arms of 10 and 12). It measures how much the synthetic records disclose about the training patients: normalised distance to closest record (DCR), near and exact copies, nearest-neighbour distance ratio, a leave-one-out membership-inference attack and an attribute-inference attack, with patient-level cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals. Fidelity (mean |Δ Spearman ρ| and Kolmogorov–Smirnov) is reported as a comparison axis. Contents: privacy_eval.py (generators, metrics, attacks, Table I), supplementary_analyses.py (Table II, per-patient atypicality, discretised-real baseline), make_figures.py (Figs. 2–4), copula_diagnostics.py (rank and marginal-family diagnostics of the Gaussian Copula with n < p), requirements.txt with the exact library versions. The README maps every command to the table or figure it reproduces. The de-identified dataset is not included in this record. Download it from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23091123 and place it in dataset/ .

summary: An authentic group of pre-Columbian ceramics, probably from Risaralda, appears to rhyme with Japan's 5,000-year-old Jōmon Venus. The resemblance is real; a historical connection is not. This GLIAG essay shows how two distant societies independently turned clay and the human body into instruments of memory, identity and ritual, and why archaeological context determines what we can responsibly know. The Japanese comparator is identified securely: the 27 cm, 2.14 kg clay dogū known as the Jōmon Venus, recovered intact at the Tanabatake site in Chino, Nagano, and dated by the responsible museum to the Middle Jōmon, about 3000 BCE. The Colombian objects are, on their custodian's account, authentic, Colombian and probably from Risaralda, reportedly recovered by guaqueros; their context, ceramic phase and date are undocumented. The essay sets out a disciplined visual comparison across eight analytical axes, discusses the body as vessel, gender and fertility, convergence without contact, and guaquería as knowledge loss, and closes with a research programme for the Risaralda objects. Nothing in it demonstrates trans-Pacific contact; the strongest explanation is convergent figuration. Bilingual edition, English then Spanish. This Zenodo edition (Revision 2.1, 31 October 2026) reproduces the web edition first published on Petroleum & Energy Insights on 13 September 2026 (GLIAG-ESS-2026-038-CH REV 002), with an amendment register, full references, licence and citation. Figure 1 of the web edition (two source images) is not reproduced for rights reasons. The essay is not an appraisal, title opinion or authentication of any object.
title: Two Worlds, One Human Form: the Jōmon Venus of Japan and anthropomorphic ceramics from Cauca Medio, Colombia

summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.
title: From NAM Data to Trusted Evidence: RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure for Next Generation Risk Assessment

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.
title: An exact projected-angle likelihood and population inversion for wide-binary eccentricities

summary: This study presents the first comprehensive investigation of the horsefly (Diptera: Tabanidae) fauna of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, Azerbaijan, based on field surveys conducted between 2021 and 2025. A total of 451 specimens were collected and identified, comprising 37 species belonging to the subfamilies Tabaninae, Chrysopsinae and Pangoninae. Four species Tabanus nemoralis , T. obsolescens , Haematopota pallidula and H. pandazisi are recorded for the first time from Azerbaijan, while ten species are new records for Nakhchivan, raising the known Tabanidae fauna of the country to 90 species. Tabanus bifarius (20.39%) and T. bromius (17.52%) were the most frequently captured species, whereas Haematopota pandazisi , was rarely sampled, represented by only a single specimen. Ecological diversity analysis revealed the highest species richness in Julfa and Babek, while Ordubad (Goygol) and Ordubad (Pazmari) exhibited markedly reduced diversity, reflecting a clear altitudinal zonation of the fauna across the region. These findings substantially expand the known distribution and diversity of Tabanidae in Azerbaijan and provide baseline data for future ecological and veterinary research in Nakhchivan.
title: New contributions to the fauna of horseflies (Diptera, Tabanidae) in Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan

summary: 智能奈米機器人自主建築修復極限 41/90 INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURAL REPAIR AT THE LIMIT INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURAL REPAIR AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 41 of 90). It investigates whether locally operated micro-scale robotic inspection and repair methods might detect concealed cracks, moisture ingress, damaged mechanical interfaces and environmental faults, then restore independently measurable properties without concealing failure. The core coupling is Micro/Nano Sensing x Local Repair x Structural Reliability. Every proposed integrated test is limited to unoccupied scaled habitat panels, damaged coupons, environmental chambers and supervised hardware-in-the-loop systems; no inhabited dwelling, nanorobotic building maintenance system or structural certification is claimed. The falsifiable candidate predicts higher independently verified fault recall without worsening preregistered post-repair air-quality recovery under equal inspection exposure, material supply, energy, sensing, computation, time and human-operations budgets. Repair success is separately conditional on load-path requalification, credible reference identity, moisture containment and a functioning physical stop. A controlled localized robotic repair system must compete with scheduled expert inspection, replace-on-failure maintenance and expert-performed local treatment. Concealed moisture, common-mode sensor drift, inaccessible crack ligaments, incompatible repair chemistry and hidden support fixtures are ways the hypothesis can fail. Negative specimens, refused states, destructive tests and incomplete repairs remain in the full denominator. Thirty mechanically and statistically distinct research plates include Paris-regime fatigue crack growth, mode-I and mixed-mode fracture, energy release, cohesive-interface work, load balance, fatigue survival, detection recall and false clearance, ultrasound and acoustic observability, thermal and moisture transport, contaminant mass balance, resin flow, cure kinetics, correlated uncertainty, materials and energy accounting, conditional causal effects and physically verified stop latency. Each mathematical plate states its mechanism, dimensional assumptions, independent reference, blinded contradiction and research-chapter links. The seed Paris relation da/dN = C(Delta K)^m is a conditional empirical model for particular fatigue regimes, not a universal law of repair or evidence that a crack has healed. Eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations examine specimen provenance, hidden crack truth, fracture and fatigue, imaging and sensor drift, repair-material chemistry, robotic deposition, wall-module utility boundaries, environmental requalification, long-cycle maintenance and independent laboratory reconstruction. Two hundred individually worded Research Gates challenge different physical witnesses, resource-matched rivals, coupled faults, false-clear decisions and reproducibility limits. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separate future scientific objects, including fracture-reference capsules, moisture witnesses, cure validation rigs, aerosol exposure ledgers, physical interlocks and cross-site specimen relays. These are research proposals and evidence contracts, not demonstrated autonomous repair devices. The research is hypothetical, non-occupancy and intentionally vulnerable to refutation. Existing studies establish bounded robotic crack inspection and concrete sealing methods, polymer-glass simulation mechanisms, fatigue testing practices and material measurement approaches, but do not validate the integrated F41 architecture. summary: AnaTele is an open-source desktop tool for investigating ArduPilot flight logs (.tlog, .bin, .log). It infers flight phases, replays the recorded path in 3D, evaluates a versioned declarative rule pack with four explicit result states, and ranks competing failure hypotheses by capped evidence-family support minus contradictions, without assigning probabilities. Every finding links to the exact log record. It includes a fault-injection quadcopter simulator and a hash-verified shareable analysis format (.ant). Documentation: avinashistoocool.github.io/AnaTele
title: AnaTele: evidence-first investigation of ArduPilot flight logs

summary: CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:移動城市循環經濟與材料永續極限 55/90 CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 55 of 90). It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. Relevant method references include Ostapska et al. (10.1016/j.spc.2024.05.014), Formentini et al. (10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145459), Attia et al. (10.1016/j.autcon.2024.105521), Mao and Cao (10.1016/j.spc.2024.12.021), Poschmann et al. (10.1002/cite.201900107) and Keating et al. (10.1126/scirobotics.aam8986). The Flagship 13 mother genealogy identifiers (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839) were provided by the author and their metadata have not been independently confirmed. No external study cited here establishes this integrated F55 architecture. summary: Annotatsiya. Maqolada O‘zbekiston sug‘urta kompaniyalarining moliyaviy barqarorligini choraklik hisobotlar asosida baholashning integral indeks taklif etilgan. Asosiy e’tibor indikatorlar yo‘nalishini aniqlash masalasiga qaratilgan bo‘lib, zararlilik koeffitsiyenti va mukofotlar o‘sishi bozor etalonidan har ikki tomonga chetlanish sifatida olingan. 36 ta kompaniyaning 2021-2025 yillardagi ma’lumotlarida bunday indeks kompaniyalarning bozordan chiqishini an’anaviy indeksdan ancha yaxshi ajratib berishi asoslangan. Kalit so‘zlar: sug‘urta kompaniyasi, moliyaviy barqarorlik, integral indeks, zararlilik koeffitsiyenti, ob’ektiv vaznlar, ROC ( Tasniflash sifatini baholash egri chizig‘i) tahlil. Аннотация. В статье предлагается интегральный показатель для оценки финансовой устойчивости страховых компаний Узбекистана, основанный на данных из общедоступной квартальной отчетности. Основное внимание уделяется определению динамики показателей: коэффициент убыточности и темпы роста страховых премий рассматриваются как отклонения, в ту или иную сторону,   от рыночного ориентира. Анализ данных по 36 компаниям за период 2021-2025 гг. показывает, что данный показатель позволяет выявлять компании, покидающие рынок, значительно эффективнее, чем традиционный индекс. Ключевые слова: страховая компания, финансовая устойчивость, интегральный индекс, коэффициент убыточности, объективные веса, ROC-анализ. Abstract. The article proposes an integral index for assessing the financial stability of insurance companies in Uzbekistan based on quarterly reports. The main attention is focused on determining the direction of indicators, with the loss ratio and premium growth considered as deviations from the market benchmark in both directions. Based on data from 36 companies for 2021–2025, it is demonstrated that such an index distinguishes companies exiting the market significantly better than the traditional index. Keywords: insurance company, financial stability, composite index, loss ratio, objective weights, ROC analysis.

summary: يهدف البحث الى اعداد برنامج علاجي سلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة لدى الطالبات، والتعرف على تأثير البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة لدى الطالبات، ولتحقيق الهدف استخدمت الباحث المَنهجُ التجريبي وبتصميم المجموعتين التجريبية والضابطة المتكافئتين ذو الإختِبار القبلي والبعدي لملائمته مع مشكلة واهداف البحث، حدد مجتمع البحث بطالبات المرحلة الثانية للدراسة الصباحية في كلية التربية البدنية وعلوم الرياضة_ جامعة بغداد، للعامُ الدراسي   2025 - 2026   و البالغ عددهم (110) طالبة مُوَزَعات على (4) شعب وهي (أ، ب، ج، د) وتم تحديد مجتمع البحث بطالبات المرحلة الثانية كون هذه المرحلة تدرس مادة السباحة، أما عينة البحث، فقد اختيرت بالطريقة العشوائية باستخدام القرعة، إذ أُجريت قرعة بين الشعب الأربع لتحديد مجموعتي البحث (التجريبية والضابطة)، وأسفرت عن اختيار شعبتي (ب) و(د). وبعد ذلك، اختيرت (25) طالبة من كل شعبة بالطريقة نفسها، لتُمثل شعبة (ب) المجموعة التجريبية، في حين مثلت شعبة (د) المجموعة الضابطة، وبذلك بلغ العدد الكلي لعينة البحث (50) طالبة، أي ما نسبته (45.45%) من مجتمع البحث.ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة، طبقت الباحثة الاختبارات القبلية على المجموعتين قبل البدء بتنفيذ الوحدات التعليمي، واجريت المعالجات الإحصائية المناسبة، وقد استنتجت الباحث بإنّ أسهم البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي بشكل إيجابي وفعّال في تنمية مستوى الدافعية العقلية لدى الطالبات، من خلال تعزيز الانتباه والتركيز والرغبة في التعلم، وكذلك وجود تحسن ملحوظ في تعلم السباحة الحرة لدى أفراد المجموعة التي طبّق عليها البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي، تفوق المجموعة التجريبية التي استخدمت البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي على المجموعة الضابطة التي اعتمدت الأسلوب التقليدي في كل من الدافعية العقلية والأداء المهاري. . The research aims to develop a behavioral intervention program focused on mental motivation and freestyle swimming acquisition among female students, and to determine the program's impact on these aspects. To achieve the research objective, the researcher employed the experimental method—specifically a design featuring two equivalent groups (experimental and control) with pre- and post-tests—due to its suitability for the research problem and objectives. The study population consisted of second-year female students in the morning program at the College of Physical Education and Sports Sciences, University of Baghdad, during the 2025–2026 academic year. The total population comprised 110 students distributed across four sections (A, B, C, and D); the second-year cohort was selected because the swimming course is taught at this stage of the curriculum. The research sample was selected by randomly assigning the class sections to the experimental and control groups. Subsequently, the researcher randomly selected 25 female students from each section—specifically Section B (25 students) and Section D (25 students)—resulting in a total sample of 50 students (representing 45.45% of the population). The researcher then administered pre-tests and post-tests to both the experimental and control groups. Appropriate statistical analyses were conducted, leading the researcher to conclude that the behavioral therapeutic program contributed positively and effectively to enhancing the female students' level of mental motivation by fostering attention, concentration, and the desire to learn. Furthermore, a marked improvement in freestyle swimming skills was observed among the participants who underwent the behavioral therapeutic program; the experimental group utilizing this program outperformed the control group—which relied on the traditional method—in both mental motivation and skill performance.
title: تأثير برنامج علاجي سلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة للطالبات. The Effect of a Behavioral Therapeutic Program on Cognitive Motivation and Freestyle Swimming Learning Among Female Students

summary: This record provides the frozen Python research scripts and derived experimental evidence for a study of selective sensor-quality gating in wearable human activity recognition. The included code covers subject-disjoint evaluation on PAMAP2 and MHEALTH, synthetic sensor degradation, comparisons with uniform, static and confidence-based fusion, and a Windows-host pipeline timing benchmark. Derived CSV and JSON files include evaluation reports, per-window classification results, static fusion weights and timing measurements. Original PAMAP2 and MHEALTH sensor recordings are not redistributed; they must be obtained from their respective official sources (DOIs: 10.24432/C5NW2H and 10.24432/C5TW22). The original experiment scripts are preserved byte-for-byte and contain Windows-specific paths and dependencies; they should not be interpreted as turnkey portable software. The reported gains are condition-dependent and exploratory, and the timing measurements do not establish embedded-device energy efficiency or latency. No research manuscript, publication figures or LaTeX sources are included.
title: Selective Sensor-Quality Gating for Wearable Activity Recognition: Research Code and Derived Evidence
