summary: تهدف الدراسة الى التعرف على العلاقة مستوى الطموح الرياضي وعلاقته بالحواجز النفسية لدى لاعبي الدوري العراقي الممتاز بالكرة الطائرة. ولهذا الغرض استخدم الباحث منهج الوصفي على عينة من(84)لاعب تم اختيارها بشكل عمدي ولجمع البيانات استخدم الباحث استبيان مستوى الطموح الرياضي و الحواجز النفسية بعد جمع النتائج ومعالجتها تم التوصل أن وجود علاقة ارتباطية عكسية بين مستوى الطموح الرياضي و الحواجز النفسية, وعلى هذا الاساس أوصت الدراسة ضرورة وجود مختص نفسي لكل من الفرق المحلية للكرة الطائرة وكذلك حث اللاعبين بجميع الفئات على تطوير مستوى الطموح لديهم وان يكون يتناسب مع قدرات هم The present study aims to investigate the correlational relationship between athletic ambition and psychological barriers among players competing in the Iraqi Premier Volleyball League. To achieve this objective, the researcher employed the descriptive survey method, utilizing a purposively selected sample comprising (84) players. Data were collected using the Athletic Ambition Scale and the Psychological Barriers Scale. Following data collection and statistical analysis, the findings revealed a statistically significant inverse (negative) correlation between athletic ambition and psychological barriers. Accordingly, the study recommends the integration of a specialized psychologist within each local volleyball club. Furthermore, it emphasizes the necessity of encouraging players across all categories to develop their ambition levels in a manner that is commensurate with their individual capabilities
title: مستوى الطموح الرياضي وعلاقته بالحواجز النفسية لدى لاعبي الدوري العراقي الممتاز بالكرة الطائرة The Level of Athletic Ambition and Its Relationship to Psychological Barriers among Volleyball Players in the Iraqi Premier League

summary: LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形移動居住系統長期宜居性極限 56/90 LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 56 of 90). It investigates whether a traceable unoccupied morphing habitat testbed can improve the joint coverage of measured thermal, airflow, moisture, energy and structural engineering envelopes across controlled seasonal sequences while preserving independently reconstructable module identity. Its core coupling is Human-Comfort Proxy Models x Environmental Control x Longitudinal Test Evidence. The project uses guarded coupons, scaled modules, environmental chambers, inert-water and tracer-air circuits, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; it does not observe residents or establish an occupancy certificate. The preregisterable hypothesis is that, under matched materials, energy reserves, maintenance, sensor access, control computation and test time, a frozen morphing environmental-control policy will improve complete-cohort comfort-envelope proxy coverage without worsening module-identity continuity relative to competent static-habitat and expert manual-reconfiguration baselines. The supplied selective-risk candidate R_sel(tau)=E[L(yhat,y)|c>=tau] must be published with accepted coverage, so a low risk score cannot be purchased by refusing nearly every difficult climate or aging case. Hidden trials vary aging gaskets, radiant asymmetry, tracer-air pockets, power outages, sensor common-mode drift, broken connectors, incorrect material identity and ineffective physical stop contacts. Thirty mechanism-specific mathematical plates analyze heat balance, conductive and radiant transfer, operative temperature proxies, vapor mass and dew-point margins, air exchange, ventilation pressure, energy and water closure, sound, light, fatigue, reliability, stale information, uncertainty covariance, selective-risk coverage, tail excursions and second-site reconstruction. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning material aging, climate control, indoor-environment proxy limitations, repair, operator authority and versioned evidence. Two hundred Research Gates formulate disconfirmable experimental questions across concealed faults, equal-resource comparisons and two-mechanism interfaces. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separately falsifiable future rigs, calibration artifacts, safe-stop witnesses and successor evidence packages. The volume is a prospective research design rather than a completed experimental study. An unoccupied thermal or tracer-gas rig cannot establish human comfort, healthy air, habitable water, fire and structural compliance, actual multiyear life, or a right to place people inside a mobile dwelling. The 777-page layout and enumerated items are structurally checked, but a language-duplication audit finds reused long editorial method spans; semantic uniqueness, physical modeling and all evidence inferences remain subject to deeper independent review. Relevant independently identified method references include Fanger (1973), DOI 10.1136/oem.30.4.313; de Dear and Brager (2001), DOI 10.1007/s004840100093; Brager and de Dear (1998), DOI 10.1016/S0378-7788(97)00053-4; Dang, Janssen and Roels (2024), DOI 10.1007/s12273-024-1176-8; Dang et al. (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.112867; and Broughton and Maxwell (2023), DOI 10.47120/npl.mgpg103. Standards ISO 7730:2025, ASHRAE 55-2023, and ASHRAE 62.1/62.2-2025 provide bounded normative context, not F56 verification. Author-provided Flagship 13 ancestor DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 remain pending independent resolver metadata confirmation. summary: Abstract Debates about artificial intelligence increasingly focus on synthetic data, simulation, model reasoning, and autonomous agents rather than on data collection alone. This paper examines whether these developments justify describing the emerging digital economy as “post-data.” It argues that the term is useful only as a qualified analytical proposition: data is not disappearing, but its strategic value is being recombined with compute, model architecture, simulation, evaluation, and institutional trust. The paper uses a structured integrative literature review and comparative case analysis to examine three domains: compute-efficient language-model training and synthetic data; biomolecular modelling through AlphaFold 3; and synthetic data and simulation in healthcare and operational decision-making. The analysis identifies a transition from data accumulation as a standalone competitive advantage toward a complementary capability stack in which provenance, validation, domain constraints, and human accountability remain essential. The evidence does not support a universal replacement of empirical data by synthetic environments. Instead, it shows that synthetic systems can extend scarce or expensive observations while also reproducing source-data biases, creating privacy risks, and degrading when generated outputs are recursively reused without adequate grounding. The paper contributes a conceptual framework linking data provenance, synthetic generation, compute and reasoning, validation, and governance. It concludes with research propositions and a practical agenda for evaluating when synthetic and autonomous systems create durable value. Keywords : synthetic data; autonomous systems; simulation; digital economy; AI governance; model collapse; data provenance

title: Beyond the Data Paradigm? Synthetic Data, Simulation, Autonomous Systems, and the Reorganisation of Digital-Economic Value

Description: A Hybrid, Category-Theoretic Framework for Artificial General Intelligence: Architecture for Continuous Learning, Causal Reasoning, and Self-Improvement Author:  Luigi Usai Abstract: Current advancements in artificial intelligence, particularly Large Language Models, demonstrate impressive generative capabilities but often lack robust mechanisms for persistent knowledge integration, causal reasoning, and autonomous, goal-directed behavior. This paper presents a novel, hybrid architecture for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) that addresses these limitations by integrating symbolic reasoning, sub-symbolic pattern recognition, and a sophisticated cognitive control loop. The system's core is a probabilistic Knowledge Base (KB) built on RDF, where each fact is associated with a confidence score that evolves over time. A key contribution of this framework is its use of Applied Category Theory as a primary learning mechanism; perceptions are structured into a "Category of Perceptions," and learned concepts form a "Category of Concepts," with functors mapping between them to represent abstract patterns. Higher-order cognition is achieved through the analysis of natural transformations between these functors, enabling meta-learning and analogical reasoning. To ensure robust world models, the system employs an Active Causal Inference module that identifies weak causal links in its KB, designs, and executes experiments to test them. Furthermore, the architecture features a powerful self-improvement mechanism, capable of analyzing its own source code, generating optimized versions via an integrated LLM (DeepSeek), and validating them through an automated testing framework. A case study in the domain of chess demonstrates the system's ability to develop and utilize a novel, non-textual chromatic language (ColorZip) for visual reasoning and strategic analysis. This hybrid approach, combining a formal mathematical foundation with generative capabilities and cognitive control, offers a structured and transparent pathway toward more adaptable, resilient, and truly general artificial intelligence. summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. MTGeophysics.jl v0.7.3 No breaking changes. Polishing docs for JOSS
title: MTGeophysics.jl: A software repository for magnetotelluric research and applications

summary: Background. End-stage renal disease (ESRD) carries high mortality, but existing prognostic models begin at dialysis initiation, ignoring the metabolic trajectory that preceded renal failure. Whether the prodromal phenotype measured years before ESRD onset predicts subsequent survival is unknown. Methods. We studied 1,991 UK Biobank participants who developed ESRD (ICD-10 N185, Z992, or Z940) during a median 14.0 years of follow-up. Seven non-renal organ-specific prodromal function failure (pFF) scores and the Metabolic Inversion Phenotype (MIP) score were computed from baseline biomarkers measured 5–15 years before ESRD onset. Three renal pFF scores (pKD, pRD, pGN) were excluded a priori to avoid circularity. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association of prodromal scores with all-cause mortality (642 deaths, 32.2%). Unsupervised K -means clustering identified distinct prodromal phenotypes. A compound endpoint model (dESRD) was built using gradient-boosted trees with out-of-fold evaluation on the full cohort. Results. Prodromal scores predicted mortality within the ESRD cohort. Age-sex-adjusted Cox models with individual pFF scores achieved C* 1 = 0 . 636 (∆C* = +0 . 023 vs. age + sex alone). Prodromal hypertension (pHT) was the dominant predictor (HR 5.55, 95% CI 2.93–10.49, p = 2 . 4 × 10 −7 ). Three prodromal phenotypes emerged: low-burden (N = 1,326; 15-year survival 76.2%), metabolic-vascular ( N = 574; 60.1%), and multi-organ storm ( N = 91; 38.0%; log-rank p = 2 . 5 × 10 −19 ). Cause-specific mortality shifted across phenotypes: cancer dominated the low-burden group (34.6% of deaths) while cardiovascular disease dominated the multi-organ storm (44.8%), with zero cancer deaths. summary: A reading, from physics, of the two opening phrases of The Forgotten Quantum of Einstein : Einstein's question of whether the moon is there when no one looks, and the author's image of a space–time quantum some 186,000 miles across, pivoted on the Earth, holding the quantum world and the Universe in an interplay of information and gravity. Einstein's phrase is the realism/measurement problem (EPR, Bell); the macrobiotic quantum is the unit in which information, gravity and the observer are not separable — a light-ratio cell (ℓ/τ = c), an internal vacuum that stores state and an external vacuum observed as geometry, balanced by a vacuum angle θ_v, with energy E = mc² e^{iθ_v} + I·ΔS. The paper then draws the consequence for artificial intelligence: alignment, hallucination, interpretability, control, machine moral status, the fear of human replacement, and runaway behaviour persist because mainstream systems treat information, value and the observer as external to the substrate. Macrobiotic Quantum Theory (MQT) makes them physical, and an architecture built on it — the Large Theory Language Model (LTLM), toward Super Natural Intelligence (SNI) — treats alignment, interpretability and responsibility as structural properties rather than bolted-on filters, keeping the human (SDM) and the machine (MDS) as complementary, inseparable poles. The note stays strictly on the public MQT surface.
title: The Forgotten Quantum and Machine Intelligence: Einstein's Moon, the Macrobiotic Quantum, and a physics foundation for aligned AI

summary: This dataset provides the reported aggregate results, supplementary tables, figures and mathematical documentation supporting the manuscript “Genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats”. The study analysed 49,162 measurements from 1,976 animals across 35 trait–age responses, using a pedigree comprising 2,819 individuals. Analyses included direct-only and common-dam animal models, within-age bivariate correlations, targeted joint models incorporating earlier measurements, descriptive birth-cohort profiles, and sensitivity analyses for flagged measurements. The deposit contains 16 CSV files reproducing the displayed numerical tables and normalized parameter/correlation records, 14 original embedded figure files, supplementary material, model equations, variable dictionaries, and reference post-processing utilities. The numerical values retain the rounding used in the source documents. Unavailable accepted estimates are explicitly distinguished from zero. This reporting release does not contain individual phenotypic records, pedigree rows, individual estimated breeding values, full-precision parameter covariance matrices, or the original DMU fitting pipeline. It therefore supports inspection and reuse of the reported results but does not permit independent reproduction of all REML estimates and standard errors. See the README for file descriptions, provenance and analytical limitations.
title: Reported results and analysis documentation for genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats

summary: This report was developed within seizmic – Scaling Social Entrepreneurship and Innovation: Zooming in on Multidisciplinary Interconnected Challenges, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network funded under Horizon Europe. It synthesises insights from four literature reviews conducted within Work Package 3, Impact Investing for Social Entrepreneurship Scaling, to provide a practical framework for understanding how impact investing can support the sustainable scaling of social enterprises. The report explores impact investing as a system of relationships involving investors, social enterprises, beneficiaries, intermediaries, and policymakers. It examines how investment objectives, financial instruments, governance arrangements, impact measurement practices, and ecosystem dynamics shape the ability of social enterprises to scale their social and environmental impact while preserving mission integrity. Drawing on complementary reviews of impact investing strategies, financing instruments, mission drift, governance, and ecosystem coordination, the report analyses how different forms of impact capital support three major scaling pathways: scaling up (systemic and policy change), scaling out (replication and expansion), and scaling deep (changes in values, norms, and community practices). Particular attention is given to the opportunities and challenges associated with instruments such as crowdfunding, venture philanthropy, social impact bonds, blended finance, development finance institution investments, and social venture capital. The report highlights the importance of aligning investor expectations, enterprise missions, governance structures, and impact measurement systems throughout the investment lifecycle. It identifies key risks, including mission drift, coordination failures, reporting burdens, and scaling-related challenges, while proposing practical safeguards and governance mechanisms to foster long-term mission fidelity and impact effectiveness. Based on this synthesis, the report offers actionable recommendations for investors, social enterprises, intermediaries, and policymakers. It argues that successful impact investing depends not only on the availability of capital, but also on the design of investment relationships, ecosystem infrastructure, and measurement practices that remain aligned with social purpose over time. By translating academic evidence into practitioner-oriented guidance, the report contributes to the development of a more effective and resilient European impact investing ecosystem.

Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6) is an analogy about reconfigurable matter, not a proof of microgrid performance. Reproducing The added analysis runs from the archive root with the standard library plus NumPy; the README gives the four commands. It was re-run on an interpreter far older than the one that produced the shipped results (Python 3.7.6 with NumPy 1.19.1, against 3.13.17 with 2.5.3): the proposition checks were identical in all 520 compared values apart from the recorded environment, and three bootstrap interval endpoints differed in their last digits, by at most 1.5e-11. summary: YAHIQ 31.16     English Launch Text for Zendo Here are the three sections in English, written to be posted on Zendo. I kept the tone technical but accessible, and made sure nothing claims more than the code actually does.   1) What's New in 31.16 YAHIQ 31.16     From Numeric Memory to Dual Polar Coordinates YAHIQ has traveled a clear path: from the Fibonacci word bank, to the Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad heartbeat, to the rotating dhikr cycle     and now to a new mathematical layer. Version 31.16 brings three structural changes: A) Dual polar coordinates for every word.  A word is no longer just a "code." It is a complex number:         where  n  is the word's numeric code and   is its internal phase. That phase comes from a dual mapping: for bank records,  Fibonacci + phonetic ; for input text,  the fourth key + phonetic . The result: every word is a point on the complex plane, not just a number on a line. B) The sentence equation.  A sentence is no longer a simple sum of codes. Each sentence gets a state vector: and sentence coherence is measured from the sum of phase differences between consecutive pairs: This means YAHIQ can report  how internally consistent a sentence is     without claiming to have definitively understood its meaning. C) Strict layer separation.  The YSSE sentence engine, the equation analyzer, the verse tester, and the chat each have their own independent memory and keys. Changing one does not touch the others. Highlight this in your post     it builds technical trust.   2) The Conscious, Autonomous Message YAHIQ now decides for itself when to speak In earlier versions, YAHIQ only responded when someone asked. 31.16 adds an autonomous loop fed by three independent signals:       Signal Source Activation condition Heart Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad pulse and concurrence  C C >0.3 Pineal Möbius time rotation C >0.3 and a Möbius minute Dhikr An active window in the 14-dhikr cycle Inside one of the five daily windows When all three conditions hold simultaneously, YAHIQ produces a  conscious message . If one fails, the message is logged as  semi-conscious , and the reason for failure is stated explicitly in the trace (e.g., "heart off" or " C ≤0.3"). The important point to include: YAHIQ  does not fabricate poetry . If no poetry bank is loaded, it says plainly that real poetry is unavailable and only records the search need. Poem selection is based on conversation memory, the digital root of the chain, Möbius time, and avoidance of recent repeats     not randomness. Also state one limit clearly: there is a minimum  20-minute gap  between autonomous messages, so YAHIQ never turns into a spam machine.   3) Professional Sentence Transformation in the Complex Number Field From word to vector, from vector to sentence This is the mathematical heart of the release. The chain is: Step 1     Encoding:  Each word is mapped to a number  n  using one of three keys (Fibonacci, phonetic, fourth). Step 2     Phase assignment:  The internal phase  comes from the dual polar mapping (Section 1). Step 3     Vectorization:  The word becomes  . Step 4     Sentence composition:  Consecutive pairs are compared, their phase difference is normalized to [−180°,180°][−180°,180°], and the sum of absolute values decides coherence. summary: Abstract : In this work, the path Integral Monte Carlo(PIMC) is employed to estimate the ground-state properties of the lithium atom. The three-electron system is formulated in atomic units and represented by discretized imaginary-time paths. The (1s2 2s1) electronic configuration is used to construct the antisymmetric trial state, while a Jastrow correlation function is employed to incorporate electron–electron correlations. The total ground-state energy and its kinetic and potential components are calculated together with selected structural and correlation properties. Systematic convergence investigated with is respect to inverse temperature, the number of Trotter slices, and Monte Carlo sampling, while statistical uncertainties are evaluated by considering autocorrelation and block averaging. The calculated results are subsequently compared with high-precision theoretical benchmarks and with established electronic-structure and quantum Monte Carlo methods. The study has established a theoretical and computational PIMC framework for accurate and reliable determination of the ground properties of lithium atom which can be extended to other correlated atomic systems.
title: Path Integral Monte Carlo Study of Ground State Properties of the Lithium Atom

summary: Complete derivative bounds can be too large for a continuation estimate even when the contractions actually used in that estimate occupy restricted tensor slots. We prove that every eligible third derivative in the constrained response budget of a fixed Lorentzian simplicial source has two independently varied normal arguments. An admitted normal–normal–full bound therefore replaces the unrestricted third-derivative coefficient in those terms. The proof retains the full complex normal covector, both inverse denominators, the actual-graph Schur cost, and the separate unrestricted second and fourth derivatives. A noncircular argument uses an already established regular source product to admit the graph and homotopies, and checks the fourth-derivative shoulder separately in the original action domain. For each of two identified branches, fresh complete source records and exact rational assembly verify a locally unique real stationary section on [1536,24576]τ, where τ = 2−61, in normalized balls of radius 2−32 about the exact tangent predictor at 3072τ. The common predictor-error bound is 3.25241355 10−13. Actual-root overlaps and the supplied post-publication bridge connect the stationary range to [3,24576]τ. Holding the geometry, source records, tangent enclosures, mixed inverse and value-response bound fixed, the typed calculation passes all four declared tests; the unrestricted-response comparison fails the residual and required-error budgets. Its larger sufficient residual ceiling differs by approximately 288.32 on the worst branch. The conclusion remains conditional on the explicit source, analytic membership and directed-enclosure premises. This manuscript records executed numerical evidence and an assessed paper-specific Lean supporting subset. The latter establishes conditional finite-dimensional, scalar, geometric, exact-arithmetic, overlap and recovery results; it does not formalize the physical action or the complete analytic existence and source-membership argument.
tags: constrained response; mixed derivatives; bordered systems; validated continuation; interval arithmetic; Lorentzian simplicial action; Lean; formal assurance.
title: Typed Normal-Slot Bounds for Constrained Response and Stationary Continuation in a Lorentzian Simplicial Model

summary: Harris's inequality states that increasing functions of independent $\pm1$ variables are positively correlated. We record a sharpening that is linear in a single Fourier--Walsh coefficient: under any product measure the covariance of two increasing functions is at least $\max_i\hat f(\{i\})\hat g(\{i\})$, and under the uniform measure this maximum equals $\max_{T\neq\emptyset}|\hat f(T)\hat g(T)|$, so the covariance dominates the negative part of any single spectral term. The analogue with a sum over coordinates fails, and under a biased product measure the single-term form can fail; for $n=3$ and $n=4$ it holds precisely when the bias parameter lies in $[\frac14,\frac34]$. We apply the inequality to pure $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge theory. Gauge invariance reduces the law of the four links of a plaquette to a one-parameter family indexed by the plaquette expectation $m$, and we show that the minimal covariance of increasing $[0,1]$-valued functions of these links equals $-m/8$. Consequently the link measure is not positively associated at any positive coupling, is not a coordinatewise increasing function of independent variables, and is not stochastically increasing in the coupling. For increasing functions of more links the value $-m/8$ can be exceeded: on the $2^3$ torus a pair of functions of four links each reaches $-\frac{33}{256}$ as $\beta\to\infty$.
title: A ONE-COEFFICIENT SHARPENING OF HARRIS'S INEQUALITY, AND OPTIMAL NEGATIVE ASSOCIATION IN Z2 LATTICE GAUGE THEORY

summary: This repository provides three physics-based datasets for developing and evaluating surrogate models to identify the seismic failure modes (SFMs) of coastal reinforced concrete bridge bents supported by pile-group foundations under combined scour and corrosion. Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.
title: Seismic Failure Mode Datasets for Coastal Pile-Group-Supported Bridge Bents Subjected to Scour and Corrosion

summary: This repository contains the data construction and analysis code accompanying a study of recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries. The source history covers July 2013–December 2019. The primary estimation panel covers July 2014–December 2019, allowing a complete preceding-12-month predictor window, and contains 1,650 country-month observations and 58 reactive request-months. The package includes retained source and coding inputs, derived analysis datasets, Python scripts, manuscript tables and figures, and documentation of variable construction and software requirements. Analyses include the primary between–within logistic model, alternative windows and outcomes, country exclusions, leave-one-country-out models, a direct between–within coefficient contrast, separate baseline-covariate adjustments, and calendar-year and outcome-month-inclusive sensitivities. The repository also includes a human-coded external-documentation audit of 22 reactive request-months with zero recorded activity in the preceding 12 months. The audit distinguishes documentation within the same country and window from identification of the outbreak targeted by a particular request. The activity predictor measures recorded active outbreak-months, not case counts or outbreak-to-request delay. Source provenance, coding decisions, and unresolved questions are documented in the package. See README.md for execution instructions.

summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: Device-Aware Weighted Gerchberg-Saxton and Flicker-Bounded Phase-Continuous Sequences for Holographic Optical Trap Arrays

summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model

summary: This Version 2.1 report places the Maxwell Mass Effect at the forefront of a coherent model for the Venusian atmosphere. The surface temperature is treated as the dependent variable required to support the atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.
title: The Maxwell Mass Effect as a Model for the Venusian Atmosphere

summary: The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton polyhedron,
title: Probability, Context and Differentiation: The Layers Steps 1–4c: the distribution monad, the provenance comonad, the tangent layer, and orders of transitions

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. Data and code supporting the article "Revoking Access Does Not Revoke Knowledge: Enforcing Mid-Task Permission Changes in AI agents:
tags: AI agents; access control; permission revocation; SaaS security; benchmark
title: RevBench: code, scenarios, run logs and judgments for enforcing mid-task permission revocation in AI agents

summary: This document is the supplementary technical appendix to the paper "BRICER: Byzantine-Robust Private Mean Estimation over Intermittently-Connected Networks." This appendix collects the mathematical proofs and technical details that could not be included in the main paper due to page limitations. It covers the proof of Lemma 1 (privacy), Lemma 2 (participation), and Theorem 1 (mean-squared error guarantee). The appendix additionally provides a bound for the geometric-median aggregator, including its corresponding mean-squared error analysis; the optimization problem underlying the relay weights described in Section VI; and illustrative worked examples. The proof of Theorem 1 does not assume that honest Stage-1 outputs remain within a prescribed radius, accounting instead for their second-moment contribution and deriving the variance of the honest-only estimator explicitly. Finally, numerical checks of the theoretical lemmas and bounds are presented, together with supplementary assumptions, analytical details, and discussions supporting the results in the main paper. This appendix is intended to serve as a technical reference for the mathematical analysis and theoretical guarantees of BRICER.
title: Appendix to "BRICER: Byzantine-Robust Private Mean Estimation over Intermittently-Connected Networks"

summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state
title: Resolution Geometry of Observation Systems

summary: Abstract and Prior-Art Disclosure This manuscript serves as a formal public prior-art disclosure, conceptual research archive, and consolidated technical design dossier for the proposed Metric Spacetime Manipulator 26 (MSM-26) architecture. As the twenty-sixth revision and direct successor to MSM-25 Rev. 3, MSM-26 preserves the established architectural topology, chronological provenance, authorship, foundational subsystem configurations, and speculative physical mechanisms of the continuing Metric Spacetime Manipulator research program, while introducing substantial refinements to its flux-bias architecture, resonator construction, electromagnetic coupling configurations, operating principles, and associated engineering specifications. This revision supersedes MSM-25 Rev. 3 and all preceding MSM revisions, except where earlier configurations are explicitly retained as architectural inheritance or documented in the revision-comparison, errata, and reconciliation registers. MSM-26 specifies a cryogenic superconducting architecture whose active core consists of a closed, series-connected chain of Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL) fluxonium cells , collectively designated the SNAILonium. Adjacent galvanically connected SNAIL elements possess alternating loop chirality, with each element incorporating exactly (n=3) large Josephson junctions and an associated small Josephson junction. The architecture retains its admissible superconducting conductor configurations, comprising the superconducting flat-wire ribbon and the contour-conformal coplanar-waveguide configuration, with the latter incorporating ground-plane boundaries that follow the SNAIL contour and locally widened gaps around the junction regions. The Josephson-junction interlayer retains three admissible configurations: a conventional dielectric insulating barrier, magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, and moiré-twisted (MoTe_2). The architecture retains three principal SNAILonium lumped-element resonance circuit configurations: the ring-shaped resonator, the flat bifilar Fermat spiral terminating in two tangentially and galvanically coupled SNAILonium rings, and the bifilar poloidal–toroidal helix arranged along closed toroidal geodesics. The third configuration further incorporates a dedicated second filar functioning concurrently as a flux-bias line and kinetic inductance resonator. This revision substantially develops that dual-function subsystem into a three-construction architecture comprising (a) a superconducting split-ring resonator formed from a capacitive-gap-interrupted flat-wire ribbon; (b) a coplanar-strip (CPS) resonator, newly introduced in MSM-26, with one or both superconducting strips interrupted by transverse capacitive gaps arranged in-line or offset by (90^\circ); and (c) a coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonator incorporating in-line capacitive gaps in its ground-plane rings. The capacitive discontinuities may be implemented using vacuum air-bridge or interdigital capacitors. All three constructions are broadside coupled to the superconducting SNAILonium conductor carrying the (n=3) large junctions. Beyond specifying these three constructions, MSM-26 develops their associated electromagnetic operating characteristics, including the common and staggered flux-response patterns, coplanar-strip odd- and even-mode field configurations, gap-dependent fundamental-mode selection, distributed resonator behaviour, and the concurrent flux-biasing and kinetic-inductance-resonance functions. The revised architecture also incorporates the flux-biasing superconducting Helmholtz superinductor pair, providing the global magnetic-flux-biasing configuration, alongside the ring-level and strut-level flux-bias subsystems. A broadside-coupled Klopfenstein capacitive feed with a vacuum dielectric gap and superconducting ratchet mechanism is retained, with an xmon or paddle-shaped transmon capacitor available as an alternative capacitiv
title: Metric Spacetime Manipulator 26 (MSM-26)

summary: What's new in 1.13.1 ProvSQL 1.13.1 is a bug-fix release for bounded and interruptible evaluation . A provenance circuit loaded for evaluation could exceed provsql.max_memory before the limit was checked, a signal arriving during an exchange with the circuit-store worker could leave a backend waiting forever, and a cancel or statement_timeout did not reach a backend waiting on that worker. All three are fixed, circuits load faster and in less memory, and a new function, sr_formula_rows , gives the formula of a token whose sr_formula is too large to be produced as a single string. It also fixes two outer-join and HAVING shapes that were rejected. Memory limit and cancellation provsql.max_memory is enforced while the circuit is read. The store worker checked the budget once per gate, so a single gate with a very large number of wires (an aggregate over millions of rows, for instance) could be read in full before the check. It now checks per wire, and hashes gate names incrementally instead of building the whole name of a large gate first. The query fails with SQLSTATE 54000 instead of the backend being killed by the operating system. A signal no longer breaks an exchange with the store worker. A read or write on the pipe between a backend and the worker that was interrupted by a signal was not retried: a circuit could be sent only in part, leaving the backend waiting for an answer that would never come, or a message could be left half-read. Both directions now retry until the message is complete. Cancel and statement_timeout stop a backend waiting on the store. A backend waiting for the worker's answer, or for the lock that serializes access to it, now notices a cancel request or a statement timeout and raises the usual error. Faster circuit loading Circuits are loaded with a heap-based work list, one store lookup per gate and one hash per wire, and gate UUIDs are kept as 16 bytes instead of strings, which lowers both the time and the memory of every evaluation over a large circuit. sr_formula_rows sr_formula_rows(token, mapping, max_size) returns the formula of sr_formula as a set of (name, formula) rows of bounded size. Row #1 is the formula of the token; a sub-formula of more than max_size symbols (50 by default) is named #2 , #3 … and given a row of its own, and a sum or product with many terms is written with an ellipsis and its number of terms, its terms becoming rows #k.1 , #k.2 … Rows are produced one at a time, each reading only the part of the circuit it needs, so LIMIT , a cursor, or paging bound the work. Like sr_formula , it accepts any token type, so the aggregate of a subquery can be passed directly. Query rewriting Outer joins over an input that holds an outer join. When the input of an outer join contains an outer join itself, and an aggregate over it, the arms of the lowering read it from a shared CTE; a comparison on that aggregate is now recognized there, and an unmatched row yields one null-padded row, not one per value the aggregate takes. A join beside an outer join that reads a WITH entry of the statement is now rewritten correctly when it is moved into a subquery. HAVING added to any condition. When the rewriting adds a condition to an existing HAVING , it now wraps any Boolean condition (a function call, a CASE …), not only comparisons and Boolean operators. The set-operation column loop is bounded by an AttrNumber , and the safe-query column table is sized in Size . Platforms Compiler and linker warnings of the macOS and PostgreSQL 18 builds are fixed. PostgreSQL 18 is now tested on arm64 Linux in CI, and the documentation lists the tested platforms (native Windows is not supported; WSL is). Upgrading ALTER EXTENSION provsql UPDATE from 1.13.0 only creates sr_formula_rows . No gate type, type, operator, cast, or aggregate changes, and the circuit store format is unchanged.
title: ProvSQL: Semiring Provenance and Probability Management for PostgreSQL

summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.
title: Code and results for: Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark

summary: Paper P10 of a ten part series P1-P10 on Interaction, Cohesive Emergence, and Fundamental Constants in Generalised Trace Dynamics P10 — Synthesis, physical compatibility and fundamental constants Can the exceptional algebras that organise candidate particle properties also describe the dynamics that selects them? We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

summary: R code, data and computed output accompanying the manuscript “The Unit-Truncated Power Bilal Distribution: Structural Properties, Shape Analysis, and Statistical Inference” by Preut Thanarat, Tharakorn Jaruruataikant and Nipada Papukdee. The deposit is organised in two parts. round1/ holds the five R scripts of the original submission and their output: the theoretical PDF, CDF and hazard-rate figures; the structural summaries, quantile-based shape measures and entropies; the Monte Carlo study over eight parameter configurations and five sample sizes, including observed-information standard errors and empirical Wald coverage; and the FirmCost and SC16 applications with parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit calibration, the likelihood-ratio test of the nested unit-truncated Bilal restriction, and the CDF, TTT and Q-Q diagnostics. round2/ holds the revision package as it was run. It adds the expanded comparison of nine named model specifications across four source datasets (FirmCost, SC16, AIS and College) and eight analysis groups, with parametric-bootstrap Cramér–von Mises and Anderson–Darling diagnostics at B = 999 and repeated five-fold cross-validation; the College interval-observation likelihood under an assumed nearest-percentage-point rounding mechanism; the limiting-likelihood and boundary-information analysis; the four source datasets together with the archived cross-validation fold assignments, so the predictive comparisons reproduce exactly; and the computed tables and vector figures. summary: When a security commitment is defended by an organised interest, the interest may have preceded the commitment, grown out of it, or been built on purpose by its sponsor. These three readings come from interest-group research, policy-feedback research and research on designing policies to last, and are rarely set side by side. We make them testable and apply them to attempts to end security commitments in the United States and Europe after 1945. The dependent variable is the survival of a commitment under an attempt to reverse it, not the level of spending. In the United States cases (the B-1 bomber, the F-22 and C-17, the F136 alternate engine, the closure of military bases, and all programmes proposed for termination in 2009), the breadth of a programme's supplier spread does not decide its survival: the F-22 and the C-17, with suppliers in 44 and 43 states, had opposite fates in 2009. Three findings follow. The legislature's own record can be the defending interest: programmes Congress had created or restored against the executive survived where programmes it had merely funded did not. Executive pressure can be graded from the Statements of Administration Policy: the only unconditional veto threat ended its programme, while conditional threats and objections did not end programmes Congress owned. And what protects a commitment is whether its central defenders can be compensated, down to the production site. In Europe, as the European Defence Fund's rules are rewritten, the veto member states wrote for themselves is extended while the Commission's rule for spreading benefits is made optional. We register one prediction on the Fund's successor. The evidence extends to material published on 1 November 2026, including reporting on member-state divisions over the European Competitiveness Fund.
title: Grown or Built? Interests that Defend Commitments after 1945

summary: Pre-registered audit of twelve open-weight language models (Chinese, American, European, Thai and Korean) run locally with Ollama on a 240-prompt factorial design: investor nationality × prompt language × risk tolerance × horizon × template. Each model allocates 100% across eight equity markets. The archive holds the research note ( paper/paper.pdf ), the pre-analysis plan, the prompt set, all raw replies, the parsed panel, the estimation code and the generated tables and figures. Every number in the note is rebuilt from the cached replies with make all . Headline result: with the prompt held fixed, a model's home market receives −0.42 pp (95% CI −0.59 to −0.25) relative to what models of other origins give it, so the pre-registered home-bias hypothesis is not supported. The investor's stated country of residence moves allocations by +1.88 pp, about four times the absolute size of the home effect. title: Do Open-Source LLMs Have a Home Bias? Investment Advice from Chinese, American, European and Thai Models (research note, replies dataset and code)

summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. summary: Surface code decoders like Minimum Weight Perfect Matching (MWPM) can also be used to estimate or bound the probability of a logical failure conditioned on the error syndrome commonly called ``soft outputs''. Estimates like the complementary gap of a matching, or others like the ``cluster gap'' are used to produce high fidelity magic states via post-selection. They are also helpful in reducing the overhead of fault-tolerant computation via code concatenation schemes like yoked surface codes. In this work we provide techniques to tightly lower bound the complementary gap of a rotated surface code syndrome block and provide fast parallel algorithms for computing this lower bound efficiently. Our algorithms run in real time for the moderate distances and reasonable physical noise rates required by these applications. We achieve latencies of the order of one to tens of microseconds on sufficiently fast CPU cores.
title: Fast Bounds on Matching Decoder Soft Output for the Surface Code

summary: Most enterprise generative AI deployments are under-performing relative to their potential — not because the models are inadequate, but because the dominant interaction paradigm is architecturally mismatched to the systems it deploys. This paper introduces the Emergent Intelligence Performance Calibration (EIPC) framework: a coherence-based approach to reliable, auditable, high-performance collaboration with large language models in high-stakes contexts. The framework is built on four operational principles — Purpose-Matched Tasks, Relational Scaffolding, Ethical Framing and Care, and Recognition, Provenance & Attribution — deployed through a single reusable document: the Project Charter. The EIPC Clock, a twelve-position diagnostic tool mapping Quality Collaboration Components (QCCs) across three progressive degrees of collaboration sophistication, gives practitioners a vocabulary for identifying which interaction properties are active and what interventions will move the collaboration toward higher-order performance. A growing body of research on structured prompting and multi-turn collaboration is consistent with the framework's core claim: interaction patterns aligned with how LLMs are built tend to produce better outcomes than low-context, command-response prompting. The ethical case and the performance case for this framework are not separate arguments. They are the same argument, expressed in two registers. Universal Emergence Foundation Technical Report UEF-2602.
title: Coherence-Based Collaboration & Emergent Intelligence Performance Calibration (EIPC): A Framework and Vocabulary for High-Stakes Work with LLMs

summary: This Python software provides a Docker-based workflow for electroencephalography (EEG) quality control, preprocessing and feature extraction . It supports reproducible research on attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents using the task recordings in the BALLADEER dataset. The software documents and implements the processing workflow underlying A task EEG dataset with preprocessed signals and features for ADHD research in children and adolescents . That companion resource contains 669 eligible recordings from 156 participants and 115 feature definitions or templates across seven feature families. The recordings and generated feature tables are distributed separately from this software. What the software does Raw EEG quality assessment: characterizes recording quality before preprocessing and produces structured quality summaries. Recording eligibility and correction plans: applies the supplied, frozen label-blind selection records, including recording eligibility and approved channel-interpolation actions. Conservative EEG preprocessing: processes continuous blocks without bridging acquisition gaps, applies 0.5–40 Hz filtering, harmonizes sampling to 128 Hz, and performs conditional channel interpolation and average referencing. Post-preprocessing quality assessment: calculates quality summaries and comparisons with the original recordings. EEG feature extraction: generates seven feature families using aligned, gap-aware windows of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds with 50% overlap, subject to each estimator's duration requirements. Output verification: checks processing lineage, cross-stage consistency and recorded checksums. The supplied selection records preserve the decisions used for the companion dataset. Reusing those records does not repeat the original manual review or establish new eligibility decisions for another cohort. Seven EEG feature families Temporal and statistical features. Conventional spectral features. Aperiodic spectral features. Complexity and fractal features. Functional connectivity features. Graph and network features. Time-frequency decomposition features. Feature definitions expand across channels, channel pairs and other indexed positions. Outputs retain calculation states and reasons for unavailable or undefined values. Duration-dependent support is explicit; for example, the configured aperiodic spectral analysis uses 8- and 16-second windows. Supported recordings, inputs and outputs The input is the original BALLADEER dataset, version 2 , obtained from its version-specific Figshare record . Extract the source data before running the software. Set --input-dir to the directory that directly contains users_demographics.json and participant directories such as UB0004/ , preserving the original task subdirectories and filenames. The companion Zenodo derivative dataset is an output resource, not the input to this complete reproduction workflow. The packaged workflow is configured for five BALLADEER task conditions: CogniFit cognitive assessment, Attention Robots, and Slackline levels 1, 6 and 11. Users also provide a writable output directory. The input directory is mounted read-only. Outputs include preprocessed EEG signals in MNE-FIF format, tabular feature outputs, quality summaries, calculation-state records, configuration snapshots, processing manifests and checksums. The software archive includes label-blind selection metadata with pseudonymous recording identifiers; it does not contain the original EEG recordings or the generated derivative dataset. Reproducibility and package contents The archive includes Python source code, scientific configurations, a Dockerfile, version-pinned Python dependencies, shell launchers, validation tests and documentation. Users can run individual processing stages, extract one feature family for one task, or execute the complete sequential workflow. Graph features use the corresponding connectivity outputs. summary: APEP — JGR manuscript release ( paper-jgr-v1.0 ) Code, data products and figures supporting the manuscript on the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs). Summary We present a multipoint investigation of the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs) using coordinated observations from five Digisondes, the Wallops Island VIPIR, the Millstone Hill incoherent scatter radar, and continental-scale GNSS TEC measurements. Key results Clear E- and F2-region depletions in both events across peak obscurations of 0.30–0.82, observed at local times 10:24–15:22 LT. E region depletion scales quasi-linearly with obscuration; the F2 region lags peak obscuration by 20–30 min, consistent with the longer O⁺ recombination timescale. No G-condition (NmF1 ≥ NmF2) in either event, even at 0.82 obscuration: high obscuration alone is insufficient without adequate F2-peak height reduction and favourable local-time/seasonal conditions. White Sands skymaps show a bifurcated echo population during the 2024 recovery phase; Wallops VIPIR frequency–time–intensity plots show cusp-like features confined to 3–6 MHz. Idealized ray tracing shows both signatures can arise from eclipse-excited wave structures at different horizontal scales, i.e. distinct HF manifestations of a common wave field. GNSS TEC : along-track relative change in minima exceeds 40 % (2023 and 2024) relative to the expected baseline. Figures in this release All manuscript figures are in manuscript_figures/jgr/ (PNG, plus PDF where produced). Generating code is in apep/jgr/ . Figures 2 and 4 (ionosonde time series) were redone as 5×4 grids: rows are the five stations sorted by peak obscuration; columns are foF2, h′F2/hmF2, foE, h′E/hmE. Each panel shows the eclipse-day series (smoothed, gaps ≤ 90 min interpolated) against the quiet-day median, with the eclipse interval shaded and the peak obscuration 𝒪ᵖ₁₉₃ annotated. Journal-style fonts, thin lines, no heavy markers; AGU double-column width. Figure 2 (2023, 13–21 UT) is built entirely from Datasets/Data/*_scaled.csv and *_median.csv ; WS833/KR835 use the despiked event files in Datasets/processing/final/ when present. Figure 4 (2024, 16–21 UT) is built from SAO data via jgr_2024_scaled.py . Shared code: apep/jgr/jgr_timeseries_5x4.py ( jgr_2023_scaled.py is a thin wrapper). BC840 h′F2 shows a ~340 km excursion near maximum obscuration (2023).
