The ten-million-vector index reaches 0.8827 hit@10 at 0.1794 ms per query in a four-thread batch benchmark, while validation selects no skew update. Exact streamed attention over ten million keys evaluates compressed memory on 1,024 held-out queries. Independent matrix solves, automatic differentiation, finite differences, interval arithmetic, full-flow tests, and nine Rocq-checked algebra lemmas support reproducibility. Directionality alone does not establish retrieval superiority.
title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction

summary: Prediction errors from video world models are often treated as physical surprise, but they can also reflect appearance, static content, motion, or ordinary prediction difficulty. We present an evaluation framework that separates what frozen representations contain, how they organize appearance and physical differences, and what changes a model's own prediction error. On IntPhys2, a benchmark of physically possible and impossible events, we compare representations from latent prediction, masked pixel reconstruction, and simple visual statistics. Appearance remains easy to decode, while V-JEPA2 exposes modest information about whether events are possible or impossible. Looking at the latent geometry, appearance changes become smaller compared with differences between videos, their directions line up more consistently across scenes, and their overlap with physical changes decreases in deeper layers. Across action-conditioned models, incorrect actions raise prediction error, while appearance changes also produce substantial responses. In Physion++ video clips, repeating a single frame can produce higher error than the original clip, while changing color throughout the clip can lower it. Using Kubric, a simulation and rendering framework, we find that impossible events can produce lower error than possible events. A fixed error threshold also incorrectly flags many possible events as impossible. A model can therefore represent physical information and respond to incorrect actions without its native prediction error reliably measuring physical surprise.
title: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?

summary: We present Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0, a unified streaming causal world model for Physical AI. It models and generates causal physical evolution in the real world, and unifies heterogeneous conditioning inputs for view-consistent generation. The architecture integrates View-Temporal Attention (VTA) to capture cross-view spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics, together with Multi-view Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) to encode positional relationships across views and time. WorldRec 2.0 reconstructs static and dynamic 3D Gaussians from multi-view, multi-temporal observations in a single forward pass and uses their renderings as explicit scene context to preserve geometry and appearance during long-horizon generation. Conditioning inputs are fused through VAE latent concatenation in a shared representation space. We incorporate Gated Linear Attention (GLA) into the temporal layers of VTA for efficient streaming inference, reducing computation and KV-cache memory during multi-view rollouts. A physical-interaction data pipeline covers diverse interactions and long-tailed events. From Pre-train onward, these data are combined with large-scale videos and heterogeneous visual modalities to learn visual, geometric, and dynamic priors. During Mid-train, training across diverse view configurations further improves the model's ability to capture how actions and object states shape subsequent scene evolution. After distillation-based Post-train, we apply the model to closed-loop simulation, closed-loop training, and World Action Model (WAM) applications. These applications generate physically consistent future states and support world-state prediction, policy learning, and action generation for Physical AI.
title: Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0: Causal World Models for Real-World Driving and Embodied Intelligence

summary: A causal video generator produces two key--value (KV) states for every segment: the KV it uses while denoising that segment, and the KV it writes into the cache for later segments to read. In a pretrained generator the two already differ substantially, later segments attend to them differently, and replacing the written KV with the generation KV degrades the continuation. We propose dKV Forcing (dKV denotes differentiable KV) to learn a dedicated memory representation from its future use: a writer-specific low-rank residual on the shared backbone separates memory writing from generation and is trained through the future reads of what it writes. Learning a write from its future use needs gradients through the cache, which the mutable cache in common use cannot provide. dKV Forcing replaces the training-time cache by persistent differentiable pages with local rematerialization and, in one temporal traversal, computes exactly the gradient that a two-pass reconstruction of the same objective computes. One traversal computes the full memory gradient at $7\%$ generator-update overhead over detached-write training, with $28\%$ less resident memory and $20.8\%$ shorter training cycles than the two-pass reconstruction. Over Self Gradient Forcing (SGF), the same objective trained with the same traversal, writer adaptation raises VBench-Long aesthetic quality by $6.6$ points at 60\,s and $8.5$ points at 240\,s with the highest subject and background consistency, and rollout dropout of the residual keeps most of this gain while restoring the motion of training without write gradients.
title: dKV Forcing: Separating Generation and Memory Representations through a Differentiable KV Cache

summary: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.
title: SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts

summary: Interactive world generation requires both accurate local control and stable scene consistency over long rollouts. Existing methods improve local generation through camera or geometry conditioning and extend historical context with memory mechanisms. However, long-horizon exploration remains challenging as target-view guidance becomes incomplete and inconsistencies accumulate across repeated scene updates. We present \textbf{GSExplorer}, a generation--reconstruction framework built around a persistent 3D Gaussian world state. At each step, the current 3DGS scene provides multimodal rendering conditions for a condition-driven video generator, while camera geometry is injected through a separate Relative Ray Encoding branch. Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. We further design a data-construction pipeline that reproduces realistic 3DGS degradation during scene extrapolation, yielding 293K training pairs of degraded multimodal renderings and real target videos. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. On 481-frame leave-and-return rollouts, it also shows strong revisit consistency, demonstrating the value of maintaining a reliable 3D world state for continued exploration.
title: GSExplorer: Interactive World Generation with a Persistent 3D Gaussian World State

summary: We reproduce the central claims of INP-Former, a reconstruction-based method for multi-class industrial anomaly detection. INP-Former extracts Intrinsic Normal Prototypes (INPs) from each test image and uses them to guide a decoder that reconstructs normal features, without a stored memory bank. Using the authors' released code, we reproduce the reported performance on MVTec AD and VisA and extend the evaluation to MVTec AD 2, where image AUROC with the default settings is 63.4, compared with 99.7 on MVTec AD. On MVTec AD, a five-seed ablation shows that most of the performance comes from the INP mechanism, while the two auxiliary losses add small changes whose direction depends on the metric. A paired comparison with both losses disabled confirms the benefit of INP on MVTec AD 2. The default of six prototypes transfers less well: the plateau beyond four prototypes reproduces on MVTec AD and VisA, but on MVTec AD 2 a single prototype outperforms six in AU-PRO on the public split and on both hidden test splits. We also measure practical trade-offs in resolution, backbone size, training length, and LoRA adaptation, and examine performance by defect size, lighting condition, and a stricter AU-PRO limit. Several conclusions from the original benchmarks, including the default prototype count, do not carry over to harder data. Code: https://github.com/garasnote/Repro-INPFormer
title: Reproducing INP-Former: Reconstructing Intrinsic Normal Prototypes for Industrial Anomaly Detection

summary: Interactive video world models draw each frame from a memory bank of earlier frames stamped with their capture times. With frames, weights and noise fixed, reversing the timestamps of two views flips the state that generators of two families draw: they take the newest timestamp as the truth. That reading is right as long as states never return. After an agent undoes an action, the newest view of a region is outdated and the only view of the present is older; memories for changing worlds delete that older view, and memories that keep it hand the generator the past. Temporal databases separate when a record is stored from when its content holds, its valid time. ReDate keeps every frame and dates each retrieved token by its valid time, read from the agent's action log. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as one that has just reached a new state, so ReDate needs no training. We prove that trusting the newest timestamp is right exactly when every current view is dated after every outdated one, that without a view taken after the return only the action log tells a reverted region from an up-to-date one, and that a generator able to draw from its own prediction gains more from re-dating than from deletion when the moved tokens keep little weight. After an undo, ReDate raises the share of FAR's steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 and HY-WorldPlay's from 0.003 to 0.19. We also propose a calibrated state metric to test any memory after undos.
title: Old Is Not False: Valid-Time Memory for Interactive Video World Models

summary: The Neptunian desert and savanna are separated by a ridge, an overdensity at orbital periods of approximately 3-6 d identified with Kepler. Like the hot Jupiter pileup at larger radii, this feature has been linked to the accumulation of successful outcomes of high-eccentricity migration (HEM). We revisit the ridge independently using TESS occurrence posteriors for FGK main-sequence stars. We quantify its excess over adjacent regions and compare six occurrence profiles using leave-one-out cross-validation and Bayesian evidence. For planets with radii of approximately 5-8 $R_\oplus$, the ridge has twice the occurrence density of the denser neighbouring region ($J=2.05^{+0.52}_{-0.44}$), with 99.9% posterior support (one-sided Gaussian equivalent of $3.1σ$). This contrast agrees with the discovery study and earlier Kepler occurrence measurements. Both predictive performance and Bayesian evidence strongly favour profiles peaking within the ridge over a single power law. The lognormal is preferred, suggesting a narrower inner wing and a more extended outer wing, although evidence for asymmetry remains weak. In the same period window, the analysis recovers the hot Jupiter pileup (approximately 10-16 $R_\oplus$) with a contrast consistent with that of the ridge and excludes an analogous excess among sub-Neptunes (approximately 2-4 $R_\oplus$) with $3.4σ$ posterior support. TESS thus provides an independent detection of the Neptunian ridge. Its possible asymmetry would be compatible with HEM, in which tidal disruption could produce a sharper inner edge and variations in circularisation efficiency a more gradual outer decline. Establishing whether the ridge has this shape requires more precise occurrence measurements, with PLATO's expected planet yield offering a promising opportunity to help unveil its morphology.
title: The Neptunian ridge through the lens of TESS

summary: One way to compare two graphs $G_1, G_2$ is to check whether there is some graph $H$ in a graph class $\mathcal{H}$, such that the number of homomorphisms from $H$ to $G_1$ is not equal to that from $H$ to $G_2$. This is the field of homomorphism distinguishability which has gained a lot of traction in recent years. In this paper, we study the case where $\mathcal{H}$ is the class of graphs of treewidth $k$. This has connections to important concepts in logic, machine learning, combinatorial optimization and proof complexity. In particular, Dvořák showed that $G_1$ and $G_2$ can be distinguished by a homomorphism count from a graph of treewidth $k$ iff $G_1$ and $G_2$ are distinguishable by the $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm. While the relation between the iteration number of this algorithm and the depth of the tree-decomposition of a distinguishing graph is understood, our understanding of the \emph{size} of $H$ is limited. We show a $2^{Ω(n^{k/2})}$ lower bound on the size of a graph of treewidth $k$ required to distinguish two graphs of order $n$. This bound is proved via a new combinatorial game along with a construction which uses a recent compression technique for CFI graphs. It is almost tight to the known $2^{O(n^{k+1})}$ upper bound and is an exponential improvement on the previous best known lower bound.
title: An Almost-tight Size Lower Bound for Bounded Treewidth Homomorphism-Distinguishability

summary: We derive the black-hole endpoint from the finite-support causal-chain framework of Papers I–II and the extended-tetrad gravity sector of Paper III. A horizon is the local saturation surface of the chain, n(r_H) = n⋆, N_local(n⋆) = 0, e^(4i)_μν(r_H) = 0. Radial conformal transport through the horizon extinguishes and the would-be interior projector vanishes, Π_in = 0, and hence H_in := Ran Π_in = {0}. Evaporation is governed not by this local extinction factor but by the exterior channel transmissivity N_chan(M) = 1 − M_SB/M; Ṁ_th⁽⁰⁾ = −[1/(15360πM²)]N_chan(M)⁴. Here the superscript (0) denotes the stationary, leading-adiabatic coefficient. The thermal coefficient follows from exterior boost temperature, horizon area, two radiative polarizations, and the universal bosonic phase-space integral. The entropy is the scalar support capacity of the saturated membrane, S_H = A/(4ℓ_P²), with the factor 1/4 fixed by scalar projection through the four-component carrier. Information is preserved on the supported radiation–membrane Hilbert space, and the Page result is the exact capacity envelope rather than evolution into an interior. At leading adiabatic order, the exterior branch approaches r_H = ℓ_SB, the thermal channel closes, and Bondi/ADM balance fixes M_grav^final = M_SB. The endpoint is therefore a fixed-mass, bounded-memory relic, not complete evaporation, not information loss, and not a progenitor-scaling entropy remnant.
title: Causal Chain Physics IV: Black Holes Without Interiors, Incomplete Evaporation, and the Cosmic Time Boundary

summary: We construct a finite-support quantum theory of gravity from a discrete causal spin chain and three axioms, without taking spacetime, a metric, or classical geometry as microscopic inputs. The fundamental degrees of freedom are operator-valued, and causal composition closes under an extended SO(5,1) algebra. Algebraic localization introduces parallel index structures and fixes four-indexed extended tetrads as identification maps. Localizing the first-order transport already generated by causal composition on that carrier fixes the covariant derivative without an independent connection, and its commutator defines curvature. The quadratic invariant F² separates an intrinsic algebraic curvature, giving the time-dependent scalar Λ(t), from the sectors that yield the Einstein–Hilbert and Euler terms after symmetry breaking. A derived Higgs-like transition then produces ordinary tetrad geometry and General Relativity. With the inherited chain normalization, it gives the a priori dimensionless result μ_SB/M_P = 5/(16√11), with no fitted threshold; conversion to GeV uses the measured Planck scale. The broken phase has a finite physical mode sector whose spin-2 excitations are collective tetrad fluctuations rather than fundamental spacetime quanta. The Supplement proves finiteness of the physical one-loop tetrad self-energy and each fixed graph, gives constructive finite-matrix definitions of the physical spectrum and all projected vertices, and proves exact unitary evolution on the invariant terminal-occupancy space. Numerical diagonalization, evaluation of infrared loop residuals, and convergence of any auxiliary continuum/decompactification diagrammatic reorganization remain open. Geometry and spacetime are therefore derived concepts in a finite-support, background-independent gravitational construction.
title: Causal Chain Physics III: Emergence of Spacetime and Exact Finite-Support Quantum Gravity

summary: We show that a pre-geometric axiom set generates structures normally assumed in relativistic physics. The microscopic input is a closed, bi-infinite ordered history of binary choices; coarse-grained histories use local binary projectors and a decoherence functional; amplitudes compose unitarily between nearest-neighbor sites. No spacetime manifold, metric, connection, Lorentz group, or action principle is assumed. Four independent binary-projector implementations furnish {I, P, T, PT}. Their faithful amplitude realization forces a four-component complex carrier; unresolved crossing order with antiunitary reversal yields Grassmann history variables. The coherent-state functional integral is primary, not the quantization of a prior classical field theory. Bilinear closure gives the unique local noncompact algebra SO(4,1), while coarse-grained spin sums generate the collective SO(5,1) sector, whose infrared İnönü–Wigner contraction yields the Poincaré group. Local spinors, Clifford closure, transport generators, and Poincaré invariance thus arise from causal composition rather than background symmetry. The same representation supplies the homogeneous cosmological limit. The compact orbital sector of the Hilbert space representation has no preferred position or direction, giving the cosmological principle; its infrared contraction fixes spatial flatness. Coherence loss in the resulting shell ensemble defines entropy, a thermodynamic arrow, and Gibbs temperature. The noncompact radial sector supplies the timelike support depth for homogeneous vacuum curvature. Inverse square scaling of this depth gives Λ(t) ∝ t⁻² before saturation. Summed-history interference stops opening new resolved radial sectors at log₁₀ n⋆ = 60.3884215, saturating the timelike curvature radius. The late-time floor is Λ⋆ = 13/(64 n⋆²ℓ_P²) = 1.30 × 10⁻⁵² m⁻², the asymptotic cosmological constant.
title: Causal Chain Physics I: Causal Discreteness, Poincaré Invariance and Cosmological Vacuum Curvature

summary: We derive the bosonic sector of the causal-chain framework. Gauge and scalar fields are not primitive continuum fields; they arise from closed double-loop spinor bilinears and enter the Minkowski-limit scalar-completed branch connection. The propagating gauge algebra is the rank-five left-right algebra SU(3)_C ⊗ SU(2)_L ⊗ SU(2)_R ⊗ U(1)_(B−L), while the scalar-completed branch connection carries sixteen active branch channels, 8_C + 3_L + 3_R + 1_L + 1_R = 16, because the single B−L line appears on both causal branches. Thus the two abelian entries are branch coefficients of one generator, not two independent U(1) groups. The ultraviolet organization is the SO(10) bilinear envelope of the sixteen-state fermion carrier; the propagating algebra is selected by closed-loop branch propagation. The universal closure normalization is g⋆ = g′⋆ = 0.500 at the Paper III scale μ_U ≡ μ_SB = 1.15035058 × 10¹⁸ GeV. After branch-normalization conversion, the three measured gauge directions of the upward scalar-completed RG check return to this same closure window, while downward running gives percent-level weak-scale gauge extractions. The continuum branch-kernel roots are v_R = 4016.1085 GeV, v_L = 260.8335 GeV, thresholds rather than benchmark right-sector pole masses. The stopped detector-current quotient annihilates the orthogonal right-vector exchange kernel below the right opening and therefore fixes the low-energy overlap to ε_R(0) = 0. Above μ_R,EW^PW = 3.9230019 TeV the pre-quotient right currents and actual W_R, Z_R gauge bosons are active, predicting a positive high-energy scattering threshold. The correlated cosmological signature is ΔN_eff^(ν_R) = 0.138439, or N_eff^right = 3.182439. The scalar-color channel also yields an even 203.6 GeV response pole and a stable odd composite with mass M_X = 3.92 TeV, derived downstream in Paper XI.
title: Causal Chain Physics VI: Emergence of Bosons, Planck Scale Coupling Convergence and Dynamical Electroweak Symmetry Breaking

summary: The Sundarbans mangrove system constitutes a globally consequential blue carbon sink, yet vertically resolved soil organic carbon (SOC) inventories, particularly at depth, remain under-constrained. This study deployed a geospatial deep-learning pipeline integrating multi-source Earth observation data (optical, SAR, and DEM-derived covariates) to spatially upscale SOC stocks to 1 m depth across the Bangladesh Sundarbans. Stratified coring across five sites positioned along the salinity–tidal inundation gradient to represent four major vegetation zones (n = 25; one pit per site × five depth intervals: 0–20, 20–40, 40–60, 60–80, 80–100 cm) captured physicochemical and SOC attributions. A Kruskal–Wallis test confirmed a positive SOC gradient with depth (H = 21.7, df = 4, p < 0.001); post-hoc Dunn’s pairwise comparisons showed 60–100 cm layers differed significantly from all shallower layers (p < 0.01, Bonferroni-adjusted), with the dominant pool residing below 40 cm, implying systematic underestimation by conventional shallow-core (<30–40 cm) assessments. To partition total ecosystem carbon and establish soil-pool dominance, above- and belowground biomass were parameterized using species-specific allometric equations, revealing high stem density but comparatively low basal area consistent with a regenerating stand structure dominated by Heritiera fomes and Sonneratia apetala. Analysis of a previously published Landsat-derived mangrove record (1988–2022) revealed net contraction in mangrove extent; loss-agent raster attribution, based on shoreline-proximity buffers, land-cover transition sequences and cyclone-track coincidence, identified chronic tidal abrasion and erosion as the primary driver rather than anthropogenic conversion or cyclonic disturbance. Benchmarking against a previously published global 30 m machine-learning SOC product revealed a 4.2-fold underestimation of SOC stocks in the Bangladesh Sundarbans, particularly in peat-enriched, anoxic substrata. Assimilation of deep-profile in situ observations with the pipeline significantly improves spatial prediction fidelity and establishes a robust baseline for Measurement, Reporting, and Verification for greenhouse gas inventories, highlighting the necessity of incorporating deep-soil carbon pools for inventorizing erosion-vulnerable seaward margins.
title: Blue Carbon Stock Mapping of the Sundarbans Mangrove Ecosystem, Bangladesh (2000–2025): A Hybrid GeoAI Ensemble Framework

summary: Diversity-Plankton.R README: Functional Diversity Analyses in Synechococcus Communities Under Environmental Stress Overview This repository contains the final analyses used in the manuscript examining how functional diversity influences the growth, recovery, and temporal dynamics of experimental Synechococcus communities exposed to environmental stressors. The script quantifies relationships between both initial functional diversity (before stress exposure) and assembled functional diversity (after community assembly) with ecological responses including community growth, recovery, and changes in functional diversity through time. All analyses presented in the main text and supplementary materials are generated from this workflow. Study Objective The analyses test whether variation in functional diversity predicts the performance and resilience of microbial communities under four environmental treatments: Control Atrazine Heating Heating + Atrazine Specifically, the script evaluates whether: Initial functional diversity promotes community growth during the disturbance phase. Assembled functional diversity promotes recovery following disturbance. Functional diversity changes in response to environmental stress. The strength and direction of functional diversity effects depend on species richness and treatment context. Input Data Required files File Description all-data-with-diversity.rds Full experimental dataset containing strain composition, species composition, trait information, and functional diversity metrics across all sampling days (0–20). all-data-with-diversity-normalised.rds Normalized functional diversity dataset (Hill diversity, q = 2) restricted to experimental sampling days used for analyses. trait-summary.rds Trait-space boundaries and summary statistics used for trait visualizations. Data Processing Analyses focus on sampling days: Day 0 (pre-disturbance) Day 10 (end of disturbance phase) Day 20 (post-disturbance recovery phase) The script derives: Response variables Community growth Log-response ratio between Day 0 and Day 10 abundance: Growth = log(N10 / N0) Community recovery Log-response ratio between Day 10 and Day 20 abundance: Recovery = log(N20 / N10) Functional diversity change Change in functional diversity during disturbance: FD change = log(FD10 / FD0) Functional diversity recovery Change in functional diversity during recovery: FD recovery = log(FD20 / FD10) Community composition variables species_richness — number of species in each community strain_richness — number of strains in each community Both variables are parsed directly from species and strain composition identifiers. Statistical Analyses Four generalized least-squares (GLS) models are fitted using the nlme package. To account for treatment-specific heteroscedasticity, all models include a varIdent variance structure. Model 1: Community Growth Response: Growth Primary predictor: Initial functional diversity (diversity_0) Model 2: Community Recovery Response: Recovery Primary predictor: Assembled functional diversity (diversity_10) Model 3: Functional Diversity Change Response: FD change Primary predictor: Initial functional diversity (diversity_0) Model 4: Functional Diversity Recovery Response: FD recovery Primary predictor: Post-stress functional diversity (diversity_10) Model Structure All models include: diversity * species_richness * treatment + strain_richness where: Functional diversity is the focal predictor. Species richness modifies diversity effects. Treatment represents environmental stress context. Strain richness is included as an additive covariate. Outputs Main Text Output Description figures/fig1_trait_medians.png Median trait values for all strains and species. figures/fig2_fd_slopes.png Treatment-specific functional diversity effect sizes and confidence intervals. figures/fig3_fd_trajectories.png Functional diversity trajectories through time across treatments and diversity levels. tables/table2.xlsx T
title: Functional, interspecific, and intraspecific diversity jointly shape growth and recovery of Synechococcus communities under environmental stress

summary: Version 1.02, 3 November 2026. Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020) estimate that one additional industrial robot per thousand workers lowers a U.S. local labor market's employment-to-population ratio by 0.39 percentage points and its hourly wages by about 0.77 percent. Rebuilding their design from raw IPUMS, IFR, and EU KLEMS data, I reproduce these estimates bit-exactly. I then ask what conventional robustness checks leave open: which industries, places, periods, and shocks actually identify the estimate? The regression spans 722 commuting zones and 19 industries, but the variation behind an instrumental-variable estimate can be far narrower. The sign is robust; the support is narrow. Negative estimates persist across conventional specification changes, 60 strong European instrument windows, alternative U.S. treatment windows, and the published periods through 2014. Yet automotive carries about 84 percent of normalized absolute Rotemberg-weight mass, and automotive exposure in six Rust Belt states supplies 95 percent of the net first-stage covariance. Without automotive, the remaining 18 industry shocks do not strongly predict U.S. robot exposure. Longer horizons, later start years, and adding Germany to the instrument all strengthen it through the same margin. The automotive component shows no detectable relation to 1970–1990 employment and wage changes, and a direct effect of the instrument would have to absorb 72 percent of the reduced form before conventional significance disappears. Inference is weaker than the regional first stage suggests. With 19 underlying industry shocks, exposure-robust first-stage F-statistics are 6.2 and 6.3 rather than 34, small-sample Anderson–Rubin tests do not reject a zero effect ( p = 0.059, 0.063), and other implementations of the same test disagree; in known-truth simulations, nominal 95-percent state-clustered intervals cover in only 60–66 percent of replications. Measurement assumptions also bind. In the original penetration metric, perpetual-inventory robot capital preserves the estimates at 5 percent depreciation, but faster assumed depreciation counts the automotive installations behind the first stage as replacement rather than net additions, eliminating shock-level relevance at 10 percent and all relevance at 15 percent. The benchmark is reproducible and robust in sign, but it is identified from an automotive margin in historically industrial labor markets; that margin defines its scope and the concrete content of its exclusion restriction. More generally, coefficient robustness and breadth of identifying support are distinct properties that shift-share studies should report separately. JEL Codes: J23, J24, O33, R23, C18, C26 Keywords: Industrial robots; automation; replication; shift-share IV; Bartik instruments; Rotemberg weights; identifying support; weak-instrument-robust inference; Anderson–Rubin; plausibly exogenous; perpetual inventory; robot capital; local labor markets
title: Robots and Jobs Revisited: A Bit-Exact Replication, Shift-Share Anatomy, and Capital-Stock Extension of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020)

summary: We ask whether the folded Causal Chain Physics continuum admits a traversable spacelike channel and, if not, whether matter can move onto new constituents without scanning and reconstruction. The first answer is negative. One radial ladder ends at one boundary, spacetime is the image of one extended-tetrad map, and a black-hole horizon is a local pullback of that boundary. With no second exterior or earlier carrier edge, the no-channel theorem excludes traversable wormholes, metric shortcuts, baby-universe branches, and topology-changing escape channels. A fold-symmetric black hole may occur as initial data but remains terminal in both temporal orientations. The same principle gives the positive result. Orbital recurrence can repeat an informational type, but not a physical token, whose identity follows one continuous supported map. On Paper III's finite physical sector, an exact transporter preserves every reference correlation while returning the source and carrier to a fixed blank. Local, state-independent exchanges can therefore move the protected organization without cloning or a hidden blueprint, subject to explicit capacity and latency bounds. Unlike measure-and-prepare reconstruction, standard teleportation preserves an unknown state using entanglement, a Bell record, and causal feed-forward. Direct translocation uses no measurement record or remote conditional operation: the output continues the same supported map on different constituents. Proposed tests move a reference-entangled molecular qubit through an exchange chain and a coherent bond-form through dissociation, photonic transduction, and reassociation; a superconducting precursor tests the same clean-reset condition. These are causal tests, not faster-than-light transport.
title: Causal Chain Physics XII: No Traversable Wormholes and Causal Form Translocation—Spacelike No-Go, Orbital Recurrence, and Physical Identity

summary: We derive the baryon, active-lepton, and dark-matter inventory of one scalar-completed electroweak event. The CCF covariant derivative creates the first-order wall and its chiral source; bounded-support Parisi–Wu (PW) and continuum transport are two resolutions of that source, while the weak anomaly converts the left-handed bias into baryon and lepton number. The fixed-root PW calculation gives η_B,1^PW = 5.26082 × 10⁻¹⁰; the matrix-resolved continuum reconstruction gives 5.13315 × 10⁻¹⁰. Their computed hard-scale response defines the non-Gaussian theory-resolution interval η_B = 5.26 (+0.30, −0.40) × 10⁻¹⁰, which contains the independent Paper II baryon-loading range (5.37–5.48) × 10⁻¹⁰. The same event produces the flavor-scalar active source L_ν = 4.022200 × 10⁻² (1, 1, 1) and ξ = 5.87649332 × 10⁻² (1, 1, 1). An equal right-handed counterasymmetry makes this a chiral separation rather than net lepton-number creation. On the Paper II background its direct weak-rate map gives Y_P^weak = 0.24527; counting the right and active radiation once gives Y_P^full = 0.24712. An exact reflection protects one odd closed-support scalar pole with J = 0 and M_X = 3.9230019 TeV + O(Λ_QCD). The allowed Φ_G^a B_i^a operator is a heavier transverse J = 1 excitation, not the ordinary static-source gluelump ground state. The Lorenz/support theorem gives the exact temporal-source identity J_(u,G) = 0, excluding a scalar-color Coulomb kernel and Sommerfeld ladder while retaining transverse color interactions. Deconfined freeze-out then yields Ω_X h² = 0.130 (+0.028, −0.015), overlapping the Paper II requirement 0.1230–0.1234 without a cosmological fit. This number is the abundance before the ordinary-QCD transition. The complete source, spin-ordering, and late-survival proofs are given in the Supplemental Material; post-transition finite-range scattering remains a separate connected-amplitude matching problem.
title: Causal Chain Physics XI: Baryogenesis, Active Leptogenesis, Scalar-Color Dark Matter, and Cosmological Matter Concordance

summary: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices. PlantVLM-Edge combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and on-device serving with an offline chat interface, allowing growers to ask open-ended questions and receive diagnoses, symptom explanations, and management guidance without cloud connectivity. The framework is backbone-agnostic: we validate it with two different VLM types with varying scale and architecture (Qwen3-VL-2B and LLaVA-1.5-7B), four quantization schemes, and two diagnostic domains (plant diseases and insect pests), and we deploy all variants on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Eight-bit quantization affects answer quality minimally relative to the full-precision model, and 4-bit activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ) retains 98.6% of full-precision answer quality on both domains while reducing the weight memory of the 2B backbone by 49%. In its most compact form, PlantVLM-Edge requires 2.01 GiB of weight memory, returns its first token in about 0.12 s, and completes a 64-token diagnostic response in 0.78 s. These results demonstrate that timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is practical on edge devices, providing a foundation for next-generation crop monitoring and decision support systems.
title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis

summary: Matrix multiplication dominates both PHY signal processing and Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference, yet these domains place opposing demands on the matrix engine. Signal processing requires low-latency execution of relatively small matrix operations, whereas DNN inference, particularly at large batch sizes, prioritizes high throughput and energy efficiency for large matrix multiplications. While offering efficient memory access profile, a Systolic Array (SA) adds fill and drain delays per matrix. Those can be amortized for large matrices but not for small matrices. Conversely, a tensor unit completes the kernel in few cycles but would require repeated reads of same operand tiles over large matrices. This makes SA too slow for signal processing and tensor too inefficient for AI. We show that this need not be a choice between systolic and tensor structuring of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units. We propose a single engine that operates primarily as a SA and, through low-cost reconfiguration, transforms into a tensor-style engine on a per-operation basis. MUXes create both the spatial reduction adder tree and temporal reduction accumulators from the existing MACs and registers within the systolic array. The proposed reconfigurable SA simulated using modified SCALESim simulator, verified on an Zynq 702 FPGA and synthesized using ASAP 7nm FinFET library. SCALE-Sim simulations shows up to 7.5x lower latency for small complex value PHY kernels. Even on DNN workloads, it achieves up to 1.65x speedups over vanilla SA execution with trivial increase of memory accesses, retaining the systolic array's memory access advantage. Synthesis results estimate reconfigurable fabric costs only 8% power and 13.6% area overheads.
title: A Cross-Domain Matrix Engine for Signal Processing and Deep Neural Net Inference

summary: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.
title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference

Crossed blinded feedback, hidden replay and synchronized ECG, EMG and posture controls challenge interpretation of subjective sensation as a distinct mechanism. Unidentifiable effects or consent failure halt claims. F83 QIGONG BREATHING AND HUMAN BIOELECTRIC REGULATION AT THE LIMIT — Compares qigong-labeled breathing with ordinary paced breathing under matched respiration, electrode geometry and motion. Masked rate matching and exchanged session labels test whether sweat activity, respiratory rhythms or contact impedance account for surface EDA/ECG differences. Uncontrolled artifact prohibits special-energy inference. F84 VOLITION, MIND-BODY UNITY AND INTELLIGENT NEUROFEEDBACK AT THE LIMIT — Challenges apparent intent-related information using live versus timestamp-matched replayed neurofeedback, yoked sham feedback and identical EEG bandwidth. Cross-validated information gains must survive face-EMG, breathing and expectancy controls. Label leakage, unsafe feedback or ignored human stop authority veto interpretation. F85 EXTERNAL QIGONG CLAIMS, CLASSICAL QI THEORY AND SCIENTIFIC FALSIFIABILITY AT THE LIMIT — Subjects alleged remote effects to sealed target schedules, signal isolation, independent randomization and double-blind instrument readings. Shams, shielded blanks and equal operator schedules confront electromagnetic, acoustic, thermal and experimenter leakage. Nonblind-only effects or selective exclusions trigger refusal; remote qi remains unestablished. SECOND RESEARCH UNIT / SOURCE FIDELITY & SUCCESSOR SCIENCE Research Unit II · F86–F90 / Knowledge, Causality & Continuity F86 CLASSICAL ACUPUNCTURE KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS AND TRUSTWORTHY MEDICAL AI AT THE LIMIT — Measures source-attribution error when classical manuscripts are converted into provenance-typed biomedical knowledge graphs. Blinded conflicting translations, swapped citations and out-of-era terms test edition drift and label leakage against a source-linked retrieval baseline. Unsupported upgrades from historical narration to medical fact must be rejected. F87 INTELLIGENT NANO-ACUPUNCTURE AND CLASSICAL ACUPOINT KNOWLEDGE INTEGRATION AT THE LIMIT — Compares sensing at predeclared classical points against anatomy-matched same-layer control locations. Concealed point/nonpoint coordinate substitutions confront contact geometry, skin thickness and mismatched historical annotations; independent anatomical registration is the comparator. No stable point-specific improvement or sensor integrity stops the claim. F88 AI CLOSED-LOOP ACUPUNCTURE AND CAUSAL VALIDATION OF CLASSICAL PATTERN MODELS AT THE LIMIT — Uses approved retrospective randomized data to ask whether classical pattern labels add transportable causal response information beyond symptom severity. Blinded rater disagreements and sham/reference contrasts challenge expectancy and confounding; common-support and sensitivity checks are mandatory. There is no authorized autonomous acupuncture intervention. F89 QUANTUM SENSING, NANO-ACUPUNCTURE AND CLASSICAL LIFE PHILOSOPHY AT THE LIMIT — Tests matched-resource readout precision using NV-diamond sensing and an optimized conventional instrument with identical distance, bandwidth, integration time and calibration standards. Blinded sensor swaps challenge photon-dose and geometry advantages. No reproducible independent precision gain, or claims of novel meridian energy, warrant refusal. F90 CLASSICAL ACUPUNCTURE PHILOSOPHY AND FUTURE INTELLIGENT BIOMEDICAL CIVILIZATION PLATFORMS AT THE LIMIT — Tests whether a successor laboratory can replay frozen accept/reject decisions after a hardware or software generation change. Concealed vendor-metadata swaps confront semantic lookalikes, circular citations and operator rescue. Human-readable provenance ledgers and FAIR archiving are baselines; lost source identity or human veto is a hard stop. Physical Scope, Falsifiability & Evidence Status The work is restricted to consented non-invasive observation, inert phantoms, passive instruments, approved historical datasets, document-based source analysis and offline simulation. No anatomical qi conduit, external qi transfer, mind-to-matter coupling, quantum physiological force or treatment efficacy is established. Sensor calibration, independent ground truth, blinded denominators, source provenance and human stop authority remain essential. Research lineage is the STARLI 90 Flagship Master v1.3, with source-provided methodological DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.23480803, 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318840.
