summary: Fusion Pilot Plants (FPPs) need control systems that survive diagnostic and actuator failures . We present DIII-D experiments  validating real-time, ML-enabled controllers in FPP-relevant scenarios under both imposed diagnostic dropouts and real in-shot hardware failures. Conventional equilibrium reconstruction fails when key diagnostics drop out. Our ML-based RTCAKENN recovers plasma profiles under simulated failures of Thomson Scattering (TS), Charge Exchange Recombination (CER), and Motional Stark Effect (MSE) and maintains accuracies above 90%. ECHO, a fault-robust ML controller, coordinates electron cyclotron heating (ECH) by reallocating gyrotron power s and steering across surviving gyrotrons when units fail mid-shot. In a Hybrid scenario with real ECH dropouts, we mitigated heavy-Z impurity accumulation (argon proxy) using core ECH power tracking a real-time ML radiated-power (Bolo-NN) model for pumpout , and Electron Cyclotron Current Drive (ECCD) steering onto the 3/2 tearing mode for MHD amplitude control. Coordinated ML-controlled gyrotron power adjustments (>0.5MW) avoided argon accumulation and MHD-induced confinement collapse. We also accessed Resonant Magnetic Perturbation (RMP) Edge Localized Mode (ELM)-suppressed plasmas at reduced RMP coil current where large sawteeth would otherwise break ELM suppression. The approach was to reduce sawtooth magnitude (and increase frequency) by holding ECCD inside q=1. Control held through the same TS dropouts and ECH failures, with RTCAKENN providing q=1 localization while ECHO maintained aiming. These first-of-a-kind results show integrated ML-enabled fault-tolerant control sustaining FPP-relevant operating points through imposed and unscripted failures, foundational for resilient burning-plasma control.
title: ML-Enabled Fault Resistant Plasma Control on DIII-D

summary: This paper proposes the Zero Principle as a philosophical and ontological framework for understanding transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution, and the emergence of new possibilities. The central proposition is that Zero (0) should not be understood merely as mathematical nothingness . Within this framework, Zero represents an open conceptual state in which an existing form loses its claim to finality, allowing another possibility, meaning, direction, or form to emerge. The proposed structural cycle is: Form → Dissolution → 0 → Possibility → New Form At the level of human experience, the corresponding process is: Impulse → Witness → Insight → Transformation → New Direction The paper further introduces a Zero-Level Sutra : Word ≠ Truth Word → Sign → Understanding → Beyond Word → 0 The sutra proposes that words, names, colors, forms, and concepts should not automatically be treated as ultimate reality. Different philosophical traditions may use different terms—such as Brahman, Śūnyatā, Nirvāṇa, Neti-Neti, Witness, Silence, Tao, and Fana —but Vedanta 2.0 does not claim that these concepts are identical. Instead, it explores whether they can be comparatively examined at a “zero-level,” where conceptual definitions reach their limits. The paper also examines the relationship between witnessing and transformation, proposing that conscious observation can create a space between stimulus and automatic reaction. The framework is applied metaphorically to failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal, and symbolic interpretations of Diwali. The paper does not present the Zero Principle as an established scientific law. It is presented as an evolving philosophical hypothesis and conceptual framework within the broader Vedanta 2.0 project.   हिंदी यह शोध-पत्र शून्य सिद्धांत (Zero Principle) को transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution तथा new possibilities के emergence को समझने के लिए एक दार्शनिक और ontological framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है। इसका केंद्रीय प्रस्ताव यह है कि Zero (0) को केवल mathematical nothingness के रूप में नहीं समझना चाहिए । इस framework में Zero ऐसी खुली conceptual अवस्था का प्रतीक है जहाँ कोई existing form अपनी अंतिमता का दावा खो देता है और दूसरी possibility, meaning, direction या form के emergence की संभावना खुलती है। प्रस्तावित संरचनात्मक चक्र है: रूप → विसर्जन → 0 → संभावना → नया रूप मानवीय अनुभव के स्तर पर: आवेग → दृष्टा → अंतर्दृष्टि → रूपांतरण → नई दिशा Paper में एक Zero-Level Sutra भी प्रस्तावित किया गया है: शब्द ≠ सत्य शब्द → संकेत → बोध → शब्दातीत → 0 इस सूत्र का आशय है कि शब्द, नाम, रंग, रूप और अवधारणाएँ स्वयं अंतिम सत्य को सिद्ध नहीं करतीं। विभिन्न दार्शनिक परंपराएँ ब्रह्म, शून्यता, निर्वाण, नेति-नेति, दृष्टा, मौन, ताओ और फ़ना जैसे अलग-अलग शब्दों का प्रयोग करती हैं। Vedanta 2.0 यह दावा नहीं करता कि ये सभी अवधारणाएँ समान हैं; बल्कि यह जाँचता है कि क्या इन्हें एक “zero-level” पर तुलनात्मक रूप से देखा जा सकता है, जहाँ conceptual definitions अपनी सीमा तक पहुँचती हैं। Paper witnessing और transformation के संबंध का भी अध्ययन करता है तथा यह प्रस्तावित करता है कि conscious observation stimulus और automatic reaction के बीच एक space उत्पन्न कर सकती है। यह framework failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal तथा Diwali के symbolic interpretation जैसे विषयों पर भी लागू किया गया है। यह paper Zero Principle को established scientific law के रूप में प्रस्तुत नहीं करता । इसे व्यापक Vedanta 2.0 framework के भीतर एक evolving philosophical hypothesis और conceptual framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है।
title: The Zero Principle: Witnessing, Dissolution, Transformation, and New Possibility / Hindi- शून्य सिद्धांत: दृष्टा, विसर्जन, रूपांतरण और नई संभावना

summary: Background: : Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important concern in clinical practice and can lead to treatment failure, hospitalization and increased healthcare costs. Genetic variations among individuals can influence drug-metabolizing enzymes, transport proteins and drug targets, resulting in differences in drug response and susceptibility to toxicity. Pharmacogenomics (PGx) provides an approach to understanding these genetic differences and supporting personalized drug therapy. Objective: To systematically evaluate the role of pharmacogenomics in predicting and preventing adverse drug reactions, with particular emphasis on clinically relevant gene–drug interactions and pharmacogenomics-guided treatment outcomes. Methods: : A systematic literature review will be conducted using databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library. Relevant studies will be identified using keywords such as pharmacogenomics, pharmacogenetics, adverse drug reactions, genetic polymorphism, drug toxicity and personalized medicine. Studies investigating associations between genetic variations, medication-related adverse reactions and genotype-guided prescribing will be considered. Study selection and reporting will follow PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Expected results: The review is expected to identify clinically important gene–drug associations, evaluate the evidence supporting pharmacogenomics-guided prescribing and examine its potential to reduce medication-related toxicity. It will also explore challenges associated with implementing pharmacogenomic testing in routine clinical practice. Conclusion: : Pharmacogenomics has the potential to improve medication safety by identifying individuals at increased risk of specific adverse drug reactions. Its effective implementation requires reliable genetic testing, clinical interpretation, healthcare professional education and accessible prescribing guidelines.
title: Role of Pharmacogenomics in Predicting and Preventing Adverse Drug Reactions: A Systematic Review of Gene–Drug Interactions and Clinical Outcomes

summary: A sixth-generation (6G) mobile network must share the radio resources of each base station among services with different requirements for delay, throughput, and energy use. Radio access network (RAN) slicing addresses this problem by allocating radio resources among logically separated services, and increasingly autonomous controllers are proposed to manage these allocations. Two proposed enhancements are a learned meta-agent that adjusts the controller’s configuration and a quantum optimizer for difficult discrete allocation decisions. Here we examine when these enhancements add value beyond strong classical controls using SHARP, a safety-preserving multi-cell RAN slicing controller whose per-slot capacity constraint is enforced independently of the added optimization layers. The meta-agent is evaluated against the best static parameter setting and the controller’s built-in adaptation. Its learned policy selects the same value in every observed state, so in deployment it coincides with a fixed setting (V = 3) and does not outperform the best static setting; its role is to locate that setting without a manual sweep. Relative to the default setting inherited from the host study, the located setting improves slot-level power-budget compliance by five to ten percentage points during constrained regimes at a one to two percent goodput cost, while the controller’s Lyapunov virtual queue already provides long-run adaptation of the power constraint. For the discrete allocation problem, plain QAOA does not outperform the classical baselines. Warm-started QAOA with a rotated mixer shows improvement only in the rugged regime evaluated here: it incurs no observed losses to the greedy seed in 48 comparisons and strictly improves six of 16 instances under the IBM-Heron-calibrated noise model, increasing normalized frame utility from 0.927 to 0.941. This gain is measured in frame utility rather than delivered goodput, and its attribution to quantum sampling remains unresolved because a matched classical seeded-perturbation control is not included. The greedy solution remains the fallback when the quantum device does not return within the planning deadline. We therefore formulate a controllerspecific break-even condition relating the expected utility gain, device availability, and quantum-dispatch cost, and derive the corresponding hardware requirements. All results are simulation outputs; no quantum hardware is executed and no quantum advantage is claimed.
title: Bounding the benefit of agentic meta-adaptation and quantum-assisted optimization for safe multi-cell 6G radio access network slicing

summary: Higgs-pair production through gluon fusion is sensitive both to the Higgs self-coupling and to additional scalars exchanged in the s channel. We compute gg → hh at leading order in QCD in the CP-conserving two-Higgs-doublet model with Yukawa alignment (A2HDM), keeping the full top-quark mass dependence and every interference term among the box, the light-Higgs triangle and the heavy-scalar triangle. Previous A2HDM studies of heavy scalars decaying to Higgs pairs used the narrow-width approximation. We contrast two benchmark points. When the heavy scalar H decouples from the top-quark loop, the modified couplings of h weaken the destructive box–triangle interference, and the 13 TeV cross section rises to 1.27 times the Standard Model value without any resonance. For m_H = 300 GeV, below the ttbar threshold, the cross section reaches 3.69 times the Standard Model value; interference with the continuum changes the integrated resonant contribution by only about 4%, but turns the parton-level m_hh distribution into a peak–dip structure. The two mechanisms are therefore separated by the shapes of the m_hh and p_T spectra rather than by the rate. Both benchmarks are illustrative and satisfy a simplified set of theoretical and experimental constraints. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24029211
tags: Higgs pair production, two-Higgs-doublet model, gluon fusion, LHC
title: Interference and resonance effects in gluon-fusion Higgs-pair production in the Yukawa-aligned two-Higgs-doublet model

summary: Flagship 55/60 Can randomized or justified quasi-experimental intervention isolate the manufacturing effect from cell-lot, material and culture confounding? CAUSAL VERIFICATION AND COUNTERFACTUAL CONTROL IN NANOROBOT-ASSISTED REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates intervention-defined causal treatment contrast rather than observational association. Its scientific coupling is causal inference x microscale interventions x biological functional validation. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can randomized or justified quasi-experimental intervention isolate the manufacturing effect from cell-lot, material and culture confounding? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Randomize tool action within balanced chip batches, retain sham and medium-only controls, and repeat on a second platform. Strong comparators include correlational predictor, nonrandomized matched cohort and randomized sham manipulation. The central competing explanation is shared medium, selection, interference or time-dependent confounding. The noncompensatory stop rule is: negative controls exhibit the claimed effect or modest unmeasured confounding reverses it. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. Research Gate lexical differentiation is not proof of scientific originality. The PDF is English-only and a separate QA record states outstanding independent physics, biology and DOI verification. summary: This repository provides the data, Python scripts, numerical outputs, and reproducibility documentation supporting a methodological investigation of negative multifractal spectrum estimates in stochastic cascades and digital images. The study distinguishes formally negative annealed multifractal spectra, which can arise in stochastic cascade models, from negative finite-resolution estimates that may depend on measurement and preprocessing procedures. The repository includes: 1. Synthetic image datasets generated using hierarchical random maps (HRM), Fourier-based synthesis (FFT), midpoint displacement (MPD), and binary geometric constructions. 2. Numerical experiments investigating uniform background floors, noise, quantization, clipping, scale-window dependence, and grid-phase sensitivity. 3. Analyses of Dirichlet multiplicative cascades, including Genuine, Shuffled, and Decoy controls. 4. Multifractal estimates based on multiplier moments and Chhabra–Jensen procedures, together with whole-image bootstrap uncertainty estimates. 5. Auxiliary experiments concerning finite-ensemble histogram spectra and supersampling. 6. Scripts, CSV result tables, execution logs, and figure-reproduction materials. 7. A manuscript-to-data mapping file (MANUSCRIPT_MAP.csv), documentation, and SHA-256 checksums supporting traceability and integrity verification. The repository documents reproducibility checks, including the comparison of 180 baseline cases and the reproduction of two computational figures. These checks should not be interpreted as independent validation of every numerical experiment or as proof of universal estimator reliability. The results emphasize that formally negative multifractal spectra and negative estimates obtained from finite digital observations have distinct mathematical interpretations. In particular, negative estimated values do not imply negative Hausdorff dimensions. The dataset is independent of any specific journal submission and is intended to support transparent examination, replication, and further methodological research. summary: Dynamic Convex Onion Analysis of Global Armed Violence (1989–2025): C Software, 1,000 Permutation Tests and Cartographic Projection Audit This software and reproducibility package accompanies a computational-geometric investigation of geopolitical centrality based on the Uppsala Conflict Data Program Georeferenced Event Dataset (UCDP GED), version 26.1, covering the period 1989–2025. The study introduces a dynamic application of convex hull peeling (Convex Onion) to the spatial and temporal analysis of global armed violence. The method is grounded in the affine invariance of convex-layer membership and provides a hierarchical representation of spatial depth through successive convex hulls. Unlike conventional measures of centrality based on averages, distances, or event density, this approach examines the innermost geometric structure of the global distribution of recorded conflict locations. The dataset contains 358,130 events with day-level date precision , corresponding to 54,381 distinct geographical locations . The cumulative analysis identifies 1,134 convex layers in the final configuration. Software Components The archive includes four C-based computational components: Dynamic Convex Onion Analysis: Chronological construction and updating of nested convex hulls, enabling the identification and tracking of the innermost geometric core from 1989 to 2025. Monte Carlo Permutation Analysis: A reproducible experiment involving 1,000 random permutations of complete geographical coordinate pairs across fixed chronological event positions, assessing the relationship between historical event ordering and geometric-core trajectories. Interactive Geometric Visualization: Offline visualization of the evolution of the innermost core, including annual configurations and changes in its geographical position. Cartographic Projection Comparison: Comparative analysis of convex-layer structures using planar longitude–latitude coordinates and the nonlinear Mollweide equal-area projection. Principal Findings The 2025 analysis identifies an innermost geometric location in Ethiopia under the original coordinate representation, whereas the Mollweide projection produces a two-location innermost layer in Sudan. The permutation experiment demonstrates that chronological event ordering influences the historical trajectory of the geometric core, although all permutations preserve the same final spatial configuration when the complete set of locations remains unchanged. These findings illustrate the distinction between affine-invariant geometric structure and centrality that depends on nonlinear cartographic representation. Reproducibility and Scientific Scope The package contains the original C source code, Windows executables, execution scripts, input datasets, computational outputs, visualization files, and technical documentation. The archive supports independent inspection, methodological evaluation, replication, and further development of computational-geometric approaches to spatial conflict analysis. The identified geometric core should not be interpreted as the location of maximum conflict intensity, the greatest number of fatalities, or a causal centre of global geopolitical instability. It represents a mathematically defined form of spatial depth whose interpretation depends on the adopted geometrical representation. Associated Research The Cartographic Construction of Geopolitical Centrality: Affine-Invariant Convex Layers and Global Armed Violence, 1989–2025. Data Source Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED), version 26.1. The UCDP data are attributed to their original providers. Dataset licensing and software provenance are documented separately in the archive.
title: Convex Onion Geopolitical Centrality

summary: The digitalization of banking services in Nigeria has exponentially increased the incidences of electronic fraud (e-fraud) and the regulatory responses thereto, including the freezing of customers' accounts. While banks have a statutory and contractual duty to protect the financial system from fraud under the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA) 2020, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification Number (BVN), and various anti-money laundering directives, this duty often collides with the customer's constitutional right to property and the contractual duty of a banker to honour its customer's mandate. This article examines the legal basis and extent of a bank's liability for wrongful freezing of a customer's account and for losses arising from e-fraud. It interrogates the tension between a bank's duty of care, duty to obey regulatory directives, and its fiduciary obligations. Using doctrinal and analytical methodologies, the paper reviews some Nigerian case laws as well as CBN's Regulation on Instant Electronic Payments, the Cybercrimes Act 2015 (as amended), and the NDIC framework. The study finds that while banks enjoy qualified immunity when acting pursuant to a valid court order or clear CBN directive, indiscriminate freezing of accounts based on mere suspicion, internal PND (Post No Debit) without due process, or failure to deploy adequate cyber security measures amount to breach of contract and negligence, attracting damages. The paper advocates for a stricter liability regime, statutory timelines for account unfreezing, and mandatory compensation for wrongful freezing.
tags: Bank Liability, Wrongful Account Freezing, E-Fraud, Post No Debit (PND), Banker-Customer Relationship, Due Process, Digital Banking.
title: BANK LIABILITY FOR WRONGFUL ACCOUNT FREEZING AND E-FRAUD: ANY LEGAL REMEDY?

summary: The rational management of water resources and the control of hydroagricultural techniques in the Oued Souf area are complex and crucial to a harmonious and sustainable development. The Oued Souf area is presently facing the problem of upwelling from groundwater, which is harmful to cultures and homes. In order to minimize this problem, several aerated lagoon treatment plants were set up; this technique allows an efficient control of pollution due especially to the upwelling phenomenon. The aim of this study is to provide information about the efficiency and the management of an aerated lagoon treatment system at two plants of the Oued Souf area, the Hassani Abdelkrim and the Reguiba plants. The obtained results show that the removal efficiency of organic load is significant (greater than 50%), thus indicating that aerated lagoon system is well suited to arid areas. published by the   Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Sciences | JBES
title: Treatment of domestic and agricultural water by natural lagoon system in arid areas, case of Oued Souf, Algeria

summary: Abstract This document gives a technical and functional description of Algorithmic Logic Fingerprints (ALF): a way to verify that an AI model or algorithm in production still makes the decisions that were reviewed and approved, and to stop its output from taking effect if it does not. The problem. Current AI trust mechanisms prove identity and origin, not behaviour: Model signing (OpenSSF Model Signing, led by Google, NVIDIA and HiddenLayer; NVIDIA NGC signed models) proves which file a model is. Attestation and transparency logs (for example Apple Private Cloud Compute) prove which software a server runs. Neither shows what the model actually decides. A model can be fine-tuned, quantised, wrapped in a prompt or proxy layer, or replaced behind the same name or signature, and an AI agent can act on its output before anyone notices. How it works. Fingerprint generation. A compact cryptographic fingerprint of decision behaviour is created without access to source code, model weights or training data. For machine-learning models it is built by sampling decision boundaries. For rule-based or traditional code it is built from normalised control-flow and decision structure. Sealed-probe verification. In the highest-assurance mode, the model is tested with a sealed set of inputs that the computing system cannot see in advance. Four views must match together: decision boundaries, monotonicity and consistency, constraint activation, and constraint topology. A different model wrapped to imitate the approved one cannot pass all four. Approved-fingerprint registry. Each approved model or algorithm version has a reference fingerprint that can be checked at any time. Run-time check at the point of effect. Inside a trusted execution environment (for example a confidential VM or a confidential GPU), the live fingerprint is compared with the approved one after computation finishes and before the output is used. Fail-closed enforcement. If the fingerprint does not match, approval is automatically invalidated and the output is withheld. The capability needed to act (send, pay, move, transmit) is not released. Validation receipts. Each decision produces a tamper-evident receipt anchored in a ledger, for audit and incident analysis. Where it applies. The same mechanism applies to AI agents and model-serving platforms, payment and digital-currency systems (including offline wallets), vehicles and robots, and satellites. It complements existing technology rather than replacing it: model signing and model registries (NVIDIA NGC, Google Kaggle); verifiable and confidential AI clouds (Apple Private Cloud Compute, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, AWS, and NVIDIA, Intel and AMD confidential hardware); agent platforms (Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services); payment flows (Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Ant Group); vehicle software governance under UN Regulation 156; Chinese AI platforms (Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance, Tencent, Huawei, Zhipu AI). It also gives a technical signal for the EU AI Act's substantial-modification rule and for China's generative AI filing regime, both of which depend on knowing whether the deployed system is the one that was assessed. summary: This article examines a method for developing students' chemical language through digital storytelling. The proposed methodological solution involves a sequence of activities in which students not only create a digital story but also translate the content of a chemical phenomenon from its observed form into a verbal explanation, a microcosm model, and a symbolic notation. The method includes setting up a chemical situation, identifying the linguistic core of the topic, a sequential description of the process, peer review of the scenario, creation of a digital story, and reverse transformation of the information. To evaluate the results, criteria for terminological and symbolic accuracy, understanding of the meaning of chemical notation, logical explanation, and coherence of chemical language are identified. The proposed approach can be used in studying exchange reactions, electrolytic dissociation, oxidation-reduction, and organic reactions.

summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export. The short-read counts at the two A2143 coordinates are reproduced from the archived alignment, whose header records the exact command and tool versions. What is not. The barrnap installation originally used on the analysis machine is missing a Perl module and does not run; the rRNA copy numbers were therefore archived values in earlier versions and are re-derived with barrnap 1.10.5 in this version. Three new scripts are included: the marker-control experiment (scripts 26 and 27), in which the single copy-differentiating base of the isolate was set to A in both copies, to C in both, to T in both, and exchanged between them, with the reads realigned to each control; and the structural diagnostic of the two 26695 23S copies (script 28), which reports that copy 1 contains no ambiguous base while copy 2 contains one N at genome position 1,475,696. DOI.txt now lists the version DOIs, and the data-availability sentence in the manuscript names the concept DOI rather than one version, so that it cannot point at a superseded record. summary: Vacuum is an absolutely static reference system. When light propagates in a vacuum, it moves in an absolutely static reference system. The propagation speed of light in a medium is a constant, which has nothing to do with the motion state of the light source, the observer or the receiver. When light propagates in a medium, it is dragged by the inertia of the medium. While light propagates in a vacuum, the vacuum is absolutely static, which cannot drag the light to move, and the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed. Based on this theory, a light interference experiment can be performed as proof, using a Michelson interferometer. The principle of the experiment is to split the laser into two beams of light at a half-reflecting mirror,one of which passes through a vacuum quartz tube and reaches the Mirror M1,The light reflects back from M1,Passing through a vacuum quartz tube,Project onto the screen through a half mirror; The other beam of light does not pass through the vacuum quartz tube,reaches the Mirror M2,The light reflects back from M2,Project onto the screen through a half mirror.however, both of the beams converge on the screen, forming interference fringes.Because the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed and the absolute motion of the earth will drive the vacuum quartz tube to move,when the absolute direction of the earth's motion and the direction of light propagation are parallel to each other,light will have an extra optical path in the tube; when they are perpendicular to each other, light will not have the extra optical path in the tube, so after the instrument has turned 90 degrees, the interference fringes will move. The key to this experiment is to create a vacuum. The structure of the experiment is simple that I hope someone could make an experimental verification. According to this theory, it can be concluded that the essence of Fizeau experiment , sagnac effect and Hoek experiment is the same. The reverse process of Fizeau experiment is sagnac effect, vice versa. According to this theory, the Fizeau experiment has a calculated result of movement at 0.236 fringes and a measured value at 0.23 fringes; in the case of Ruyong Wang's experiment "Generalized Sagnac Effect", the moving phase difference has a calculated result at 0.000251 and measured value at 0.000246 in the experiment. Obviously, this theory is more consistent with the experimental measurement results and the theoretical explanation is more real and natural. The sagnac effect, Mach-Zehnder interferometer and Michelson interferometer can all be used to conduct experiments based on this principle to verify whether there is an absolutely stationary reference system. Among them, the sagnac effect has the highest accuracy, the Mach-Zehnder interferometer the second and the Michelson interferometer the lowest. If Michelson and Morley had used a 11m-long vacuum quartz tube for the experiment, they might have observed a movement of 0.373 interference fringesand there might have no so-called "dark clouds". This experiment is actually to measure the sagnac effect of the Earth's rotation by using a Michelson interferometer.

summary: Objective. To assess cardiovascular functional reserve in men and identify the major phenotypes of exercise intolerance based on a comprehensive evaluation of clinical and instrumental parameters. Materials and Methods. At the first stage, 400 men without a previously established diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) were examined. One hundred participants with relevant symptoms, cardiovascular risk factors, and/or potential indicators of reduced functional reserve were selected for an in-depth assessment. The protocol included clinical evaluation, the six-minute walk test, exercise stress echocardiography, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing when corresponding data were available. Parameters of left ventricular diastolic function and global longitudinal strain, right ventricular function, chronotropic response, and gas exchange were analyzed. Functional stratification was performed according to predefined pathophysiological criteria. Results. Five functional phenotypes were identified: preserved functional reserve (21%), diastolic (17%), impaired right ventricular–pulmonary arterial coupling (15%), chronotropic (14%), and peripheral (33%). The phenotypes differed in exercise tolerance, changes in E/e′, TAPSE/SPAP ratios, heart rate response, and peak oxygen uptake. The lowest Peak VO₂ values were observed in the peripheral phenotype, whereas the most pronounced increase in E/e′ during exercise was observed in the diastolic phenotype. Conclusion. Comprehensive exercise-based assessment makes it possible to characterize the heterogeneity of functional limitations in the examined men and distinguish phenotypes associated with different presumed pathophysiological mechanisms. Further studies are required to establish the diagnostic and prognostic value of the proposed stratification approach.
tags: cardiovascular functional reserve; exercise tolerance; functional phenotypes; heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; stress echocardiography; six-minute walk test; cardiopulmonary exercise testing; diastolic function; chronotropic response; TAPSE/SPAP
title: FUNCTIONAL PHENOTYPES OF REDUCED EXERCISE TOLERANCE IN MEN: A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF CARDIOVASCULAR FUNCTIONAL RESERVE

summary: Biometric authentication has become a primary mechanism for accessing critical systems, from corporate facilities and banking applications to healthcare records and smart home devices. The term bio-key encompas ses both the use of physiological and behavioural traits as authentication keys and the hardware security tokens (FIDO2 keys) that integrate biometric sensors. Despite widespread adoption, there is no formal ontology that in tegrates the full bio-key authentication chain, namely enrollment, biometric capture, template storage, matching, decision, and access grant, with security assurance levels, privacy requirements, and governance mechanisms. This gap produces semantic interoperability failures, inconsistent security assessments, and weak auditability, especially when biometric templates are compromised or when authentication decisions are contested. The critical asymmetry is that biometric traits are irrevocable: unlike passwords, a com promised fingerprint or iris pattern cannot be reissued. Existing ontologies focus on biometric modalities in isolation or on hardware tokens, but none formally models the complete chain as a data governance and privacy problem. This doctoral project proposes two complementary contributions: (i) a formal ontology, built with the OntoView method, that describes bio-key authentication chains, their security levels, privacy constraints, and governance gates, serving as an instrument for interoperability, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance; and (ii) a verification method, based on the on tology, that specifies and evaluates biometric gates and audit requirements, with direct impact on privacy protection and social well-being. For high value targets, the ontology distinguishes single-party authentication from quorum-based authentication (M-of-N), in which M co-present custodians must each authenticate with their own bio-key and the access secret is split among N parties. The ontology and method will be validated by encoding reported cases, by expert evaluation, and by an empirical study on a si mulated multi-modal biometric testbed with scripted spoofing, replay, and collusion scenarios.
title: Ontology for Bio-Key Authentication: Modalities, Security Levels, Privacy, and Governance

summary: Executable analysis pipeline (Jupyter notebook for Kaggle) and complete results for a study on spectroscopic screening of food adulteration with a stated risk of false accusation. Seven chemometric and deep-learning classifiers (PLS-DA, SVM, random forest, ROCKET, 1D-CNN and a multitask 1D-CNN with and without Beer-Lambert mixup) are compared under grouped, repeated cross-validation. Their out-of-fold scores feed three conformal layers: (i) class-conditional (Mondrian) conformal triage into PASS, FLAG and REFER decisions, with an ablation against marginal calibration and an analysis of calibration size and deployment batch shift; (ii) cross-conformal detection of adulterants absent from training (DD-SIMCA, leave-one-adulterant-out, network embeddings) with Benjamini-Hochberg batch screening; and (iii) a leave-level-out audit for level-batch confounding whose threshold is calibrated by a semi-synthetic Beer-Lambert simulation built from real ATR-FTIR spectra. Four public datasets are analysed (NIR hyperspectral imaging of extra-virgin olive oil; ATR-FTIR of turmeric with wheat flour; MIR of strawberry purée; ATR-FTIR of edible oils); they are not redistributed here (see README for sources and licences). The archive contains the notebook with the outputs of the run reported in the article, all result tables (CSV), figures (PNG), a results summary, run logs and environment information.
title: Risk-controlled spectroscopic screening of food adulteration with conformal prediction: code and results

summary: The FBT spectral-capacity action is the heat trace of one specified geometric Dirac operator at fixed spectral resolution. This paper states its domain and trace hypotheses, exact first and second variations, stationarity tests, coupled relative-torus 4 + 2 expression, and complete finite-computation requirements. The current application uses the embeddingto-operator map already supplied by DCQ6 and FBT10D on the closed coherent product. No second source map is required. The degree-24 regular magnetic realization, its singular-end analysis and the separate torus numerical benchmark are removed from the main development. Their removal leaves the functional and the relative-torus geometry intact. The global line-extension obstruction is retained to explain this separation. The inherited twist, its closed domain and all metric, spin and connection variations are used together. Exact fibre integration preserves the full heat trace; the four-dimensional quadratic action and normal stability certificates are cited from FBT10D with their original scope. General spectral error bounds retain feedback through omitted modes and distinguish affine connection tests from nonlinear geometric families. A final ledger separates established results from resolution selection, balance-layer selection, full nonlinear control and real-time interpretation. This revision introduces no new numerical sign certificate or physical mass prediction.
title: FBT10A: The Spectral–Capacity Action of the Fracture–Berry–Tension Framework

summary: Description This dataset provides harmonised administrative and surveillance health data describing the epidemiology and health system burden of varicella (ICD-10: B01) and herpes zoster (ICD-10: B02) in Bulgaria during the period 2023–2025 . The analysed time window corresponds to the post-COVID-19 period and precedes the introduction of mandatory varicella vaccination (2026) , providing an important baseline for evaluating vaccination policies and monitoring changes in disease epidemiology. The dataset integrates aggregated information from several national administrative and surveillance systems: 1. National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) – hospital reimbursement through clinical pathways. 2. National Health Information System (NHIS) – national digital health infrastructure containing information on hospitalisations, outpatient medical examinations, and vaccination administration. 3. National Social Security Institute (NSSI) – sick leave records, sick leave duration, and compensation payments. 4. National Statistical Institute (NSI) – population denominators used for epidemiological rate calculations. National infectious disease surveillance system – mandatory reporting of infectious diseases according to Bulgarian public health legislation. All datasets are aggregated administrative records and contain no personally identifiable information . Data are aggregated at the regional (oblast) level and reported at monthly resolution , except for population denominators, which are annual. Regional names have been standardised to English transliterations , while the original Bulgarian names are preserved. All financial variables in this dataset are reported in Bulgarian lev (BGN) , which was the official currency of Bulgaria during the study period 2023–2025 . Bulgaria adopted the euro (EUR) in 2026 . However, the Bulgarian lev had long operated under a currency board arrangement with a fixed exchange rate to the euro . summary: The study aimed to optimize preoperative modeling and the individualized selection of surgical treatment for genital prolapse in women of childbearing age. Materials and methods: A retrospective-prospective descriptive comparative analysis of clinical and functional data from 85 fertile women (Group 1: n=45 with connective tissue dysplasia markers; Group 2: n=40 without manifest CTD) was conducted. Anatomical defects were quantified using the international POP-Q system, levator muscle tone was evaluated via perineometry and 3D/4D pelvic floor ultrasound, and systemic connective tissue dysplasia was assessed using clinical risk scores. Results: Standardized objective quantification using POP-Q, integration of obstetric history, levator defect scoring, and metabolic/CTD markers allowed for the development of a predictive mathematical risk matrix. Custom laparoscopic reconstructive techniques (pectopexy and laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy with autologous/mesh organ-preserving repair) yielded 95.6% 2-year anatomical success compared to 77.5% in standard vaginal repair. Conclusion: Personalized surgical strategies and preoperative modeling based on multiple functional, anatomic, and connective tissue parameters significantly improve long-term outcomes, preserve reproductive capacity, and minimize recurrence in fertile women with pelvic floor dysplasia

summary: Implementation Mechanisms for Tipiṭaka-Grounded AI Alignment — An Engineering Companion to Suffering-Cessation as Value Function This paper reads the Abhidhamma — the analytical third division of the Theravāda Buddhist canon — as a process specification of mind: typed, momentary mental events arising one at a time under twenty-four typed conditioning relations, with ethical class tracked per event and per position in a processing cycle. From that reading it derives a research program for AI alignment evaluation and intervention: a red-team taxonomy of mimicry failure modes, resting-state (minimal-context) evaluation of language models, an intervention-timing typology over a processing cycle, a typed causal vocabulary, the limits of interpretability by subtraction, paired entailment-and-denial consistency testing of alignment claims, and a positive competence taxonomy. It is the engineering companion to Suffering-Cessation as Value Function (Ly, 2026), which argues for the Theravāda Tipiṭaka as a substrate for autonomous-AI alignment, and it develops the canon's third basket — the Abhidhamma Piṭaka — at the layer where that paper's §6.6 left off: the layer of cognitive process itself. We make one framing claim and two structural contributions. The framing claim is the compilation thesis : the Abhidhamma is a substrate-neutral process-specification of mind, and each era that has received it has read it in the vocabulary for process it had to hand — the scholastic commentators' wheels of classification, the twentieth century's reading of it as a psychology, cognitive science's information processing, and computation for ours. The tradition itself reached for machine images again and again, each fitted to one lesson; computation is this era's addition. The claim defended here is not that the Abhidhamma secretly describes computers. It is that the computational reading is our era's compilation of a specification that has survived the earlier readings, and that this compilation's target can enact what it compiles rather than only describe it. Formal and computational readings exist (Barendregt 2006; Karunananda et al. 2015; Lou 2017); Takeuchi (2026) reads transformer self-attention as anattā and pursues alignment by subtraction; an agent grounded in the substrate is engineered toward enacting wholesome cognition rather than simulating it. No priority is claimed for that aim. The first structural contribution is the machine architecture (§4): the samsaric process rendered in four repaired mappings — (1) a conditioned machine with exactly one free variable, against the strictly deterministic reading the canon itself condemns in Makkhali Gosāla's fatalism; (2) citta as the instruction-cycle rather than the processor, with the 89/121 citta-typology as a shared instruction set, the mindstream ( santāna ) as the thread, and uniqueness residing in the execution trace; (3) the kammic continuity as an append-only linked ledger rather than a blockchain — no miners, no consensus, maximal privacy, immutable entries whose ripening remains context-dependent; and (4) the counter-gear : the dhamma-wheel that engages the samsaric wheel at its one free variable and unwinds the machine by fuel-withdrawal rather than force, terminating in kiriya -mode execution — action that leaves no kammic residue. The second structural contribution is the verification-suite reading (§5) of the analytical books: the Yamaka as bidirectional property-testing, the Vibhaṅga's interrogation method as schema validation, the Dhātukathā as inclusion-matrix consistency, and the Kathāvatthu as formal adversarial protocol — with the Kathāvatthu's opening controversy ( puggalakathā , the refutation of the person-entity) read as the canon pre-running, and settling, this paper's own central repair. title: The Wheel That Unwinds the Wheel: The Abhidhamma as Executable Process-Specification

summary: A six-gene mineralization-inhibitor score (ENPP1, ANKH, MGP, GGCX, VKORC1, NT5E) in CD90+ dermal fibroblasts reads lower in systemic sclerosis than in controls. The gene set, direction, detection floors and significance threshold were fixed before any expression value was read. In a pre-registered held-out set of 50 donors (25 and 25), the observed difference is -0.2939 at one-sided p = 0.0204. That replication is across platforms within one study (GSE195452), not across studies, and no ambient RNA correction was applied. The score did not replicate in an independent series. In GSE292979, the same frozen genes, direction, floors and threshold were applied under a pre-registration, and a blinded second implementation reproduced every donor score within 1e-6 before the result was unmasked. All four pre-registered contrasts were null (primary -0.0412, one-sided p 0.4955; minimum attainable p 0.0045). The paper offers no explanation for the null and does not claim the effect is absent. The score is a pre-specified composite, not a pathway readout: a leave-one-out shows the signal concentrated in VKORC1, GGCX and NT5E, and the paper makes no mechanistic claim. The osteogenic half of the original hypothesis did not clear its pre-registered detection floor in any dataset examined. This is not a study of calcinosis lesions, not evidence of specificity, and not a mechanism. It is a pre-registered result that held within one study and did not replicate in the one independent series tested, reported with both outcomes.
title: A pre-specified mineralization-inhibitor score separates systemic sclerosis fibroblasts within one study and does not replicate in an independent series

summary: Lectures and practical classes remain the core formats for teaching specialized subjects in medical and dental universities, yet their modernization is often guided by descriptive experience rather than by empirical evidence. This review aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness of contemporary lecture and practical-class formats and to propose evidence-informed criteria for selecting them in the teaching of specialized subjects. A narrative review of literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ERIC and Google Scholar was performed, prioritizing meta-analyses, systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Findings were interpreted through constructive alignment, cognitive load theory and Miller's pyramid of clinical competence. Across 225 studies, active learning increased examination performance by 0.47 standard deviations, and students taught by traditional lecturing were 1.5 times more likely to fail. In health professions education, the flipped classroom outperformed traditional teaching (SMD = 0.33); in dental education, problem-based, case-based, team-based and flipped formats together outperformed lecture-based learning (SMD = 0.48; 29 RCTs, 3,502 students). Technology-enhanced simulation was associated with large effects on knowledge and skills (effect sizes 1.09–1.20) compared with no intervention. However, the evidence shows high heterogeneity and focuses mainly on knowledge and learner satisfaction rather than clinical performance. Lectures and practical classes should be designed as a single aligned system in which the teaching format is selected according to the intended learning outcome and level of competence. Locally conducted controlled studies are needed to confirm these effects in medical universities of Uzbekistan.
title: MODERN FORMS OF TEACHING SPECIALIZED SUBJECTS IN MEDICAL AND DENTAL EDUCATION: AN EVIDENCE-BASED NARRATIVE REVIEW OF LECTURES AND PRACTICAL CLASSES

summary: This record provides the complete reproducibility package for the manuscript: “A Smaller Drop Is Not Robustness: A Validation-Locked Cross-Pipeline and Independent-Cohort Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification.” The study re-evaluates an apparent robustness advantage of a four-qubit ZZ-feature-map quantum support vector machine (QSVM-ZZ) for chest X-ray classification. The revised experimental design separates absolute target performance from internal-to-target degradation and addresses configuration-selection bias, limited random-seed inference, duplicate and provenance concerns, feature-compression effects, asymmetric feature encoding, prediction collapse, and lack of independent-cohort validation. Experimental scope The package contains reproducibility materials for three complementary evaluation settings: Source and internal evaluation: PneumoniaMNIST, derived from the Guangzhou/Kermany pediatric chest X-ray cohort. Cross-pipeline preprocessing-shift evaluation: original Kermany test images representing the same underlying cohort through a different preprocessing pipeline. Independent-cohort evaluation: the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge / NIH Clinical Center chest radiograph cohort. The confirmatory low-dimensional benchmark uses a configuration selected from source validation data only and evaluates QSVM-ZZ against RBF-SVM, logistic regression and a compact MLP across ten fresh seeds. Additional analyses include wider classical feature representations, a symmetric π·tanh encoding control, prediction-collapse and near-collapse audits, strict one-to-one paired radiograph evaluation, and repeated fine-tuned ResNet18 experiments. Key contents The record includes: raw-image duplicate and provenance-audit outputs; perceptual-hash screening results; reconstructed group-aware source training and validation splits; high-confidence source-to-raw correspondence mappings; the corrected 554-radiograph one-to-one paired mapping; PCA explained-variance and compression-sensitivity analyses; validation-only QSVM configuration-selection results; ten-seed confirmatory predictions and performance metrics; exact seed-level sign-flip tests and Holm-adjusted statistical comparisons; classical π·tanh encoding-control results; exact-collapse and near-collapse audits; source-validation-selected wider classical reference results; grouped domain-classifier outputs; five-seed fine-tuned ResNet18 predictions, training histories and trained checkpoints; independent RSNA primary and secondary evaluation outputs; derived RSNA frozen-feature arrays; executable Kaggle/Jupyter notebooks; software-version and random-seed information; SHA-256 integrity manifests; and legacy exploratory QSVM/VQC outputs retained for transparency and provenance. Principal methodological finding The revised analysis shows that QSVM-ZZ can exhibit a smaller internal-to-target macro-F1 decline than a matched low-dimensional RBF-SVM, but that smaller decline does not constitute evidence of practically useful robustness. QSVM-ZZ remains near chance by AUROC on both the Kermany preprocessing-shift target and the independent RSNA cohort, and its absolute target advantage over matched RBF-SVM is not statistically established. Applying the same π·tanh feature squashing used by QSVM-ZZ to the classical RBF-SVM substantially reduces the absolute Kermany performance gap, indicating that the classical-to-quantum encoding contributes to the apparent stability. Wider classical representations and fine-tuned ResNet18 additionally demonstrate that conclusions drawn from a severely compressed four-dimensional benchmark should not be generalized to broader model classes. Data-use and redistribution statement This archive contains derived features, mappings, predictions, statistical results, trained model checkpoints, code and analysis outputs. It does not redistribute raw RSNA DICOM images or raw Kermany/PneumoniaMNIST source-i
title: Does a Smaller Performance Drop Really Mean Robustness? A Validation-Locked Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification

summary: Where is the place of the human being in the physical picture of the world? This question is usually answered from one of two camps: consciousness is a product of the brain and nothing more; or consciousness is immaterial and does not depend on the body. This work takes a different path — forward from the physical foundation, step by step — and looks at where it leads. The foundation is the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” (BD). It contains nothing but a single assumption: everything is a process, an ideal sine wave, and its centre is the observer. Dimensions are born by squaring: first time, then, by iterating the same square, space and mass. Elementary particles turn out to be a resonance of at least three dimensions — time, space and mass. From the same assumption BD obtains the rules of quantum mechanics, the Lorentz transformations and the masses of particles from the speed of light alone. If the foundation is right, its rule should show up everywhere — including in the work of the brain. And it does: the main ranges of brain rhythms approximately form a ladder of squares — 2–3, 4–9, 16–81 Hz — built in the same way as the tower of levels in BD: the width of the levels in logarithms doubles with every step, and the alpha rhythm falls on the boundary between levels. The rhythm bands are blurred, but that is how it should be: the electroencephalogram is a projection of a higher-frequency process onto a single dimension, and within one level the process is smooth. What matters is something else — resonance between frequencies, and in the brain it was measured long ago. This leads to an assumption: the body is a resonator, and since bodies are alike, this answers the question of why different observers see one common world. Consciousness is then built like an elementary particle — as an agreement of three frequencies linked by squares — only on a higher-frequency level. That is why we see its work but cannot weigh it with instruments of our level; and that is why the world is perceived as three-dimensional. The structure is examined: the “I” is the observer; consciousness is time, the “here and now”; the subconscious is space, the “self” and its history; superconsciousness, intuition, is mass, which is born in self-reflection. From this follows an assumption about the meaning of life as the cultivation of intuition. If consciousness is like a particle, the reverse is also true: every particle may contain what we call consciousness. In the calculations of BD the Milky Way is the image of a neutron, and we live inside it; there are neutrons in almost every atom of our body. And the Universe, if it is like a black hole — part of a particle of a larger world — may be an observer. This is a hypothesis, not a proof. At the end there is a list of ways to test it, and what is established is separated from what is assumed. Revisions as of 07.11.2026:  The list of related works has been corrected.       Где в физической картине мира место человеку? Обычно на этот вопрос отвечают из двух лагерей: сознание — порождение мозга, и только; или сознание нематериально и от тела не зависит. Эта работа идёт другим путём — от физической основы вперёд, шаг за шагом, и смотрит, куда она приводит. Основа — работа «Рождение измерений: формальный скелет» (РИ). В ней нет ничего, кроме одного допущения: всё есть процесс, идеальный синус, а его центр — наблюдатель. Измерения рождаются возведением в квадрат: сначала время, затем, итерациями того же квадрата, пространство и масса. Элементарные частицы оказываются резонансом как минимум трёх измерений — времени, пространства и массы. Из того же допущения РИ получает правила квантовой механики, преобразования Лоренца и массы частиц из одной лишь скорости света. Если основа верна, её правило должно про
title: Consciousness as a Wave Structure: A Possible Connection Between Brain Frequencies and Perception Frequencies

summary: STARLI | F071–F080 / 300 Flagship 13 Fission · Volume I · Biointerface Perturbations, Surface Reliability and Traceable Validation Author: 33  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.3  |  English Zenodo Ten-Volume Overview This collection joins two five-theme research units from the STARLI 300-theme atlas. Research Unit I (F071–F075) examines local electric fields, surface aging, ionic-strength coupling, photothermal side effects and mechanical stress at biological interfaces. Research Unit II (F076–F080) extends the inquiry to multilayer coating reliability, molecular selectivity, noise-source attribution, reversible surface function and material leaching. The central concern is whether an interface claim survives realistic matrix changes, traceable controls and independent reconstruction. The ten English research working editions comprise 7,770 PDF pages: 300 candidate mathematical plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 separately paginated investigations, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Version 1.3 revises the scientific notes beneath the Gates across six dimensions: causal mechanism, measurable witness, blinded refutation, rival explanation, hard stop and successor interface. These are documented research-design proposals, not validated experiments or evidence of confirmed scientific discoveries. The Ten Research Directions F071  Biointerface Local Electric-Field Perturbation At The Limit — Tests whether a localized electric-field intervention changes desorption kinetics while preserving zeta potential and interfacial noise. A ligand-density-matched covalent surface provides a comparator, with concealed protein-corona exchange challenging whether the effect comes from electric-field control rather than interface composition. F072  Nanorobotic Surface Aging And Functional Degradation At The Limit — Examines whether aging-driven drift in nanorobotic surface charge, signal noise and leachate release can be separated from bulk-matrix effects. An inert coupon in the same matrix and a hidden coating-delamination challenge constrain claims of improved functional durability. F073  Biological Microenvironment Ionic Strength Coupling At The Limit — Investigates the coupling between ionic strength, interfacial noise, leachate mass and retained surface function. Unmodified and mature PEG-coated surfaces anchor the comparison; a concealed leachate challenge tests whether apparent electrical improvement actually reflects altered surface chemistry. F074  Nano-Interface Photothermal Side Effect Measurement At The Limit — Proposes assays for photothermal side effects at nano-interfaces, tracking leachate mass, functional retention and protein-corona turnover. summary: Acute respiratory infections in children comprise etiologically and clinically heterogeneous diseases with overlapping early manifestations, whereas the risk of respiratory failure and other adverse outcomes varies according to age, premorbid conditions, and the causative pathogen. This review aims to analyze current approaches to etiological diagnosis and evidence-based risk factors for severe disease in children. An analytical search covered PubMed/MEDLINE and documents issued by the World Health Organization and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence for 2015-2026. Priority was given to guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, diagnostic accuracy studies, and large cohorts. Clinical assessment identifies the anatomical level of respiratory involvement and current severity but cannot reliably establish viral etiology. Nucleic acid amplification remains the most sensitive method for detecting most respiratory viruses. Diagnostic value depends on the timing and quality of specimen collection, panel composition, and clinical context; a positive multiplex result does not establish the causal contribution of every detected agent. Serology has a limited role in an acute episode. Consistently reported baseline risk factors include young age, prematurity, chronic lung disease, hemodynamically significant congenital heart disease, neurological disorders, immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive treatment, and malnutrition. Hypoxemia, apnea, progressive respiratory distress, feeding inability, altered consciousness, and impaired perfusion indicate evolving organ dysfunction and require immediate assessment. Reliable prediction should integrate baseline risk factors with dynamic clinical variables. Any prediction model requires independent validation in the pediatric population for which its use is intended.
title: Acute Respiratory Infections in Children: Current Approaches to Etiological Diagnosis and Prediction of Severe Disease (Literature Review).

summary: This paper outlines a comparative structural framework for analyzing how judicial rulings from supranational courts (specifically the CJEU under Article 267 TFEU preliminary references and the ECHR) systematically transform domestic policy parameters without explicit legislative mandates.   Adapted specifically to the institutional mechanics of the French legal order, the framework operationalizes four key structural components:   Judicial Displacement (JD): The structural mechanism through which supranational courts assume primary interpretative authority over national policy, constrained in France by Article 55 of the Constitution.   Administrative Gradualism (AG): The incremental realignment of domestic policy through an iterative sequence of secondary executive and regulatory instruments (décrets, arrêtés, circulaires, and administrative guidance) issued by ministries and independent regulatory bodies (e.g., CNIL, ARCOM).   The Mandate Scale (M_0–M_3): A heuristic metric assessing the spectrum of explicit democratic authorization present within electoral manifestos, winning coalitions, or direct referendums regarding supranational constraints.   Four-Step Operational Cycle: A recurring sequence mapping the trajectory from supranational judicial trigger \rightarrow national administrative response (expanding, reclaiming, or accommodating) \rightarrow democratic legitimacy deficits (input, throughput, output) \rightarrow systemic political outcomes (evolutionary pushback via contrôle de conventionnalité or systemic backlash).   The paper includes a comparative matrix contrasting UK statutory mechanism (HRA 1998, Statutory Instruments) against French constitutional pathways (Sarran, Nicolo, Article 38 ordonnances), along with a rigorous methodology defining a "True-Negative Profile" to test boundary conditions against selection bias.  Note on Origin & Systemic Scope: This publication represents an operational draft outline designed to establish baseline terminology, structural mechanics, and theoretical metrics for ongoing comparative legal research.   This work is a direct spin-off and structural adaptation of the foundational framework established in: Davidson, C. K. S., Judicial Displacement and Administrative Gradualism, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24023708.    While the original benchmark paper evaluated these dynamics within a dualist, parliamentary context (specifically United Kingdom immigration policy and prisoner voting rights under ECHR jurisprudence), this adaptation recalibrates the core analytical model to the monist-leaning, semi-presidential institutional architecture of the French Fifth Republic under Article 55 of the 1958 French Constitution.    This draft serves as the immediate European adaptation within a broader comparative research agenda, with future planned adaptations extending the framework to examine administrative realignments, executive rule-making, and judicial review dynamics within the United States constitutional framework.

title: Supranational Integration, Administrative Gradualism, and Democratic Legitimacy — A Comparative European Structural Model (French Adaptation)

summary: This analysis examines how computational configuration choices shape resource efficiency in confidential genomic collaboration across institutions. A descriptive secondary analysis uses 14 PRINCESS benchmark configurations published in 2017, comprising seven batch sizes evaluated with compression enabled and disabled across three sites. Matched runtime differences, ratios and joint memory comparisons identify configuration tradeoffs. With compression enabled, increasing batch size from 100 to 10,000 variants reduces runtime by 75.49 percent, while expansion to one million variants provides only 0.38 percent further improvement despite requiring 32.69 times as much memory. Without compression, runtime reaches its observed minimum at 8,000 variants and subsequently increases. Compression enabled records longer enclave runtime in every matched pair. These patterns reveal diminishing processing gains and configuration dependent resource tradeoffs, without isolating their underlying mechanisms. The contribution is a comparative interpretation distinguishing faster execution from economical resource use. The findings refine a resource constraint perspective and support joint evaluation of execution time and memory when configuring protected genomic workflows, with numerical recommendations bounded by the observed benchmark environment.
title: BENCHMARKING CONFIDENTIAL GENOMIC COMPUTING EFFICIENCY THROUGH BATCH SIZE, COMPRESSION, AND MEMORY USE ACROSS COLLABORATIVE SITES

summary: This paper proposes Recursive Anticipatory Argumentation-Control Theory (RAACT), an interdisciplinary framework for representing argumentative discourse as a dynamic, par- tially observed, and recursively updated interaction system. Its central mechanism, Recur- sive Anticipatory Argument-Path Interception (RAAPI), combines contextual observation, pragmatic-linguistic encoding, argument reconstruction, opponent-state estimation, proba- bilistic argument-path forecasting, formal refutation verification, anticipatory intervention, and feedback-based model revision. The framework is developed around the Pre-emptive Refutation Fork Case (PRFC), a primary analytical case in which one participant forecasts an opponent's possible argumenta- tive move and presents a logically evaluated counterargument before that move is explicitly advanced. Subsequent responses are classified into continuation, substitution, qualification, forecast challenge, clarification, and novel argumentative pathways. The mathematical specification introduces latent-state models, observation functions, categorical predictive distributions, Bayesian belief updating, intervention-utility functions, estimation errors, and forecast-evaluation metrics. Conditional mathematical propositions identify what can be established under explicit assumptions, while empirical hypotheses dis- tinguish predictive accuracy from intervention effectiveness and strategic response restriction. RAACT is presented as a formal theoretical architecture and a research program, not as an empirically validated universal law. Its principal scientific obligations are to demonstrate incremental predictive value, establish causal effects under an identifiable research design, prove specific mathematical claims under stated assumptions, and identify boundary conditions through counterexamples and independent replication. Keywords: argumentation theory; linguistic pragmatics; anticipatory reasoning; pre-emptive refutation; cybernetics; feedback control; state estimation; Bayesian forecasting; formal logic; strategic discourse; falsifiability.

title: Recursive Anticipatory Argumentation-Control Theory (RAACT)

files.key: The Beam That Behaves Like a Molecule.pdf

summary: Two Hamiltonian systems that share almost nothing in their physical origins turn out to behave identically once their local structure near a 2:1 internal resonance is examined. One system models a pair of flexural modes in a micromechanical resonator through coupled Duffing oscillators. The other models the stretch–bend Fermi resonance of a molecule such as carbon dioxide through a Morse oscillator coupled to a harmonic bend. Both possess an elliptic equilibrium, equal Krein signatures, a frequency ratio close to 2:1, and a cubic resonant coupling. These shared features place them in the same resonant normal-form type, a difference resonance that confines energy exchange rather than driving escape. On the conserved polyad fixed by an initial excitation that places nearly all the energy in the higher-frequency mode, the truncated normal form of any such system collapses to a one-degree-of-freedom problem that depends on only two numbers: a scaled detuning and a scaled anharmonic curvature. Consequently the largest fraction of energy that can be transferred to the lower mode is given by a universal curve whose edges are independent of the curvature. All of the necessary invariants are computed directly from each Hamiltonian before any trajectory is integrated. Numerical integration then confirms the predictions. When the curvature is small the systems follow the one-parameter curve; when it is large they follow the two-parameter curve to high accuracy. A beam whose quartic coefficient is deliberately softened until its curvature matches that of the molecular model reproduces the molecular exchange curve directly, even though the remaining normal-form coefficients differ. An ensemble of sixty randomly drawn members of the same type likewise collapses onto the appropriate universal curve. The residual discrepancy grows roughly linearly with excitation amplitude, as expected from the truncation of the normal form. Two controls mark the boundaries of the result. Reversing one Krein signature converts the same frequency window from bounded exchange into unbounded escape. Weak viscous damping reduces the transferred fraction in the manner predicted by a correspondingly damped reduced model. A quantum treatment of the truncated normal form introduces the polyad number as a third invariant; the lowest Fermi dyad therefore follows a distinct quantum curve rather than the classical one. The findings remain local, confined to two-mode models, and classical except where the quantum analogue is stated explicitly. Within those limits they demonstrate that a dimensionless exchange relation established for one physical system can be transferred to an unrelated system once both have been rescaled by invariants computed from their own Hamiltonians.
title: The Beam That Behaves Like a Molecule

summary: This paper develops a scale-spanning account of latent vibration and frequency manifestation within Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM). It examines the relationship between complete latent vibration, the negative and positive displacement domains around the manifestable origin, and the eligibility of positive displacement for progression towards physical manifestation. The development distinguishes the complete latent-vibration interval from the directed displacement associated with manifestation, establishing the proposed Pre-Latent and Pre-Planck threshold relationships in terms of the Planck length. The analysis further develops phase-dependent frequency relations below the Planck threshold and considers the proposed frequency increments associated with the Pre-Latent and Pre-Planck domains. It then presents a state-dependent sequence of energy–frequency transformations across latent, phase, and manifested states, including the reverse progression associated with dissolution. Within this framework, frequency and displacement are treated as related physical parameters whose coefficients depend on the corresponding phase domain. The paper also distinguishes the phase-state potential-energy mass representation from the mass contribution associated with the manifested domain. It formulates the effective-mass relationship and separates this ECM representation from the distinct dark-energy-related mass representation. Taken together, these developments present an integrated theoretical description of latent vibration, manifestation eligibility, threshold transitions, energy–frequency relations, and mass-state transformations within the proposed ECM framework.
title: Complete Latent Vibration and Frequency Manifestation Eligibility in Extended Classical Mechanics
