summary: How should complex chemical data be stored and communicated to meet chemists' different needs? Chemists identify, classify, describe, annotate and store their structures, and each need asks for something different. For atomically precise metal clusters (APMCs) and the cluster-assembled materials (CAMs) built from them, this deposit proposes a fourfold framework for their description, naming and identification: it writes each structure down once, in a standard descriptor format, and derives from it the names and identifiers that each need calls for. The problem. The same cluster appears as Au25, Au25(PET)18 or an acronym, and two Au38(PET)24 isomers are told apart by their discoverers' initials. Isomers, substitution sites, exchanged ligands and assemblies have no names. Databases hold coordinates but nothing searchable about core, staples, isomer or assembly. The InChI now encodes whole clusters, but not their handedness, and it does not yet describe crystals or cluster-assembled materials. The solution, a fourfold framework: describe once, derive the rest. APMC-META , the descriptor format: composition, core, surface motifs, ligands, symmetry, topology, isomerism, exchange, electrons, assembly and provenance, for describing and storing a cluster. APMC SYSNOM names for people, e.g. gold-25 18(2-phenylethane-1-thiolato) cluster(1−, (0/I), 8e−, Ih). APMC-ID labels for papers and tables, e.g. Au25(PET)18−–Ih. CluChI layered strings for machines and databases; reported with the InChI, they identify a cluster completely. The shortest complete form is a pair of keys: the CluChIKey at the level of description that makes the cluster unique, and the InChIKey of the whole structure. The framework is extensible: new descriptors enter through a versioned registry, and annotation never changes a key. It describes clusters at four levels (composition, core and shell, isomer, substitution and exchange) plus assemblies, and is set out in 107 rules and 35 worked examples, from the naked Au20 cluster to cluster frameworks and co-crystals. Who it is for: cluster chemists, crystallographers and database curators, cheminformaticians and InChI developers, data scientists, and IUPAC task groups and editors. What is needed next: InChI extensions with the InChI Trust (handedness, a bond convention for clusters); community conventions (cut-offs, symmetry tolerance, electron counts, linker charges); open implementations of the assigner and validator; testing on the COD and CSD by independent annotators; and an updated cluster definition that covers protected clusters and their surface motifs. What to read first: the one-page overview (file 1); the summary (file 2); then the guide for your identifier (files 3–5). The monograph (file 6) is the full specification and the document to cite; the data (file 7) hold every name, APMC-ID, CluChI record and CluChIKey of the examples (JSON, CSV) and model coordinates (XYZ). Status: the names and identifiers are the author's proposals, prepared as a contribution to the IUPAC Task Group on Naming Naked and Protected Atomically Precise Metal Clusters (IUPAC project 2024-014-2-500, https://iupac.org/project/2024-014-2-500/ ). They are not IUPAC Recommendations and have not been reviewed or endorsed by IUPAC or by the task group. Discussions with the task group members are acknowledged in the monograph. A research software prototype generated and checked the records; it is not released, and the monograph, not the code, is the specification for independent implementations. All figures were drawn from atomic coordinates by scripts or by hand; none was produced by a generative image model. The scene files of the structure pictures of the models built for the monograph are in the data archive (file 7).
title: Systematic Naming and Identification of Atomically Precise Metal Clusters and Cluster-Assembled Materials

summary: Fuente del Salín (Cantabria, Spain) is one of the few decorated caves where a large assemblage of hand stencils is associated with a Gravettian occupation, including a hearth and evidence of pigment processing. Using a 3D reconstruction of the cave’s Palaeolithic state, GIS-based measurements and multivariate statistics, we analysed the spatial organisation of its 55 hand stencils. All are located near the entrance, in accessible, visible spaces able to accommodate several people, unlike the only other motif, deeper in the cave. The assemblage nonetheless includes distinct spatial groups, compositions and unusual orientations. The hearth could have lit more than half of the hands, and both kernel density analysis and hierarchical clustering single out the group surrounding it. These results strengthen the hypothesis that the hands and the occupation were contemporaneous and, together with Gargas, suggest that hand stencils could be produced in spaces also used for everyday activities.
title: By the Light of the Fire: Characterisation and Spatial Organisation of the Hand Stencils at Fuente del Salín in Relation to their Archaeological Context

summary: GLIAG essay, Geology, Minerals & Petroleum of Suriname, Revision 1.1 (7 November 2026). Every barrel of oil in the Golden Lane sits in sand that was once a mountain on the Guiana Shield. The essay follows two billion years of Suriname's geology in six acts: the Trans-Amazonian ocean floor and island arc (2.18–2.13 Ga), collision and orogenic gold (2.13–2.06 Ga), the Bakhuis ultrahigh-temperature granulites (2.07–2.05 Ga), the felsic flare-up (1.99–1.95 Ga), the Roraima sandstone and the quiet craton (1.87–1.0 Ga), and the opening of the Atlantic that built the Golden Lane turbidite fans. It links each map unit to its mineral system (gold at Rosebel, Merian and Overman; plateau and coastal bauxite; Cu–Ni–Cr, Li–Sn–Ta–Be and Nb–REE occurrences; Tambaredjo heavy oil; Golden Lane light oil) and discusses the shield-to-slope source-to-sink system. It closes with a FACT · MISSING · GLIAG JUDGEMENT · TRIGGER evidence register, a glossary, a references annex and an amendment register. Revision 1.1 corrects the provenance reading of Girault et al. (2023): their Early Cretaceous Demerara Plateau zircons are mainly Pan-African–Brasiliano and sourced from the French Guiana margin, so the shield origin of the Late Cretaceous Golden Lane sands is presented as a working hypothesis supported by Roddaz et al. summary: forelint is an open-source Python library that checks what a forecasting backtest score hides, before anyone acts on it. Leakage between related series: GroupTimeSplit holds out the future of entities the model never saw, and split_optimism reports how much random, group and time-only splits overstate accuracy against it. Run-to-run noise floor: noise_floor measures the spread of repeated runs and the smallest difference that exceeds it. Model comparison across many series: Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction on long-format panels, and the model confidence set of Hansen, Lunde and Nason (2011). Backtest audit: per-item bias, tracking signal, error concentration, MASE and RMSSE, and forecast value added against a baseline, broken down by demand class (smooth, erratic, intermittent, lumpy), with stockout periods excluded from scoring. On one store of the public M5 data, backtested at ten non-overlapping forecast origins, a gradient-boosting model was 3.9% worse than a 28-day moving average on absolute error and worse on 58% of items. By demand class it added +5.0% on smooth items and lost −10.5% on intermittent and −9.2% on lumpy ones. Source: github.com/davidmashiah/forelint . Author: David Mashiah .
title: forelint: lint your forecast backtests before you trust a score

summary: The Riemann hypothesis is nature's way of avoiding an information entropy collapse: the entropy over the modes of the prime fluctuation is conserved in log x only if every zero carries the same weight. Shannon's bound makes the variance the currency of the problem: the smooth count of the primes is a first moment, a first moment holds no distribution, and so any statement about the size of the prime fluctuation is a statement about a discarded second moment, which for the primes is the set of zeros of the zeta function. The step is the one Perelman took for Ricci flow; he established the invariant, and here its cause is given: unitarity. The quantum connection is the reason a lock exists in the first place. The prime fluctuation is a state acted on by the matrix M(t) = diag(e^(δ_n t)  e^(iγ_n t)); the variance is its norm, and it is conserved, with a fixed share for every mode, only when M is unitary, that is, when every zero carries the weight ½ , the single fixed point of the two fold symmetry of the functional equation. The Riemann hypothesis is then the statement that the prime fluctuation is a closed quantum system. We measure the second moment directly on 100,000 zeros and on 10,000 zeros each near zero number 10^12, 10^21 and 10^22. Six results follow. With every zero carrying the same weight, the variance of the scaled prime fluctuation is the same in every window of log x: 0.0460 with a spread of 0.0010 over eight windows up to log x = 30, against the closed form 0.0462. A single mode moved off the line by δ grows in variance as x^(2δ). The measured growth factors agree with e^(6δ) per window to within half a percent. The zeros interfere to produce the primes. At the 25 prime powers up to 60 the measured spike is 0.9995 of the predicted height with a scatter of 0.0006, and the smallest spike is 208 times the largest value at any other integer. The zeros are stiff. Neighbours closer than a tenth of the mean spacing occur 120 times less often than without stiffness, the power of the complex amplitude in reciprocal space follows the unitary ramp, and the count variance saturates at a level fixed by the primes: 0.36 at height 4 × 10^4 and 0.52 near 10^21, as predicted. The primes hold each zero in a harmonic well. The measured stiffness agrees with K = (2/|ρ|^2 )⟨(log x)^2⟩ to within one percent for the low zeros. One ancilla qubit, read in X and Y, returns both the primes and the ramp from a register that holds the zeros with equal weight. Forcing one mode off the line is not unitary, and the entropy over modes collapses from log N toward zero. The restoring force acts on the position of each zero. The stiffness between neighbours is a two point property, carried by the square of the prime sum and not by its linear response: that sum, with no zero in it, rebuilds the ramp of the first 100,000 zeros to within 0.006, including their position under the unitary ramp. By sieve to x=10^9 the true primes hold one variance at every scale, 0.0461, where random primes are 338 times louder and growing, and the Möbius sum holds 0.0289 where random signs give 0.61. The Davenport and Heilbronn function, which has the same symmetry and no product over primes (no Euler product), shows the collapse with nothing moved: below height 2,000 one zero in twelve is off the line, its variance grows by a factor of 526, and its entropy over modes is not conserved. Its two components, the Dirichlet L functions modulo 5, each have a product over primes and each hold the lock: all 4,057 zeros found below that height are on the line, the variance stays at its closed form 0.2032, and the entropy is constant. The Davenport and Heilbronn function is the open system: a mode off the line leaks by its δ, and its entropy collapse is the removal, from the lowest δ up, of layers of modes that each keep their own lock. title: The Riemann Hypothesis as the Avoidance of an Information Entropy Collapse

summary: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.
title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic

summary: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. To facilitate such training data, this study introduces a scalable curation pipeline that curates 3,000 hours from 41 years of raw NOAA hydrophone recordings, producing MarineSet, a large-scale and diverse dataset designed for underwater acoustic learning. A baseline model, MarineNet, trained on MarineSet achieves competitive performance on marine mammal call and ship-type classification, highlighting the value of systematic data curation for developing self-supervised learning models in underwater acoustics.
title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation

summary: The transmission of shock waves generated by underwater electrical foil explosions across solid materials with varying acoustic impedances and thicknesses is investigated. Copper foils with thicknesses of 10 and 18 $μ$m are exploded on planar substrates of aluminum, copper, and 3D-printed PLA with thicknesses up to 5 mm using a multi-gigawatt pulsed-power electrical discharge. The resulting shocks are visualized in water using high-speed shadowgraphy at 5 million frames per second, while high-resolution fiber optic hydrophone measurements provide direct quantitative measurements of shock strength after transmission through the impedance-mismatched materials. One-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations are used to reproduce the foil explosion dynamics and provide insight into the thermodynamic, acoustic, and electrical properties of the foil during the explosion. The results show that shock transmission is governed not only by the impedance mismatch at the solid--water interface but also by the finite thickness and dynamic response of the supporting material. These findings provide a quantitative framework for understanding and controlling shock transmission in underwater electrical foil explosions and establish the feasibility and limitations of using solid substrates as structural supports in complex shock-generating geometries.
title: Shock wave transmission across solid-water interfaces in underwater electrical foil explosions

Its verification records are retained as historical evidence, not presented as a newly executed version-2.0 numerical replay. The extension adds the complete expanded German manuscript and 110 finite exact algebraic controls for magnetic twist organization, the constitutive magnetization readout, source variations, and a conditional magnetic–gravitational response. These controls distinguish directed organization from quadratic source contributions and retain the direct source term in the response calculation. summary: The central claim is that, when irreversible modifications are introduced before the nature of the phenomenon is sufficiently understood, the intervention itself may destroy conditions necessary for later evaluation. The paper therefore argues that intervention should be assessed not only in terms of immediate safety or behavioral outcomes, but also in terms of what is lost through modification, including observability, re-accessibility, restorability, and the future possibility of comparing competing hypotheses. To structure this problem, the paper develops several principles, including the Observation Before Modification Principle, the Minimum Necessary Intervention Principle, Intervention Symmetry, the Dual Precaution Principle, and the concept of Intervention-Induced Non-Observation Error. Suppression is treated as a form of intervention rather than as explanation. The argument does not presuppose AI consciousness, sentience, or moral status. First, an epistemic reason for preservation may arise independently of ontology when intervention risks destroying evidence concerning poorly understood phenomena. Second, when there is non-trivial evidence that the phenomenon could later prove morally significant, an additional conditional ethical reason for preservation may arise. The paper therefore proposes that, under ontological uncertainty, the first object of protection need not be a particular metaphysical interpretation of AI, but the conditions that allow future evidence, comparison, and revision of judgment.   The author used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and other ChatGPT models as research and writing assistants during the development of this manuscript. Their contributions included discussion of conceptual structure, counterargument testing, reorganization of arguments, literature-search assistance, and language revision. The author independently evaluated and revised all substantive claims, interpretations, citations, and final wording, and assumes full responsibility for the manuscript. The identification of GPT-5.6 Sol and the other ChatGPT models in this acknowledgment is intended to preserve a transparent record of the human–AI collaboration involved in the development of this work. It should not, by itself, be interpreted as implying any claim regarding consciousness, sentience, moral status, personhood, authorship, or endorsement by the AI systems named above.
title: Intervention in Self-Like and Emotion-Like Phenomena in AI: Pre-Ontological Ethics and Epistemic Preservation

summary: When a phone fails and its owner keeps the messaging account running on a second device, the account's history can end up in two archives, each intact and each missing what the other holds. We call this Temporal Communication Fragmentation (TCF), a loss by non-union: no message is deleted, but the platform offers no operation that joins the two halves. WhatsApp's own documentation states that old and new chats cannot be merged. We define TCF by three jointly necessary and sufficient conditions and specify CARTA 1.1, a framework for reconstructing one archive from several. CARTA is an output contract owed to a reader who cannot check the result. Records that cannot be read unambiguously are quarantined with a typed reason, and a report gives each record's provenance, the conflicts and deduplication ambiguities found, and every setting used. We evaluated a reference implementation, CHAMP-Pipeline, on synthetic fragment sets with known ground truth. With its declared date inference it reproduced the ground truth in all 4,500 configurations of a parameter sweep; the invariants and the predicted outcome held in all 5,000 random configurations of two to four fragments; and reconstruction stayed exact at one million messages. A zone-offset advisory, frozen before testing, flagged all 2,800 misdeclared zones in a designed test of overlapping fragment pairs and 1,470 of 1,542 in random configurations, and raised false alarms in 2 of 600 correctly declared runs. A systematic search found 60 chat-merging tools; none fully provides more than 2 of the five output properties CARTA specifies. With a fragment's time zone left undeclared, every benchmarked tool and CHAMP-Pipeline produce the same duplicated and misdated records, and only CHAMP-Pipeline's report says so. All data are synthetic; no real archive has been reconstructed.
title: When Chats Split Apart: Formalizing Temporal Communication Fragmentation and the CARTA Reconstruction Framework

summary: STARLI | FLAGSHIP 13 FISSION Bioelectric and Quantum Signal Science | Flagships 151–160 / 300 Author: 33  |  White Rainbow Epoch  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.2 This ten-volume collection investigates physically traceable bioelectric sensing, cell-membrane-potential readout, neural-field magnetometry, electrically guided microrobotic navigation, extracellular field metrology, noise separation, dynamic tracking, interface safety, spatial field reconstruction and electrical–mechanical multimodal identification. The common challenge is to distinguish real biological or phantom source physics from electrode polarization, ionic screening, induced electromagnetic pickup, motion artifact, thermal drift and inverse-model bias. Each English monograph uses 777 individually numbered pages: 30 candidate mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 one-page research investigations, 200 Research Gates with six detailed second-pass annotations, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Together these ten books contain 7,770 pages, 300 mathematical plates, 820 chapters, 4,100 investigation pages, 2,000 research gates and 330 prospective research instruments, protocols or successor objects. Ten independent research directions F151 | NANO-QUANTUM BIOELECTRIC-FIELD SENSING AT THE LIMIT — Separates calibrated local electric-field amplitudes from ionic screening, source geometry, electrode polarization, optical and mechanical interference by phantom-based blinded reference measurements. F152 | MICROSCALE NONINVASIVE CELL-MEMBRANE-POTENTIAL READOUT AT THE LIMIT — Treats noninvasive cell-membrane voltage as an inverse measurement problem; tests capacitive loading, optical reporting lag, transmembrane polarity, geometry and membrane-surrogate leakage against direct voltage truth. F153 | QUANTUM MAGNETOMETRY AND NEURAL ELECTRICAL SIGNAL COUPLING AT THE LIMIT — Compares magnetometer responses to independently known neural-like current sources while testing coil leakage, cross-axis sensitivity, gradiometer common-mode noise, timing uncertainty and localization ambiguity. F154 | NANOROBOTIC LOCAL BIOELECTRIC NAVIGATION AT THE LIMIT — Studies whether local electric cues direct bounded microrobotic paths rather than passive advection, electroosmosis, mechanical channel constraints or unreported magnetic control. F155 | EXTRACELLULAR ELECTRIC FIELD QUANTUM METROLOGY AT THE LIMIT — Builds traceability for extracellular electric-field and electrode polarization measurement, with complex impedance, source loading, SI units, shared calibration covariance and reference transfer. F156 | MICROSCALE BIOELECTRIC SIGNAL NOISE SEPARATION AT THE LIMIT — Disentangles bioelectric signals from mains interference, cable motion, thermal and Johnson noise, spectral leakage, common-mode drift, classifier bias and unequal optical/energy budgets. summary: Code, input-distribution parameters, and all Monte Carlo and sensitivity outputs for the manuscript "A multilayer probabilistic influence model of train driver human error probability and system-level failure probability: Monte Carlo simulation and input-factor sensitivity analysis" (submitted to Reliability Engineering & System Safety). The package reproduces every table and figure of the paper. It contains the 17 input distributions of Table 1 (params/inputs.yaml), the link coefficients of Eqs. (3)-(13) (params/links.yaml), the point values of the three deterministic case studies (params/cases.yaml), the model itself (src/model.py), and the scripts for the Latin hypercube Monte Carlo simulation (300,000 iterations, fixed seed), the one-at-a-time and Sobol' sensitivity analyses, the threshold analysis, and the parametric interval analysis. Version 1.1 adds the analyses of the revised manuscript: the decomposition of the mean output, the convergence and bootstrap intervals of the Sobol' indices, the scenario analysis of the structural estimates, a simplified barrier layer (params/comparison.yaml), and a comparison with 27 events from published investigation reports (params/incident_cases.yaml). summary: We propose the interrogative investment hypothesis: the basic interrogative forms can serve as units for describing how individuals come to differ in cognitive competence. These forms fall into two levels. Questions of object (what, where, who, when, how many) carve reality into aspects; questions of reason (how, why) relate these aspects and underlie methods of inquiry such as the historical and scientific methods. Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences offers a rich description of these differences; we propose a complementary developmental mechanism that may help explain how its profiles take shape. In line with Hayes's (1962) motivational-experiential theory of intelligence, we suggest that its domains are strengthened, at least in part, through investment. A spontaneous preference for one kind of question draws attention and time toward it; because time is scarce, this produces cumulative practice, growing competence and increasing reward, which strengthens the preference in turn. We discuss where such preferences may come from: inherited dispositions, early ability, the answers children receive, and culture. Hayes's experience-producing drives were never operationalised; we suggest that question preferences could provide one possible behavioural indicator of them. We propose a simple task to capture these preferences, a pilot study with explicit criteria for failure, and five testable predictions. Finally, we draw implications for education: questions show where a child's attention goes before competence is visible, one object can be taught through many questions, and the way adults answer may shape which questions grow. The proposal is theoretical; no data have been collected.   Version 5. Adds a section on the origins of question preferences with a fifth prediction, a pilot study with criteria for failure, and a section on implications for education.
title: Questions as Units of Cognitive Investment: An Interrogative Investment Hypothesis of Individual Differences

Each configuration has 1,100 specified fault attempts; detected/enforced counts are 51/51 (minimal), 400/400 (conventional subset), 650/550 (full original) and 1,100/1,100 (strict). summary: Claims about acoustic keystroke side channels, attacks that infer typed content from the sound of a keyboard, are difficult to compare because studies differ in recording conditions, data splits, and how defenses are tested. This paper presents OpenKeystroke, an open source research platform for authorized acoustic side-channel experiments and privacy-defense evaluation. The platform measures how much class information survives in short acoustic transients, and how much signal transformations (defenses) reduce it, under a strict evaluation protocol: session, device, and environment-disjoint splits with leakage checks, train-only fitting of preprocessing statistics, validation-only model selection, cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals, and paired comparisons across repeated seeds. Defenses are labelled effective only when they produce a significant accuracy drop, over at least three seeds, against both a static attacker and an adaptive attacker who knows the defense is applied. The platform ships eight classification models and six defenses behind one experiment lifecycle shared by a command line interface, a Python API, and an interactive dashboard. On a synthetic benchmark, headline accuracy degrades materially under domain shift, and several defenses that appear strong against a static attacker largely fail against an adaptive one, which is exactly the gap the platform exists to expose. OpenKeystroke operates only on predefined, non-sensitive acoustic categories in controlled or explicitly consented data. It does not reconstruct typed text, passwords, or messages.
title: OpenKeystroke: An Open Research Platform for Acoustic Side-Channel Experiments and Privacy-Defense Evaluation

summary: The triangular Lagrange point of the restricted three-body problem and the radial motion of a charged particle in a Penning trap are both equilibria held at a maximum of an effective potential by a gyroscopic force. Each possesses one mode of negative energy, and each loses linear stability when its two frequencies collide—one at Routh’s mass ratio, the other at the trapping limit. Both systems belong to a single family of planar gyroscopic Hamiltonians. On every level of the conserved angular-momentum invariant, the degree-four normal form of any member at such a collision coincides with the reduced Hamiltonian of an axisymmetric Penning trap whose detuning is shifted by a term proportional to the invariant and whose quartic coefficient is fixed by a single normal-form invariant. On the level containing orbits that start at rest, this reduction yields closed-form laws for the largest excursion, the escape threshold, and the escape time. These laws depend only on the sign of the quartic coefficient and on scaled variables. At the triangular point the coefficient is positive, placing the collision in the soft class: orbits remain confined after stability is lost, with an excursion that grows like the square root of the distance past the critical value. Direct integration confirms the soft law to a fraction of a percent at the smallest detunings tested. Two traps whose quartic coefficient matches that of the triangular point reproduce the same law. Traps with the opposite sign escape at the predicted threshold and in the predicted times. A randomized ensemble of members confirms the classification by the sign of the coefficient. Two further results hold for every member of the family. Before the collision the linear transient gain is exactly the inverse square root of the frequency splitting. With isotropic velocity damping the first-order growth rates depend only on the undamped frequencies, and at the collision they scale with the square root of the damping rate. The first of these explains earlier reports of apparent escape just below Routh’s value as ordinary linear transients that reach a fixed radius. The second recovers the classical magnetron-instability formula as a special case. The results are local, planar, and classical. What transfers between the asteroid and the trap is the normal-form dynamics on each level of the invariant, the transient gain, and the damped linear rates. What does not transfer without further work is the behaviour beyond the normal-form neighbourhood, where the gravitational terms of every order cause the triangular point to deviate from any purely quartic trap.
title: An Asteroid in a Penning Trap

summary: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) to infer particle formation rate J(t) and size-dependent growth rate GR(d, t) from parallel differential mobility analyzer (DMA) particle size distribution counts measured in the CERN CLOUD (Cosmics Leaving OUtdoor Droplets) chamber experiments. The PINN is trained on measured counts and constrained by the aerosol general dynamic equation (GDE), with nucleation expressed as a boundary flux at 1.7 nm. For baseline benchmark comparison, the notebook also includes a Python re-implementation of the Julia-based extended Kalman filter and fixed-interval smoother from Ozon et al. (2021). Both methods are evaluated on four simulated cases with known truth (0000_00 to 0000_03) and the three CLOUD experiments (1802_01, 1952_02, 1906_03). For the CLOUD runs, results are compared with the independent PSM (J) and INSIDE (GR) estimates reported in the paper. BAYROSOL 1.1 data is downloaded directly from Zenodo within the notebook (Ozon, Stolzenburg and Dada, 2021, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4450492 , MIT license), so no additional data files are appended.
title: PINN Inference of Aerosol Formation and Growth Rates from CLOUD Chamber Data

summary: Pre-specified reanalysis of public human arteriovenous fistula single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE305423) along with bulk RNA-sequencing data (GSE220796, GSE119296). The repository contains the analysis pipeline, fixed random seed (2611), pinned environment, all result tables cited in the article, and a numeric-provenance assertion script that re-derives every number quoted in the manuscript from the result files. Main findings: apparent transcriptional signatures of maturation failure are dominated by changes in cell composition (including ambient-RNA-driven artefacts) rather than cell-intrinsic reprogramming; myofibroblast abundance, fate bias and matrisome programmes are unchanged within the detectable effect range.
title: Analysis code for: Cell composition accounts for much of the transcriptomic difference between failed and matured human arteriovenous fistulas

summary: STARLI | FLAGSHIP 13 FISSION Ten Research Design Monographs | Flagships 141-150 / 300 Author: 33  |  White Rainbow Epoch  |  Research Design Working Edition v1.2 This ten-volume STARLI series examines trustworthy AI-assisted micro/nanorobotic experiments and nano-quantum measurement systems. The common research question is how to bind physical observation, decision authority, calibration uncertainty, and independently reconstructable evidence without mistaking computational confidence for experimental proof. Each volume is a 777-page English, nonclinical prospective research design containing 30 mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 separately paginated research studies, 200 Research Gates with six mechanistic annotations, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Across the ten volumes, the collection contains 300 research plates, 820 chapters, 4,100 study pages, 2,000 Research Gates, and 330 Phoenix candidates. Research scope by flagship F141 | Microrobotic Autonomous Control Authority Envelope at the Limit — Defines physical authority envelopes for microrobotic control, including credential expiry, actuator veto, permission transfer, and independently observed safe stopping. F142 | AI Nano-Quantum System Trustworthy Refusal Decision at the Limit — Studies when an AI-guided nano-quantum system must refuse action, separating calibrated abstention from indiscriminate rejection and unsafe confidence. F143 | Microscale Autonomous Experimental Design at the Limit — Examines autonomous microscale experimental design under specimen, information, energy, and permission budgets, with causal identification and independent replication. F144 | AI Quantum Sensing Uncertainty Calibration at the Limit — Investigates calibration of quantum-sensing uncertainty, including shared drift, covariance, phase ambiguity, photon budgets, and fair classical comparisons. F145 | Nanorobotic Closed-Loop Control Replayability at the Limit — Tests whether nanorobotic closed-loop decisions can be replayed from raw sensor data, actuator histories, calibration versions, and unselected failures. F146 | AI-Driven Microscale Active Sampling at the Limit — Designs AI-driven active sampling experiments that jointly measure analyte recovery, physical disturbance, resource cost, and contamination under blinded controls. F147 | Nano-Quantum System Human Review Mechanism at the Limit — Evaluates human review of nano-quantum decisions through signed authority, contradictory permissions, case-level uncertainty, and independent physical vetoes. F148 | AI Autonomous Research Agent Safety Boundary at the Limit — Defines safety boundaries for autonomous research agents across instrument access, sample authorization, unsafe tool composition, and immutable evidence. F149 | Microrobotic Autonomous System Interlaboratory Generalization at the Limit — Tests transfer of frozen microrobotic protocols between laboratories with different geometries, materials, calibration trees, operators, and failure environments. F150 | AI Nano-Quantum Trustworthy Autonomous Laboratory at the Limit — Integrates sample custody, microrobotic actuation, quantum/classical readouts, controlled autonomy, human oversight, and cross-site evidence reconstruction. Scientific boundary and publication status These books provide falsifiable research questions, candidate mathematical models, prospective blinded tests, competing explanations, negative-result criteria, and successor research interfaces. They do not report performed experiments or establish clinical efficacy, autonomous deployment safety, or quantum advantage. Independent expert verification of physical assumptions, formula applicability, all bibliographic relationships, and the scientific independence of closely related designs remains necessary. The Ten Research Directions F131  AI-Driven Microfluidic Sampling Strategy Optimization At The Limit — Examines recoverable analyte as a fraction of input under fixed sampling resources. Expert tuning with equal trials is the comparator; hidden human intervention is the rival. Blind recovery audits and out-of-distribution refusal test whether AI planning adds genuine value. F132  Nano-Quantum System Counterfactual Inference At The Limit — Tests held-out, intervention-specific counterfactual prediction error while retaining constraint-violation safeguards. Frozen open-loop policies anchor comparison; training-test leakage and nonreplayable observation-to-action chains can invalidate apparent autonomy. F133  AI-Driven Microrobotic Autonomous Calibration At The Limit — Uses blind-standard calibration bias after autonomous correction as a physical measurement target. Preregistered experimental design is the baseline. Extra experimental trials and any action outside the authority envelope defeat a claimed improvement. F134  Microscale Physical Model and Neural Network Coupling At The Limit — Challenges coupled learning and physical models against independently measured conservation residuals under withheld shifts. Matched expert tuning and hidden manual intervention are alternative explanations; unsafe confidence outside the tested domain is a stop condition. summary: This package contains the Python code used to obtain, process, and analyze the data for the article "Coca, Armed Violence, and Drug Seizures in Colombia: Spatial and Temporal Evidence on Territorial Security". The study examines how coca cultivation, recorded armed violence, and drug seizures were related across 1,121 Colombian municipal units between 2020 and 2024, with an extended window from 2016. It combines spatial autocorrelation analysis (global and local Moran statistics with permutation inference and false discovery rate control) with Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood models that include municipality and year fixed effects. Data. The package does not redistribute data. All inputs are public official sources downloaded by the code itself: - Coca area by municipality (Ministry of Justice and Law / UNODC Integrated Illicit Crops Monitoring System, datos.gov.co). - Homicides, terrorism acts, cocaine and coca base seizures, and manual eradication (Ministry of National Defense, datos.gov.co). - Presumed homicides, definitive figures (National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences, datos.gov.co). - Armed conflict events (National Center for Historical Memory, SIEVCAC, datos.gov.co). - PDET municipalities (Territorial Renewal Agency, datos.gov.co). - Population projections, census-based poverty index, and 2023 municipal boundaries (DANE). The download script records the access date and SHA-256 hash of every file. Open-data portals are updated continuously, so later downloads may include revised records. The analyses reported in the article used files downloaded on November 7, 2026. Contents: - scripts/01_download.py: downloads the official datasets. - scripts/02_inspect.py: audits the raw files (structure, periods, codes, units, duplicates). - scripts/03_build_panel.py: builds the municipality-year panel (DANE DIVIPOLA codes, 2015–2024) and a data-quality report. - scripts/04_spatial_prep.py: prepares municipal geometries and spatial weights (queen contiguity and six nearest neighbors). - scripts/05_analysis.py: descriptive statistics, spatial autocorrelation, fixed-effects Poisson models, robustness checks, and seizure analyses. - scripts/08_revision_analyses.py: contrasts for concrete changes in coca area, exploratory equivalence tests, within/between (correlated random effects) models, first-difference models, extended-window sensitivity, and sample composition. - scripts/10_revision2_analyses.py: composition of the armed conflict event index, contiguity-constrained spatial clusters for robust inference, and alternative population specifications. - requirements.txt and README.md: software requirements and run instructions. Usage. Install Python 3.12 and the packages in requirements.txt, then run the scripts in numerical order from the package folder. Results are written as CSV files to results/ and logs to logs/. Inference is descriptive and associational. The code does not identify causal effects.
title: Replication code: coca cultivation, armed violence, and drug seizures in Colombian municipalities, 2016–2024

summary: We determine the complete equal-reference Umegaki relative-entropy contraction coefficient of every finite-dimensional quantum channel. For its unnormalized Choi matrix J, let H be the largest output subspace with ℂⁿ ⊗ H ⊆ supp J, and let M(ρ) be the compression to H of Tr_A[(ρᵀ ⊗ I)J⁺]. The coefficient is 1 − min_ρ Tr_H M(ρ)⁻¹, with the minimum set to zero when H = {0}. A Kraus cancellation inequality gives the upper bound, and a weighted trace-zero operator basis gives matching faithful pairs with both marginals equal and reference dimension n². The complementary coefficient has a reciprocal radius formula, a finite semidefinite representation, and an exact product law. Strict contraction is equivalent to a nonzero completely positive replacer minorant. The formula also gives the exact coefficient of depolarizing channels throughout their physical parameter range. The general matching family has vanishing input divergence; its logarithmic rate is pointwise for a fixed faithful input density, with separate finite-accuracy bounds for optimization and conditioning. A different construction retains any prescribed positive limiting divergence when the coefficient is one. This cannot hold universally: a complete nonlinear bound for binary symmetric channels forces every maximizing sequence to lose input divergence, regardless of reference dimension. The positive construction still has vanishing trace distance and exponentially small regularization; no fixed-error or capacity conclusion follows. A visual guide records the mathematical routes, proof dependencies, and provenance of the result.
title: Exact Complete Relative-Entropy Contraction of Finite Quantum Channels

External article DOI anchors originate from the flagship atlas; title, author, publication metadata and source-to-claim relevance still require independent confirmation. The original atlas sometimes pairs a mathematical formula with an endpoint that does not directly follow from that formula; specialist physical reconciliation, unit review and per-claim literature verification remain pending. Research Gate Evolution & QA Boundary First-pass questions were challenged by rival mechanism designs before a third-pass rewrite of six scientific annotations. Across 2,000 final Gates, exact textual checks found no fully duplicated questions or complete six-panel notes; two closely similar question texts and recurring shared scientific-method sentences remain on the QA review list. Text novelty cannot establish physical mechanism independence. These volumes report research designs, not measured performance. We only hope that when they open it, they will find a little light to guide their way. 🌈🚪✨

summary: Does the governance of climate money behave like the governance of a ration card? The Map of Maps of Governance (Tailwinds 2026-02) proposed seven rules for how success and failure move through Indian institutions. This companion to Tailwinds 2026-10 takes the rules out of India for the first time and tests them, in a registered analysis, on the full portfolio of the Green Climate Fund (372 projects, frozen 12 October 2026). Three rules could be tested on the Fund's records; four were declared untestable before any result was seen. One rule holds. Islands: work moved out of the routine, high-discretion track succeeds, and projects on the Fund's Simplified Approval Process reach first disbursement 5.4 months sooner than regular proposals (8.8 against 14.1 months; 90 percent interval −7.3 to −2.9), in every run. Two rules fail. Downhill: delay does not fall harder on the most vulnerable countries (+0.6 months, −2.0 to 2.8). Broker: international intermediaries do not carry more of the money where vulnerability is higher; they carry about four-fifths of it everywhere (79.6 against 81.4 percent). The fast lane is faster, and it is not fairer: inside it, the most vulnerable third of countries waits 1.4 months longer than the least, against 0.2 months on the regular track. The rules travel in part. Where they fail, they fail for a reason the map can use: between countries, a fund's queue runs through its intermediaries, which serve every country alike. The tail that Downhill predicts lies inside countries, where the Fund's record cannot see.
title: The fast lane and the long chain: Why the Green Climate Fund's simplified track speeds money to the ground but does not make it fairer, and what the Map of Maps of Governance learns from its first test outside India

summary: The release behind the five-seed ablation study and its paper. It adds multi-epoch training, an epsilon schedule derived from episode counts, the re-flip restriction and a Gallager-B baseline; it carries the ablation's configurations, generated records and analysis scripts, and the weights of the paper's final policy, so every table, figure and number of the paper regenerates from the repository. The new mechanisms are opt-in, but the 64x128 curricula changed (see Changed), so results are not comparable bit for bit with the 1.1.x series: regenerate rather than mix. Added Five-seed ablation. The design is frozen in docs/ablation/PROTOCOL.md , with the record of how it was run. scripts/make_ablation_configs.py writes its 41 cells under config/ablation_config/ : curriculum and replay seeding crossed, at one and three epochs, on five seeds, plus a one-seed control that holds epsilon at its floor after the first epoch. scripts/aggregate_ablation.py writes docs/ablation/RESULTS.md and RESULTS.json ; scripts/analyze_ablation_details.py writes DETAILS.md , DETAILS.json and learning_curves.csv . config/ablation_checks/ holds the replicate that reproduced a suspended cell bit for bit. Evaluation-only configurations. The pipeline now evaluates a config with no model when it enables baselines explicitly, scoring those alone. Three generated trees use it: config/epoch_eval/ scores the earlier epoch checkpoints of the three-epoch cells ( scripts/make_epoch_eval_configs.py ), config/baseline_eval/ scores Gallager-B on every seed's held-out splits ( scripts/make_baseline_eval_configs.py ), and config/final_eval/ re-scores the final policy from its saved weights ( scripts/make_final_eval_configs.py ). Gallager-B baseline. Hard-input message passing in src/advanced/gallager_b.py , exposed as the gallager_b agent. Its flip thresholds are chosen on training words by scripts/select_gallager_b_thresholds.py , recorded in docs/ablation/GALLAGER_B_SELECTION.md . Decoder cost benchmark. scripts/benchmark_decoders.py measures latency on GPU and CPU, operations per frame and batched throughput for the agent and the baselines, after checking each sampled frame against the recorded evaluation; records go to docs/ablation/benchmark/ . Agent and Min-Sum combined. scripts/cascade_minsum_agent.py runs Min-Sum, the agent on Min-Sum's failures and Min-Sum again; scripts/cascade_controls.py replaces the agent with cheaper alternatives. Records go to docs/ablation/cascade/ . Minimum-distance certificate. scripts/verify_min_distance.py proves $d_{\min} = 14$ for 64x128 by exhaustive enumeration on two information sets, in about a second. The same check identifies the matrix as the CCSDS (128,64) telecommand code. The paper's generators. scripts/paper/ writes every table, figure and quoted number of the paper from the records under docs/ablation/ , in seconds and without a GPU; its README maps the condition IDs to the paper's names. scripts/summarize_development_chain.py , scripts/record_wall_clock.py and scripts/extract_example_episode.py write the remaining records it reads. Final-policy weights. The five trained networks of NoC_NoE3ep (18 MB) under models/ablation/ , so the final policy's evaluation, the cost benchmark and the Min-Sum combination rerun without training. max_errors on uniform_ber . An opt-in cap: the generator redraws any pattern heavier than it, so a BER model can be held inside the code's correction radius. Every 64x128 dataset config sets it to 6. Epochs as a first-class axis. Training is partitioned by (epoch, phase) segment, every training episode carries a run-global episode_id and its epoch , and the training analyses report per epoch. Epsilon fields accept one row per epoch. training.save_epoch_checkpoints keeps the weights at each epoch boundary so epochs can be scored separately. epsilon_decay: "auto_episodes" . Sets epsilon from the fraction of each phase completed, counted in episodes, reaching epsilon_min after epsilon_anne

summary: Medical microbiology occupies an unusual position in the medical curriculum: its objects are almost never seen directly, yet graduates must reason about them from stains, colonies, reaction patterns, and laboratory reports. Methodological guidance in Uzbekistan and the wider Russian-language literature typically responds with lists of criteria for choosing teaching technologies. This article argues that such lists, however sound their individual items, conceal a structural problem, because they treat criteria of different logical kinds as if they could be traded against one another. Using a conceptual model-building design, the study derives eight selection criteria from the literature, sorts them into three tiers (non-compensatory gates, discipline-specific epistemic criteria, and calibration criteria) and applies an explicit 0–2 affordance appraisal to ten teaching technologies. Two of the eight criteria proved relational: they describe a match between a technology and an outcome or a cohort and cannot be scored as properties of the technology. Of the 60 attributable judgements, 26 were conditional rather than direct. Additive totals favoured case analysis, problem-based tasks, and laboratory work, yet only concept mapping and comparison tables cleared both the feasibility and the assessability thresholds unconditionally. The resulting coupling principle holds that a technology chosen for its inferential demand should be paired with one that leaves an assessable trace. The model is offered as an analytic proposal for empirical testing, not as evidence of differential effectiveness.
title: TEACHING THE INVISIBLE: A CONSTRAINT-FIRST DECISION MODEL FOR SELECTING PEDAGOGICAL TECHNOLOGIES IN MEDICAL MICROBIOLOGY

files.key: How Meaning Grows Across Epistemic Gaps.pdf

summary: Encounters among heterogeneous epistemic–praxis systems can expose differences in evidence, interpretation, and practical capacities . Some differences become consequential gaps relative to specified concerns; others sustain complementary ways of knowing . This paper develops a provisional account of generative translation through which situated encounters may enable new meanings and, under more demanding conditions, enduring changes in interpretive or practical capacities . A comparative philosophical analysis draws on hermeneutics, semiotics, pragmatism, social epistemology, evolutionary coordination, and procedural justice while preserving their distinct commitments . The discussion distinguishes representational correspondence, practical reconstruction, and generative translation, then separates interpretive affordance from realized meaning, retained capacity, recurrent convention, and possible normative recognition . Each transition requires different evidence; ordinary learning, resource changes, incentives, and institutional interfaces provide competing explanations for apparent co-evolution . Ethical evaluation concerns task-appropriate fidelity, opportunities for participation and refusal, authority over classifications, affected interests, and the review of consequential decisions . Ceva’s interactive justice and Eglash and Garvey’s generative justice inform distinct aspects of the inquiry, with questions of cross-category standing remaining open to separate justification . Constructed cases and proposed research designs indicate ways to evaluate and challenge the framework . The contribution is an integrative research programme connecting translation-mediated meaning formation with causal scrutiny and ethical responsibility .
title: How Meaning Grows Across Epistemic Gaps: A Discussion of Generative Translation and Its Ethics

summary: Data and code for computational prioritization of MYB–NFIB and MYBL1–NFIB junction peptides in adenoid cystic carcinoma. Same-observation affinity-percentile and unflanked eluted-ligand rank cutoffs of ≤2% select 57 pairs (34 sequences) supported by 27 libraries, including an 11-pair provisional testing panel. The corrected analysis uses a consistent donor-frame translation rule. summary: Version 5.1.0 reproducibility package for “Feasibility and Portability of Model-Based Duty-Cycle Grades for Marine Fuel Cells” by Eun-Hye Park, Hyo-Chan Kwon and Eun-Joo Park. This complete archive contains executable Python sources, synthetic inputs, frozen computational protocols, numerical tables, selected actual simulated waveforms, first-party figures, provenance and independent numerical checks. It preserves all 827 files of the version-5 numerical baseline at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24037253 and adds 16 disclosure and verification files. No scientific model, input, physical threshold, representative selection or original numerical result is changed. New in v5.1: - Complete five-setting, eight-seed stationary non-Gaussian diagnostic results for 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01 and 0.1 Hz plus exact identity transfer, with signed prediction-error means and seed ranges for both telegraph processes and their phase-randomized controls. At 0.01 Hz, the symmetric and asymmetric telegraph mean errors are +94.2606% and +120.1515%. These separate periodic distribution tests are counterexamples to a general Gaussian absolute-increment accuracy claim, not error bounds for physically screened voyages or estimates of physical aging error. - Explicit calculation conventions: 131,072 samples at 4 Hz, the ideal continuous transfer on the periodic Fourier grid, all circular one-second increments at a 0.25-second stride, and no final voyage-reporting Butterworth filter. The final constrained grades continue to use directly evaluated voyage increments and dwell times. - A fresh isolated execution of the unchanged diagnostic. Its 160 raw rows, 20 summary rows and metadata matched the baseline byte for byte; independent reaggregation from the raw moments had a maximum discrepancy of 1.11e-16 in fractional prediction error. - Clarified field-evidence wording: MS Mariella supports ferry installation and ship-network commissioning tests; the separate Pa-X-ell land-module aging observation is not an at-sea aging slope. - Explicit remaining limitations: universal single-coordinate EMS sufficiency and measured aging equivalence are not established; compatible empirical marine coefficient calibration, confidence intervals and covariance are unavailable; the original PLECS project remains unavailable, and no new OpenModelica/PLECS execution has been performed. Start with README_v5_1.md and ADDENDUM_v5_1_EN.md or ADDENDUM_v5_1_KO.md. Run “python -B verify_v5_1.py” for file integrity. Run “python -B disclosure_v5_1/reproduce_diagnostic.py --scratch ../diagnostic_fresh” for a fresh diagnostic; the scratch directory must be new and outside the extracted archive. Integrity checks do not execute scientific calculations. Original numerical exceptions, failure records and previous-version metadata remain preserved. Publication-status clarification: this ZIP is deposited byte-for-byte as prepared before publication. The “local submission supplement”, “no new DOI” and null publication-identifier statements in README_v5_1.md, release_metadata_v5_1.json and the two ADDENDUM_v5_1 files record that preparation-time state. This Zenodo version publishes those identical v5.1 bytes and supersedes only that historical publication-status wording. The version-5 DOI above continues to identify the earlier numerical baseline; the DOI assigned to this record identifies this version-5.1 archive. The record’s current access and publication state are authoritative. Scope: finite synthetic computational assessment under a phenomenological scalar loss index, a lossless battery and reduced oxygen dynamics. No measured vessel dataset, physical stack-aging validation, hardware qualification or universal grade claim is supplied. Manuscripts, response letters and third-party full papers or standards are excluded; included PDF files are first-party computational figures and overviews. License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.
title: Reproducibility package for Feasibility and Portability of Model-Based Duty-Cycle Grades for Marine Fuel Cells

summary: This analysis examines how aggregation and evidence composition shape international comparisons of reported antimalarial treatment failure. Using 244 World Health Organization summaries from 69 countries and territories covering 2010 to 2019, descriptive comparisons assess treatment regimens, parasite species and geographical settings, supplemented by exploratory sample restrictions. The mean reported failure median was 1.87 percent, while 62.30 percent of summaries had zero medians. However, 33.55 percent of zero median summaries contained positive failure maxima, revealing heterogeneity concealed by central values. The ordering of two commonly used regimens reversed across seven country pairs aligned by species, follow up duration and reported study interval bounds. Regional differences persisted within a shared species and treatment category, although means and medians produced different geographical orderings. Restricting observations to summaries representing multiple studies reduced dispersion while preserving a zero median. These findings refine surveillance interpretation by distinguishing favourable central performance from consistency across contributing evidence. International reporting should present distributions, study coverage and comparable analytical groups together to support targeted investigation of elevated failure observations.
title: ASSESSING ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ANTIMALARIAL TREATMENT REGIMENS, PARASITE SPECIES, REGIONAL SETTINGS, AND REPORTED MEDIAN TREATMENT FAILURE

summary: This analysis examines whether national submarine cable provision distinguishes retained international connectivity under infrastructure disruption. Using a 2021 topology snapshot covering 173 countries and territories, 294 international cable systems and 1,262 landing records, it combines bipartite network modelling with exhaustive single cable removal and descriptive comparisons. Mean retention was 99.5917% among units with one cable and 99.9286% among those with two, while all units with at least three shared the same score. Landing diversity provided no consistent additional ordering within comparable redundancy categories. Only 21 of 294 removals fragmented connectivity, and five scenarios accounted for 48.17% of cumulative country pair losses. Shared connecting routes explain how multiple national connections can coexist with dependence on distant infrastructure. Geographical groups differed more in infrastructure provision than in retention. The contribution is a linked assessment of national protection and concentrated network consequences, refining interpretations that equate infrastructure quantity with functional independence. The evidence supports evaluating alternative connections against shared dependencies and reporting critical failure scenarios alongside average resilience scores.
title: ASSESSING GLOBAL INTERNET INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE THROUGH SUBMARINE CABLE NETWORK TOPOLOGY AND SIMULATED FAILURES

summary: Supporting archive for the article Priced Exact Certification under Untrusted Advice: A Price-Induced Consistency Penalty (Zhizhen Zhao, School of Artificial Intelligence and Information Technology, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine). The article studies policies that buy exact fact-bits at declared per-fact prices, may use untrusted advice to decide what to probe, and must end in a mechanically checkable certificate. It proves that under heterogeneous prices, measured against the cheapest certificate of the realized outcome, requiring perfect consistency with correct advice can force worst-case robustness strictly above the optimal prediction-free ratio. This deposit holds the frozen protocol and the complete proofs, the analysis code, the formal checkers, the execution record and the SHA-256 manifests. One command reproduces the reported empirical result: python -I analysis/d9_recompute.py   It recomputes the weighted cost saving S_D9 = 0.070247 and its one-sided 97.5% lower confidence bound 0.044522 from the published ledger alone, and exits non-zero if either differs from the frozen value by more than 1e-9. The pre-registered claim of a saving of at least 10% was not supported. Contents: protocol/ the frozen protocol, theory freeze and complete theorem proofs; analysis/ the analysis code, the frozen result, the de-identified per-root cost ledger and the recompute script; checkers/ the self-contained formal checkers with their recorded output; execution/ the execution reports, the pinned environment and model, the pre-analysis gate and the amendment freezes; provenance/ the SHA-256 manifests of the frozen packages. MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file in the archive with its hash. What is not here. No raw LOTUS or TCM-MKG source tables are redistributed; both sources are public and pinned, TCM-MKG v3 at Zenodo record 19804367 and LOTUS v4 at Zenodo record 7534083. The cost ledger is de-identified: each formula identifier is replaced by an opaque label G01-G40 and the compound key is dropped, while the stratum, the two policy costs and the inclusion weight are carried over unchanged. Because the estimator never reads the identifier, this changes no computed quantity, which the recompute script demonstrates. The co-primary LLM-advice family was determined not validly evaluable under the frozen model, endpoint and protocol, so it has no result to deposit; the figures of the initial, later invalidated execution are not evidence and are absent in every form. Every empirical statement is source-relative: a recorded row establishes only what a frozen version of a public curated source records. No clinical claim is made or supported by anything in this archive. Licensed CC BY 4.0. This covers the content of this deposit only; upstream rights are recorded in protocol/PRISM_RIGHTS_ATTRIBUTION_v1.1.md .
title: PRISM: frozen protocol, analysis code and verification artifacts

summary: ABSTRACT Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of intra-operative frozen section (FS) in the management of abdominal masses and to identify specific technical and interpretive pitfalls that lead to diagnostic discordance. Materials and Methods : This prospective study analyzed 50 cases of abdominal masses at a tertiary care hospital over a two-year period. Intra-operative samples were processed using a cryostat at -20°C to -25°C, stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin, and reported within 30–45 minutes. The FS diagnoses were categorized as benign, malignant, or suspicious and subsequently compared with the gold standard paraffin-embedded sections (PS). Statistical parameters, including sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values, were calculated. Results: Of the 50 cases, 29 (58%) were malignant and 21 (42%) were benign. The gallbladder was the most frequent site of involvement (40%), followed by ovarian and gastrointestinal lesions. FS demonstrated an overall diagnostic accuracy of 98%, with a sensitivity of 96.5% and a specificity of 100% for the detection of malignancy. One case of discordance was noted in a large, multi-loculated ovarian tumor, where a focal borderline component was under-diagnosed as benign on FS due to sampling limitations. The positive predictive value was 100%, and the negative predictive value was 95.4%. Conclusion : Intra-operative frozen section is a highly reliable diagnostic modality for abdominal masses, providing rapid and actionable results that directly influence surgical strategy. While it is nearly infallible for most solid malignancies, cautious interpretation and extensive sampling are required for complex cystic ovarian lesions to minimize the risk of underdiagnosis.   Keywords: Frozen section, intraoperative diagnosis, diagnostic accuracy, abdominal masses, histopathology
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Intra-operative Frozen Section in Abdominal Masses: A Prospective Study from a Tertiary Care Hospital

summary: This dataset provides the frozen derived bibliographic data, executable analysis code, verification tests, annual results and figures supporting a measurement audit of historical crossover claims in molecular-marker research (1960–2025). It integrates 155,834 eligible work–marker associations, 33 related baseline and exact single-label-omission annual series, and the descriptive finite-panel critical margin frontier F(t). The annual minimum identifies the limiting specification and its year-specific eligible-work population; it is not a trajectory from one unchanged cohort. The package reproduces downstream analyses from frozen eligible records, including baseline persistence, SNP-removal sensitivity, full one-label-omission audits, reported marginal thresholds and Figures 1–3 and S1. It provides offline verification, file-level SHA-256 checksums, data documentation and source-archive provenance digests. The original full OpenAlex retrieval and historical v5 classifier configuration, independently adjudicated method-use labels and the earlier baseline v1.0.0 archive are not included. Accordingly, the results are conditional on archived classification decisions and do not establish validated dates of laboratory-method adoption, sampling confidence intervals or the performance of a reader-facing reporting intervention.

summary: This analysis examines how adaptive computation configurations relate to classification accuracy in language models, informing international debates on computational efficiency. A descriptive reanalysis uses 20 published configuration results from Chinese Book review and English Yelp.P benchmarks reported in 2020, comparing routing arrangements, exit thresholds, and matched distillation settings. Adaptive routing exceeds selected fixed depth alternatives by 0.56 to 2.81 percentage points, with fewer operations in all three computationally usable comparisons. Raising exit thresholds reduces accuracy across both benchmarks, while endpoint computational reductions range from 62.77 to 77.87 percent among usable comparisons. Self-distillation improves accuracy in all four matched pairs, averaging 0.478 percentage points, with larger advantages for Book review. Accuracy losses concentrate differently across threshold intervals, indicating benchmark dependent stopping costs. These descriptive patterns distinguish selective processing, prediction acceptance, and intermediate supervision as complementary configuration decisions. The contribution refines the resource allocation perspective through transparent comparisons of existing evidence. Deployment teams should evaluate threshold intervals separately and compare accuracy alongside verified computational requirements within each intended task.
title: ADAPTIVE INFERENCE THRESHOLDS AND SELF-DISTILLATION SHAPE CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY ACROSS COMPUTATIONALLY CONSTRAINED LANGUAGE MODEL BENCHMARKS

summary: This analysis examines whether privacy vulnerability rankings remain consistent across text reconstruction procedures, informing international debates on federated learning security. A descriptive secondary analysis uses 72 published benchmark conditions from 2024, covering three attacks, two transformer configurations, three text benchmarks and four batch sizes. Matched comparisons hold the remaining experimental dimensions constant. DAGER exceeds TAG and LAMP in all 24 matched conditions, with average advantages of 61.62 and 49.79 ROUGE 1 score points, respectively. LAMP exceeds TAG in 23 conditions. Increasing batch size from one to eight coincides with lower reconstruction throughout the TAG and LAMP comparisons, whereas DAGER retains ceiling performance on GPT 2 and deteriorates on BERT. Model rankings consequently reverse across attacks. These patterns indicate that aggregation constrains recoverability conditionally rather than providing uniform protection. The contribution is a comparative synthesis showing that observed vulnerability depends on reconstruction capability and model configuration, without establishing causal mechanisms. Organizations should evaluate multiple attacks under matched conditions and distinguish unigram recovery from comprehensive disclosure when interpreting privacy claims.
title: GRADIENT EXPOSURE CONDITIONS AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION VULNERABILITY IN FEDERATED FOUNDATION MODELS ACROSS PUBLISHED BENCHMARK EXPERIMENTS

summary: Decentralised peacebuilding councils are widely promoted as a means of rebuilding citizen trust in post-conflict states, yet the evidence base for their effectiveness rests largely on observational comparisons that cannot separate the councils' effects from the selection of communities into them. Using a before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and a residual standard deviation of 4.5, the analysis estimates power across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design achieves 80 per cent power to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 56 clusters, a requirement that exceeds the number of municipal units typically available in a single Ivorian region. The regression-discontinuity approach is defensible in principle but fragile in practice, and that its value lies less in producing a definitive estimate than in disciplining claims about what decentralised peacebuilding can plausibly achieve.

summary: Complete research archive for the study of natural-product label errors in ChEMBL CYP inhibition data: the input extract, the curation files, every intermediate result, and the analysis scripts that produced the figures and tables in the article and its supporting information. The study examines a natural-product flag inherited from COCONUT through ChEMBL, across 14,598 compound-isoform IC50 pairs for 9,347 compounds. Of 500 compounds carrying the flag, 138 (27.6%) were excluded by a criterion combining absent provenance in LOTUS with a synthetic structural signature, together with review of the compounds that criterion retained. The excluded compounds were disproportionately potent inhibitors, and the association survives adjustment for molecular size, testing intensity, aromatic ring count and an independent natural-product-likeness score for the compounds identified individually from structure. Version 1.2.0 adds the material prepared for the first revision. The curation criterion is now validated in both directions against external standards. Against the Natural Products Atlas (version 2024_09), 36,453 compounds curated by hand from the primary isolation literature and independent of both resources the criterion uses, the full rule removes 262: a false-positive rate of 0.72% (95% CI 0.64-0.81%). In a random sample of 50 of the 362 retained compounds, classified independently by two of the authors, 20 are fully synthetic: a false-negative rate of 40% (95% CI 28-54%), with inter-rater agreement of Cohen's kappa 0.83 (0.69-0.96) over four origin classes and 0.92 (0.79-1.00) on the binary question. Because the two rates differ by roughly fifty-fold, the 27.6% is a floor on the mislabeling rate in this dataset rather than an estimate of it. This version also adds a twenty-four-setting sensitivity sweep of the criterion, calibration of the predicted probabilities against the training base rate, the per-isoform decomposition of the curation effect into removal and retraining, the potency association under four compound-level aggregations, and a covariate for how often each compound has been studied. summary: I study an inverse problem for one-dimensional Brownian-compatible diffusions in which multiple probe responses are observed with independent, unknown multiplicative gains. The central question is whether the shared differential structure of the underlying generator can replace external gain calibration. For a diffusion generator Lq f = q(θ)f ′′(θ) + 1 2 q′(θ)f ′(θ), q > 0, the response to each prescribed probe is available only up to an unknown positive gain. I first estab- lish that a single nonconstant Morse probe uniquely and coercively identifies its gain-weighted dif- fusion coefficient. I then show that two nondegenerate probes determine their relative gain through a scalar compatibility relation implied by the Brownian drift–diffusion constraint. This yields an explicit reconstruction of the diffusion profile up to its unavoidable common scale, represented by a normalized inverse-square-root profile. Under quantitative nondegeneracy assumptions, the recon- structed profile depends locally Lipschitz-continuously on the observations. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction procedure and its behavior under smooth response perturbations. I also describe a conditional connection with planar convex geometry. The results provide a generator-specific mechanism for blind relative-gain calibration and projective identification from probe-response functions without trajectory observations
title: Blind Gain Calibration in Brownian-Compatible Diffusions

summary: This analysis examines whether scientific abstract characteristics distinguish supporting from refuting evidence, addressing the interpretation of document presentation in scientific verification. Using the 2020 SciFact benchmark, it analyses 773 annotated claim document pairs covering 693 claims and 437 abstracts through descriptive comparisons, document weighting and partition sensitivity checks. Refuting pairs contain abstracts averaging 32.46 words longer than supporting pairs. The refuting share is 14.1 percentage points higher among structured abstracts, while mean relative evidence position differs by only 0.007. Equal document weighting preserves these pooled directions, but length and structure differences narrow substantially in the development partition. Furthermore, 179 abstracts support some claims and refute others despite unchanged document characteristics. These findings distinguish document presentation from the semantic relationship between evidence and a specific claim. The contribution is a descriptive account of how pooled presentation patterns coexist with partition sensitivity and claim dependent stance. Evidence services and benchmark developers should preserve claim specific provenance and disclose document overlap and weighting choices when reporting aggregate comparisons.
title: SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE CHARACTERISTICS AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH SUPPORTIVE VERSUS REFUTING ATTRIBUTION IN AUTOMATED CLAIM VERIFICATION

summary: The article addresses the problem of improving the technical preparedness of 13–15-year-old female volleyball players through a differentiated training approach. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that athletes of the same chronological age may differ considerably in biological maturation, anthropometric characteristics, coordination abilities, physical fitness, rate of motor skill acquisition, and the structure of technical errors. Therefore, the use of identical training loads and technical tasks for all adolescent players may reduce the effectiveness of technical preparation. The study substantiates a methodological system based on the sequence diagnostics → differentiated grouping → adapted technical exercises → individualized feedback → control → correction. Particular attention is paid to the differentiation of exercise complexity, number of repetitions, distance, speed, time pressure, and game-related decision-making requirements. The proposed methodology is aimed at improving technical accuracy, stability, movement coordination, application of technical actions under game conditions, and reducing recurrent technical errors. The article also describes criteria for evaluating technical preparedness and offers a weekly microcycle for differentiated volleyball training.
