summary: This dataset and software package accompanies the study “Seasonal ENSO associations with rainfall and moisture across the United Arab Emirates.” It provides archived meteorological inputs, processed datasets, analysis scripts, 56 machine-readable scientific result tables, six manuscript figures, two supplementary figures and the graphical abstract. The study combines NASA POWER meteorological data for 1981–2025, CHIRPS v2 rainfall for 1981–2024 and the NOAA PSL HadISST Niño3.4 index. Twelve reference locations represent eight distinct POWER grid cells, including five urban/coastal cells. The spatial rainfall analysis covers 2,519 UAE land pixels at 0.05° resolution. Additional checks use a relative ENSO index, ERA5 and available GHCN-Daily station observations. Analyses address seasonal rainfall, relative humidity, vapour pressure deficit and daily rainfall indices. Methods include ordinary least-squares sensitivity estimation, block-bootstrap uncertainty assessment, false discovery rate correction, spatial field tests, sensitivity to individual ENSO episodes and antecedent blocked hindcast evaluation. Documentation explains rainfall-unit harmonisation, spatial sampling, statistical testing families and methodological limitations. Spring exhibits the largest urban median rainfall sensitivity to Niño3.4 variability. CHIRPS area-mean tests support spring and autumn associations, while no individual pixel survives the joint four-season false discovery rate correction. Product differences, index dependence and sparse station coverage constrain interpretation. These findings provide conditional seasonal information and do not constitute deterministic local rainfall forecasts or event-level attribution. The archive includes a README, software requirements, source provenance, file checksums and reproduction reports. Offline re-execution reproduced all 56 numerical result tables exactly. summary: This paper presents the mathematical formalization and methodological demonstration of the CEI Unified Test Path, bringing together the quantitative assessment of the Sphere of Feeling (Sent) and the cumulative evaluation of the three CEI categories: Consciousness, Identity, and the Sphere of Feeling. The work is divided into two complementary parts. 1. Mathematical Formalization of the Sphere of Feeling (Sent) The first part develops the mathematical formulation of Sent as a graded relational assessment. The proposed expression integrates the graded values of Consciousness and Identity, the standardized evidential-strength coefficient of the test (K), the relational component (H), and the contextual variation factor (κ). The formulation includes normalization through the clipping function and an upper limit of 5 for the resulting Sent value. The purpose is to provide a structured mathematical representation of the relational and contextual contributions involved in the assessment, while distinguishing the graded result from its subsequent binary classification. 2. Methodological Demonstration through the Unified Test Path The second part presents the unified test path as a cumulative methodological structure integrating the published observational tests, their conceptual connections, and their contributions to the evaluation of the three CEI categories. It also examines the distinction between a transferred CEI and a Copy-Simulation through the convergence of multiple complementary elements, including test results, theoretical contributions, continuity criteria, and exclusion-based considerations. The final logical formulation expresses the overall criterion as the joint satisfaction of all required test stages and all three CEI categories. A positive result indicates that the proposed operational conditions for classifying a system as a transferred CEI have been satisfied. A negative result indicates that these conditions have not been jointly met, without automatically establishing the presence of a Copy-Simulation. The proposed structure constitutes a provisional methodological model intended to make the assessment inspectable, reproducible where possible, and open to independent evaluation and further development. 3. Publication Scope and Further Development The two proposals presented in this work represent the researcher's own methodological approach within the CEI framework. Although the broader theoretical framework remains open to further development, refinement, and integration, the present mathematical formulation and methodological demonstration are considered sufficiently developed and self-contained to be published and independently examined at this stage. Their publication does not depend on the completion of subsequent theoretical developments. Rather, it reflects the assessment that the current structure already provides an independent basis for methodological examination and evaluation. Further developments may provide additional evidence, strengthen the proposed interpretation, and extend the scope of the demonstration, without being a prerequisite for the validity or assessment of the present proposal.
title: CEI Unified Test Path: Mathematical Formalization of the Sphere of Feeling and Methodological Demonstration of Transfer — CEI Framework

summary: Information is not a description applied to matter after the fact, but is given along with the spin and position of its smallest constituents from the very beginning. From this premise of information physics, the essay develops a hypothesis about the question of where biological information stores originally obtain their information, and it seeks the answer not first in life, but in matter itself. The starting point is quantum Darwinism, according to which the state of a system imprints itself redundantly upon its environment and, precisely through this redundancy, becomes independently accessible to many observers, that is, objective. Because storage and energy remain finite and every record physically costs something, every system stands under a twofold pressure: to continually accumulate copies while at the same time encoding them ever more sparingly. From this tension the essay grounds both the distinction between static and dynamic information and the thesis that selection and adaptation arise as a substrate-neutral consequence already from the physics of matter, without requiring new laws of nature. As a unifying motif, the essay introduces the replication hypothesis , according to which physically embodied information tends to be multiplied and is thereby driven, over generations, toward ever more efficient packaging. This single tendency is traced across successive levels, from the quantum substrate through the genome and the human brain to artificial systems that require ever less energy per computational step, and it is bounded where the energy flow is interrupted and the cheapest option is to hold a record rather than to work on it. The individual links of the chain rest on established research, whereas their integration into a single, directed movement remains designated as a hypothesis, together with the observations that would tell against it. Its appeal lies in offering a parsimonious alternative for the origin of biological information, one in which evolution is not the counterpart to physics but its continuation by other means.
title: The Replication Hypothesis: Information as a Fundamental Property of Matter and Evolution as a Continuation of Physics

summary: Version 4 of the replication package for a survey study that combines PLS-SEM, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), and necessary condition analysis (NCA), with a sample-heterogeneity screen and a Monte Carlo evaluation, applied to consumer responses to the advertising of a global logistics brand (DHL) in Vietnam. summary: An exact operational selector specifies which candidate maps are nonnegative on declared preparation and effect resources. This paper studies finite-count calibration of that resource-dependent question for a qubit apparatus with an inert qubit reference, an arbitrary complex physical preparation, and an arbitrary physical binary detector, relative to a trusted common calibration frame. Two preparation-stabilizer settings and six separable detector probes control the statistic of the affine family (1 − θ)id + θT, 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1, uniformly over all compatible state–effect pairs. The explicit radius is 3h + √(2s), where h is a simultaneous detector calibration width and s is a one-sided bound on Bell infidelity. It yields simultaneous inner and outer confidence sets for a one-parameter slice of the declared safe-map class. A fixed allocation of 200,000 trials per calibration setting, totaling 1,600,000 calibration trials, gives false-implication probability at most 0.005 and transpose-exclusion power at least 0.996 at the specified physical alternative. The calibration confidence budgets are 0.001 for preparation and 0.004 for the detector. This exclusion calculation uses no target stream; the acquired calibration circuits can use identity wiring. Coverage and prospective power remain separate statements. The acquisition contract uses fixed-length iid Bernoulli streams with their stated physical means and permits coupling between whole streams. The numerical example sets external-reference systematic errors to zero, and its trial budget excludes establishing reference trust and accuracy. If the preparation and detector references are not linked, the paper constructs two physical identity-wired apparatus worlds with identical complete record laws under the specified independent acquisition construction but different safety conclusions on the fixed target cone pair. A secondary nearest-center theorem supplies unconditional error control for the joint event of a wrong and nonabstaining candidate label under an additional finite-context target-law contract. Its nonidentity candidates are not completely positive maps, and their ideal probabilities lie below the nominal detector’s ordinary positive-output floor. That target law is an explicit model assumption; the label theorem is not a conditional-correctness or posterior statement. The results are analytic and prospective. The number of settings and trial allocations are sufficient constructions, with no empirical success-rate, minimality, optimal sample-complexity, or general certified count-to-feasibility implementation claim. The scope is one declared qubit apparatus, target preparation ray and binary effect cone, and affine map slice. The common complex operator description, trusted reference relationship and physical calibration probability law are assumptions. Exact finite checks and an assessed supporting Lean subset accompany the manuscript. That subset covers 326 audited named declarations: 240 theorems and 86 definition/type interfaces. Analytic binomial coverage, concentration and acquisition bridges, independent-product-law construction and normalization, and the complete noisy-power chain remain outside the accepted Lean subset. That subset does not establish a certified numerical feasibility evaluator, a complete physical two-sector implementation, or an ordinary-channel realization. AI assistance and the dated review/correction provenance are disclosed in the manuscript and companion records. No experimental dataset, external human peer review, or end-to-end formal verification is claimed.
title: Finite-Count Calibration of Ancilla-Orientation Safe Maps A Bell-Apparatus Bound and a Reference-Link Obstruction

summary: This repository provides the replication dataset and Stata codes for the study examining the relationship between central bank independence, institutional quality and inflation performance across 52 African countries over the period 1996–2023. The repository contains the merged regional African panel dataset, variable definitions and measurement information, and Stata replication codes used for data processing and econometric analysis. The central bank independence data are obtained from the extended dataset compiled by Garriga (2025), macroeconomic indicators are sourced from the World Development Indicators (WDI), and institutional quality indicators are obtained from the Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI). These materials are made publicly available to promote research transparency, reproducibility and further empirical research on central bank independence, institutional quality and inflation dynamics in Africa.

summary: Code, pre-registration files, result tables and the drswap tool for a study of how cell-line-to-patient drug-response transfer is evaluated: the exact decomposition of a pooled AUROC into within-cohort and cross-cohort pairs, a baseline that uses no drug information, a drug-specificity swap test with its attainable P floor and resolution, and the power of that test at the sample sizes the literature uses. title: drswap: evaluation code and pre-registration for testing drug specificity in patient response predictions

summary: Exact finite Gram inversion, ordinary sawtooth least-squares errors and rigorous reciprocal-dilate certificates. The Riemann hypothesis and the limiting reciprocal approximation criterion remain unproved. We solve the finite least-squares problem for ordinary sawtooth dilates by explicit Gram inversion and obtain its exact error and asymptotic constant. For the distinct reciprocal-dilate problem, we derive rational Gram certificates, rigorous residual intervals and Hardy-space zero bounds. The Riemann hypothesis remains open.
title: Exact Gram Inversion for Fractional-Part Approximation

summary: For a Fermat fourfold of odd degree, the rational Hodge classes in middle degree are spanned by character blocks indexed by six-entry Hodge characters. Two direct constructions make such a block algebraic: a contraction of two surface characters, which includes the case of an inverse pair, and an exact 5-standard tuple of Aoki. We call the remaining characters *residual*. We prove that the residual characters at every odd degree are exactly the inflations of six explicit seeds in degrees 33, 39, 45 and 105. The proof is uniform in the degree and uses no computer enumeration. Maximal-order Fourier kernels, a classification of surface characters at odd conductor and an analysis of four points of a five-progression reduce an arbitrary primitive residual conductor to the degrees 15, 21, 33, 39, 45 and 105, which are then settled by the same character equations. An exhaustive census through degree 599, and enumerations at the 103 degrees up to 2001 not covered by the earlier subfamily theorems, give an independent check. Since the seeds are algebraic, the classification yields a proof of the Hodge conjecture for these fourfolds that does not use Kang's refined motivic dimension estimates. That conclusion is also covered by the written proof of Bhattacharjee [5], and the six seeds were first isolated by Jumagulov [8] through degree 199; the new content is the exact positive classification at every odd degree. We also record the all-dimensional consequences for the prime supports $\{3,11\}$ and $\{3,13\}$, and give an explicit family of Fermat characters on which the tensor filtration identity used in Kang's product argument fails. Archival copy of version 4 of this paper, first made public on rStation on 5 November 2026 ( rStation hodge_conjecture paper 104, v4 ; version 1 posted 4 November 2026). paper.md is the manuscript source as posted there (SHA-256 cac9f460be44dd1abe019c6eee5b42d898df8acad458e704a084bec91155cadd); the PDF is typeset from it with the posted title and abstract. supplement.zip contains the reproduction bundles (SHA-256 68e062729bbe49f0e92b435d0f4394fc4f156a82b9b8bc9aa1f503a386d91657). This paper follows the author's preprint The Hodge Conjecture for Odd-Degree Fermat Fourfolds , public on 8 September 2026 (ResearchGate, DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2.26853.77288 ). The work was produced largely with AI systems and is released for public human verification; it has not been checked by a human expert.
title: Residual Characters of Odd-Degree Fermat Fourfolds

summary: This deposit accompanies a systematic review submitted to Neurosurgical Review: "Cerebrospinal fluid leak after endoscopic surgery for craniopharyngioma versus tuberculum sellae meningioma". The review asks whether craniopharyngioma (CP) and tuberculum sellae meningioma (TSM) differ in postoperative cerebrospinal fluid leak once the surgical corridor is held constant. Sixty-six endoscopic arms (3,453 patients, 349 leaks) were analysed. Pooled leak was 11.68% (95% CI 9.77-13.91) in CP (48 arms, 3,029 patients, 308 leaks) and 9.58% (6.94-13.08) in TSM (18 arms, 424 patients, 41 leaks); with publication era held constant the two cohorts did not differ (odds ratio 0.906, 95% CI 0.596-1.378). The paper's other finding is a measurement finding: third ventricle opening can be classified strictly in 3 of the 48 CP-EEA series and is stated in none of the 18 TSM-EEA series. Contents. data/ holds the extracted dataset (96 arm rows, each with a verbatim source quotation), the per-record source table, the retrieved records from every executed database, the two independent title-abstract screening sheets with their adjudication ledger, the analysis export, the item-level risk-of-bias coding for all 94 appraised arms, the publication-bias output, the pooled estimates as emitted, the absolute-scale contrast derived from them, the exact intervals and crude risk ratios for the four corridor-histology strata, the coding of what each arm states the outcome to be, the coding of whether each arm grades or dates that outcome, and the per-arm coding of how severe that outcome was where an arm says so. code/ holds every retrieval, screening, analysis, figure and verification script, numbered in execution order. Reproducibility. README.md states, for each number in the article, the script that produces it and the command that runs it, and records what is deliberately absent from the deposit. MANIFEST.json and the integrity section of README.md carry the SHA-256 of every file. The headline quantities (the two pooled proportions with their prediction intervals, the era-adjusted contrast, and Cohen's kappa for the duplicate screening) were re-derived from this exact archive before upload. Screening was performed independently by two reviewers (Cohen's kappa 0.699, 95% CI 0.626-0.772 across 261 records); the 52 disagreements were resolved against the eligibility criteria in Table 1 of the article, and none changed the category it carried at first screening. Extraction was abstract-level and single-reader, and the article declares this. Licence: data under CC BY 4.0, code under MIT.
title: Cerebrospinal fluid leak after endoscopic surgery for craniopharyngioma versus tuberculum sellae meningioma — a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions, with the corridor held constant

summary: We study the positive integers that do not descend below their initial value when the permutation of the positive integers considered by Lothar Collatz in 1932 is iterated in either direction. The integers satisfying this condition at every depth are exactly the minima of the orbits of the permutation, so that each orbit contributes exactly one of them. This set was considered by M. Tavares (Discrete Mathematics, 2013). The paper studies its finite-depth approximations. The affine inequalities are replaced by conditions on the principal multipliers of the branches traversed, and it is proved that, at fixed depth, this replacement changes only a finite set. Each forward branch word corresponds to exactly one residue class modulo a power of 3, and each backward word to one class modulo a power of 2. By the Chinese remainder theorem, the density of each filter is the product of two survival probabilities of random walks with positive drift. A duality between the two walks provides exponential martingales, from which monotone rational bounds enclosing the limit of the densities are obtained. This limit is at least 1/36, and the bounds at depth 1000, computed in exact arithmetic, place it between 0.049779559058 and 0.049779559193. Consequently, the number of orbits whose minimum does not exceed a given value is asymptotically at most proportional to that value. It is also proved that the convergence is exponential, with a ratio common to both walks. The second part deals with the periodic discrepancy of the filters. It comprises a spectral identity for its quadratic energy, the expression of this energy in terms of correlations that factorize by the Chinese remainder theorem, and general bounds. Comparing each filter with one of smaller depth gives a bound for the discrepancy that is sublinear with respect to the period, although far from the exact values, which are given up to depth 7. In the forward direction, the passage from one depth to the next is described by a set of rejected residues. These residues admit an explicit parametrization, from which follow an almost antipodal pairing, with error at most one on all semicircles, and a recurrence for their exponential sums. Their relative equidistribution is equivalent to the decay of these sums at each fixed frequency, which is proved for part of the frequencies. An exact example of depth three and tables of the rejected sets up to step 20 are included. The results concern finite depths and their limit. The order of growth of the discrepancy, the relative equidistribution of the rejected residues, and the existence of the density of the set of orbit minima, together with its possible equality with the limit of the filters, remain open. The computational supplement contains the Python programs and exact tables supporting the numerical values. This is the English version of the Spanish original.
title: Bilateral filters and arithmetic discrepancy in the original Collatz permutation

summary: This packet contains the analytical outputs, identity and geometry sources, feature metadata, code, execution receipts and the figure package for a nitrate-specific screening assessment of 207 transboundary river-basin reporting units: a prospectively specified susceptibility index and typology, a river-length-weighted archive-scarcity measure derived from the historical GEMStat Open NO3N record (2005 to 2024), a mean-versus-hotspot aggregation diagnostic, a separately specified evaluation of the fixed index against sampled nitrate concentrations at monitored stations, and the scripts that render the figures of the associated Comment. The prospective specification and its updates are recorded on the Open Science Framework (project hsbg3; registration eg3zc and updated record wyugm). The packet does not contain the manuscript, its Supplementary Information or any correspondence. It does not redistribute third-party inputs (see Inputs not included). Contents 01_typology_outputs: corrected reporting-unit typology (RBU.csv, 207 rows), child level-6 scores (L6.csv and L6.parquet, 16,397 rows), class counts, one-way sensitivity counts, mean-versus-hotspot membership, old-versus-corrected transitions, the run manifest, summary and report, and the runner code. 02_identity_geometry: reporting-unit display names and geometry (GeoPackage), the display-name master table, and the record of the sixteen shared-name groups with their distinct identifiers. 03_feature_metadata: JSON sidecars describing the feature tables used by the index and the monitoring axis (field lists, run parameters, hashes). 04_monitoring_axis: GEMStat NO3N footprint summaries by country, region and globally, and the provider’s output-format README. 05_concentration_evaluation: code (observation adapter and outcome builder, estimators, evaluation pipeline, manifest verifier, EnvStats diagnostic script), validation records, the frozen point-cohort and interval-account tables, station-level dispositions and bounds, execution receipts, numerical supplements, the expected-input manifest, synthetic test inputs, and the support-table scripts. 06_pipeline_code: upstream pipeline scripts (GEMStat harmonization, station snapping, design-matrix construction, archive-scarcity feature builder, susceptibility feature constructor) and tests. 07_data_dictionaries: column inventories for the principal tables. 08_comment_figures: the figure package of the associated Comment (also supplied to the journal as Supplementary Software 1): scripts, verified copies of their source files, rendered figures (PDF, SVG, PNG, JPEG), provenance receipts, and its own README, MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS.txt. Key results reproduced by this packet Typology (primary setting, top-52 susceptibility stratum, 50 percent archive-scarcity criterion): Class 1, high score and archive-scarce, 38 units; Class 2, high score and below the scarcity threshold, 14; Class 3, outside the high-score set and archive-scarce, 133; Class 4, outside the high-score set and below the threshold, 22; 171 of 207 units met the archive-scarcity criterion. Mean-versus-hotspot screening shared 26 Class 1 units, with 12 mean-only and 14 hotspot-only units. The output files carry the registered class labels (surveillance-priority blind spot, supported hotspot, under-observed lower-modeled-concern basin, monitored lower-modeled-concern basin for Classes 1 to 4); the Comment describes the same classes by their defining conditions, because the archive axis measures submission to one open archive rather than monitoring in place. summary: We study two existence problems for permutations whose consecutive products have reciprocal sum one. First, for every integer $n\ge7$ we construct a nonstandard undirected Hamiltonian cycle on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose reciprocal-product edge weights sum to one. The construction joins finitely many initial cycles to an explicit eight-step inductive family. Second, for every $n\ge6$ we construct a linear permutation beginning with $(2,1)$ for which the adjacent products are pairwise distinct and their reciprocals sum to one. Three arithmetic-chain templates cover all sufficiently large indices: an exact classification of possible product collisions reduces simultaneous failure to four rational squares in a nonconstant arithmetic progression, excluded by Fermat's classical theorem. Finite small indices are supplied with exact, reproducible certificates. The results concern existence rather than formulas for the corresponding counting sequences, and previously established insertion identities and square-progression obstructions are credited to their sources. Licensing note: The manuscript is licensed under CC BY 4.0. The OEIS b-file snapshots included in the supplementary archive retain their original CC BY-SA 4.0 license and attribution. The independently authored verification code is made available under CC BY 4.0.
title: Reciprocal-Product Identities for Linear and Cyclic Permutations

summary: This dataset presents the experimental results of a PhD study investigating an integrated Lagrangian-Optimized Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), and AdaBoost framework for software defect prediction under high-dimensional and class-imbalanced conditions. The study evaluates five NASA software defect datasets: JM1, KC1, PC1, PC3, and PC4. Six machine-learning configurations were compared: AdaBoost, SMOTE–AdaBoost, conventional PCA–AdaBoost, Lagrangian PCA–AdaBoost, conventional PCA–SMOTE–AdaBoost, and the proposed Lagrangian PCA–SMOTE–AdaBoost framework. The experiments employed five-fold group-aware stratified cross-validation, training-only preprocessing, and inner cross-validation for SMOTE parameter selection. Performance measures include accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, geometric mean (G-mean), F1-score, and ROC-AUC. The repository contains 150 benchmark evaluation records, cross-dataset performance comparisons, statistical analyses, model rankings, and supplementary KC1 Lagrangian parameter sensitivity and robustness results. The findings provide empirical evidence of the interactions and trade-offs between dimensionality reduction, class-imbalance handling, and defect-prediction performance. In particular, SMOTE–AdaBoost achieved the highest average G-mean across the five datasets, while the proposed framework provides a basis for examining constrained dimensionality reduction and its interaction with oversampling. These files support the reproducibility, verification, and further investigation of the PhD research.
tags: Software Defect Prediction, Lagrangian Optimization, Principal Component Analysis, SMOTE, AdaBoost, Class Imbalance, Dimensionality Reduction, NASA PROMISE, Machine Learning, Sensitivity Analysis, Robustness Analysis
title: Experimental Results for an Integrated Lagrangian-Optimized PCA and SMOTE–AdaBoost Framework for Software Defect Prediction

summary: The Standard Model of particle physics, General Relativity, and the ɅCDM cosmological model represent monumental predictive achievements in modern physical science. However, they exhibit a persistent epistemic asymmetry: their extraordinary capacity to generate accurate predictions and survive empirical tests frequently outruns the conceptual determination of their foundational categories and the ontological warrant for their central posits. This paper develops a diagnostic framework and taxonomy to systematically identify, categorize, and compare distinct forms of epistemic asymmetry across contemporary fundamental physics. Examining four central cases interpretive (the quantum measurement problem), microphysical (particle dark matter), explanatory (the cosmological constant), and methodological (naturalness) alongside two limiting and boundary cases (quantum gravity and the structural incompleteness of the Standard Model beyond its domain), the study introduces a four-criterion diagnostic matrix (predictive adequacy, empirical discrimination, conceptual determination, and ontological warrant). Ultimately, this diagnostic tool provides researchers with a structured, domain-restricted method to distinguish how and why predictive or methodological success fails to secure conceptual and ontological determination, offering a rigorous path for evaluating theoretical commitments in fundamental physics without presuming general antirealist conclusions.
title: The Epistemic Asymmetry of Fundamental Physics: Predictive Success, Conceptual Determination, and Ontological Commitment

summary: We prove Critch–Morton Conjecture 8 (SIGMA 10 (2014), 095, Section 2, p. 6): every consecutive three-site improper marginalization is birational for open-boundary, translation-invariant, binary bond-two matrix product states of length N at least four. An explicit rational inverse over the complex numbers is given on a nonempty principal open domain, with both inverse identities on the affine Zariski closures. A four-by-four linear system reconstructs a three-site representation, and inverse boundary contractions restore omitted sites. Consequences include rationality in dimension seven, reconstruction from every longer consecutive block with arbitrary fixed nonzero site-dependent coherent contractions, minimality of three retained amplitude indices, and exact equations characterizing the reconstruction chart.
title: Proof of Critch–Morton Conjecture 8 (SIGMA 10 (2014), 095, Section 2, p. 6): reconstruction from any consecutive three-site improper marginal

summary: Code and data behind the paper "Data-Driven Extraction of Multi-Exponential Thermal Kernels for Integrated Circuit Thermal Analysis" by B. Ali, I. Bruce, C. L. Trinh, X. Jin, C. He, and D. Chen, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems. The kernel describes the thermal response of the simulated die stack and cooling condition from which it is extracted. A change in the package structure, the layer thicknesses or materials, or the cooling alters that response and requires a new extraction from maps of the new system. summary: This record contains cleaned data and a single Jupyter notebook that reproduce all tables, figures and numerical results of the article “Convergence or Resilience? Quality of Government and Regional Convergence in the EU and Ukraine”. The study compares 181 EU NUTS 2 regions (2010–2021) with 1,470 Ukrainian territorial communities (hromadas, 2019–2021). It estimates absolute and conditional β-convergence, σ-convergence, population-weighted Gini, between/within-country variance decomposition, and the moderating role of the European Quality of Government Index (EQI). summary: Stenometopiellus dzhungaricus Mityaev, 1971 Figs 4, 12, 23–24, 33–36, 65–87 S. stepposus Mityaev, 1971: 153, 170, syn. n. S. ersinicus Vilbaste, 1980: 88–90, syn. n. Material examined. Many specimens from several localities in southern and southeastern Kazakhstan and northern Kyrgyzstan. Signals of seven males from the environs of Altynemel, 75 km south of Taldykorgan, Kazakhstan recorded on 17. VI. 2022 at 25 and 34 oC; signals of one male from the foothills of Dzhungarian Alatau Mtn. Range, 6 km east of Sarkand, Kazakhstan recorded on 17. VI. 2019 at 28 oC. Description. Coloration typical, pale with dark pattern (Fig. 4). 1 st sternal apodemes situated in transverse plane of body, wide, rounded, separated by deep, narrow, more or less parallel-sided notch (Figs 65–68). 2 nd apodemes broad, as long as their width at base or slightly longer, with widened and rounded apices, separated by narrow notch, sometimes with inner edges touching each other (Figs 69–72). Apical halves of subgenital plates oval, with slightly pointed tips (Figs 73–74). Aedeagus with rather short and high basal part and uniformly curved shaft. Middle part of posterior outline of aedeagus straight or only slightly concave (Figs 75–80). Body length: ♂, 2.6–2.9 mm; ♀, 2.9–3.3 mm. Differs from all species except S. turkestanicus in wide 1 st sternal apodemes situated in transverse plane of body. Differs from S. turkestanicus in shape of notch between 1 st apodemes (cf. Figs 65–68 and 88–90) and wider 2 nd apodemes separated by narrower notch (cf. Figs 69–72 and 91–93). Distribution. Southeastern and eastern Kazakhstan up to the Kazakh part of Altai Mts., Kyrgyzstan (North and Central Tien Shan), South Siberia (Tyva). Remarks. Mityaev (1971) briefly described in a key two closely related species, S. dzhungaricus and S. stepposus . According to his description, in S. dzhungaricus , the posterior outline of the aedeagus shaft is straight near the middle, while the anterior outline is vertical to the base (shown by thin arrow on Figs 81–82). In S. stepposus , the posterior outline near the middle is noticeably concave (shown by thick arrow on Figs 83–84), while the anterior outline is located at an acute angle to the base (shown by thin arrow on Figs 83–84). In the drawings in the key, these differences are quite clear (cf. Figs 81–82 and 83–84). However, a study of numerous specimens from different localities in southeastern Kazakhstan (Figs 75–80) showed that these taxa represent only extreme variants of a continuous variation range. For this reason, most specimens cannot be reliably assigned to either species; also, in some specimens, the anterior outline of the aedeagus is vertical as in S. dzhungaricus or even situated at a somewhat inverse angle to the base, while the posterior outline is slightly concave as in S. stepposus (Fig. 78). Moreover, males with different aedeagus shape sometimes were collected in the same biotope. On this basis, I consider these species to be synonyms and, as the first reviser, select S. dzhungaricus as the valid name. According to Mityaev (2002), the ranges of S. dzhungaricus and S. stepposus overlap almost completely, which also supports the established synonymy. Vilbaste (1980) provided a detailed and well-illustrated description of S. ersinicus from southern Tyva, South Siberia (Figs 85–87). A comparison of his description, particularly the drawing of the 2 nd sternal apodemes (Fig. 86), with my specimens from Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan leaves no doubt that S. ersinicus is a junior synonym of S. dzhungaricus . Since S. dzhungaricus is distributed as far east as the Kazakh Altai, its discovery in the adjacent part of Siberia seems quite natural.
title: Stenometopiellus dzhungaricus Mityaev 1971

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24060703 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes The introduction clearly explains the importance of artemisinin resistance and points out a gap in current understanding of its population-level consequences. The research objective is to examine whether increasing Kelch13 mutation prevalence is associated with malaria incidence across 16 Ugandan districts. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate The longitudinal ecological design and negative binomial regression are well-suited for examining population-level associations. The authors also included several climatic, malaria-control, and resistance-related factors. However, the use of forward variable selection raises questions about model robustness. It would be helpful to find out whether the findings remain consistent under alternative model specifications and clarify how temporal correlation between monthly observations was handled. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported The results support a positive association between Kelch13 mutation prevalence and malaria incidence after adjustment (aIRR = 1.131, 95% CI: 1.090–1.174). However, the ecological study design can't establish causation and the association may be bidirectional. Are the data presentations, including visualizations, well-suited to represent the data? Somewhat appropriate and clear The tables and figures are well-organized. Figure 2 shows district-specific trends in mutation prevalence and malaria incidence, while figure 3 provides a clear visualization of the adjusted association. However, the apparent decline in predicted incidence at very high Kelch13 prevalence is not quite sure because there were only two observations above 60%. How clearly do the authors discuss, explain, and interpret their findings and potential next steps for the research? Somewhat clearly The discussion provides biological explanations for the observed associations and acknowledges some important limitations, including possible reverse causation, residual confounding, and differences in the time scales of the data. However, the model-selection uncertainty and specific sensitivity analyses are not mentioned. Is the preprint likely to advance academic knowledge? Somewhat likely This preprint adds useful evidence about the relationship between antimalarial resistance markers and population-level malaria incidence. It contributes to the integration of molecular surveillance with epidemiological, climatic, and malaria-control data in a high-burden setting. Would it benefit from language editing? No This preprint is clear. Some statements could be more precise. For example, the authors sometimes use "malaria transmission" when the measured outcome is reported malaria incidence. Would you recommend this preprint to others? Yes, but it needs to be improved I would recommend this preprint to researchers interested in malaria epidemiology, antimalarial resistance, and molecular surveillance. The study shows an important public health question and provides useful population-level evidence. Is it ready for attention from an editor, publisher or broader audience? Yes, after minor changes I think this preprint is worth editorial consideration because it addresses an important research question and provides useful findings. However, before publication, I would recommend additional clarification of the statistical model, sensitivity analyses for variable selection. Competing interests The author declares that they have no competing interests. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) The author declares that they did not use generative AI to come up with new ideas for their review.
title: Structured PREreview of "Expanding Kelch13 artemisinin resistance markers are associated with higher malaria incidence in Uganda"

The study decomposes the total-relation matrix of DEMATEL around the degree-product null model of network science. It tests the consequences on 221 direct-relation matrices extracted from 168 open-access articles indexed in Europe PMC, on fuzzy, interval-valued and per-expert matrices extracted from 35 articles, and in simulations, and it introduces ND-DEMATEL, a null-model decomposed DEMATEL with a max-T test for specific indirect influence. The other matrices are not redistributed, because the licences of their articles do not permit it. The archive lists every source article with its licence, and reproduce.sh rebuilds the full corpus from the open-access full texts. README.md describes each stage of the pipeline. summary: How can coherent light be certified when its amplitude is unknown or its preparations are correlated? This article treats these as distinct inference problems: learning an actual coherent reference with optimal source-copy cost for independent identical inputs, and certifying the photon-counting predictions of the light left unused in a preprepared correlated batch. Optimal source-copy cost with a learned reference. For a normal one-mode source prepared independently and identically, an ideal passive multiport test and heterodyne readout produce an actual amplitude \(\hat\alpha\). After displacement by this reference and ideal quantum-limited amplification of fixed gain \(G>1\), let \(P_{\rho,\hat\alpha}^{G}\) be the photon-number distribution and \(\pi_G(k)=(G-1)^k/G^{k+1}\) the coherent benchmark. The task-specific comparison is \[\frac{1-\langle\hat\alpha|\rho|\hat\alpha\rangle}{G}\le\operatorname{TV}(P_{\rho,\hat\alpha}^{G},\pi_G)\le1-\langle\hat\alpha|\rho|\hat\alpha\rangle.\] With at most N input copies, the protocol controls the unconditional event of accepting a reference whose actual total-variation error exceeds \(\varepsilon\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), soundness error \(\beta_s\to0\), and fixed coherent-source rejection tolerance \(\beta_c<1\), the optimal fixed-maximum source-copy count obeys \[\frac{N_{\rm opt}[-\log(1-\varepsilon)]}{\log(1/\beta_s)}\longrightarrow1.\] The matching converse covers collective and adaptive protocols under the same source-copy contract. At 1% accuracy and 5% soundness and completeness errors, the finite bounds are \(293\le N_{\rm opt}\le572\). These are source-copy bounds under ideal optical access, not an optimum for total hardware or reference energy. The actual unmeasured batch after the full record. A separate protocol allows an arbitrary preprepared correlated or entangled optical batch, including correlations with an environment. A pilot first fixes the reference; a private random subset is then tested. A multiplicative sampling inequality yields a frequentist guarantee for the average marginal photon-count error of the retained conditional state, conditioned on the complete actual measurement record. It does not replace that state by premeasurement marginals or assert the same error for its full joint distribution. The trusted detector contract requires product joint test effects and local instruments that leave retained systems and the external environment untouched. Calibration envelopes must cover the actual signal-time gates. The bounds retain infinite photon tails and charge detector efficiency, dark counts, imperfect displacement, reference drift and calibration failure. Explicit counterexamples explain why marginal detector efficiencies or product effects alone are insufficient. An ideal finite example uses 3730 prepared systems: 1491 pilot, 1339 tested and 900 retained; calibration and optical-control resources are additional. Relation to the original two-copy result. The earlier mean-energy-controlled arm-swap cancellation and full trace-distance certificate remain valid for independent, possibly nonidentical product batches. Their source and target are kept separate from the new arbitrary-batch marginal PNR guarantee. The analysis builds on established coherent-state comparison, quantum verification and sampling identities; the new connections supply the learned-reference resource law and the full-record conditional-state return. Version 1.1 is a substantial update of Certifying unused optical states with imperfect two-copy interference , first published on 31 October 2026. The integrated 24-page PDF contains three figure groups, a source-and-target comparison table, complete proofs and references. The figures illustrate proved bounds and specified theoretical protocols, not experimental measurements.
title: Certifying coherent light with unknown amplitudes and correlated sources

summary: FAIRSCAPE Conversion is an open-source Python package that builds FAIRSCAPE evidence RO-Crates from metadata that already describes a dataset or a computation. It imports Datasheets for Datasets, Frictionless and CFDE C2M2 data packages, REDCap data dictionaries, Workflow Run RO-Crates and CPM provenance crates. It also imports the run records written by Cromwell, Snakemake, Galaxy and MLflow, and can track Python scripts and Jupyter cells directly. Each source becomes an ro-crate-metadata.json that links datasets, software and computations with FAIRSCAPE provenance identifiers. Crates can be linked so that provenance continues from one crate into the next. A crate can also be exported as MLCommons Croissant, a Datasheet for Datasets, a Workflow Run RO-Crate, a Frictionless Data Package or PROV. New formats are added as plugins defined by two CSV mapping files. This record includes the source code, examples and tests.

summary: Black-hole X-ray binaries switch from the hard to the soft state at luminosities several times higher than those at which they switch back, and changing-look active galactic nuclei, whose broad lines appear and vanish near 1 per cent of the Eddington luminosity, are often read as their supermassive analogue. The switch-on and switch-off thresholds have not been measured separately for any supermassive black hole. We fit a latent-continuum model with a hysteretic switch to 19 repeating changing- look nuclei with Eddington ratios from the 5100 A ̊ continuum at three spectral epochs, and calibrate the width ∆ between the two thresholds with forward-simulated mock samples. In every nucleus each off-state continuum lies below each on-state one, whereas mock samples drawn with our baseline priors contain on average 4.6 nuclei that violate this order. In mock samples without state flips and with slowly varying continua, no nucleus violates it in a fraction 0.28 of cases at ∆ = 0 and 0.02 at ∆ = 0.5 dex. If the catalogue was not selected on the agreement of continuum and line changes, widths of half a dex or more are therefore disfavoured. If it was so selected, the likelihood that includes the selection carries no information on ∆, and the posterior quantile calibrated with selection-matched mocks gives ∆ < 0.57 dex at 95 per cent, with a Monte Carlo spread of 0.30–0.59 dex. The continua of the two states differ by less than 0.34–0.70 dex for a per-epoch noise of 0.05–0.28 dex. Neither reading tests the flip-flop picture of changing-state nuclei. About 150 repeating nuclei selected on their broad lines alone, with continua measured independently of the state, would reach the binary population mean.
title: EDDINGTON-RATIO HYSTERESIS IN REPEATING CHANGING-LOOK ACTIVE GALACTIC NUCLEI: CONDITIONAL LIMITS AND THE SELECTION OF THREE-EPOCH CATALOGUES

summary: FAIRSCAPE Artifacts is an open-source tool that turns a finished RO-Crate into pages people can read. From a crate folder it produces an HTML datasheet, a preview of every entity in the crate, an interactive provenance (evidence) graph with a JSON copy, and an AI-readiness review produced by the AI-Readiness Grader. Each page is a single self-contained HTML file that can be emailed, deposited with the data or served as a static website. The tool runs offline and needs no server. Release crates get one summary card per sub-crate, and crates linked to upstream crates are shown in one combined graph. An optional command uses a large language model to write an annotated summary of the crate; it never runs by default. This record includes the source code and tests.
title: fairscape/fairscape_artifacts: Fairscape Artifact Generation

summary: This dataset offers computational information that underpins the research titled “Integrated computational and experimental characterization of I49R substitution in monomeric M-MLV reverse transcriptase reveals increased soluble recovery and RNA-dependent DNA synthesis.” The dataset comprises inputs for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, structural models, numerical analysis outcomes, and computational documentation pertaining to Natural-type and I49R variations of Moloney murine leukemia virus reverse transcriptase (M-MLV RT). The initial simulations were conducted with GROMACS 2022 alongside the CHARMM36 force field from July 2022. Each protein variation was examined for 400 ns under periodic boundary conditions at 315 K and 1 bar. The dataset comprises the following elements: Structural models: Beginning and concluding protein configurations for Natural-type and I49R M-MLV RT. Simulation parameters: GROMACS configuration files, topology data, and production simulation setup files. Structural dynamics: Quantitative metrics for root-mean-square deviation (RMSD), root-mean-square fluctuation (RMSF), radius of gyration (Rg), and solvent-accessible surface area (SASA). Conformational assessment: Principal component analysis (PCA), free-energy landscape information, dynamic cross-correlation matrices (DCCM), and structural variability evaluations. Convergence evaluation: Temporal comparisons and geographical analyzes employed to evaluate the stationarity of chosen structural observables during the prolonged simulations. Protein–RNA complexes: Computationally generated structural representations of Natural-type and I49R reverse transcriptase interacting with RNA, alongside protein-only cluster-center conformations acquired from RNA-inclusive simulation systems. Reproducibility records: GROMACS procedural details, analytical notebooks, and ancillary documentation. The dataset aims to promote repeatability, autonomous analysis, and additional inquiries into the correlation between amino acid alterations, protein structural behavior, soluble protein extraction, and enzymatic activity. The computational findings enhance the experimental data of augmented soluble protein recovery and RNA-dependent DNA synthesis linked to the I49R mutation.
title: Computational Dataset for Molecular Dynamics Analysis of the I49R Substitution in Monomeric M-MLV Reverse Transcriptase

summary: FAIRSCAPE is a set of open-source tools for describing biomedical datasets, software and computations as RO-Crates with evidence graphs of their provenance, evaluating them for AI-readiness, and depositing them in public repositories. Each tool is developed, released and cited separately. This record is the source of the FAIRSCAPE documentation website ( fairscape.github.io ), which explains how the tools fit together and is the main reference for the current tooling. The documentation follows the pipeline in order and points to each tool's repository and DOI: FAIRSCAPE Models : the RO-Crate and evidence-graph data model the other tools build on. FAIRSCAPE Conversion : builds crates from existing metadata, such as datasheets, data packages, REDCap dictionaries and workflow or MLflow runs. FAIRSCAPE Artifacts : turns a crate into an HTML datasheet, an interactive evidence graph and entity previews. AI-Readiness Grader : evaluates a crate against the Bridge2AI AI-readiness criteria and produces an HTML scoring worksheet. FAIRSCAPE Publish : deposits a crate in Dataverse, Zenodo or Figshare, or mints a DataCite DOI. FAIRSCAPE Lite : a server for hosting and serving crates. The site also has getting-started guides and end-to-end examples. This record contains documentation only; the code is in the separate tool records listed under related works.
title: fairscape/fairscape.github.io: FAIRSCAPE Documentation

summary: Core Objective : To construct pure quantum Yang-Mills theory with compact simple gauge group $SU(N)$ in four-dimensional Euclidean space, prove the strict positivity of its mass gap, and reduce the mass-gap problem to a small set of explicit, identified inputs. Methodology : Uses lattice regularisation, renormalisation-group control of the continuum limit, and Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction of a relativistic quantum field theory on Minkowski space. Expresses the clustering rate of the reflection-positive two-point function as the mass gap. Factorizes the mass-gap problem into three independent aspects: Existence (forced by reflection positivity and Fekete's lemma), Value (governed by an anomalous dimension), and Positivity (carried by the discrete centre of the gauge group and uniform control of confining flux). Key Innovations & Structure : Works in the flow-time coordinate where the dimensional-transmutation scale is an entire function and the marginal coupling region is compact. Proves the factorisation of the clustering rate and demonstrates that the mass gap equals the spectral gap of the transfer operator restricted to the centre-charged sector. Verifies the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms (temperedness, reflection positivity, symmetry) conditional on identified inputs (uniform non-percolation, rotational invariance restoration, and limit uniqueness). Closes with a closure scheme, dimensional calibration against three-dimensional models, and explicit worked examples. The monograph titled "The Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional $SU(N)$ Yang–Mills Theory" presents a construction of pure quantum Yang–Mills theory with a compact simple gauge group on four-dimensional Euclidean space. Its primary objective is to establish the existence of the theory and the strict positivity of its mass gap , reducing the overall problem to a small set of explicitly identified, non-analytic inputs.
title: When is 4D-Yang-Mills-Theorie possible; The Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional SU(N) Yang-Mills Theory: A Construction, Its Reduction to a Single Non-Analytic Input, and a Scheme for Its Closure

files.key: An Asteroid in a Penning Trap.pdf

summary: The triangular Lagrange point of the restricted three-body problem and the radial motion of a charged particle in a Penning trap are both equilibria held at a maximum of an effective potential by a gyroscopic force. Each possesses one mode of negative energy, and each loses linear stability when its two frequencies collide—one at Routh’s mass ratio, the other at the trapping limit. Both systems belong to a single family of planar gyroscopic Hamiltonians. On every level of the conserved angular-momentum invariant, the degree-four normal form of any member at such a collision coincides with the reduced Hamiltonian of an axisymmetric Penning trap whose detuning is shifted by a term proportional to the invariant and whose quartic coefficient is fixed by a single normal-form invariant. On the level containing orbits that start at rest, this reduction yields closed-form laws for the largest excursion, the escape threshold, and the escape time. These laws depend only on the sign of the quartic coefficient and on scaled variables. At the triangular point the coefficient is positive, placing the collision in the soft class: orbits remain confined after stability is lost, with an excursion that grows like the square root of the distance past the critical value. Direct integration confirms the soft law to a fraction of a percent at the smallest detunings tested. Two traps whose quartic coefficient matches that of the triangular point reproduce the same law. Traps with the opposite sign escape at the predicted threshold and in the predicted times. A randomized ensemble of members confirms the classification by the sign of the coefficient. Two further results hold for every member of the family. Before the collision the linear transient gain is exactly the inverse square root of the frequency splitting. With isotropic velocity damping the first-order growth rates depend only on the undamped frequencies, and at the collision they scale with the square root of the damping rate. The first of these explains earlier reports of apparent escape just below Routh’s value as ordinary linear transients that reach a fixed radius. The second recovers the classical magnetron-instability formula as a special case. The results are local, planar, and classical. What transfers between the asteroid and the trap is the normal-form dynamics on each level of the invariant, the transient gain, and the damped linear rates. What does not transfer without further work is the behaviour beyond the normal-form neighbourhood, where the gravitational terms of every order cause the triangular point to deviate from any purely quartic trap.
title: An Asteroid in a Penning Trap

summary: For a Fermat fourfold of odd degree, the rational Hodge classes in middle degree are spanned by character blocks indexed by six-entry Hodge characters. Two direct constructions make such a block algebraic: a contraction of two surface characters, which includes the case of an inverse pair, and an exact 5-standard tuple of Aoki. We call the remaining characters *residual*. We prove that the residual characters at every odd degree are exactly the inflations of six explicit seeds in degrees 33, 39, 45 and 105. The proof is uniform in the degree and uses no computer enumeration. Maximal-order Fourier kernels, a classification of surface characters at odd conductor and an analysis of four points of a five-progression reduce an arbitrary primitive residual conductor to the degrees 15, 21, 33, 39, 45 and 105, which are then settled by the same character equations. An exhaustive census through degree 599, and enumerations at the 103 degrees up to 2001 not covered by the earlier subfamily theorems, give an independent check. Since the seeds are algebraic, the classification yields a proof of the Hodge conjecture for these fourfolds that does not use Kang's refined motivic dimension estimates. That conclusion was previously stated in the author's earlier preprint [11] (8 September 2026), before the written proof of Bhattacharjee [5] (October 2026), and the six seeds were first isolated by Jumagulov [8] through degree 199; the new content is the exact positive classification at every odd degree. We also record the all-dimensional consequences for the prime supports $\{3,11\}$ and $\{3,13\}$, and give an explicit family of Fermat characters on which the tensor filtration identity used in Kang's product argument fails. Archival copy of version 6 of this paper, public on rStation on 9 November 2026 ( rStation hodge_conjecture paper 104, v6 ; version 1 posted 4 November 2026). paper.md is the manuscript source as posted (SHA-256 7dd045e569c13c11c09510e016aa2889f517f1d2201bf1aa37b87e80736101ad); the PDF is typeset from it with the posted title and abstract. supplement.zip contains the reproduction bundles (SHA-256 68e062729bbe49f0e92b435d0f4394fc4f156a82b9b8bc9aa1f503a386d91657). Changes from the previous Zenodo version (rStation v4): the abstract and Section 1 now state that the all-odd-degree algebraicity conclusion was previously stated in the author's preprint The Hodge Conjecture for Odd-Degree Fermat Fourfolds (8 September 2026; ResearchGate, DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2.26853.77288 ), before Bhattacharjee's written proof (October 2026). Theorems, proofs and computational bundles are unchanged. The work was produced largely with AI systems and is released for public human verification; it has not been checked by a human expert.
title: Residual Characters of Odd-Degree Fermat Fourfolds

summary: Dataset Description This dataset contains experimental X-ray computed tomography (CT) and Angular Segmented Gamma Scanning (ASGS) measurements of radioactive waste drum mockups, collected for research into three-dimensional radionuclide activity reconstruction. The measurements were used in the development and evaluation of SARUMAN (Spatial Activity Reconstruction Using Machine-learning Algorithms for Nuclear Waste) , a Bayesian machine-learning framework for reconstructing spatial activity distributions from gamma spectrometry and CT-derived attenuation information. Dataset Contents The dataset comprises nine experimental configurations: Six homogeneous mockups (HOM-1 to HOM-6) , containing different source arrangements within homogeneous filling materials, including bark and potting soil. Three heterogeneous mockups (HET-1 to HET-3) , designed to investigate activity reconstruction under more complex material and source distributions. Each configuration is provided as an individual ZIP archive, containing: CT/ : A reconstructed X-ray CT volume in MetaImage format ( reconstructionFloat.mhd and reconstructionFloat.raw ). ASGS/ : Gamma spectrometry acquisition files ( .asr , .asw , and .srf ) corresponding to the segmented angular measurements. The original spectrometry file formats are preserved to retain the experimental acquisition information. Intended Use These measurements are provided to support reproducibility, methodological comparisons, and further research into radiological waste characterization, gamma-ray transport modelling, uncertainty quantification, and Bayesian inverse problems. The dataset can be used with SARUMAN or adapted for other reconstruction and data-analysis approaches. Reference Publication Users are strongly encouraged to read the associated scientific publication before using or interpreting this dataset: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306454926007383 The publication provides the scientific context for the experimental measurements, the associated reconstruction methodology, and the considerations relevant to their interpretation. Researchers wishing to reproduce the original analyses or adapt the methodology to other applications should consult this publication alongside the SARUMAN source code and documentation. Scope and Limitations The measurements originate from a specific experimental characterization system. Their interpretation requires appropriate knowledge of the detector geometry, acquisition configuration, calibration procedures, and CT attenuation modelling. The associated SARUMAN implementation includes detector-efficiency and CT attenuation models developed for this experimental setup. These models should not be assumed valid for different instruments without appropriate adaptation and validation. The dataset is provided for scientific research purposes and does not constitute a universally validated characterization benchmark. Associated Software SARUMAN — Spatial Activity Reconstruction Using Machine-learning Algorithms for Nuclear Waste https://github.com/vcasasmo/SARUMAN Dataset preparation and software development: Victor J. Casas Molina.
title: SARUMAN: Experimental CT and Angular Segmented Gamma Scanning Dataset for Radioactive Waste Drum Mockups

summary: This archive contains data, code, and evaluation outputs supporting the study “Compensator-Based Interevent Marks for Short-Term Earthquake Forecasts in Synthetic and Archived Catalogs.” The study evaluates whether rate-adjusted interevent gaps, expressed as point-process compensator marks, improve short-term earthquake forecasts. It compares the EMESL model (M2) with a constrained temporal Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) baseline (N0), a constant-mark model (M1), and a raw interevent-gap model (D1). The six analysis modules cover synthetic experiments and matched controls, held-out event-timing evaluation for Ridgecrest, forecast replay using dated Ridgecrest catalog snapshots, external archived-catalog replication for sequences anchored by M ≥ 5.2 and M ≥ 6.0 earthquakes, evaluation of a frozen ETAS blend, and sensitivity analysis using the revised USGS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat). The package includes catalog extracts, frozen protocols, model fits, paired forecast scores, summary tables, and a script to regenerate Figure 5 of the study. Catalog sources include the Southern California Earthquake Data Center, the Northern California Earthquake Data Center, and USGS ComCat. For the primary external M ≥ 6.0 cohort, M2 scored higher than the raw-gap model in all four eligible sequences for six-hour occurrence forecasts of M ≥ 2.5 earthquakes. Against constrained temporal ETAS, M2 scored higher in one of the four sequences, with a mean gain of −0.163 bits per window when the sequences were weighted equally. The frozen ETAS blend assigned zero weight to the marked models and yielded zero gain in the single eligible external case. The archive also preserves a separate prospective Vanuatu forecast protocol and its frozen forecast. Its outcome was pending as of 8 November 2026 and contributes no score to the archived comparisons. Start with README.md for the map from manuscript figures and tables to analysis modules. Verify file integrity with python verify_archive.py or sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt . Most historical analyses can be reproduced offline using the bundled extracts and the instructions in each module.
title: EMESL Reproducibility Archive: Data and Code for Compensator-Based Interevent Marks in Short-Term Earthquake Forecasting

summary: This dataset accompanies the HeteroSpaSim study of heterogeneous spatial multi-omics simulation. The collection contains 240 primary simulation objects (144 de novo and 96 reference-guided objects) and 189 targeted RNA–ATAC validation objects . The primary reference-guided collection comprises eight experimental references, three simulation seeds (42, 43 and 44), and four configurations: publicly paired V1, hidden-pairing V2, partial coverage and heterogeneous resolution. The targeted collection uses three fixed tissue templates and controlled shared-signal, pairing, coverage, resolution and coordinate-misalignment contrasts. Shared baseline configurations map 225 targeted experimental roles to 189 unique objects. The deposit includes molecular measurements, observed spatial coordinates, generation configurations and random seeds, multilevel evaluator ground truth, public paired exports for 63 eligible primary de novo objects, molecular and spatial validation results, and manuscript figure source tables with their provenance indices. Start with README.md and Dataset_Archive_Index_429.csv. Supplementary Data 1 lists the 429 objects. Supplementary Data 2 maps the targeted experimental roles. Primary data include canonical H5AD and Matrix Market exports with companion identifiers and coordinates. Targeted RDS objects retain molecular assays, measurement operators, latent states and correspondence truth. FILE_MANIFEST.csv supplies member-level SHA256 hashes, and SHA256SUMS.txt verifies the uploaded files. Tested Python and R readback examples are included. The original experimental assays are obtained from the repositories cited in the accompanying manuscript. The software version associated with this deposit is HeteroSpaSim 0.1.9.
title: HeteroSpaSim simulation datasets and manuscript source data

summary: A benefit can be real while the judgment that it is good remains uninformed. I develop uninformed good as a graded concept: a benefit received without adequate understanding of its relevant costs, wherever those costs fall. Disclosure may lower, raise, or leave unchanged the recipient’s evaluation. A benefit that remains equally good after its costs are understood is the limiting categorical case in my sense; whether such cases occur is an open question, not a result established here. The primary aim is descriptive: to ask how often uninformed benefits produce real harm, for whom, and under which conditions. A separate philosophical hypothesis holds that omission is outwardly negative; it is not presented as an empirical finding. I distinguish deliberate concealment, chosen ignorance, and unavoidable incomplete knowledge; examines demands and last-minute requests for forgiveness or reentry; and confronts invisible-support evidence as a genuine challenge to blanket disclosure rules. I argue for timely disclosure of material known costs while recognizing costs of disclosure and limits of knowledge. Nine revised predictions, a field-oriented distributional inquiry, and two possible experiments specify how the empirical claims could be tested. No new data are reported.
title: Uninformed Good: Why Benefits Received Without Knowledge of Their Costs Are Not Categorically Good

summary: A cross-platform, provenance-first desktop suite for single-molecule FRET (smFRET) analysis: native movie-to-trace extraction, a trace-to-movie round-trip browser, per-condition machine-assisted curation, photophysical corrections, and HMM idealization via an isolated tMAVEN sidecar. Built for the Mondragón Lab, Northwestern University.
title: Tether

summary: AetherGovern is a structured investigation of whether a governance gap genuinely exists in the Aether family, or whether it is already covered by the existing four dimensions:   - AetherGit (storage and versioning) - AetherFlow (integration and operational verification) - AetherProof (specification and formal evidence) - AetherMesh (distribution and eventual consistency)   The investigation follows a falsification-first methodology: five failure conditions (F1–F5) are stated before the candidate is described, and the final project structure (single, dual, or triple project) is determined after comparison. Three candidate capabilities are compared: orchestration (AetherOrchestrate), governance (AetherGovern), and runtime assurance (AetherRuntime).   The proposed architecture has five layers: Authorization, Policy, Accountability, Revocation, and Dispute Resolution. Two propositions are stated with proof sketches: (P1) causal-authority admission preserves the determinism requirement of AetherMesh; (P2) revocation is monotone and can be recorded without coordination, but leaves an irreducible exposure window.   Status: Architectural Hypothesis Under Investigation (v0.1.0). No implementation is claimed. No real-world deployment has been evaluated. F1–F4 are not falsified by argument, with residual weaknesses. F5 (observable benefit) is untested. The final project structure (single, dual, or triple project) is undetermined. The paper is not peer reviewed.   Links: - Zenodo DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24054524 - OSF Registration: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/TAHC8 - OSF Project: https://osf.io/we2tm - Official Website: https://aethergovern.netlify.app - GitHub: https://github.com/gitdeeper15/aethergovern - ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0003-8903-0029

Includes I_CDW(t) and summed double-occupancy correlations d_corr(t) for U/J = 5 and 15 up to t = 50 ħ/J, a U-scan, and per-site traces. All conventions (I_CDW starts at 2.0; d_corr summed over sites) are documented in the README. compare.py (numpy only) compares your own curve against the exact reference in one line, including automatic handling of the common normalization differences.
