summary: Platforms such as Facebook, WhatsApp, Twitter, and Telegram have a substantial influence on the dissemination of information in modern society. Numerous individuals rely on them without verifying the veracity of their information or the sources of their knowledge. False information is referred to as "Fake News" and is disseminated through both traditional and non traditional media channels including social media. Contemporary media consumers uncritically embrace the news they read online, rather than taking the time to critically assess it. This method has led to a heightened trust in internet content, which has facilitated the spread of misinformation. This article describes a machine learning (ML)-based approach to classifying and detecting fake news anomalies in online social media data. This framework accepts social media data as input. Features are chosen using the term frequency identification term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF IDF) and chi-square tests. The categorization model is then built utilizing approaches such as artificial neural network (ANN), support vector machine (SVM), and random forest (RF). The classification model is trained and tested on a preprocessed data set. Finally, fake news is discovered, and the suggested framework is evaluated using measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. ANN is performing better for fake news classification and detection.
title: TF-IDF, chi-square, and ANN machine learning techniques for fake news anomaly detection in online social networks

summary: Global proteomic profiling of human platelet lysate (hPL) by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS). The dataset was generated to identify the bioactive protein components of the platelet-derived preparation used in a study of platelet factor 4 (PF4) and cellular senescence. Acquisition. Single hPL sample, in-solution trypsin digestion, EASY-nLC 1200 coupled to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 (FAIMS, compensation voltage -45 V; full MS 350-1400 m/z at 60,000 resolution; MS/MS at 15,000 resolution, HCD 27% NCE). Processing. DIA-NN v1.8 against Homo_sapiens_9606_SP_20231220.fasta (20,429 entries) plus reverse decoy; trypsin/P with up to 1 missed cleavage; carbamidomethylation of cysteine and N-terminal methionine excision as fixed modifications; FDR < 1%. Contents. (1) all identified proteins with coverage, peptide counts and label-free intensity; (2) all identified peptides with charge, uniqueness and intensity; (3) the 15 most abundant proteins. README.md documents the full sample preparation, LC-MS parameters and processing settings. Because the analysis is a single-sample descriptive profiling rather than a comparative experiment, these tables contain the entire quantitative content of the acquisition.
title: Proteomic profiling of human platelet lysate by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry

summary: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.
title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples

summary: Mixtures of logistic regressions provide a flexible framework for modeling binary responses, extending standard logistic regression to accommodate unobserved heterogeneity while retaining an interpretable regression structure. In this paper, we study such models with an unspecified mixing distribution. We analyze a sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) and derive nonasymptotic bounds on the estimation error of the resulting mixture regression function under both fixed and random designs. Our results reveal an explicit tradeoff between statistical estimation error and the approximation error induced by the sieve radius, from which we derive convergence rates under several tail conditions on the mixing distribution. For computation, we propose a finite-particle algorithm that approximates the sieve NPMLE by optimizing the locations and weights of a finitely supported mixing distribution. The method offers numerical advantages over existing algorithms and comes with rigorous convergence guarantees. For any fixed dataset, we establish global convergence of the likelihood to the restricted NPMLE value when the number of particles exceeds a finite threshold. When the true mixing distribution is finitely supported, we further establish uniform global convergence guarantees and derive error bounds that separate algorithmic and statistical errors. Our analysis also yields a denoising bound for the mixing distribution and an identifiability result that complements existing results in the literature.
title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions

summary: English abstract This work develops a metalinguistic axiomatic framework for cognition, knowledge, theories, intelligent systems, and AI. At the cognitive level, the framework distinguishes objectified items, registered meta-level interfaces, and residual metalanguage, retaining failure and unevaluability. Evaluation, object admission, name binding, and state writeback each have separate conditions. At the knowledge level, knowledge-base membership is distinct from verified or assertable status. Provenance, composite status, four-valued judgment, argumentation, tracing, and safe introduction serve distinct roles. At the theory level, theory objects comprise object and relation sets under co-rootedness and well-founded dependency conditions. Theory evaluation, transformation, and positioning have separate conditional interfaces. At the intelligent-system level, maintenance constrains optimization. Boundary, stable, and higher-order intelligence depend on stated criteria; AI generation and model scale alone do not establish these qualifications. Behavioral interfaces conditionally connect complete action, interaction goals and evaluations, and traceable joint descriptions. A six-step metatheoretical workflow organizes the deconstruction, reconnection, and reconstruction of existing theories. Task-relative textual and geometric representations organize theoretical expression and retrieval without replacing the underlying theory texts. The contribution combines theory-internal axiomatic or quasi-axiomatic reconstruction with cross-level interface organization. It makes domains, dependencies, admissibility, failures, and theoretical effects explicit. Empirical scales, engineering realizations, and system effectiveness require independent implementation and testing. 中文摘要 认知、知识、理论、智能系统与人工智能研究常使用相互分离的概念语言。产生结果与引入对象、保存信息与接受知识、改善输出与维持系统等不同任务,也因此容易混淆。本文建立一套元语言公理化框架,通过对象层与元层接口连接这些研究层次。框架区分已对象化项目、已登记元语言接口,以及当前对象语言不能吸收的元语言余项,并保留失败与不可评价。 在认知与知识方面,框架分别规定求值、对象引入、名称绑定与状态写回的资格。知识库成员不等于已验证或可断言知识。来源、复合知识标签、主显示、四值判断、论证、回溯和安全引入各有职责;它们不构成所有候选必经的流水线。 在理论层,理论由对象集及其中的关系对象集构成,对象集须满足共根与依赖良基条件。原始对象与基本原理由内部前驱读取,理论品质、变换和结构位置则通过各自的条件接口处理。 在系统层,维持约束优化,边界、稳定和高阶智能按明示判据区分。AI的生成与规模本身不证明这些资格成立。行为附录通过条件接口接入完整行为结构、互动目标与评估,以及可追溯的联合描述。行为分类不等同于趋人化或主体资格。 前四章的部分接口被组织为六步流程,并由四组异质方法示例说明。收束命题仅在各步资格与输入输出条件成立时连接环节;示例本身不独立证明这些条件。第8章规定任务相关的文本与几何表示,并区分假设与待定承接位。索引调用受答案覆盖、局部正确性和完整成本约束。 本文结合选定概念的理论内重建与跨层接口组织,明确各项内容的对象域或元层角色、资格、依赖、失败值与理论效力。工程实现、经验量尺和系统效果仍需独立实现与检验。 Full texts and supplementary material This record provides the full text in English and Chinese, together with separate English and bilingual Chinese-English theory-framework diagrams to support reading and cross-referencing of the main text. summary: The evolution of DARIAH-IT from a distributed research infrastructure into a federated ecosystem of data centres, computational resources, digital services, scientific workflows, and research communities raises a fundamental technical and scientific question: how can an SSH research infrastructure preserve its essential functions when individual nodes, services, data resources, or dependencies suffer degradation, become unavailable, or are compromised? Addressing this question requires moving beyond component-level cybersecurity towards a systemic approach in which criticality, dependencies, functional continuity, recovery and adaptation become architectural properties of the infrastructure. Operational resilience must therefore be accompanied by epistemic resilience: the capacity of the infrastructure to preserve the conditions that make digital resources and computational processes trustworthy, interpretable, and scientifically reusable.  The relationship between cultural memory and machine memory provides a particularly relevant perspective for this discussion. As cultural knowledge is increasingly encoded into structured datasets and processed through automated and AI-supported environments, research infrastructures mediate between human interpretations of cultural memory and their computational representations. Their role therefore extends beyond the preservation and accessibility of digital resources to ensuring that cultural knowledge remains contextualised, interoperable, traceable, and reusable throughout its digital lifecycle. This workshop presents a resilience-by-design framework for the gradual evolution of DARIAH-IT, the Italian node of DARIAH (Digital Research Infrastructure for the Arts and Humanities), towards a Critical Research Infrastructure. The approach begins with a criticality assessment aimed at identifying which combinations of data, services, workflows, computational resources, identities and organisational dependencies are necessary to maintain essential scientific and cultural functions. Inventories of critical services, dependency maps, risk-impact matrices and domain-specific threat models form the basis for analysing the propagation of failures and identifying individual points of failure within the federation. Starting at an architectural level, the outlined framework requires investigating how geographically distributed resources can evolve from a set of interconnected nodes into a resilient federated infrastructure. Relevant mechanisms include containerised microservices, multi-cluster orchestration, service meshes, zero-trust API gateways, OAuth2/OIDC and mTLS, secure CI/CD pipelines, immutable backups, distributed replication, and business continuity and disaster recovery procedures. The central problem is therefore one of controlled interdependence: designing a federation in which services and resources can cooperate while preventing individual failures from propagating across the wider ecosystem. A complementary dimension concerns the resilience of scientific workflows. Workflows create dependencies that span services, datasets, computational environments, authentication mechanisms and external resources. Their resilience therefore requires reproducible execution environments, explicit dependency management, provenance tracking, continuous monitoring and mechanisms to detect and respond to anomalous behaviour. The evolution of the DARIAH-IT orchestration environment towards native containerised and distributed execution provides an experimental context for the study of adaptive workflows, anomaly detection, agent-based orchestration, federated learning and semi-automatic recovery mechanisms. For SSH infrastructures, however, operational continuity alone is not sufficient. A technically successful failover or recovery may still constitute a scientific failure if provenance, authenticity, semantic consistency, reproducibility or reliability are compromised. Resilience must therefore be
title: From a Federated Research Infrastructure to a Critical Research Infrastructure: A "Resilience by Design" Approach for DARIAH-IT

summary: A typical omics core facility might run sequencers and mass spectrometers from several vendors, each with its own idea of where a run is written, when it is finished and where it may be uploaded. For human-derived data this is not enough, because analysis must take place inside a trusted research environment (TRE) whose ingress is isolated: it cannot be mounted as a network drive and may accept uploads without letting the sender read them back. A facility therefore has no single route from all its instruments into a TRE, and no way to check that a run arrived intact. We present OmiCZ Gateway, developed for OmiCZ, the Czech node of the European Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI). It is a containerized, vendor-agnostic service that detects completed runs with configurable per-instrument rules, sends finished parts of a run while acquisition continues, computes a SHA-256 checksum for every file at the source, uploads over the S3 API with resumption after failure, and waits until a companion service inside the TRE recomputes and confirms every checksum. Availability and implementation: OmiCZ Gateway is implemented in Python with a web interface and runs with Docker Compose. Source code is available under the MIT license at https://github.com/BioIT-CEITEC/omicz-gateway-component (gateway, v1.3.1) and https://github.com/BioIT-CEITEC/omicz-inbox-bucket-watcher-component (TRE-side verifier, v0.1.0).  Web interface demo:  https://bioit-ceitec.github.io/omicz-gateway-component/ .
title: OmiCZ Gateway: vendor-agnostic, verified transfer of sequencing and mass spectrometry data into a trusted research environment

summary: Тривалий час в Україні поширений напрям органічного виробництва, проте останніми роками він набув стрімкого розвитку, навіть за умов війни Україна посідає провідні позиції щодо експорту такої продукції. За впровадження органічного виробництва ряд операторів в Україні стикаються з проблемою забезпечення якісного, органічного посадкового матеріалу, особливо проса. Площі за ведення органічного виробництва в Україні становлять 1 % від загальної площі сільськогосподарських угідь. Тому метою досліджень було вдосконалення елементів технології вирощування проса, як основи для отримання якісного посадкового матеріалу за органічного виробництва. Дослідження проводили впродовж 2022–2024 рр. на базі ПСП ім. Т.Г. Шевченка с. Тростинка, Васильківського району Київської області. Вивчали сорти проса Омріяне і Біла Альтанка та дозволені в органічному виробництві допоміжні продукти й умови їх внесення. Дозволені допоміжні продукти в органічному виробництві позитивно впливали на покращення енергії проростання, зокрема за застосування Біокомплексу-БТУ отримали 93,0 % у сорту Омріяне та 92,0 % – у сорту Біла Альтанка. Польова схожість досліджуваних сортів становила в межах 76,3–76,6 %. Кількість рослин проса у сорту Омріяне у фазу повних сходів була на рівні 243,0–245,8 шт./м², підвищення цього показника обумовлено застосуванням біопрепаратів. У разі застосування таких препаратів як Біокомплекс-БТУ та Органік-Баланс отримали врожайність проса на рівні 3,74–3,90 т/га порівняно з контрольними ділянками 2,49–2,73 т/га. English title: The influence of auxiliary products in organic production on sowing qualities and yield properties of millet seeds. Organic production has been widespread in Ukraine for a long time, but in recent years it has developed rapidly, even in war conditions, Ukraine occupies a leading position in the export of such products. When introducing organic production, a number of operators in Ukraine face the problem of providing high-quality organic planting material, especially millet. The area for organic production in Ukraine is 1% of the total area of farmlands. Therefore, the aim of the research was to improve the elements of millet cultivation technology as the basis for obtaining high-quality planting material under organic production. The research was carried out during 2022-2024 on the basis of T.H.Shevchenko private agricultural enterprise, village Trostinka, Vasylkiv district, Kyiv region. The millet varieties («Omriyane» and «Bila Altanka»), the auxiliary products permitted in organic production and the conditions of their application were studied. Permitted auxiliary products in organic production had a positive effect on the improvement of germination energy, in particular with the use of «Biocomplex BTU» obtained 93,0% in the «Omriyane» variety and 92,0% in the «Bila Altanka» variety. The field germination of the studied varieties was in the range of 76,3-76,6%. The number of millet plants of the «Omriyane» variety in the phase of full emergence was at the level of 243,0-245,8 pl./m², the increase of this indicator was due to the use of biological preparations. With the use of such preparations as «Biocomplex BTU» and «Organic-Balance», the millet yield was obtained at the level of 3,74-3,90 t/ha compared to the control plots of 2,49-2,73 t/ha. summary: R analysis code and summary result tables for the paper “Metabolic gene-expression scores add no prognostic information on late recurrence of ER-positive breast cancer: a multicohort, multi-omic study”. The study tests whether gene-expression scores of four metabolic programs (glycolysis, fatty acid oxidation, oxidative phosphorylation and the lysosome), 159 metabolic pathways and 2319 metabolic genes in the primary tumour carry information on distant recurrence after 5 years in ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer (METABRIC, with external MetaGxBreast cohorts and GSE17705). It also examines what the scores measure (variance decomposition, split-half reliability, matched metabolite levels, copy number) and compares them with random gene sets of the same size. Contents: analysis and figure scripts (folder scripts/), summary result tables needed to run the figure and table scripts (folder 04_tables/), gene-set definitions (gene symbols only) and the cohort and covariate tables derived from the open clinical data. The README describes the data sources, the order in which to run the scripts, and which script produces each figure and table. METABRIC gene expression data are under controlled access (European Genome-phenome Archive) and are not included. Changes in this version: the figure and table numbering follows the published paper; Figure 1 and Figure 5 labels updated; new script for Supplementary Fig. S16; the random-gene-set benchmark script no longer writes the size-matched Hallmark comparison or the former four-panel figure (the Hallmark subsets are still drawn, so that the random-number sequence and all reported values are unchanged); Supplementary Table S4 updated. The changed scripts were run again from this repository and reproduced the published output tables. Licence: MIT.
title: Analysis code for: Metabolic gene-expression scores add no prognostic information on late recurrence of ER-positive breast cancer: a multicohort, multi-omic study

summary: la versione 7.3 del modello teorico dedicato allo studio di un microrotore fotonico con contrapeso e del suo possibile comportamento in differenti condizioni fluidodinamiche. Il modello analizza l'interazione tra luce a tre lunghezze d'onda (532, 800 e 1064 nm), dinamica rotazionale, resistenza viscosa, rumore stocastico e condizioni termiche, considerando un ciclo di rotazione di 720°. La ricerca integra calcoli quantitativi, soglie fisiche, analisi di sensibilità e verifiche di coerenza, distinguendo i risultati ottenuti dalle ipotesi ancora da validare. Il lavoro non costituisce una dimostrazione sperimentale del dispositivo né della sua funzionalità nel sangue. Rappresenta una base teorica verificabile, con limiti esplicitamente dichiarati e una serie di misurazioni sperimentali necessarie per procedere alla validazione.fornire un modello trasparente e riproducibile che possa essere analizzato, criticato e ulteriormente sviluppato dalla comunità scientifica Version 7.3 of the theoretical model is dedicated to the study of a photonic micro-rotor with a counterweight and its potential behavior under various fluid-dynamic conditions. The model analyzes the interaction between light at three wavelengths (532, 800, and 1064 nm), rotational dynamics, viscous drag, stochastic noise, and thermal conditions, considering a 720° rotation cycle. The research integrates quantitative calculations, physical thresholds, sensitivity analyses, and consistency checks, distinguishing between the results obtained and hypotheses that remain to be validated. This work does not constitute an experimental demonstration of the device or its functionality within blood. It serves as a verifiable theoretical foundation—with explicitly stated limitations—that outlines the experimental measurements required for further validation. The goal is to provide a transparent and reproducible model that can be analyzed, critiqued, and further developed by the scientific community.
title: Dalla finestra alla soglia Il conto chiuso di un microrotore ottico a 720◦ nel sangue intero

summary: The study evaluates the effectiveness of a methodology for developing professional digital competencies of pre-service primary school teachers through improved software and methodological support. The methodology combined a six-block methodological model, the integrating educational platform “DigiPed” with five curriculum-aligned modules, a unified cycle of innovative methods and a multi-stage assessment system. A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design with non-equivalent intact groups was carried out in 2023–2025 at three higher education institutions in Uzbekistan with 770 students (experimental group n = 386, control group n = 384). Competence was measured on motivational, cognitive, activity and reflective criteria combined into a weighted integral index K = 0.20k₁ + 0.25k₂ + 0.35k₃ + 0.20k₄; assessors were blind to group membership. At baseline the groups did not differ (χ² = 0.08–3.39; t = 0.13–1.03). After three semesters the experimental group’s mean integral score rose from 56.77 to 67.52 and the control group’s from 56.26 to 59.24 (t = 9.79, p < 0.05). The share of experimental students at the low level fell from 62.7 % to 30.8 % (control group: 51.8 %), and differences were significant on all criteria (χ² = 49.75–68.31). The efficiency coefficient was η = 1.14 overall and 1.13–1.17 across institutions, indicating that the effect is transferable beyond a single university.

Each run also includes composite logs and the well path from DISKOS, Norway's national subsurface data repository, all on one measured-depth index. summary: Data behind the benchmark in the article "How should sub-cellular spatial transcriptomics be quality controlled? A guideline from a benchmark with injected damage" (manuscript in preparation). Forty public Visium HD sections were thinned to fixed depths (12, 25, 50 and 100 mean UMIs per 8 µm bin, and 200 on six sections), and low-quality regions (LQRs) of known size and position were injected: signal loss (1% of counts kept) and mitochondrial elevation. LQRs were 32, 64 and 256 µm across in the tissue interior and at the tissue edge, and 512 µm across in the interior of 38 sections. Each QC method and bin size (an arm) was run on every condition. One archive per section holds, for every depth: the parameters and random seed of each injection step, the ground truth (the 8 µm bins inside an LQR), the 8 µm bins each arm removed, the arms that stopped with an error, and the scores and marker-gene validation. README.md describes the layout and MD5SUMS.txt the checksums. The count matrices are not included. They are rebuilt from the public sections with the benchmark code and the recorded parameters. The source of every section, as the file it was read from, is in sources.tsv: 35 sections released by 10x Genomics and five from Cervilla, Grases Mendoza and Porta-Pardo (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.17999961); sources.tsv gives the licence of each. They are also listed below as related works.

summary: Hybrid models combine softmax attention with linear attention, which compresses history into fixed-size recurrent states to balance model quality and inference efficiency. However, linear attention has not pushed this compression to its limit: we find that the queries, keys, and values of linear layers concentrate in a stable, low-dimensional subspace, a phenomenon we call the linear attention sink, so each state is effectively low-rank, with a rank that varies across states. Yet existing serving systems keep these redundant states dense, reading and rewriting them in full at every decoding step, so their memory traffic grows with the batch size and dominates the decoding cost. Thus SinkState stores each recurrent state in an adaptive low-rank form throughout inference with buffered updates and a local SVD restricted to the top subspace. SinkState further consolidates the remaining components asynchronously on the CPU. On four hybrid models with Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers, from 4B to 120B parameters, SinkState reduces the peak memory of recurrent states by up to 2.6x (1.9x on average) and speeds up decoding by up to 1.58x (1.25x on average) over Mamba-SSM and FLA, while maintaining accuracy.
title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving

summary: Air pollution is a leading environmental risk factor to human health worldwide. Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) is of particular concern due to its ability to penetrate the lungs and enter the cardiovascular system, contributing to respiratory disease, cancer and early mortality. Accurate, high-resolution exposure estimates are therefore essential for assessing health risk and informing effective intervention strategies. However, regulated ground monitoring networks offer limited spatial coverage, and remote sensing and chemical transport models (CTMs) often fail to resolve local-scale variation in PM 2.5 concentrations. A further limitation is that most machine learning approaches to this problem are deterministic, providing no indication of predictive confidence. This study addresses both gaps with a Bayesian deep learning framework that downscales coarse CAMS CTM output to 1 km resolution by leveraging fine-scale land use, population and meteorological covariates and trained against ground observations. Predictive uncertainty was quantified via Monte Carlo dropout, a Bayesian approximation method that adds minimal computational cost. The model achieved strong deterministic accuracy (R 2 = 0.814) with well-calibrated, if slightly conservative, predictive intervals (95% coverage = 0.969) on held-out test data, offering a scalable approach for high-resolution exposure mapping with quantified uncertainty.
title: Uncertainty-aware deep learning for downscaling air quality concentrations

summary: This report documents the curation and open publication of measurements from a long-term Turkey oak ( Quercus cerris ) thinning experiment in the Gargano area, southern Italy, monitored from 1988 to 2026. Nine 0.5-ha plots compare an unthinned control with two thinning regimes: 15% basal-area reduction over two interventions and 33% basal-area reduction in one intervention. Legacy spreadsheet records were cleaned, validated, and organized into a documented SQLite database (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24142797) containing tree measurements, experimental design, controlled vocabularies, metadata, and provenance. The curation workflow addresses duplicate identifiers, irregular or gappy measurement series, unusable records, and missing values, with imputations explicitly flagged. The resource includes a richly documented database, a JSON file with PROV-O provenance, and an entity-relationship diagram of the database schema. It is intended to make the data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable in accordance with FAIR principles, and to provide a reproducible example of data curation for long-term forest research.
title: Data curation example - Almost 50 years of forest monitoring

summary: This repository provides the data, spatial analysis polygons, statistical outputs and reproducible Python workflows associated with the manuscript “Satellite-based aftercare screening for data-scarce landfills: 27 years of vegetation trajectories and baseline sensitivity in Vietnam”. The study examines six Vietnamese landfill sites represented by eight analysis polygons over 1999–2025. The archive includes date-level Landsat Collection 2 observations and Sentinel-2 cross-check exports; approximate site and sector polygons; controlled interrupted time-series analysis; recovery and repeated-parity metrics; Kieu Ky within-site contrasts and baseline-length sensitivity; Typhoon Yagi relative vegetation departures; and supplementary results tables B1–B9. The supplied scripts reproduce statistical tables and article figures from the archived exports without requiring Google Earth Engine access. Google Earth Engine scripts and a Colab notebook are included for re-extraction, subject to user credentials and project setup. These observations support first-stage landfill aftercare screening and prioritisation of field inspections; the analysis polygons are interpreted study areas rather than surveyed waste footprints. KEYWORDS: RELATED MANUSCRIPT: Satellite-based aftercare screening for data-scarce landfills: 27 years of vegetation trajectories and baseline sensitivity in Vietnam (Do not invent or enter an article DOI unless already assigned.)

summary: Augmented reality (AR) is increasingly used in education, but most classroom studies focus on engagement rather than specific emotional or cognitive processes. We re-examined data from a six-week pilot project where AR was integrated into drama lessons for 59 primary-school students in four classes. Our goal was to see what the observations reveal about emotion recognition, emotion regulation, collaboration, problem solving, and reflective reasoning. QuiverVision and CoSpaces Edu were used for role-play, collaborative storytelling, exploring moods in space, replaying conflicts, and reflection. The data included teacher observation rubrics, structured checklists, student exit tickets, and records of regulation strategies. In this paper, we use affective computing as a conceptual framework, not as a description of the technology used in the pilot. Emotions were not detected automatically; instead, the analysis relies on human observation and student self-reports. Of the 106 exit-ticket responses from Weeks 1 and 2, happiness was the most common emotion (73 out of 106; 68.9%). Forty-eight students had emotion-recognition ratings recorded at Weeks 1, 2, 3, and 5, and these ratings changed over time (Friedman χ²(3)=34.21, p<0.001; Kendall's W=0.238), with the mean score rising from 2.90 (SD=0.66) in Week 1 to 3.46 (SD=0.50) in Week 5. Regulation strategies also varied by phase: socially oriented responses were frequent in Week 2, while breathing, pausing, and reframing were more common during the explicit regulation activities in Week 5. Because the prompts and tasks differed each week, these distributions are descriptive and do not show a causal pre/post change. Exploratory correlations found that collaborative storytelling was linked to problem solving, strategy use was associated with returning to role, and understanding emotions was connected with cooperation. Overall, the results show that a pedagogy-first AR drama approach is feasible and highlight what a future study would need: validated measures, comparison groups, multilevel analysis, follow-up data, and carefully controlled multimodal affect sensing.
title: GENEDIS 2026 – Paper 79 – Augmented Reality-Enhanced Drama Through an Affective Computing Lens: A Six-Week Pilot Study of Emotional Intelligence, Emotion Regulation, and Reflective Reasoning in Children

summary: This record provides the computational benchmark instances, initial solutions, final feasible solutions, and source code supporting the study: "Coordinating Cross-Docking and Vehicle Routing under Time-Dependent Congestion-Zone Charges: An Integrated Optimization Approach." The synthetic benchmark includes 18 problem instances covering six customer-set sizes (8, 12, 14, 20, 30, and 50), together with 18 common initial solutions and saved algorithmic solutions from Direct MILP, VND4, Integrated ALNS, and Sequential ALNS. The archive also includes the selected model and algorithm source code required to inspect and reproduce the computational methods. For the three 50-customer instances, no feasible Direct-MILP incumbent was obtained within the recorded time limit. The three VND4 solutions are feasible budget-limited incumbents; the final N4 scans were not completed, and no full N4 local-optimality certificates are claimed. A separate Tehran V5 case-study component includes the available initial and algorithmic solutions and associated source code. Its original problem-instance JSON is not included because redistribution rights for the underlying travel-time/network data require further review. Consequently, this component is not fully self-contained for independent reruns. Execution logs, checkpoints, intermediate solutions, development history, and rerun archives are not included.
title: Computational Dataset and Source Code for Coordinating Cross-Docking and Vehicle Routing under Time-Dependent Congestion-Zone Charges

summary: This record contains the Python code and the reference outputs for the manuscript *What bonus–malus claims identify about accidents that are never claimed* by Wei Zhu (University of Groningen). The code simulates a bonus–malus portfolio in which policyholders report only losses above Lemaire-type retentions, and computes the cross-cell envelope lower bound on unclaimed accidents, its plug-in and fixed-comparison-cell estimates with a one-sided confidence bound, sensitivity factors for departures from common severity, the power of the tail restriction, and the bias and error of audit designs selected on claim history. It also produces the empirical analysis of the French motor liability data freMTPL2: claim frequencies by recorded bonus–malus coefficient, the contrast built on the protection of a first claim and its placebo, and a check on the fremotor1 data. README.md maps every table and result of the paper to the script that produces it, and run_all.py reruns all scripts and compares the regenerated tables with the reference ones. The data (freMTPL2 from OpenML and CASdatasets, fremotor1 from CASdatasets) are public and are not included; data/README.md lists the files and their SHA-256 checksums. Requirements: Python 3.11 or later with NumPy, SciPy, pandas, statsmodels, patsy and pyreadr.
title: Code for: What bonus-malus claims identify about accidents that are never claimed

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24146492 . Peer review report: Caetano et al., investigate the diversity of mammalian box C/D small nucleolar RNAs (SNORDs) by combining Fibrillarin- and Snu13-associated RNA sequencing with extensive analysis of publicly available datasets. They identify 21,732 candidate loci, including a large population of unusually short single-stranded RNAs (20-50 nt), termed tiSNORDs. This work is important because it challenges the current annotation of the mammalian snoRNAs and raises fundamental questions about snoRNP biogenesis and the emergence of regulatory RNAs. Particularly convincing are the enrichment of characteristic box C/D sequence signatures, the association of selected candidates with Fibrillarin, and the demonstration that a 36-nt tiSNORD can guide RNA methylation. The observations concerning terminal stem structures, RNA stability and host-gene expression provide further support for the biological relevance of at least a subset of these RNAs. Therefore, the study is interesting and potentially significant. Addressing several methodological and interpretative concerns , particularly regarding library-preparation biases, statistical validation of candidate identification, and the distinction between mature RNAs and RNA fragments would strengthen claims and introduce reproducibility. Major points: 1. RNA library preparation and size-selection bias. Approximately ~70 % of tiSNORDs are 20-50 nt long, yet the size-selection used with the TruSeq small RNA library preparation kit is not specified. Size-dependent recovery and sequence-dependent ligation biases could substantially influence this distribution. The authors acknowledge such biases for SNORD50 and substantial technical variability between datasets. Clarification of the selected insert range and, ideally, independent analysis of RNAs across a broader size range would strengthen this central conclusion. One would be to use splint-ligation library preparation to get 'unbiased' small RNA library for sequencing (e.g. Maguire et al., 2020; PMID: 32496547). 2. Statistical validation of sequence signatures. The identification of tiSNORDs relies heavily on canonical C/D-box motifs, their terminal positions and uridine enrichment (Figures 1C to 1G). However, no explicit null model accounts for the search criteria, meaning that some positional enrichment is expected by construction. Small RNA-seq ligation biases may also influence nucleotide frequencies (Kim et al., 2019; PMID: 30605524). Permutation analyses using length- and composition-matched intronic sequences processed through the same pipeline would help ensure statistical significance and estimate false-positive rates. Potential spike ins would be of use as well. 3. Distinguishing mature tiSNORDs from RNA fragments. Although the authors demonstrate stable endogenous expression of tiSNORD candidate and successful processing of selected ectopically expressed candidates, these findings cannot necessarily be extrapolated to thousands of low-abundance sequences. Examining coverage across candidate loci, overlapping fragments, flanking regions and potential longer precursors would help distinguish independently matured tiSNORDs from RNA processing or degradation/fragmentation products. 4. Confidence in the proposed repertoire. 12% of candidates exceed one count per million, and substantial discrepancies are observed between independent datasets (Supplementary Figure 3). The authors appropriately acknowledge these limitations further in the text, but the claim that more than 20,000 loci substantially expand the snoRNA repertoire is a potential since it does not have biochemical validation and mentioning that they are "putative" in the abstract would help the reader to understand the scope of this article. title: PREreview of "A novel class of tiny box C/D-like RNAs reveals hidden complexity in the mouse box C/D RNA repertoire"

summary: Data and code to reproduce all tables and figures in "Priced In, Not Zoned Out: Social Capital, Land-Use Regulation, and US Housing Prices." The package tests whether bridging social capital lowers housing prices through trust, or civic and bonding social capital raises them by restricting supply. It contains: - County data (1,747 counties): FHFA residential land prices per acre (Davis, Larson, Oliner and Shui 2021), Social Capital Atlas measures (Chetty et al. 2022), Census building permits 2012-2024, and Wharton WRLURI 2018 metropolitan means. - Metropolitan data (530 CBSAs): WRLURI 2018 and population-weighted social capital. - State panel, 1975-2019: OECD regional house price indices (FHFA), BEA per-capita income and population (SAINC4), CPI-U; 51-unit and 50-state (DC excluded) versions. - Stata 19.5 do-files: CD, CIPS, Westerlund bootstrap cointegration, PMG/MG, CS-ARDL, CS-DL, CCE-MG, Driscoll-Kraay, Mundlak CRE, MMQR, and county/metro fixed-effects models. - Python scripts: 50-state estimates, MMQR with state-cluster bootstrap, density interactions, and robustness checks. - Codebook, README with sources and terms of use, and Figures 1-2. WRLURI survey microdata are not redistributed; only metropolitan-area means derived from them are included.
title: Replication package: Priced In, Not Zoned Out: Social Capital, Land-Use Regulation, and US Housing Prices

summary: R code to reproduce all estimates in the article "Gateway or add-on? Prepaid cards and banking depth in Chilean households". The script uses the 2024 Chilean Household Finance Survey (Encuesta Financiera de Hogares, EFH 2024) of the Central Bank of Chile. It estimates survey-weighted probit models of prepaid card use (EFH item u_tprepago) as a function of banking depth (unbanked, demand account only, current account), non-bank credit, and respondent and household characteristics. Models are estimated separately in each of the 30 implicates, variances are computed with the 1,000 EFH bootstrap replicate weights, and estimates are combined with Rubin's rules. The script reports average marginal effects, contrast models for prepaid vouchers and any prepaid use, interaction analyses (current account x income stratum, age x gender), regressions for a digital financial inclusion index, and Oster (2019) bounds. Results are exported to an Excel workbook. The EFH microdata are not included. They are available from the Central Bank of Chile upon registration. See README.md for data access, software requirements, run instructions and the mapping between output sheets and the article's tables.
title: Replication code for: Gateway or add-on? Prepaid cards and banking depth in Chilean households

summary: Abstract Generative visual AI is increasingly used in early-stage design to produce sketches, concept renderings and alternative visual directions. However, visually convincing outputs do not necessarily constitute traceable or justified design decisions. In human–AI co-creation, generated images may remain weakly connected to design intent, evaluation criteria, evidence and design rationale, making the creative process difficult to review, reuse, and, where applicable, assess consistently. This paper proposes a process-level methodological framework for human–AI co-creation with generative visual AI systems. The framework is conceived as a lightweight traceability schema linking design problem, design intent, evaluation criteria, generative input, AI output, selected and rejected features, specifications, evidence, design decisions and iteration records. Its purpose is not to explain the internal behaviour of the generative model, but to document the human interpretation and decision-making process around generated visual artefacts. The proposal is illustrated through a postgraduate conceptual product design case in which generative visual AI was introduced after a systemic intent-structuring phase. The case provides evidence of feasibility for reconstructing the relationship between prior intent, generated outputs, and design decisions, but it is not presented as a controlled validation. The paper contributes to creative AI and human–AI interaction by reframing generated outputs as intermediate artefacts that require explicit links to intent, evidence and accountable design decisions.
title: From Generative Output to Traceable Design Decisions: A Process-Level Framework for Human–AI Co-Creation in Conceptual Design

files.key: An Asteroid in a Penning Trap.pdf

summary: The triangular Lagrange point of the restricted three-body problem and the radial motion of a charged particle in a Penning trap are both equilibria held at a maximum of an effective potential by a gyroscopic force. Each possesses one mode of negative energy, and each loses linear stability when its two frequencies collide—one at Routh’s mass ratio, the other at the trapping limit. Both systems belong to a single family of planar gyroscopic Hamiltonians. On every level of the conserved angular-momentum invariant, the degree-four normal form of any member at such a collision coincides with the reduced Hamiltonian of an axisymmetric Penning trap whose detuning is shifted by a term proportional to the invariant and whose quartic coefficient is fixed by a single normal-form invariant. On the level containing orbits that start at rest, this reduction yields closed-form laws for the largest excursion, the escape threshold, and the escape time. These laws depend only on the sign of the quartic coefficient and on scaled variables. At the triangular point the coefficient is positive, placing the collision in the soft class: orbits remain confined after stability is lost, with an excursion that grows like the square root of the distance past the critical value. Direct integration confirms the soft law to a fraction of a percent at the smallest detunings tested. Two traps whose quartic coefficient matches that of the triangular point reproduce the same law. Traps with the opposite sign escape at the predicted threshold and in the predicted times. A randomized ensemble of members confirms the classification by the sign of the coefficient. Two further results hold for every member of the family. Before the collision the linear transient gain is exactly the inverse square root of the frequency splitting. With isotropic velocity damping the first-order growth rates depend only on the undamped frequencies, and at the collision they scale with the square root of the damping rate. The first of these explains earlier reports of apparent escape just below Routh’s value as ordinary linear transients that reach a fixed radius. The second recovers the classical magnetron-instability formula as a special case. The results are local, planar, and classical. What transfers between the asteroid and the trap is the normal-form dynamics on each level of the invariant, the transient gain, and the damped linear rates. What does not transfer without further work is the behaviour beyond the normal-form neighbourhood, where the gravitational terms of every order cause the triangular point to deviate from any purely quartic trap.
title: An Asteroid in a Penning Trap

summary: v2026-11-10b release — scoring-shortcut full fix (correctness patch, no new data). Fixes four shortcuts in the v4 scoring pipeline discovered during audit of scripts/score_v4.py + scripts/enrich_v7_scores.py . Same v7 union peak set (2,085,175 peaks), same 10 cohorts (67 patients), same 430 pseudobulks as v2026-11-10. enhancer_candidate_matrix.parquet , peak_provenance.parquet , and union_peak_reference.bed are byte-identical. Only the scores and derived reports changed. Shortcuts fixed: (1) spec_pct_myeloid was ranking log1p(cpm_myeloid) — strength on a different scale — not specificity; now the percentile rank over distal peaks of log2(min(cpm_microglia, cpm_TAM) / max cpm among 8 non-myeloid primary CTs) , the honest pan-myeloid AAV-designer ratio. (2) spec_pct_{malignant_AC,MES,NPC,OPC} was hardcoded 0 for all four subtypes (they weren't in PRIMARY_CTS), which capped subtype primary_score at 0.5 — pure strength ranking. Now each subtype's spec is the rank of log2(cpm_sub / max cpm among {other 3 subtypes, malignant pooled, 9 non-malignant primaries}) . (3) The column named strength_frags_per_cell_wn_<ct> was computed as raw_count_mean / 1000 × width_scale with a hardcoded 1000 cell-count divisor. Now it's the true per-cell density: mean over patients of (raw_count / n_cells_patient × 500 / peak_width) . Per-pseudobulk cell counts were gathered for all 10 cohorts: 5 from existing TSVs, 4 from per-cohort h5ads via patient_id × pool_label , dejong non-myeloid from the 103 GB integrated atlas h5ad via a fine→coarse pool rule, raviram from integrated per-sample h5ads. The unified pseudobulk_cellcounts.tsv (671 rows, 97.4% of matrix pseudobulks) is included for provenance. (4) All percentile ranks now computed over distal peaks (|dist_to_tss| ≥ 2 kb) only, not all peaks including promoters. Visible impact: subtype primary_score rose from median ~0.498 (strength-only, capped) to ~0.998 (honest spec + strength). Myeloid median log2FC rose from 0.232 to 1.308 (shortcut ranked strength twice; honest ranks true selectivity). Strength rankings no longer biased toward peaks whose signal comes disproportionately from large pseudobulks. HTML viewer: same template as v2026-11-10 (expansion rows with UCSC Genome Browser links, 14-CT bar pairs on shared atlas-wide CPM scale, per-patient CPM grid, per-cohort detection chips, distance-band + patient-detection filters). summary: Code, protocol and registration documents, run-level records, figure scripts and image data for the manuscript Limits of calibrating a synthetic X-ray CT degradation model by matching unlabelled image statistics: A controlled case study (K. Rew, J. Chung, S. Lee; submitted to PLOS ONE). summary: The Kung–Traub conjecture states that the convergence order of a memoryless scalar iterative method using n evaluations of a function and its derivatives per iteration cannot exceed 2^(n−1). We prove this bound for real scalar, deterministic, causal methods with adaptive queries and partially defined rules, without requiring continuity or computability of those rules. For every total method T with budget n and every p > 2^(n−1), we construct an entire function F, real on the real axis, a simple root α, and a sequence x_m → α such that |T_F(x_m) − α| / |x_m − α|^p → +∞. The construction uses properties of Wronskians of polynomial spaces, concentration of zeros, and quantitative perturbations that preserve exactly the responses to previous queries. We also develop two formalizations of computation: a fixed-budget query model and a model of procedures with internal states and performed evaluations. We prove exact representations that preserve, within the budget under consideration, the domains of valid computations, outputs, records, and evaluation counts by derivative order. From this correspondence, we obtain the order barrier for local realizations and the real formulation of the Kung–Traub bound with the specified operational cost. The results are established for real functions and real nodes. Historical documentation: Earlier versions of this research, completed on September 17–18, 2026, together with their available provenance records, are preserved at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24147519 .
title: The Kung–Traub Conjecture for Memoryless Real Scalar Methods: Proof and Formalization of Computational Procedures

summary: Heterogeneous evidence systems frequently combine observations that differ in measurement process, provenance, semantic representation, reliability, temporal coverage, spatial resolution, and statistical dependence. Naive aggregation can consequently amplify duplicated sources, conceal systematic bias, misrepresent uncertainty, and force consensus across claims that are not genuinely comparable. This manuscript proposes Cross-Domain Evidence-Constrained State Reconstruction (CDECSR), a research architecture whose default mechanism is Provenance-Aware, Uncertainty-Preserving State Reconstruction (PAUSR). The architecture preserves four macro-stages: taxonomic and semantic anchoring; error, dependence, and reliability parameterization: triangulation, robust fusion, and contradiction management; and latent-state estimation, validation, and controlled revision. These stages are operationalized through fourteen layers. The formal framework distinguishes the underlying target state from observations and model-dependent estimates. It represents heterogeneous observations through source-specific measurement models, accounts for shared provenance and correlated errors, and treats source reliability as a conditional quantity rather than a direct measure of truth. The proposed output is a state estimate or posterior distribution accompanied by uncertainty, provenance, unresolved contradictions, assumptions, validation results, and a reproducibility record. The architecture is specified through the Conflicting Reports in an Environmental Crisis (CREC), a structured primary case in which field reports and other observations may disagree about event location, timing, intensity, extent, and progression. The manuscript also defines a falsifiable research program, conditional mathematical results, counterexamples, simulation requirements, validation protocols, and a fourteen-step pathway toward a research paper.
tags: cross-domain inference; state reconstruction; evidence fusion; truth discovery; provenance; correlated evidence; robust estimation; uncertainty quantification; contradiction management; reproducibility.
title: Cross-Domain Evidence-Constrained State Reconstruction Theory

summary: The work looks at the Riemann hypothesis from the standpoint of the model “The Birth of Dimensions” (BD). The number arrow is understood as a projection of a process — the comparison of the standard-observer with its surroundings. Four reference quantities follow from the construction: 1 — the observer and the standard; 0 and ∞ — two infinities converging into one point; 1/2 — the level of lost phase, a line perpendicular to the arrow; 2 — the first distinction, the point of doubling. Together they define a sphere: the arrow is a tangent to the circle through the observer, the rotation goes about an axis, the spin-up force is applied at a point of the equator, and its trace on the arrow is 2. The main result is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD: if the original process is a sine, that is, a rotation; if everything tied to the observer is his likeness; if an instantaneous snapshot has no duplicates and balance sets the mirror, — then all zeros lie on the equator of the sphere, that is, on the line Re s = 1/2 (section 4). This is a proof within the model, not a mathematical proof. In mathematics the hypothesis remains open: of the nine links of the chain eight are known theorems, and the ninth — that the local rotations of all primes form one rotation — is equivalent to the hypothesis itself (section 5). Each step carries a status: [K] — a known mathematical fact, [H] — a hypothesis or interpretation of the author, [O] — an open question. The detailed exposition is placed in Appendices 1–10. They show that the logic of BD independently leads to what mathematicians obtained by abstract means: Riemann's mirror, the Euler product, the Gauss sum, Gram points, the Riemann–Siegel formula, the de Bruijn–Newman constant, Li's criterion, Weil positivity, the adelic approach of Tate and Connes, the Lee–Yang theorem and other results (section 6). For BD this is strong support: the model generates the same mathematics from its own principles. Version 12. The article has been restructured so that the main conclusion is not lost among the reasoning. Part I: a dictionary of BD and mathematical notions; foundations by construction (1, 0 and ∞, 1/2, 2); the picture of the sphere with a figure (the arrow as a tangent through the observer, 1/2 as the axis of rotation, 2 as the spin-up point); a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD from the postulates P1–P4; the mathematical status (eight links of the chain are known theorems, the ninth is equivalent to the hypothesis); the role of the observer; a list of known results that BD reproduces. Part II: the former detailed exposition as Appendices 1–10, with additions on the sphere, observers in every prime and the author’s position.       Работа рассматривает гипотезу Римана с позиции модели «Рождение измерений» (РИ). Числовая стрела понимается как проекция процесса — сравнения эталона-наблюдателя с окружением. Из построения следуют четыре опорные величины: 1 — наблюдатель и эталон; 0 и ∞ — две бесконечности, сходящиеся в одну точку; 1/2 — уровень потерянной фазы, прямая, перпендикулярная стреле; 2 — первое различение, точка удвоения. Вместе они задают сферу: стрела — касательная к кругу через наблюдателя, вращение идёт вокруг оси, сила раскрутки приложена в точке экватора, и её след на стреле — 2. Главный результат — доказательство гипотезы Римана в рамках РИ: если исходный процесс — синус, то есть вращение; если всё, связанное с наблюдателем, — его подобие; если в мгновенном снимке нет дублей, а баланс задаёт зеркало, — то все нули лежат на экваторе сферы, то есть на прямой Re s = 1/2 (раздел 4). Это доказательство внутри модели, а не математическое доказательство. В математике гипотеза остаётся открытой: из девяти звеньев цепочки восемь — известные теор
title: The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2: The Riemann Hypothesis in the Light of the Birth of Dimensions Model

summary: Abstract This paper proposes the Reference-Standard Inference-to-Fact Escalation Principle (RSIFEP), a general theoretical framework for analysing how a reasonable default inference about an object, individual, event, process, model, or system may be presented with a stronger epistemic status than its available justification warrants. The framework distinguishes the basis used to construct an inference from the inference itself, the evidence supporting it, the status assigned to it, the scope within which it is. asserted, and the role it plays in an operational system. A reference standard may consist of a statistical base rate, a measure of central tendency, an operational default, a validated baseline, a normative or formal standard, or a model-based analogy. These categories are related but not interchangeable. The central proposition is conditional. A default inference may be reasonable and useful without being an established fact. A status-escalation error may arise when an inference is promoted to the status of an established fact, objective description, or necessary system condition without adequate evidential, logical, or formal warrant. Such an error does not automatically produce a contradiction, paradox, dilemma, or operational failure. Those outcomes require independent definitions and additional conditions. The paper develops a six-class reference-standard taxonomy, a formal representation of reasonable reference-standard inference, a seven-stage-or-more process architecture, a twelve-category outcome taxonomy, seven theoretical propositions, a general mathematical specification, and a research programme centred on the social-media newcomer purpose-projection case. The framework also specifies its boundaries, alternative explanations, potential falsifiers, measurement requirements, and route to empirical validation. RSIFEP is presented as a proposed theoretical contribution rather than an established uni- versal law. Its novelty, explanatory advantage, measurement validity, and domain generality remain questions for literature comparison, formal analysis, and empirical testing. Keywords: reference standards; reasonable inference; default reasoning; epistemic status; status escalation; evidential warrant; scope overextension; contradiction; paradox; system-level outcomes.

title: The Reference-Standard Inference-to-Fact Escalation Principle (RSIFEP): A General Framework for Reasonable Default Inference, Epistemic Status Escalation, and System-Level Outcomes

summary: This paper proposes the Representational-Operational State-Inversion Principle (ROSIP), a candidate framework for describing cases in which an internal representation assigns a state that is the formally defined inverse of a corresponding operational state, while the operational state itself need not undergo a physical reversal. The motivating case is a false awakening: a person is asleep according to an independent physiological reference while the person's dream represents the self as awake. The proposed framework generalizes this contrast by separating the operational state of a system, the internal state of its model, the represented proposition about a shared referent, the inverse relation between comparable state features, and the attribution of the represented state as current reality. The paper defines a common semantic comparison space, an involutive inverse-state mapping, a state-divergence measure, an inversion-fit score, and a gated event-classification rule. It distinguishes representational inversion from ordinary mismatch, stale information, hypothetical simulation, false reporting, and actual reversal of physical dynamics. Eight proposed mechanism stages and fourteen analytical layers organize the framework. The manuscript identifies five foundational domains, a primary sleep-science validation pro- gram, six exploratory application domains, seven testable hypotheses, alternative explanations, falsification criteria, methodological requirements, and a fourteen-stage research roadmap. The framework's central contribution is presented as a testable formalization proposal, not as an established discovery. Its explanatory value depends on construct validity, temporal alignment, reliable measurement, independent replication, and evidence of incremental value over existing explanations. Representational state; operational state; state inversion; internal model; cybernetics; dynamical systems; state estimation; information theory; false awakening; cross-domain modeling.
tags: Representational state; operational state; state inversion; internal model; cybernetics; dynamical systems; state estimation; information theory; false awakening; cross-domain modeling.
title: The Representational-Operational State-Inversion Principle (ROSIP): A Proposed Formal Framework for Inverse State Representation, Functional Attribution, and Apparent Cross-Level Paradox

summary: Abstract This paper proposes the Functional Direction-Purpose Mismatch Framework (FDPMF), a goal-relative framework for analyzing operations whose functional direction may not correspond to an agent's specified purpose. The framework distinguishes structural direction- purpose relations from measured direct utility, capability acquisition from execution, and direct utility from broader functional value. The mathematical core defines incremental direct utility as a difference between expected goal-related outcomes under an operation and a specified baseline. This definition enables conditional statements about positive, zero, or negative contribution while avoiding the unsupported inference that a mismatch automatically makes an operation universally useless. A separate Signal-Identity Inference Module (SIIM) examines how an observed event is used to infer an agent's identity or motive. Bayesian notation is used to formalize the evidential relationship between an observation and competing hypotheses. The framework does not treat any single learned or performed behavior as a deterministic indicator of sexual orientation. The primary illustrative case concerns a heterosexual self-identified male learner being taught a sexual behavior directed toward a male recipient, where the intended use is excluded from the learner's explicitly specified personal sexual goal. The case is conditional on these assumptions and is distinguished from a control case in which the target of the learned operation is consistent with the learner's stated goal. The paper defines the framework's ontology, terminology, mathematical variables, core mechanism, propositions, boundary conditions, operationalization protocol, empirical hy- potheses, research domains, falsification criteria, and manuscript-development roadmap. No empirical results are claimed. The paper concludes that the framework is conceptually specified for investigation, while its empirical validity and novelty remain open. Keywords: functional direction; purpose congruence; goal-relative utility; causal inference; capability acquisition; signaling theory; identity inference; operationalization; theoretical model

title: The Functional Direction-Purpose Mismatch Framework (FDPMF): A Goal-Relative Theory of Direct Functional Utility, Capability Acquisition, and Signal-Based Identity Inference

summary: Observations of a common physical event may differ across sensors because the sensors operate at different elevations, coordinate frames, reference times, sampling rates, calibration states, response functions, and uncertainty regimes. Raw disagreement does not, by itself, establish a physical contradiction, a sensor failure, or the existence of a new physical phenomenon. It may arise from frame misregistration, clock offsets, distinct measurands, correlated errors, genuine event dynamics, model misspecification, or insufficient observability. This paper specifies the Unified Cross-Frame Information Convergence Architecture (UCFICA), a modular framework for diagnosing and reconciling multisource observations before reconstructing a target system state. Its operational estimation core is the Reference-Conditioned Multisource State Reconstruction Architecture (RCMSRA). The framework preserves the Multi-Elevation Spatial Observation Discrepancy (MESOD) as its primary case, the Reference-Conditioned State Reconstruction Mechanism (RCSRM) as its default mechanism, and the Cross-Dimensional State Realization Protocol (CD-SRP) as its named operational protocol. The manuscript formalizes heterogeneous measurement models, coordinate and time registration, uncertainty propagation, linear-Gaussian information-form fusion, nonlinear estimation alternatives, unknown-correlation handling, residual diagnostics, and explicit rules for unresolved or incompatible observations. It preserves the original five conceptual levels while mapping them to nine operational layers. Relativistic corrections, quantum measurement theory, and holographic or cosmological hypotheses are retained as conditional research branches rather than assumed components of every fusion problem. Conditional propositions establish the mathematical circumstances under which familiar Bayesian and linear-estimation results apply. In particular, the paper does not assume that increasing the number of sensors necessarily drives estimation covariance to zero. It defines falsifiable hypotheses, controlled simulation scenarios, empirical validation requirements, counterexamples, and a staged reproducibility protocol. No simulation or empirical result is claimed to have been obtained in this manuscript.
tags: multisensor fusion; cross-frame registration; state estimation; measurement uncertainty; Bayesian inference; observability; information-form filtering; MESOD; UCFICA; conditional multiphysics
title: Unified Cross-Frame Information Convergence Architecture

summary: We compare neural networks, exact Matérn kernel regression and their combinations as emulators of a six-dimensional radiative-transfer table on the 285-band EMIT grid, and we study how their forward accuracy carries over to reflectance retrieval. Over ten partitions of 23{,}313 states, a kernel with one length scale per input reaches $0.095\%$ mean relative radiance error and a network $0.387\%$; a kernel on the concatenated hidden features of five networks reaches $0.076\%$. Forward and inverse rankings disagree. A convex stack improves on a wide feature kernel by only $0.0006$ radiance percentage points, yet its 95th-percentile reflectance error is larger at every partition, three times larger on average. We prove that on the physical domain the constrained retrieval error is at most the retrieval-weighted component error divided by the transmission, with constant one, that the rate this implies is sharp, and that errors proportional to the transmission lose no rate. The reversal persists on the physical domain of the retrieval and when every family is retrained on physically admissible targets only; on a second radiative-transfer code, whose transmissions stay away from zero outside one opaque band, it is much weaker.
title: Learned representations and kernel corrections for radiative-transfer emulation

summary: The four-component (T, I, N, F) neutrosophic representation distinguishes pure indeterminacy I from neutrality N, in addition to truth T and falsehood F. Existing neutrosophic-graph research mainly assigns uncertain values to vertices or edges and studies the resulting graph structure. This paper addresses a different problem: a fixed weighted network is given, while a (T, I, N, F) assessment is the signal carried by each vertex. A benefit-coordinate embedding converts the semantic order into the standard product order and permits graph-Laplacian methods without merging neutrality and indeterminacy. For continuous-time heat diffusion, we prove preservation of the TINF cube, semantic order, component means, complement symmetry, and a maximum principle. A weighted Dirichlet energy is shown to decay monotonically, with exponential convergence governed by the algebraic connectivity. A stable discrete-time scheme and a soft-anchor graph filter are also established. For partially observed signals, the TINF harmonic extension is characterized simultaneously as the unique Dirichlet-energy minimizer and as a convex combination of boundary assessments. This yields complement equivariance, a semantic maximum principle, nonexpansive dependence on boundary data, and an explicit topology-perturbation bound. Complement-paired TINF prototypes are then introduced for four-state semi-supervised inference. They form a regular simplex in benefit coordinates, and nearest-prototype TINF classification is proved exactly equivalent to classical multiclass harmonic label propagation when anchors use the prototypes. In contrast, a symmetric three-component collapse makes neutrality and pure indeterminacy non-identifiable. An exact cycle example and Monte Carlo stochastic-block experiments confirm the equivalence numerically and demonstrate the information loss caused by collapse. The framework provides a mathematically auditable route for propagating four-component information over social, sensor, and knowledge networks.
title: TINF Signals on Networks: Complement-Equivariant Graph Diffusion, Harmonic Extension, and Semi-Supervised Inference

summary: The ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo community benchmark for discriminating physiological from non-physiological protein–protein interfaces (Schweke et al., Proteomics 2023) contains 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 PDB entries. We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The benchmark is described with Bioschemas/schema.org JSON-LD: every interface is annotated with its label, chains, structural features, sequence-cluster assignment, provenance and licence, and linked to the PDB structure files and to snapshots of the RCSB PDB metadata. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the source repository, and the errors found were corrected. summary: This article develops a mathematical reconstruction of a conceptual proposal called the fixed attractor. The proposal starts from a question in the philosophy of social order: why do human societies repeatedly produce forms of cooperation and coordination without converging either to a permanently unified condition or to uninterrupted, system-wide disintegration? The article approaches this question through a deliberately limited dialogue between Qur’anic concepts and stochastic dynamical systems. Five conceptual motifs are examined: persistent human difference (ikhtilaf ), countervailing action (daf ), a boundary or separator (barzakh), the regularity of social processes (sunnat Allah), and the presence of morally exceptional minorities. These motifs are treated as interpretive prompts for model construction, not as mathematical theorems contained verbatim in scripture. The formal model describes a vector of normalized social indicators evolving in an open, bounded state space. Its drift combines mean-reverting forces with cross-domain coupling; its diffusion is state-dependent and vanishes at the boundary; and its finite-activity jump component represents shocks whose state-dependent impact preserves the interior. The article corrects and makes explicit several conditions that are necessary for the model to work: uniform inward-pointing drift at every face of the state domain, a stable coupling matrix, and a jump map that preserves the domain. Under these assumptions, a logarithmic barrier function establishes non-attainment of the boundary in finite time. Additional Lyapunov, Feller, and irreducibility conditions yield existence and uniqueness of an invariant probability distribution. When the drift is centered and the jump marks have zero mean, the invariant mean equals the model’s interior reference point, while non-degenerate interior diffusion produces persistent stationary variation. A three-dimensional example is specified for political, economic, and cultural indicators. A reproducible Euler–Maruyama/compound-Poisson experiment, reconstructed from the supplied source manuscript with a consistent parameter matrix, gives illustrative sample means close to the reference point and non-zero dispersion. These computations verify the numerical behavior of the chosen model implementation; they do not constitute empirical evidence that actual societies obey it. The article therefore separates three claims that are often conflated: a theological reading, a mathematical implication conditional on assumptions, and an empirical hypothesis requiring operational definitions and historical data. Its contribution is a transparent bounded-dynamics framework and a research programme for testing it, rather than a proof of a universal law of history.
tags: social dynamics; bounded stochastic processes; invariant distribution; boundary non- attainment; coupled systems; jump–diffusion; Qur'anic concepts; social order; resilience; model validation
title: The Fixed Attractor: A Bounded Stochastic Framework for the Dynamics of Human Social Order

summary: Freestanding thin films of quantum materials naturally develop sub-micrometer, nonuniform strain fields that strongly affect their electronic, magnetic, and structural properties in both equilibrium and nonequilibrium conditions. However, current methods to quantitatively resolve these mesoscopic features are primarily restricted to scanning probes, making it challenging for dynamical measurements such as single-shot imaging and femtosecond microscopy. Here, we present a new computational framework which we denote as bend contour electron tomography (BCET), which efficiently converts bend contours in transmission electron microscope images into quantitative two-dimensional maps of strain and topography. By iteratively minimizing a designed loss function between experimental and simulated bend contour images, BCET retrieves both surface morphology and in-plane strain tensor fields without requiring scanning or diffraction mapping. We applied BCET to freestanding SrTiO 3 thin films, demonstrating the successful reconstruction of the local strain distribution and curvature field with high fidelity. Our approach provides a quantitative framework for characterizing mesoscale structures in freestanding films using wide-field imaging, opening new avenues to investigate how spatial inhomogeneity governs phase transitions and nonequilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.
title: Bend Contour Electron Tomography (BCET): Quantitative strain and topography mapping
