Because the corpus invokes 15 distinct theoretical frames, none shared by more than six studies, the review proposes a three-stage integrative framework — attentional capture, affective arousal, and evaluative elaboration and control — with two documented failure gates and a state-and-trait modulation band. A pre-specified feasibility appraisal was conducted in place of a meta-analysis. Only 8 of 30 studies reported means, standard deviations and cell sizes jointly, 12 reported an extractable effect estimate, and 4 reported confidence intervals, with a median sample of approximately 32 participants. No outcome family combined sufficient study numbers with sufficient reporting, so a structured synthesis without meta-analysis is reported in accordance with the SWiM guideline, together with the reporting and harmonisation changes that would make quantitative synthesis achievable.
title: GENEDIS 2026 – Paper 133 - Neurophysiological Markers of Healthy and Sustainable Food Choice: A Systematic Review of EEG, Eye-Tracking and Electrodermal Evidence

summary: The manuscript gives a proposed learning algorithm for an unknown polynomially sparse Pauli Hamiltonian of operator norm at most one, using only forward evolution queries whose durations are all at least a fixed positive constant T. It obtains maximum coefficient error epsilon with constant success probability and total evolution time polynomial in the qubit number and sparsity, divided by epsilon, up to logarithmic factors. Circuit and classical processing costs are polynomial; constants may depend on T. The construction uses a two-time residual inverse and does not assume controlled access to, or the inverse of, the unknown evolution. This deposit preserves the website manuscript, version 1.0, dated 1 October 2026, by Yuxuan Zhang. It is a complete proof candidate with internal review and supporting checks; independent expert verification and exhaustive priority confirmation remain outstanding. Website and supporting material: https://yuxuanzhang1995.github.io/agentic-research/fixed-duration-hamiltonian-learning/ QIQC original: https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_30954594cf01ebb3/
title: Heisenberg-scaling sparse Hamiltonian learning with a fixed minimum query duration

summary: Transect-level shoreline change rates (Theil–Sen, tide-corrected with EOT20, tan β = 0.1) for 12,787 sandy open-coast transects (2 km spacing) in Indonesia, 2013 to 31 October 2026, from Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level 2 imagery in Google Earth Engine. Includes sand-classifier probabilities for 36,765 candidate transects, training labels (first-pass, authors’ Sentinel-2 consensus, high-resolution), cross-validation and robustness diagnostics, the earlier 2013–2025 baseline for comparison, and processing scripts. Intended for screening, not site design: roughly one third of transects classed sandy are expected to be false positives, labels come from the authors, and rates are subject to a ±100 m search window and uniform beach slope. Accompanies a manuscript submitted to Civil Engineering Journal.
title: Shoreline change rates along sandy coasts of the Indonesian archipelago, Landsat 8/9, 2013–31 October 2026 (transect-level dataset and code)

summary: Coded dataset, document manifest and analysis code behind every figure, table and statistical test reported in the paper. Thirty-six Malaysian listed organizations in three strata of regulatory attention are coded on four governance dimensions — fairness, transparency, accountability and privacy — giving 144 organization-dimension cells. Each cell takes the highest level found anywhere in that organization’s corpus: 0 no AI-specific disclosure on that dimension, 1 an artifact is stated to exist, 2 an activity is described as performed, 3 a retrievable instance is reported. Every cell carries the basis note recording the passage and page it rests on. Contents. 18 CSV files, including the coding of record, four second-coder files from the reliability work and the manifest of all 79 source documents. 17 Python analysis scripts requiring no third-party packages except matplotlib for the figures. 37 working notes from coding and adjudication, and the sealed passage sets used for the second, independent application of the codebook. Reproduction. README.md lists the command that regenerates each reported result, including the four inter-coder comparisons and the four alternative readings of the coding. Not included. The 79 source documents are the copyright of the organizations that published them and are not redistributed. All are public. corpus.csv and Appendix B of the paper list every one with its page count, so the corpus can be reconstructed independently from the issuers’ own websites and from Bursa Malaysia. The second application of the coding protocol reported in Section 4 of the paper was carried out by a language model agent supplied with the codebook and the passage set, not by a trained human coder. The reported agreement figures therefore test whether the codebook can be followed consistently rather than inter-rater reliability in the usual sense.
title: Replication data and code for "Policy Without Evidence: A Three-Level Measure of Artificial Intelligence Governance Disclosure by Malaysian Boards"

summary: Code, configurations, image list, masks, pairings, seeds and per-image scores for the unified benchmark in 'From Pixels to Faces: A Comprehensive Survey of Deep Learning-Based Face Inpainting and Face Unmasking'. Generated outputs are archived separately on Zenodo.
title: Mohamed-Abokhalil/From-Pixels-to-Faces: v1.0 — From Pixels to Faces

files.key: GENEDIS 2026 – Paper 154 – Structured Cognitive Training Added to the Multicomponent Exercise Programme in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment - Protocol for a Single-Blind Three-Arm Randomised Controlled Trial.mp4

summary: Therapeutic exercise is recommended for people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), yet it remains unclear whether adding structured cognitive training to an exercise programme already incorporating dual-task activities provides additional benefit beyond the physical programme itself. This protocol describes a single-blind, three-arm randomised controlled trial of a multicomponent motor–motor dual-task exercise programme for people with MCI (MExeProMCI), with and without a superimposed structured cognitive-training programme. Fortyfive community-dwelling adults over 50 years with amnestic MCI (Montreal Cognitive Assessment ≥20) are allocated (1:1:1) to MExeProMCI-Cog, the dualtask exercise programme plus structured cognitive training; to MExeProMCI, the same programme without additional cognitive training; or to a control group receiving an educational leaflet. The primary outcome is dynamic balance, assessed with the mini-Balance Evaluation Systems Test (mini-BESTest). Secondary outcomes include functional gait, three-dimensional gait analysis during single- and dual-task walking and obstacle crossing, cognition, executive function, physical performance, fear of falling, mood, neuropsychiatric symptoms and adherence. Assessors are blinded and the primary analysis is an analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline scores on an intention-to-treat basis. Comparing the two active arms will determine whether structured cognitive training adds benefit beyond the exercise programme alone. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07334392).
title: Structured Cognitive Training Added to the Multicomponent Exercise Programme in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment: Protocol for a Single-Blind, Three-Arm Randomised Controlled Trial

summary: CylOn is a framework allowing to reconstruct HEP experiments tracks on multiple backends.
title: CylOn: An(other) Geometry Agnostic Framework for Heterogenous Track Reconstruction

summary: Frozen pre-registration of a study that compares smoke-dependent exit choice in pyFDS-Evac (JuPedSim coupled with FDS 6.10.1) with survivor exit-use data from The Station Nightclub fire (Fahy et al. 2011, Table 2). It was frozen before the first production FDS fire run. This archive is the source tree of the pyFDS-Evac repository at tag station-prereg-v1 (commit aaeda1f3). The directory assets/station_prereg/ contains: preregistration.md: targets, registered criteria and bands, run design, arms and sensitivities, fire inputs, outputs already seen, failure policy, and changes from the study plan; freeze_record.md: software versions, build, run and scoring commands for every arm, and seeds; fds/: the six FDS input decks (0.2 m central, low and high yields, ±15 s HRR shift; 0.1 m grid check), their generator, and the HRR curve digitised from NIST NCSTAR 2 Fig. 5-42; SHA256SUMS: checksums of these files, the scenario configs, the scoring script and uv.lock. The study is a comparison with survivor exit-use data, not a validation and not a forensic reconstruction. Any registered criterion that fails will be reported as a disclosed failure.
title: Pre-registration of the Station Nightclub coupled fire–evacuation study with pyFDS-Evac (station-prereg-v1)

summary: Observed Palworld stat values support a binary32 passive percent round trip, food-rate corrections, additive partner bonuses and an inclusive 30% hunger threshold, with HP unaffected by hunger. This dataset accompanies Lore Armory's v2.0 technical note for build 25246127 and contains 2,400 checked stat values across worlds A–K, distinguishing the later K2 pass and repeated party or fullness states. All have numerical predictions and match; four previously unavailable H predictions are now retrospective calculations from recovered case inputs. The observation basis distinguishes 1,834 individual numerical readbacks from 566 outcomes explicitly confirmed equal to named predictions for completed sets. The CSV records each available case label, species, level, inputs, prediction, observation and comparison status, and preserves original frozen predictions where available so that later corrections cannot be mistaken for prior confirmation. Six public mathematical copies of F–K prediction sheets retain selected and rival values, with the original commitment list, a separate checksum manifest for the public copies, and the superseded, unchecked J v1 status. The original and public-copy hashes refer to different bytes. The README supplies a hand calculation, column definitions, exact count filters, observation provenance and open questions. The rows reproduce every empirical headline count in the note; overlapping scoring subsets are explicitly marked. The package does not imply confirmation of every partner star level, food-plus-hunger evaluation order or game build.
title: Palworld Pal stat verification: observations and frozen predictions (v2.0.1)

summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. Actor adaptation estimates on-policy memory value within rollout groups with and without memory, using a reward that prioritizes resolution and penalizes step count in successful runs. Provenance-gated value credit assigns the additional value term to steps identified as using memory-supplied anchors, while every step retains outcome credit. On ChainSWE, CoReMem raises the 27B actor's resolve rate from 21.0% to 25.7%, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens, including memory-module calls, relative to the untrained actor model without memory.
title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation

summary: Deep neural networks for image processing are increasingly deployed on resource-constrained edge devices such as drones, medical systems, and smartphones, where limited computational resources and memory bandwidth pose significant challenges for efficient inference. Pruning during training often produces highly sparse convolutional kernels, offering the potential to significantly reduce computation and memory requirements. However, exploiting this sparsity efficiently at runtime remains challenging due to irregular memory access patterns and workload imbalance across processing elements. In this work, we investigate the standard convolution with sparse weights and analyze its performance characteristics through roofline analysis, showing that a 3 x 3 sparse convolution achieves an arithmetic intensity of approximately 10 FLOP/byte compared to roughly 96 FLOP/byte for its dense counterpart. We propose techniques for an efficient sparse convolution at high sparsities. Preliminary results demonstrate that our approach achieves upto 1.65x speedup as compared to dense convolution on NVIDIA A100 and upto 1.52x on NVIDIA Jetson Nano (Tegra X1) , motivating further exploration of direct convolution as a practical path to efficient sparse inference on modern accelerators/edge devices.
title: Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Sparse Convolution

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, the standard approach, gives results indistinguishable from chance across models, even when restricted to the cited passage. We determine that the cause is structural: a model answering from memory selects a citation that agrees with its output. Comparing ten attribution methods on identical claims, the contrast between the model's distribution with and without context best separates provenance. Acting on that signal does not improve provenance honesty at these base rates. The resulting detector is hence still not accurate enough to act on: it measures what the model knew rather than what it used, and separating those remains the open problem.
title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a $4$ GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an $8$ GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, $\texttt{llama.cpp}$'s K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At $1\%$ and $3.5\%$ perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are $5.7-31.4\%$ smaller than the best $\texttt{llama.cpp}$ format. A bit-exact $0.21$ mm$^2$ ASIC decoder unit ($1$ GHz, $7$ nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to $36\%$ and $38\%$ ($54\%$ and $44\%$ with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ needs $58-64\%$ less time and $53-57\%$ less energy per token than CPU $\texttt{llama.cpp}$, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6$\times$ faster at $3.89$ bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).
title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs

summary: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC2014. These findings distinguish reference informativeness from fusion benefit and reveal context-dependent utility.
title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling

summary: Actions in expert demonstrations exhibit temporal structure. An ordered-versus-shuffled analysis across five environments confirms this dependence. We ask whether action proposals that better reflect expert continuity can improve visual world-model planning. Rather than imposing generic smoothness, we learn continuations from the temporal structure of demonstrated actions. Our locality-gated deep-kernel Gaussian-process prior, LG-DKGP, combines recent and longer-range executed action history, predicts a neural continuation, and learns a temporal Gaussian-process (GP) residual. A training-derived exploration scale initializes search around the corrected mean; a frozen world model evaluates progress toward the goal. Training first fits the neural mean, then jointly optimizes the prior with the GP residual using expert future actions. The resulting planner achieves 87.07\% macro success across five simulated tasks spanning native and fragment-level goal attainment, compared with 71.03\% for INTACT, 61.66\% for PRISM, and 58.66\% for LeWM. Component interventions and expert-relative action-structure comparisons support demonstration-informed continuations and reveal task-dependent effects of visual conditioning, history length, and planning horizon.
title: Rethinking Actions: Continuity-Aware Priors for World-Model Planning

summary: This repository provides the Python implementations, numerical datasets, verification scripts, and supporting computational results associated with the manuscript “Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape Organized by Hypoxia–Immune–Matrix Feedback” . The study investigates nonlinear tumor–immune dynamics using a six-state mechanistic model coupling immunogenic and immune-escape tumor phenotypes, innate and adaptive immune responses, oxygen availability, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Particular attention is given to finite-amplitude oscillations arising through a subcritical Hopf bifurcation and a limit point of cycles (LPC), resulting in equilibrium–cycle bistability and perturbation-dependent transitions. Version 2 (v2) preserves the original numerical archive and extends the computational reproducibility materials with additional analyses and verification procedures developed during manuscript revision. The principal additions include: Generalized-Hopf analysis and investigation of reversible phenotype conversion. Ablation-specific Hopf and LPC calculations to assess the contributions of hypoxia-mediated conversion and immune-pressure feedback. Directional basin-threshold calculations and extended numerical integrations. Expanded parameter-sensitivity and robustness analyses. Additional shooting-based and adaptive-collocation verification of periodic solutions. Floquet stability screening of 252 periodic orbits, including a targeted assessment of potential period-doubling behavior. Updated bifurcation figures, numerical results, parameter provenance documentation, and reproducibility instructions.
title: Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape: Numerical Simulation Data, Bifurcation Analysis, and Computational Reproducibility

summary: What information about environmental memory must a quantum controller retain to guarantee a specified computational output? This preprint formulates that question in terms of task-sufficient process representations, intervention-valid predictions, stochastic clock laws, and explicit resource accounting. The central requirement is to preserve the outcomes and costs of the permitted decisions, with a stated accuracy contract and a finite-sample certificate. The paper connects two complementary lines of analysis. An operational construction studies Gaussian dephasing and controlled qubit tasks. A separate stochastic-clock analysis studies direct and inverse time changes, fractional relaxation, and the information that temporal coarse graining must transport. These constructions address related modelling questions but are not identified as a single microscopic noise model. The main elements are: Identical uncontrolled channels, different controlled responses. A continuum of Gaussian phase processes has the same uncontrolled coherence at every time and zero Breuer-Laine-Piilo backflow, yet different spin-echo responses. The construction shows why an uncontrolled channel family alone can fail to determine an intervention-dependent control decision. Task-sufficient equivalence and resource contracts. The manuscript defines a contract functional collecting accepted-output moments, acceptance probabilities, and physical costs over a declared policy family. Its finite linear task quotient identifies distinctions relevant to those predictions. Approximate sufficiency is accompanied by stability bounds that expose the sensitivity of conditional guarantees to low acceptance probabilities and small feasibility margins. Simultaneous finite-policy certification. Conservative confidence bounds certify conditional task bias and expected cost per accepted outcome after selection among a fixed, finite set of candidate policies. The assumptions include independent reset attempts, bounded observations and costs, and a trusted ideal reference. Failure to certify a candidate is explicitly distinguished from proof that no feasible physical policy exists. An explicit coarse-graining framework for stochastic clocks. The proposed decorated phase space records the process, permitted policy family, observable set, and clock law. The clock component transports stable laws under their natural scaling and relates domains of attraction to regular variation of waiting-time tails. Within the stated two-parameter clock-and-coupling family, the relaxation-rate direction scales with eigenvalue c^alpha. These clock results are placed in the established probabilistic renormalization literature; they do not establish hyperbolicity or convergence for the full decorated operator. A reset-sensitive fractional-relaxation calculation. Direct subordination of a quantum dynamical semigroup is distinguished from inverse-stable time change. For the latter, the paper compares uninterrupted evolution with independent renewal of the hidden clock and relevant environment. At half order and dimensionless rate one, the exact erfcx representation gives the short-time defect Delta(h) ~ 0.660989212585294 sqrt(h). The difference concerns the declared reset protocols, rather than a general assertion that every physical gate resets its environment. The reported classical benchmark uses ten candidate policies with explicit pulse depolarisation and separate X- and Z-expectation contracts. At the quasistatic endpoint, midpoint echo increases average identity-gate fidelity from 0.789293 to 0.990050. The fidelity crossover near r = 0.0467883 is distinct from the stricter X-task feasibility threshold r >= 0.9688074. For the selected Z-task input, dephasing is harmless and unnecessary echo pulses reduce the expectation. Conventional calibrated echo matches the best tested control performance; calibration, sampling, rejected attempts, and amortisation remain part of the resource account. Two q
title: Task-Sufficient Memory under Stochastic Clocks: Coarse-graining operators, fixed points, and finite-policy certification

summary: Companion research materials for the manuscript “First-passage asymptotics and identifiability in reflected damage-threshold models with growing drift, with an application to dietary-switching survival” by Bowen Xu, Ning Tang and Jiaying Li. The archive contains source code, archived inputs and results, post hoc descriptive summaries, mathematical statements and proofs, manuscript sources, documented numerical and statistical protocols, and provenance records. Independent density-solver agreement is limited to the reported converged ranges; unresolved trajectories and earlier failures are retained. The fly-record application is exploratory, and all panel distribution-free simultaneous bands include zero. Same-code reproduction is not independent scientific validation. The proofs have not been reviewed by a human mathematician, and an independent statistical assessment has not been completed. title: Code, frozen results and mathematical proofs for: First-passage asymptotics and identifiability in reflected damage-threshold models with growing drift, with an application to dietary-switching survival

summary: RadVeil removes identifiable facial and auricular (ear) surfaces from NIfTI head MRI and CT. It localizes the face the way an attacker would -- rendering the volume as a portrait and running a 2D face detector -- and accepts an anonymization only when re-detection on the output fails. Ears are located from surface evidence (protrusion detection against a scalp baseline) rather than fixed anatomical offsets. Every voxel outside the exported mask is preserved bit-exact, with datatype, scaling and header intact.
title: RadVeil: CPU-only face and ear anonymization for volumetric head imaging

summary: ArcGIS Pro toolbox and Python command-line tool that extracts the land-use/land-cover history of point samples from the Carta de Uso e Ocupação do Solo (COS) of mainland Portugal, published by the Direção-Geral do Território (DGT). For each sample point the tool reads the COS class in every edition of one COS series (Series 1: 1995–2018; Series 2: 2018–2025) and returns the class trajectory, temporal-stability metrics, the distance to the polygon boundary and an interpretation category, together with transition matrices, a provenance manifest and a data dictionary. The mathematical definitions and an interpretation guide are included in the documentation. The COS data are not distributed with the software.
tags: Carta de Uso e Ocupação do Solo
title: dgt-cos-trajectories: land-use/land-cover history of sample points from the DGT COS series

summary: This report and reproducibility package examine how a specified receiver determines which distinctions in a supplied nested quantum state become accessible in its measurement records. Two nonorthogonal states with unequal 70/30 population weights and opposite coherence have identical reduced states on every nonempty proper subset of their encoded registers. Measurements confined to those subsets cannot distinguish the candidates. Local equatorial measurements followed by comparison of their records reveal a joint parity contrast, whose accessibility depends on the receiver phase. For the worked two-register example, equal-prior single-trial discrimination succeeds with probability 95.83% under ideal retention and 79.33% with independent 80% retention at each receiver. These probabilities include incomplete records. Blind receiver settings and complete dephasing provide distinct zero-contrast controls. The report also establishes reconstruction from three real quantities within a known two-dimensional encoded subspace. A support-leakage counterexample demonstrates why this reconstruction does not extend to unrestricted states. All sixteen numerical check families pass, including 5,130 proper-subset comparisons. A verification run reproduces the archived scientific results exactly. The package includes the report, executable code, fixed configuration, numerical results, probability tables, figures, equation sources, report builder and checksums. This is an analytic and computational benchmark within declared quantum states and measurement models. It provides a bounded example of receiver-dependent information access and candidate-state identification; it does not constitute experimental validation or derive a physical mechanism of nesting.
title: Receiver Distinguishability of Nested States

summary: GPU-native Julia framework for CT and photon-counting CT simulation, reconstruction, and quantitative spectral imaging. Provides distance-driven forward projection (with Siddon ray tracing as an alternative), polychromatic Beer-Lambert physics with vendor-realistic detector response (MC-derived LUTs for GE Gemstone scintillator and Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha CdTe), FDK, helical WFBP and hybrid iterative reconstruction, sinogram and image-domain beam-hardening correction, projection-domain dual-kVp and PCCT material decomposition (K-channel profile likelihood, Cong 2022), spectral denoising, and virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI + Grant 2014 Mono+) — all dispatching transparently across CPU, Metal, CUDA, and ROCm via AcceleratedKernels.jl.
title: BasisSimulator.jl: Open-source polychromatic CT simulation with a GPU-portable reconstruction stack

summary: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.
title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity

summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.
title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation

summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law.
title: Law-determined norm inequalities do not imply complete mixability

summary: Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN): mathematical revisions, corrected datasets, and reproducible computational resources This repository provides an integrated historical, empirical, and computational resource for the Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN) framework. It brings together the foundational development of the model, original and corrected crown-network records, recalculated WCHN properties, ecological comparisons, principal component analyses (PCAs), editable network drawings, and computational tools for reconstructing and analyzing woody crown networks. The deposit is an independent scientific resource, not tied to any particular journal or manuscript. HISTORICAL FOUNDATION Four publications document the development of the WCHN framework: Souza et al. (2011): initial network analyses of Cerrado tree crowns. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11258-010-9797-7 Prado et al. (2020): formalization of network decomposition, topology, and the four original properties. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtbi.2020.110318 Prado and Trovão (2023): expansion to eight properties and comparative analyses of Caatinga and Cerrado networks. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2023.110345 Prado (2024): stochastic node-addition networks and size-matched comparisons. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40626-024-00340-5 These references enable users to trace the original definitions, subsequent revisions, and development of the framework. INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REFERENCE The definitions, revised equations, algebraic identities, mathematical properties, conditions of definition, and theoretical implications of the WCHN framework are now documented in a separate, independently published and versioned Zenodo record: Prado (2026). Algebraic Relationships and Mathematical Properties of the Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN). Version 1.0.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24181915 This mathematical reference includes the revised definitions of symmetry (SYM), complexity (COM), and topological vulnerability (VUL); exact algebraic relationships among WCHN properties; network-size dependence; and mathematical and numerical checks. In particular, revised VUL is equivalent to normalized mean node depth in a rooted tree. The near-reciprocity observed between navigability (NAV) and VUL is an empirical relationship, not an additional algebraic identity or evidence of physiological equivalence. The mathematical document was included in an earlier version of the present dataset deposit. Beginning with the current version, it is maintained exclusively in its independent Zenodo record. Earlier published versions retain their original archived files for historical traceability. EMPIRICAL DATASETS AND ECOLOGICAL REANALYSES The deposit contains the original Cerrado and Caatinga source spreadsheets, recalculated WCHN properties, ecological comparisons, reduced PCAs, and exploratory network-size-adjusted analyses. The complete field collection comprises 99 WCHNs: 75 from Cerrado and 24 from Caatinga. Recalculated tables incorporate the revised SYM, COM, and VUL definitions. The reduced PCAs use NAV, VUL, LAT, BAS, and PTP, with 24 Caatinga networks and 74 complete Cerrado networks. Previously deposited PCA and partial-correlation results are preserved without numerical recalculation in this update. Their interpretation should account for network-size dependence, shared topological information, and the revised mathematical meaning of VUL. The accompanying README_Size_Adjusted_PCA_v2.md documents the methods, results, assumptions, and limitations of the size-adjusted analyses. CORRECTED CERRADO NETWORKS AND REPRODUCIBLE TOOLKIT The deposit includes a workbook documenting corrections to 20 previously sampled Cerrado WCHNs. These are corrected records of existing observations, not additional independent networks. Six networks were reconstructed manually, including S. polyphyllum 1 as the manual feasibility pilot. Fourteen networks were reconstructed semi-automatically, be
title: Recalculated woody crown hydraulic network properties and reduced principal component analyses of Caatinga and Cerrado trees

summary: This record contains processed data inputs associated with the study “Protein restriction amplifies nucleus accumbens dopamine responses to protein-containing food during operant feeding in male mice.” The deposit includes 24 processed photometry pickle files, covering pellet-onset and pellet-offset events during fixed-ratio (FR1) and progressive-ratio operant sessions, and three supplementary files: a food-intake/body-weight spreadsheet, an operant-behaviour summary CSV, and a pellet-retrieval-latency CSV. These files are intended as inputs to the project’s figure-analysis notebooks. The photometry files are provided in  photometry_pickles.zip  under the  data/  directory; the spreadsheet and CSV files are uploaded separately. This is a deposit of processed analysis inputs, not the complete raw dataset or a raw-data-to-figures processing pipeline. The data’s provenance and processing details should be consulted in the associated study and project documentation. The photometry files are Python pickle files. Load them only from a trusted source, since deserializing pickle files can execute code.
title: Data for "Protein restriction amplifies nucleus accumbens dopamine responses to protein-containing food during operant feeding in male mice"

summary: This dataset was created using the referenced code at 10.5281/zenodo.24158671 . For more information on how this dataset can be generated, consult the README.md that is found there. The results are presented in 'Titz et al., Cascading failures and system splits in decarbonized European power systems, Joule (2026), DOI:  10.1016/j.joule.2026.102742 '. In this work, we assess the risk of cascading failures and system splits in the European power grid for different carbon reduction scenarios. We analyze the most likely and most dangerous splits, identify critical transmission infrastructures and characteristic split patterns, and we discuss potential countermeasures that can address the problem of cascades. Our results show that while the risk of splits causing power failures rises with decarbonization, it can be mitigated cost-efficiently.
title: Data accompanying 'Cascading failures and system splits in decarbonized European power systems'

summary: Overview The integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources into electric grids challenges conventional power system protection. Machine learning-based solutions can address these challenges by utilizing available data in modern smart grids. However, the lack of open datasets prevents reproducibility and fair comparisons between different approaches and their results, which hinders further progress. Therefore, we propose EvEMTBench, a synthetic dataset of faults and events generated using electromagnetic transient simulations. The physical plausibility of the power system simulation is ensured by validating the simulation parameters against established literature and providing a comprehensive documentation of the simulation procedure. The dataset is designed for training, fine-tuning, and benchmarking machine learning models by providing synchronized point-on-wave voltage and current measurements at 9600 Hz across a diverse set of topologies and voltage levels. The inclusion of a wide range of fault and operating events allows the utilization of EvEMTBench for different tasks like incipient fault detection, fault localization or event detection. The dataset is available on FAUDataCloud and the generation code is available on GitHub as well as this repository on Zenodo. Usage Guide This repository contains the code to generate the dataset. It was tested with Python 3.9 and PowerFactory 2025. The main entry point is "main_datagen.py" - this script orchestrates the dataset generation pipeline. "create_datasets.py" provides higher-level dataset creation functionality. Please refer to the readme.md file for further instructions on how to execute the code to generate custom versions of the dataset. Use Cases The dataset can be used for a wide range of power system protection related tasks, including fault detection, fault classification, fault line indentification, fault localization and fault area classification. Additionally, the dataset can be used for broader tasks like event classification and localization or incipient fault detection.
title: EvEMTBench, a simulation based dataset of faults and events for machine learning in power systems: Code for Data Generation

summary: Data belonging to the work "An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua" Using Lunaria annua , I manipulated resource availability via branch removal to test whether reduced competition induces compensatory funiculus thickening. I measured funiculus thickness and seed area in basal and apical fruits, analyzing seed fate and trait scaling relationships. Branch removal induced global funiculus hypertrophy, which was disproportionately higher in basal positions. Funiculus expansion was positively associated with seed survival and growth, though plants converted transport capacity into biomass more effectively in apical positions. Results also showed a decoupling of the within-fruit size–number trade-off, challenging classical inverse correlations.
tags: competition, plasticity, resource allocation, seed abortion, sub-individual variation.
title: An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua

summary: The rapid growth of digital payments has increased the importance of reliable credit card fraud detection systems. Traditional rule-based approaches can struggle to identify com plex and evolving fraud patterns, particularly when fraudulent transactions represent only a small proportion of transaction data. This paper presents a machine learning-based framework that combines data preprocessing, class-imbalance handling, autoencoder-based feature representation, and XGBoost clas sification. The study uses the publicly available credit card transaction dataset containing 284,807 transactions, including 492 fraudulent transactions. Robust scaling is used to reduce the influence of extreme values, while the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied only to the training data. An autoencoder learns a compact representation of trans action features and calculates reconstruction error; these outputs are combined with the prepared features for downstream clas sification. XGBoost is used to distinguish legitimate transactions from potentially fraudulent ones. The framework is evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, area under the precision recall curve (PR-AUC), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The paper also describes an API-oriented deployment workflow. Numerical results should be reported from the final reproducible experiment; illustrative or previously obtained values must not be treated as independently verified without rerunning the implementation.
title: Securing Digital Transactions: Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection

summary: Equipment-embodied growth theory predicts that reallocating fixed-capital formation from civil structures toward machinery and plant modernization accelerates industrial output, yet high-investment transition regions routinely channel over half of capital outlays into construction-installation works. Assembling regional fixed-capital simplex panels across all 14 regions of Uzbekistan (2000–2025 for technological shares, N = 364; 2007–2025 for reproduction modes, N = 266; 2016–2025 for constant-price industrial value-added growth, N = 140) alongside boundary-harmonized regional benchmarks from Kazakhstan (2003–2026Q3), we evaluate compositional reallocation hypotheses using full-simplex two-way fixed-effects regressions and 9,999 null-imposed wild cluster bootstrap replications. Across all six primary specifications conditioning on real investment scale, real investment growth, employment growth, and residual simplex shares, shifting 10 percentage points from construction-installation works into machinery and equipment yields statistically unresolved contemporaneous (+0.74 percentage points; bootstrap p = 0.7025; 95% bootstrap interval [-1.66, 3.66]) and lagged (+0.56; bootstrap p = 0.3828) industrial growth associations that remain null under predetermined scale controls (+0.63; bootstrap p = 0.3710); a one-year-ahead dynamic association (+1.52; bootstrap p = 0.0319) does not survive six-horizon Holm correction (p = 0.1914), and omitting either Karakalpakstan's 10 region-years (-0.60; bootstrap p = 0.0812) or its single 2016 observation (-0.35; bootstrap p = 0.4017) reverses contemporaneous point estimates negative. On the capital-input margin, reallocating 10 percentage points from greenfield expansion to reconstruction and modernization is associated with a 4.35 percentage-point higher regional machinery share (bootstrap p = 0.0003; 5.75 percentage points with real-scale controls, bootstrap p = 0.0003), while Uzbek-Kazakh subnational comparisons show persistent civil-works dominance whose cross-sectional financing gradients depend on regional consolidation and own-funds scope. Archive contents and offline reproduction: Version 1.0.0 ( central-asia-capital-composition-industrial-growth-v1.0.0.zip ; 99 files; SHA-256: 480f9ee676afa63aaa7eefe0848d162ceadc63d7c1f7292264b5406ef6404572 ) contains frozen official primary statistical and statutory inputs publicly available on or before 13 November 2026 ( raw_data/ ), harmonized estimation panels and variable dictionaries ( analysis_data/ ), numerical regression and diagnostic tables ( output/ and results/ ), publication-scale 300 DPI PNG and vector SVG multi-panel figures ( figures/ ), pinned Python dependencies ( requirements.txt ), and self-contained offline reproduction scripts ( python code/run_all.py and python code/render_figures.py ).
title: Dataset and Replication Code for: Bricks Over Machines: Capital Technological Composition, Reconstruction Versus Greenfield Expansion, and Regional Industrial Growth in Uzbekistan with Subnational Benchmarks from Kazakhstan

summary: A tape of n cells over three values — equivalently, two-bit cells read through their sum — is read by two headers that enclose a window; at each step a fixed rule, given the window's content and the geometry, names one of eight actions: move a header inward or outward, trim a cell from the left, the right or both, or halt. The cost is the number of cell reads, the state is O(log n) bits, and the question is how the cost must grow with n for each rule. The rules fall into three classes — fully linear, semi-linear and superlinear — separated by a worst-case cost and a mean cost. All three are populated: five natural rules are fully linear, one construction is semi-linear, and the remaining sixteen are superlinear.   The paper separates the walk from the cells it reads, proves that the collapse of the group-sum rules costs n + S - 1 reads in six lines, shows that one machine is within a constant of all three optima even when they are attained by different machines, arranges the catalogue's costs on a ladder from n^{1/2} to n^3, and states exactly what is proved, what is measured and what is open. It carries one conjecture: that no content-dependent rule can be superlinear and perfect. Negative results included: the certificate bound does not compose (on one tape the per-query certificates sum to 1,285,703 cells while their union has 1,020), and a bound on the rule's output transfers to the walk only after multiplication by the fraction of queries at which the answer can change the action, measured at 0.104 and falling like n^{-0.99}.   This version replaces the earlier one: the classification is three-class throughout, four conjectures of the earlier draft are gone, the collapse is a theorem rather than a numerical check, and the machine profile of Appendix A reports for every rule the three minima and the machine that attains each.
title: A memoryless two-header tape machine: what a window costs, and why two lower-bound techniques fail

Source reports: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, https://ncdc.gov.ng; reports were abstracted in November 2026 (URLs are in the `source_url` column of each data file). ## 1. What is in this deposit | Folder / file | Contents | |---|---| | `data/ncdc_cholera_top_lgas_published.csv` | Highest-burden LGA tables: epidemiological week 52 of 2022 and 2023, week 39 of 2024. 43 rows (15, 14, 14), 42 distinct LGAs. Columns: year, period_covered, rank, lga, state, cases, source, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv` | Suspected cases and deaths for each state listed in the situation reports (33, 31 and 36 states). Columns include as_of, status, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_national_published.csv` | National totals at each reporting point: suspected and confirmed cases, deaths, CFR, states and LGAs affected, including the full-year 2024 figure (24,842 suspected cases) from the Weekly Epidemiological Report, vol. 14, no. 52. | | `data/state_input_data_populations_coordinates.csv` | Analysis input: 2006 census population, area, state centroid (mean of LGA coordinates), cases, listed flags. | | `data/lga_coordinates_and_zones.csv` | 774 LGAs with state, geopolitical zone and coordinates. Used only to compute state centroids. Contains no case counts. | | `code/state_analysis_v2.py` | State-level analyses (Moran's I, LISA, rank correlation, Bayesian BYM2 negative binomial models, posterior predictive checks, WAIC, NB regression) and Figures 3–4 inputs. | | `code/lga_extra.py` | Table of all listed LGAs and the random-selection overlap simulation (200,000 draws; fixed seed). | | `code/analysis_top_lgas.py` | Descriptive, concentration and overlap analysis of the published LGA lists. | | `code/maps.py` | State symbol maps (Figure 2). | | `results/` | All output tables and JSON. Prefix `state_` = state-level analyses; `lga_` = LGA-list analyses. | | `figures/` | PNG figures. | | `supplement/` | Supplementary File 1 (STROBE/RECORD checklist), 2 (search protocol and reference verification log), 3 (supplementary tables), and `Supplementary_Tables.xlsx`. | | `MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` | SHA-256 checksum of every file. | ## 2. Key definitions and handling of data - **Suspected cholera:** cases as published by NCDC under its suspected-case definition; not laboratory-confirmed. - **Incidence:** reported suspected cases per 100,000 of the 2006 census population (reported, not true, incidence). - **2024:** epidemiological weeks 1–39 (10,837 suspected cases). summary: Replication package for  Neuro-Symbolic Requirements Elicitation: Utilizing Formal Verification Counterexamples as Contextual Prompts  (ASE 2026). C-GRiD combines a Large Language Model (LLM) with the TLA+ model checker TLC. Counterexamples are translated into plain-language questions for stakeholders, whose answers guide the iterative refinement of formal specifications. Version 2.0.0 provides a new experimental evaluation of C-GRiD that replaces the evaluation of Version 1 , with an executable and reproducible evaluation pipeline. The results reported in this version supersede those of Version 1. In particular, Version 2 introduces the following enhancements: TLC-based verification:  All experimental verdicts are established using the TLC model checker (TLC2 2026.11.06, bundled with the package). Executable benchmarks:  The nine benchmarks are provided as executable TLA+ models with their corresponding TLC configuration files, while preserving the constraint identifiers used in Version 1. Behavioural recall assessment:  Recall is determined through TLC refinement checks, providing an executable basis for assessing whether the specified requirements are satisfied. Complete experimental traceability:  Every LLM interaction is recorded, allowing the reported results to be re-derived without requiring an API key through  replay.sh . Experimental Evaluation Version 2 reports a new experimental evaluation using two LLM configurations: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ( claude-sonnet-5-5 , answering through a manual queue). Qwen3.6-27B (self-hosted server, temperature 0.3). The experimental setting comprises nine benchmarks, k = 3 and 5 removed constraints, five seeds, and 90 cases per approach and LLM. Strict Recall Results Approach Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B C-GRiD, perfect stakeholder 91.9% 89.6% C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder 85.4% 80.4% Gen-Once, full requirements 92.2% 59.1% Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden 83.3% 66.5% Auto-Repair (no LLM) 81.3% 81.3% Pairwise Comparisons C-GRiD with a perfect stakeholder compared with the other approaches (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test): C-GRiD vs. Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B Auto-Repair +10.6 pp, p = 0.0005 +8.3 pp, p = 0.020 C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder +6.5 pp, p = 0.003 +9.3 pp, p = 0.001 Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden +8.5 pp, p = 0.053 +23.1 pp, p < 0.001 Gen-Once, full requirements −0.4 pp, p = 0.59 +30.6 pp, p < 0.001 The evaluation shows that C-GRiD consistently outperforms Auto-Repair across both LLM configurations. Its comparison with one-shot generation also highlights the influence of the underlying LLM: C-GRiD achieves a substantial advantage with Qwen3.6-27B, whereas Claude Sonnet 5.5 achieves comparable strict recall when provided with the full requirements. These results provide further insight into the conditions under which counterexample-guided elicitation is beneficial. They supersede the results of Version 1 and are not directly comparable with them. They should be interpreted within the experimental setting and limitations documented in  RESULTS.md . Package Contents cgrid/ : C-GRiD implementation and experimental pipeline. benchmarks/ : Nine executable TLA+ benchmarks. results/ : Recorded experimental runs for both LLM configurations. legacy/ : Version 1 package, preserved for reference and comparison. Tests and supporting scripts: replay.sh : Re-derives the reported results from recorded LLM interactions, without requiring an API key. reproduce.sh : Runs new experiments using an LLM endpoint. Requirements:  Python ≥ 3.10 and Java ≥ 11. The package is intended to support independent inspection, replication, and further experimentation with counterexample-guided requirements elicitation.
title: Counterexample-Guided Requirements Discovery

summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne
title: Leonardo's Spatial Grammar: A CAD Reverse-Engineering Analysis Corpus: Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.
title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / The Revealed Geometry (it/en)

QUANTUM COMPUTING FOR INVERSE DESIGN OF 4D MATERIALS FAMILY 12 / F056-F060 / THE OTHER SIDE OF THE RESEARCH MONOGRAPH Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI / White Rainbow Era Scientific status: Prospective nonclinical proposal. All diagrams are analytical synthetic illustrations. No quantum advantage, qualified device, biomedical treatment or patient recovery has been demonstrated. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE 4D MATERIALS RESEARCH An inverse design begins with a wish: a material should bend to a specific shape after a particular sequence of heat, light, solvent or magnetic stimuli. The wish is not evidence. A specimen has a history, a printer has a feature limit, and a camera can mistake a smooth silhouette for recovered function. In this notebook the research chain is followed from physical permission to constitutive model, to competing computational designs, to damaged and rejected specimens, and finally to a negative case that another laboratory can recreate. Five independent flagships supply different scientific questions. F056 concerns a constrained inverse map from target response to material recipe. F057 studies the discrete matching of material configuration with time-dependent target shapes. F058 forces mathematical topology into a printable connected solid. F059 asks whether prediction intervals survive new lots and measurement chains. F060 refuses to consider a design validated until printed output, failures, material loss and costs have been measured. Coupling them yields a useful research system only when their evidence contracts remain distinct. The source genealogy matters. The author-provided four-dimensional microrobotics research book gives a physical vocabulary for responsive structures, fatigue and fabrication. The independent BCI-stroke study gives a separate rationale for minimizing assistance and distinguishing device function from recovery after a device is removed. The forty-family blueprint identifies the F056-F060 lineage and emphasizes the hazard of an optimum that cannot be manufactured. No source proves that a quantum-designed microbot has restored human motor function. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is the public name of the present research method. The first stage asks what material and laboratory can legitimately do. The second asks which mathematical program is meaningful. The third proposes a strong ordinary rival. The fourth tries hard, bounded counterexamples. The fifth freezes the evidence that can survive independent reconstruction. This is a set of epistemic viewpoints, not a claim about physical parallel universes. A strong scientific notebook should be able to disagree with the monograph. Where the monograph records an observable and a pre-registered test, the notebook should ask why the observable was chosen, what the test would miss, and which apparently trivial rival might explain its result. Repetition can be a conceptual return to a difficult distinction rather than duplicated filler. But no return should be mistaken for new measurement. The most important distinction is between speed of design and quality of evidence. More candidate samples, more attractive plots or more pages cannot establish physical printability. Nor can a verified specimen establish quantum computational advantage if the full pipeline costs and carefully tuned classical methods were never compared. A scientific stop is legitimate when the boundary and next decisive experiment are clear. Research Doors should remain the most alive part of this system. The question left at the end of each chapter is not an invitation to endorse the current model. It is an instruction to try to defeat it with a better observation. If the next laboratory discovers that a classical algorithm, a clamp motion or a material batch artifact explains the beautiful result, the research family has still preserved useful knowledge. That is what makes it a handoff rather than a claim of perfection. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F056 | Quantum-Assisted Inverse Design of 4D Biomedical Materials at the Limit This flagship examines coupled composition-to-actuation inverse mapping under fabrication constraints. The relevant physical endpoints are held-out curvature error [1/m], tip displacement [um] and batch yield [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a rich surrogate or uncounted classical preprocessing explains the optimization gain. A blinded test should blindly swap material lots and stimulus order after designs are frozen. Independent instruments include independent optical displacement [um], curvature [1/m], locally mapped temperature [K], material lot ID and complete query ledger; the ordinary comparator set comprises tuned Bayesian optimization, adjoint or surrogate inverse search, classical mixed-integer programming and matched evaluation budgets. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F057 | Quantum Material Configuration Search for Target Deformation at the Limit This flagship examines discrete formulation and voxel assignment search for target time-dependent deformation. The relevant physical endpoints are dynamic target mismatch [um] and valid-configuration ratio [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a simple classical lookup or favorable target selection explains the match. A blinded test should conceal target shapes and reverse their temporal stimulus order. Independent instruments include three-axis shape field [um], synchronized stimulus onset [s], printed voxel map and decoded composition identity; the ordinary comparator set comprises strong integer programming, genetic search, Bayesian optimization and conventional discrete trajectory matching under identical material alphabets. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F058 | Quantum-Assisted Topology Optimization of 4D Microstructures at the Limit This flagship examines printable topology design under minimum-feature and connectivity constraints. The relevant physical endpoints are fabricated topology fidelity [1], stiffness [Pa] and actual curvature [1/m]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that simulation favors disconnected or sub-resolution ligaments that cannot print. A blinded test should blindly print held-out topologies with fixed voxel resolution and support rules. Independent instruments include volumetric z-stack [um], print line width [um], calibrated microforce [uN], FE mesh ledger and connected-component count; the ordinary comparator set comprises calibrated SIMP, compliant-mechanism topology optimization, integer programming and mesh-matched density methods. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F059 | Uncertainty Propagation in Quantum-Assisted Material Design at the Limit This flagship examines joint propagation of process, stimulus and inferred constitutive uncertainty. The relevant physical endpoints are predictive coverage [1], calibration error [um] and variance by material lot. summary: تقدم هذه الورقة البحثية التأسيسية إطاراً معرفياً-وجودياً جديداً لمعالجة أزمة "الفائض المعلوماتي" (Information Overload)، ليس بوصفها مجرد تحدٍ تقني أو نفسي، بل بوصفها أزمة بنيوية في "السياق" (Context) و"قواعد التحويل" (Transformation Rules). من خلال صهر وتطوير أربعة أطروحات متكاملة (نظرية السياقات، معلومات الانحراف السياقي CDI، نظرية المصنوعات، ونظرية الاجترار الثقافي)، تقترح الورقة "رياضيات جديدة للوعي الدلالي". أبرز مساهمات الورقة: إعادة تعريف الوعي: نعرّف الوعي صورياً بوصفه نظاماً بديهياً توليدياً (Axiomatic Generative System) تقاس كميته بالرتبة البرهانية (Proof-Theoretic Ordinal)، ونبرهن رياضياً أن الفائض المعلوماتي في غياب سياق تأويلي يؤدي إلى "العمى السياقي" (Contextual Blindness). ميكانيكا الانحراف: تقديم مقاييس رياضية دقيقة (CDI و SDI) للتمييز بين "المفاجأة الإحصائية" (نظرية شانون) و"الانحراف المعياري عن السياق"، ولقياس "الزيف الدلالي" في الرسائل الاتصالية (مثل هلوسات الذكاء الاصطناعي). ديناميكا المصنوعات: البرهنة على "مبرهنة الصعود الميتا-سياقي" (Meta-contextual Ascent)، التي تثبت كيف تُعيد المصنوعات الرقمية (مثل النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة) تشكيل وعي المستخدم، ليس سلوكياً فحسب، بل على مستوى البديهيات والمعتقدات. السيادة المعرفية: تعميم الإطار من الفرد إلى الحضارة عبر "نظرية الاجترار الثقافي"، وإثبات أن غزارة المحتوى (K) مع ثبات قواعد التحويل (T) تُنتج "فجوة سيادية" تنمو أسّياً وتؤدي إلى التبعية المعرفية. تُختتم الورقة بتقديم برنامج بحثي متكامل ومؤشرات قابلة للقياس لبناء "مناعة معرفية" تحمي الوعي البشري من التعديل التخريبي في عصر السياقات اللانهائية. هذه الورقة تمثل نقطة التقاء رائدة بين نظرية البرهان الرياضي، وفلسفة العقل، وعلم المعلومات، ودراسات الذكاء الاصطناعي.
