summary: A georeferenced benchmark for comparing terrain-aware flood-evacuation routing methods and remotely sensed inputs in the valley below Eoeun Reservoir, Republic of Korea. The dataset combines UAV-derived land-cover predictions and a digital surface model with Sentinel-2 Level-2A predictions and Copernicus DEM GLO-30 elevations harmonized to EGM96. Two hundred fixed cases are evaluated under nine 30 m input conditions. Each case follows a start–intermediate target–shelter sequence. All 1,800 attempts are retained: 989 completed routes are provided as cell sequences and GeoJSON, and 811 input-eligibility failures carry their first reported check outcome. Thirteen GeoTIFF inputs include native UAV reference rasters at approximately 1.03 m and the derived 30 m inputs. Configurations, data dictionaries, source metadata, validation records and SHA-256 checksums support reuse on the same cases and conditions. The benchmark supports comparison of input resolution, barrier aggregation, elevation sources and route objectives. Its georeferenced outputs can be linked to subsequent field checking and evacuation-planning studies. CC BY 4.0 applies to the authors' rights; Copernicus-derived material carries the notices in NOTICE.md. The routing engine, reference and verification code, and analysis scripts may be requested from the corresponding author under separate terms. Contact: Sangik Lee (sangik@knu.ac.kr). Funding: This work was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Ministry of Education (MOE) (No. RS-2026-25536642).
title: A multiresolution benchmark for terrain-aware evacuation routing

summary: This record is the replication package for the paper "Who is who: injury rates between players and within each player in professional team sports" by Gustavo Pedro Ricou and Nicholas Mahony (Trinity College Dublin). It holds the manuscript and its supplement, the pipeline that computed every number in them, the tests that fail when the text and the data disagree, and the aggregated tables the numbers are computed from. The manuscript's data availability statement cites this record. Why the manuscript is archived here. The manuscript is archived with its code and data, not as a second place of publication, because the three are one object. Every number in the paper is computed from the archived tables by the archived code. The archived tests fail if the text and the tables disagree. So the version of record of the evidence includes the version of the text it supports, and a reader can check any sentence of the paper against the data behind it. The preprint is arXiv:2608.11228 , where this paper will appear as the next version. This record is its data complement. What the paper does. Using public match records from nine team sports, with injury records for 22,573 players in six of them, the paper measures how injury rates differ between players and with recent load. Players' usual injury rates differed: between two players picked at random, the higher was typically 1.83 times the lower. Per-hour rates that compare players therefore mix recent load with who carries it. Comparing each player's heavy weeks with the same player's weeks after a longer gap needs a check by simulation first: with no effect of load at all, heavy weeks still read as riskier, because injuries lower later load. They are the manuscript, the supplement, the three checklists and the cover letter, with their numbers, tables, figures and references (paperA/); the pipeline, one numbered stage per file (src/); the tests (tests/); the builders and the scripts that collected the match records (tools/); the hand-built evidence that no script can rebuild (data/manual/); and the analysis plans, each fixed before its results were read, with the record of how each source was collected and what its terms allow (docs/). summary: all3DSignDB is a unified benchmark database for 3D online signature verification, built by merging all publicly available 3D signature databases that provide explicit (x,y,z)  coordinates: 3DIIT, captured with a Leap Motion sensor, and DeepAirSig, captured with an Intel Senz3D depth camera. The resulting database contains 120 users, 2,400 genuine signatures, and 1,266 skilled forgeries. Together with the database, a standardized evaluation protocol is provided — inspired by the SVC-OnGoing competition — including comparison files for 1vs1 and 4vs1 enrollment scenarios under both random and skilled forgery conditions. All comparison files are publicly shared to ensure reproducibility, along with a DTW-based baseline verifier, enabling fair and transparent comparison across future 3D signature verification systems. If you are using this database in your research, please cite the following paper: Moises Diaz, Cristian Rodriguez, Gabriel Ojeda-Suarez, Miguel A. Ferrer, "all3DSignDB: A Unified Database and Benchmark for 3D Signature Verification," 58th IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST 2026), Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, 14-16 October 2025, pp. 1-6..
title: all3DSignDB: A Unified Database and Benchmark for 3D Signature Verification

summary: VERSION 0.2.0. What is new in 0.2.0. The multi-criteria decision now uses eight criteria in four dimensions (technical, economic, environmental and structural), chosen so that the same water saving is not counted twice; weights can be declared per dimension or computed from the results by the CRITIC method; and the result is reported as a choice band (the volumes whose score lies within 5% of the range from the best) rather than a single 'optimal' volume. PROMETHEE II and SMAA were corrected, and the system weight (dry mass, water load, and operating load) was added. The volume the decision points to can change: a study ranked with 0.1.0 is reproduced with 0.1.0. Release notes of each edition are in the manuals and in the repository. Novidades da 0.2.0. summary: Fertility has fallen across the developing world, but rarely at the same rate for every educational group, so a given fall in the total fertility rate can mask very different changes in who is bearing fewer children. This paper shows that the composition of such a decline, and not only its size, is a determinant of the long-run rate of population growth, and derives a statistic that measures the composition effect from standard survey data. In a dynamic model in which fertility differs by education and daughters inherit their mother's schooling imperfectly, the long-run growth rate weights each group's fertility by its stationary share times the reproductive value of its members; dividing this weight by the group's share of current births gives the long-run cost of a permanent decline in that group's fertility per unit of period fertility, a quantity that two Demographic and Health Surveys suffice to estimate. In Colombia between 2000 and 2015 this cost was 60 percent lower among women without completed secondary schooling, and the observed, education-biased decline implies long-run population growth 0.14 points per year higher than a uniform decline with the same effect on period fertility, with a 90 percent bootstrap interval of 0.06 to 0.23. The advantage emerges within two generations, holds at the 2015 composition, survives bounds for selective coresidence and a 288-specification curve, and is larger in Peru; census links between adult daughters and their mothers confirm it in Colombia, Peru, and, at ages 20 to 24, Kenya, though the Kenyan identified set turns negative at ages 25 to 29. A decline concentrated among women whose share of current births exceeds their share of the stable population is therefore inexpensive in long-run growth, which makes the composition of a fertility decline a margin distinct from its size and measurable before the decline has run its course. summary: This dataset provides reproducible maps and supporting evidence for examining the energy–water nexus and prospects for agricultural development in the Qattara Depression and its surroundings, north-western Egypt. It combines published groundwater evidence, terrain data, Egyptian electricity-system context, and comparative evidence from desalination for agriculture in Spain and Morocco. Groundwater evidence and interactive maps. The archive includes Arabic-language offline 2D and 3D viewers, source records, uncertainty notes, and PNG/PDF exports. The compilation contains 200 located study records from eight studies; 198 fall within the map display extent. These are study records, not necessarily independent wells. Reported salinity units and source qualifications are retained. No spatial interpolation of salinity or inference of aquifer boundaries is performed. The maps do not establish sustainable abstraction rates or irrigation suitability. Terrain and the multiple-plant corridor concept. The archive includes the source SRTMGL1 digital elevation model, referenced to the EGM96 geoid, and reproducible materials for a terrain panel illustrating a potential corridor of multiple desalination plants along the El-Diffa Plateau and its transition toward the depression. The red dashed guide is a preliminary terrain-based visualization, not a surveyed geological boundary or an approved engineering alignment. The gold band has no prescribed engineering width. Plant symbols are illustrative: their positions and number do not identify selected sites, capacities, or a design count. Results for the studied desalination configuration must not be extrapolated across the corridor. Energy and international comparisons. Supporting materials document the Egyptian electricity-system context and selected Spanish and Moroccan desalination cases. They distinguish installed capacity from available supply, energy quantity from consumption timing and financial value, and water-production cost from tariff, payments, and implemented subsidy. The archive does not provide a new hourly simulation of the Egyptian grid, establish electricity availability at a Qattara connection point, or transfer foreign prices to Egypt. Reproducibility and traceability. The package contains evidence files, figure inputs and outputs, scripts, dependency information, attribution notices, and SHA-256 manifests. The full source DEM is included once. The complete manuscript is supplied separately and is not embedded in this evidence archive. COMPANION_MANUSCRIPT.json identifies the associated manuscript v1.8.5 package by filename, size, and SHA-256; this is a version-specific provenance link. Manuscript v1.8.6 subsequently updates the abstract and formatting without changing the scientific figures or numerical results. Historical draft labels and publication-status fields inside the uploaded archive describe its preparation stage; the published Zenodo record provides the current deposit status. Scientific context and limitations. The materials support interpretation and verification of the conceptual study by Elsayad and Elsayad (2026), Results in Engineering , 32, Article 113445, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rineng.2026.113445 , and the related Arabic analytical manuscript. They are not a feasibility study, a comprehensive groundwater inventory, an aquifer model, or a site-design dataset. They do not demonstrate operational flexibility, financial savings, environmental acceptability, or suitability of the full corridor. Sources and rights. Terrain data originate from NASA SRTM through OpenTopography, https://doi.org/10.5069/G9445JDF . Maps, documentation, and the evidence compilation are licensed under CC BY 4.0; scripts and viewer templates are licensed under MIT. Third-party materials retain their respective terms, as documented in RIGHTS_AND_ATTRIBUTION.md and the accompanying source files. Access. The record metadata are public; the archive files are restricted. Editors an

summary: AI Safety Formalization Atlas is an open workbench for doing AI safety the formal way: a growing library of machine-checked Lean 4 proofs about the limits and guarantees of AI systems, with a transparent registry that records where each result is formalized, which maintained declarations it reuses, and where genuine gaps remain. Most AI-safety reasoning lives in prose and intuition, and the rigor that does exist is scattered across incompatible proof systems. The Atlas pulls it onto one surface, so a safety argument stops being an argument and becomes a theorem you can build on, break, or extend. It is built to grow across the field — alignment, oversight, interpretability, robustness, and the paradoxes that make these problems wicked — with formalized impossibility results as the initial seed and no ceiling on scope; impossibility and possibility run on the same machinery. Scope. Machine-checked Lean 4 formalizations span computability, logic and self-reference, social choice, and learning theory, covering both impossibility results and possibility guarantees (including a reviewed reproduction of a scalable-oversight result), exposed through a single stable root import, alongside independently reproduced external formalizations with pinned, rebuildable provenance. The current, authoritative inventory of formalized results — their status, provenance, and open gaps — is maintained in the repository's registry; this record does not enumerate it, so the description stays accurate as the library grows. Epistemic scope. A machine-checked proof establishes its encoded mathematical statement; it does not by itself establish that the statement fully captures an informal AI-safety claim. Classical results and AI-system bridge claims are recorded as separate layers, and uncertain semantic relationships are flagged for human review. The registry reports verified coverage transparently rather than claiming complete formal coverage. Licensed under Apache-2.0; individual external formalizations remain under their own licenses, recorded in the registry.
title: AI Safety Formalization Atlas

files.key: Mitigation of Snap-Through Instability in Floating CFT Planar Arch Bridges(source codes).zip

summary: Overview This repository contains the Python source codes used to generate the analytical models, structural configurations, and hydro-elastic dynamic response data presented in the study on the stability and dynamic stress resilience of Concrete-Filled Tube (CFT) floating arch bridges. To ensure absolute numerical transparency and eliminate external commercial software dependencies, the stability and modal analyses are driven by a custom-built, Pure-Python 2D Finite Element Analysis (FEA) solver . The codes also integrate Mander's triaxial concrete confinement model for composite cross-sections and utilize the Capytaine Boundary Element Method (BEM) solver for time-domain stochastic wave simulations. File Descriptions Figure_1.py (Snap-through Buckling Mechanism & CFT Effect) Generates the conceptual schematic of the snap-through instability for a hollow steel arch and demonstrates the theoretical confinement-induced buckling prevention of CFT arches under fixed-end boundary conditions. Figure_2.py (Structural Configuration & Cross-Sectional Layout) Visualizes the physical geometry of the 1,000-m span floating arch bridge system. It details the dimensions of the 11 prestressed concrete pontoons and compares the cross-sectional properties of the heavily stiffened hollow steel girder versus the proposed CFT girder under matched nominal flexural rigidity ( $EI$ ). Figure_3.py (Hollow Steel Arch: Snap-Through & Modal Analysis) Executes the Pure-Python FEA solver (using Euler-Bernoulli beam elements and consistent mass matrices) to perform generalized eigenvalue analysis and trace the non-linear static equilibrium path of the conventional hollow steel arch, identifying the initial limit-point load. Figure_4.py (CFT Arch: Stability Enhancement & Modal Analysis) Extends the FEA solver to incorporate Mander's confined concrete model, calculating the physical composite stiffness ( $EA_{eff}$ , $EI_{eff}$ ). The script outputs the enhanced non-linear static equilibrium path, demonstrating a ~310% increase in the normalized critical snap-through load ( $P_{cr}/EA_s$ ) compared to the hollow steel baseline. Figure_5.py (Hydro-Elastic Dynamic Response under Stochastic Waves) Couples the analytical structural model with the Capytaine BEM solver. It calculates the 6-DOF dynamic response (RAOs) of the pontoon foundations and simulates the time-domain hydro-elastic response under irregular JONSWAP wave spectra (45° quartering and 90° beam seas), quantifying the dynamic bending stress mitigation provided by the CFT arch ribs. Dependencies & Requirements The scripts are written in Python 3. To run the codes successfully, the following libraries are required: numpy (Numerical operations and matrix assemblies) scipy (Generalized eigenvalue problem solver via scipy.linalg.eigh ) matplotlib (High-quality academic plotting and vector graphics) capytaine (Linear potential flow BEM solver for hydrodynamics - required for Figure_5.py ) Usage All scripts are provided as standalone, single-file executables. No external CSV datasets or commercial structural analysis software (e.g., Abaqus, OpenSees) are required to reproduce the exact figures presented in the manuscript. Simply execute each script in a standard Python environment to generate the corresponding high-resolution (300 DPI) .png files.
title: Source Codes for: Hydro-Elastic Snap-Through and Dynamic Analysis of CFT Floating Arch Bridges

summary: TopoALV-TP is a regional dataset of reconstructed lake bathymetry and multidecadal water-level and storage changes across the Tibetan Plateau. It was developed using the Topography-constrained Area–Level–Volume Reconstruction (TopoALV) framework, which integrates multitemporal satellite-derived lake extents, machine-learning-based depth estimation, shoreline-distance constraints, and surrounding topography. The dataset provides 64 m resolution water-depth and lakebed-elevation rasters for 1,080 lakes, together with lake-specific composite area–water-level curves and reconstructed lake area, relative water level, and storage changes for 16 observation epochs from the 1970s to 2022, referenced to the year 2000. The time-series archive contains 17,280 lake–epoch records, with missing observations explicitly retained. Additionally, the dataset includes a nominal 8 m super-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) of the Tibetan Plateau and 1,080 three-dimensional bathymetric visualizations. The archive contains GeoTIFF rasters, CSV time series, composite area–elevation curves, metadata, quality-control diagnostics, data provenance records, and processing scripts to support reproducibility and further research. Users should note that the reconstructed bathymetry and absolute lake volumes are model-derived estimates rather than comprehensive in situ measurements. Relative water-level and storage changes should be interpreted together with the provided quality flags and supported inversion ranges. The original “1970s” observation label is preserved; the numeric year 1975 is used only for chronological sorting and does not indicate an exact observation year.
title: TopoALV-TP: Terrain-constrained lake bathymetry and multidecadal water-level and storage reconstructions across the Tibetan Plateau (1970s–2022)

summary: HEPerovskiteSys is a zero-training, Shannon-radius rule system for high-entropy and rare-earth perovskite oxides. It predicts perovskite formability from fixed Goldschmidt, octahedral and Bartel tolerance-factor windows and estimates pseudo-cubic lattice constants, with no parameters fitted to experimental data. The package contains the Python computational kernel, a Flask REST API and a React/TypeScript web workbench, together with a smoke test, MIT License and documentation. Every experimental value used in the accompanying benchmark is traceable to a cited DOI.
title: HEPerovskiteSys: a zero-training Shannon-radius rule system for high-entropy and rare-earth perovskite oxides (V1.0)

summary: This report and reproducibility package develop a conditional mathematical model connecting joint-source correlations to electromagnetic receiver records. The calculation combines full numerical evolution of a retained finite-mode scalar–gauge Hamiltonian with an explicit model of transmission and measurement. Source preparations with matching individual-mode states can retain different joint correlations. Within the specified interaction, these differences transfer to the outgoing electromagnetic mode and produce receiver-accessible contrasts. A further comparison uses preparations with matching first and second moments but different higher joint correlations. Isometric nesting preserves predictions when the state, interaction and observables are transported consistently. The receiver model includes vacuum loss, reference-phase fluctuations, calibrated gain, offset and independent additive noise. Explicit equations describe the record mean, variance and probability distribution without requiring a Gaussian source state. Under common stationary calibration, three phase-resolved variances suffice to predict another variance within the declared receiver family. Reproducible numerical verification includes 177 passing source-evolution checks and 766 passing explicit receiver checks. These establish implementation consistency within the retained model. Separate measured-data comparisons retain their observed discrepancies: the primary optical GKP receiver prediction falls outside its declared ±5% tolerance. No calibration correction is fitted, and the complete source interaction is not experimentally validated. The report specifies the independent calibration, preparation and acquisition information needed for further receiver tests, together with the physical operator and coupling correspondence required for a laboratory implementation of the source model. Contributions of suitable datasets, calibration records and controlled analogue proposals are invited. The accompanying package contains the report, consolidated equations, executable code, protocols, inputs, results, verification records and provenance archives.
title: Nested Electromagnetic Source and Receiver Model

summary: Big Bang nucleosynthesis predicts about three times more primordial lithium than old metal-poor stars show, while laboratory measurements exclude a comparable reduction of the ³He(α,γ)⁷Be capture that makes most of it. Mittermeier Attractor Theory (MAT) fixes, without lithium input, a finite-support mobility M∂ = e³ρ²/(8π^(5/2)) = 0.251864, where ρ is the plastic number. We test the hypothesis that this number multiplies both directions of ³He + ⁴He ⇄ ⁷Be + γ in the primordial plasma. A common factor on a reaction and its reverse changes how fast it runs against cosmic expansion, not where its equilibrium lies; detailed balance and all conservation laws are kept. Executed in the PRIMAT network with its standard thermal history and the MAT baryon density, the hypothesis lowers primordial mass seven from (5.44 ± 0.21) × 10⁻¹⁰ to (1.472 ± 0.053) × 10⁻¹⁰ per hydrogen nucleus, against the stellar inference (1.45 ± 0.25) × 10⁻¹⁰, while deuterium and helium-4 change by less than three parts per million. A response theorem for trace products explains the result: the surviving beryllium meets almost no reverse reaction, so its yield follows the mobility nearly in proportion, and the standard solve alone predicts the modified yield to 0.04%. The effect is decided at photon temperatures of 22–58 keV, whose Gamow energies laboratory data cover closely enough to exclude any realization as a modified cross section: the mobility must be a property of the primordial plasma. The stellar comparison is retrospective; the sharp test is the ratio to standard nucleosynthesis, 0.2704 ± 0.0012, almost free of nuclear uncertainty. The microscopic map that switches the mobility on in that plasma, and nowhere else, remains open.
title: The Primordial Lithium Problem in Mittermeier Attractor Theory: Finite-Support Scaling of Reversible Reaction Kinetics

summary: Life-cycle cost comparisons for seismic retrofit are decision-useful only when loss equations are dimensionally coherent and alternatives share a consistent cost basis. This study presents a traceable audit framework and applies it to the case of a two-storey rubble stone-masonry dwelling in Greece with five reported strengthening alternatives. We recalculate base-masonry strength estimates from stated assumptions, test the reported loss arithmetic and comparison baseline, refit displacement–exceedance relations, and examine consequence-cost scaling. Two readings of one formula differ by a factor of two; neither is validated as a physical loss. Evaluating the record’s own six-step procedure on its own stated inputs finds seventeen of the twenty-two reported loss totals consistent with those inputs; of the five exceptions, four lack an identified cause and one coincides with an internal inconsistency in the reported cost table. Correcting the comparison basis lowers reported savings, and one cost-recovery conclusion changes across arithmetic readings. A separately tested, unit-explicit loss-assessment engine provides a reusable methodological tool; it does not reproduce or validate the case building’s structural model. Version note: Author proof v2, revised 6 November 2026; accepted 2 November 2026. This is an author proof and not the publisher’s final Version of Record. The ADAPT4CE project, “Adaptive digital systems for sustainable construction and material management in the circular economy” (Grant Agreement No. 101182768), supported the cross-case synthesis, reproducibility framework, visualization, and manuscript preparation reported in this article. ADAPT4CE is funded by the European Union under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Research and Innovation Staff Exchange, Horizon Europe (HORIZON-MSCA-2023-SE). Views and opinions are those of the authors only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the European Commission.
title: Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study

summary: Introduction Scott Adams’s God’s Debris: A Thought Experiment (2001) presents a fascinating hypothesis: an omnipotent and omniscient God might have destroyed itself to experience something it could not otherwise experience—nonexistence. The universe would consequently consist of God’s debris, with existence potentially representing the gradual reconstruction of divine consciousness (Adams). I propose extending this thought experiment by identifying the Big Bang as a possible physical counterpart to God’s self-destruction and the Absolute as the ultimate destination toward which individual consciousnesses might eventually return. Furthermore, investigating the universe beyond the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) might help constrain theories about the earliest state of existence and, indirectly, inform philosophical investigations of the afterlife.
title: From God's Debris to the Absolute: The Big Bang, Cosmic Origins, and the Possibility of an Afterlife

summary: Bone resorption following tooth loss is considered an obstacle for dental implant placement in desired positions, requiring bone augmentation procedures. Many techniques have been described to reconstruct horizontal alveolar ridge  defects. But one of many, platelet concentrate fibrin is considered nowadays an efficient technique in oral surgery, which is based on concentrating platelets and growth factors that is activated in fibrin gel in order to improve the healing. The aim of this review was to discuss the use of PRF in oral surgery by exposing 3 clinical cases and discussing the properties in bone tissue engineering for PRF membranes, and wound healing with bone formation for Leucocyte platelet rich fibrin (L-PRF) used as scaffold. In the 3 clinical cases bone maturation was found excellent at 5 months as seen clinically, on X-rays and CAT scans
title: Platelets Rich Fibrin (PRF)-Associated Bovine Bone for Horizontal Reconstruction of Atrophic Alveolar Ridges: Myth or Reality? A Three Clinical Case Reports

summary: We construct a common Fourier local-norm domain for exact alternating spatial blocking and temporal decimation of an SU(3) lattice transfer model. The state consists of the current coarse action, its source- free one-time part, its full multitime and source-dependent remainder, and its scalar normalization. A two-link spatial pushforward contracts the field-dependent norm by k = e1/20/3 < 0.350424, and temporal marginalization does not increase that norm. Consequently every finite alternating iteration remains in the ball r∗ = 0.00235, with coupling radius 2 and source radius 10−4 unchanged. A direct analytic estimate gives a one-cycle Lipschitz constant below 0.431657. We prove conditional cumulant bounds under the interacting one-time reference, recertify its spatial mixing after each rebase, and preserve the generating functional of the fixed original source family. An all-order entrance certificate places a specified transfer family inside the ball. Physical consequences include preservation of all connected source responses, a uniform comparison of finite coarse-field marginals with product Haar measure, and suppression of aligned dyadic Wilson squares. The computational supplement includes the seven precursor stages and an independent rational verification of their one-link spectral input. The result closes the local iteration problem for this action space; physical-source scaling, a compatible bare-theory trajectory, reflection-compatible continuum reconstruction, and a nontrivial four-dimensional limit remain separate obligations.
title: Certified Alternating Space-Time Coarse-Graining with Full Memory -An invariant Fourier domain for an SU(3) lattice transfer model

summary: # A Spectral Construction of Natural-Number Arithmetic [Archival DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22512592) ## Arithmetic with its construction history retained This paper constructs natural-number arithmetic from a correlation spectrum and then resolves its values into the expressions by which they are generated. Its central achievement is to connect three levels that are usually studied separately: arithmetic values, the histories of arithmetic operations, and an evolution acting on those histories. The resulting system retains both the familiar numerical laws and information that numerical evaluation alone removes. The source is minimal unbiased compositional change. The least-dimensional faithful irreducible real orthogonal carrier is a rotation plane. Independent composition, exact same-shape self-similarity and unit covariance determine square-root scaling and a Gaussian law. Local information and normalized total correlation give the characteristic local and global lengths. Preservation of constants selects Neumann closure within the stated separated nondegenerate homogeneous local boundary class. Spectral projections are ordered by their Gaussian response before an integer enumeration is introduced. Orientation selects the positive analytic modes. Pointwise modulation and circle-map composition define their addition and multiplication; modulation by the first positive mode defines successor. The paper proves the Peano recursion structure, unique prime factorization and canonical transport under scale and orientation changes. Winding degree certifies the resulting natural-number arithmetic. ## Resolving how a value is generated The next construction retains ordered, bracketed addition and multiplication expressions. Only the specified zero, unit and absorbing reductions are imposed at this level. Arithmetic evaluation identifies expressions with the same value, while each value has a finite expression fibre. This gives a precise space in which the construction of a number can itself be observed. The simplest example is six. Adding six unit leaves and multiplying an additive expression for three by an additive expression for two give the same root value and the same root energy. Their leaf counts are six and five, while their accumulated internal quadratic defects are thirty and thirty-one. In both cases leaf energy plus accumulated defect is thirty-six. The equality at the root coexists with a measurable difference in the construction. A recursive positive law gives equal weight to the admissible root channels and assembles their subhistories independently. This law differs from uniform counting of all complete expressions. Phase invariance determines a finite phase extension. Summing the resolved source over histories and phases recovers the original Gaussian mass of each mode exactly. Expression multiplicity therefore enriches the source without changing its original partition function. Weighted amplitude readout, probability pushforward and conditional expectation have distinct definitions. Exact variance and entropy identities separate the information in the root value from the information remaining within its fibre. The example of six has strictly positive conditional leaf-count variance, giving a concrete instance of information preserved by the resolved construction. ## A complete operator on generation histories The same source weights determine a parent-child assembly response. The paper constructs a nonnegative self-adjoint trace-class operator on the complete counting history space. Its trace tail has an explicit Gaussian bound independent of the number of expressions in each fibre. Finite root cutoffs converge in trace norm, and the full operator generates a contraction evolution with a dissipation identity. The decisive result is a nonzero transfer from an initially invisible history difference to a later value response. A difference supported on the six histories of four has zero initial value readout,
tags: Finite evaluation fibres of arithmetic expressions
Unique factorization on generated arithmetic modes
Exact separation of value and expression-history information
Nontrivial coupling between arithmetic values and expression histories
Trace-class operator from arithmetic expression assembly
Exact memory equation for arithmetic readout
Canonical scale and orientation transport of arithmetic
title: A Spectral Construction of Natural-Number Arithmetic

summary: Nature heedlessly dispatches the metabolic efforts of microscopic organisms. Conceptive fungibility—the assumption that any sexual mate is interchangeable and equal—is opposite to the constitution of macroscopic organisms. We let microscopic organisms encounter problems faced by macroscopic organisms, such as the Allee effect, inbreeding, and sterility. Classical oncology confronts cancers with cytotoxins and maximum cell killing, letting Darwinian selection and clone breeding kill the host, with evolution being a proximate cause of death in most cancer patients ( Enríquez -Navas et al., 2015). We respond by exploiting conceptive fungibility in mitotic cells, altering semi-dormant germline properties to be meiotic through gene delivery. We specify a general interceptive apparatus, the Induced Extinction Vortex (IEV), that exploits reproductive imperatives to drive localized tumoral populations toward extinction. We specify IEV in three sequential phases (sexualization, demographic skew, and a reversion sink), each with its own threshold conditions and failure criteria. The design is method-agnostic: no delivery vehicle, meiotic driver, or receptor set is required, and any method capable of instantiating the phases falls within the proposal. The instantiation criteria are the Circuit, Metabolic, and Resectability criteria, stated in advance as points at which the implementation can fail.  Every deterrence is backed by documented or modeled demographic effects in wild taxa, such as feminizing parasites, coercive tortoises, and bottlenecked mountain lions. Evolutionary oncology has validated the changing of an adaptive response into a lethal deterrence. To our knowledge, no study combines these effects and directs them toward a clade of cellular populations. The proposal hypothesizes that an engineered reproductive dependency could create tumor population vulnerabilities analogous to mate limitation and reproductive interference. Existing research supports the component principles, but there is no evidence of a combined circuitry.
title: A Revised Intraspecific Predation: IEV, an Induced Extinction Vortex

summary: JAPAQ is a nationwide dataset of hourly air quality observations in Japan from January 2018 to December 2025. It covers the five pollutants regulated by Japan's Environmental Quality Standards — fine particulate matter (PM2.5), sulphur dioxide (SO2), nitric oxide (NO), suspended particulate matter (SPM), and photochemical oxidants (Ox) — and three meteorological variables (wind speed, temperature, relative humidity), from the Atmospheric Environmental Regional Observation System (AEROS, "Soramame") of the Ministry of the Environment, Japan. The deposit (japaq_v1.0.0.zip) contains two products built from the same records — JAPAQ-FE, the feature-enriched hourly table, and JAPAQ-KG, its knowledge graph — together with the raw observations, station metadata, and corrections log from which they are built, in five folders that follow the processing steps: 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_hourly_obs_v1.0.0.csv — raw hourly observations as downloaded: 114,237,726 records from 1,850 stations (station, timestamp, five pollutants, three meteorological variables). 4_JAPAQ-FE/japaq_fe_v1.0.0 (CSV and Parquet) — JAPAQ-FE, the feature-enriched, analysis-ready table and main data record: 110,328,514 records from 1,806 stations with documented quality control (three correction stages that remove 2,235,358 non-physical pollutant values; a physical range check for meteorology; quality flags for 2,345 implausible pollutant values and 141,448 meteorological values from faulty sensors, kept and marked), station metadata including complete resolved fields, calendar and time-of-day attributes, severity labels referenced to the Environmental Quality Standards, and a Beaufort wind-speed class (48 columns). 3_quality_control/japaq_corrections_log_v1.0.0.csv — every value set to null or flagged, with its original value, stage, and rule (2,473,666 records). 2_station_metadata/japaq_station_metadata_v1.0.0.csv and 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_station_list_v1.0.0.csv — English station metadata for 1,825 stations, including 143 stations missing from the current station list whose metadata were recovered from official NIES station files and municipality codes, with the source of each station's metadata; and the original Soramame station list (Japanese). 2_station_metadata/japaq_romanisation_log_v1.0.0.csv and STATION_METADATA_METHOD.md, and sources.csv — romanised address values, full source citations, and the recovery method for station metadata. 5_JAPAQ-KG/japaq_kg_v1.0.0.dump — JAPAQ-KG, the records of JAPAQ-FE as a Neo4j 2026.02 property graph with 220,660,640 nodes (Station, Location, ObservationTime, ObservedPollutant) and 330,987,348 relationships. JAPAQ-KG is the evaluation substrate of the AirCypher text-to-Cypher benchmark (IEEE BigData 2026). summary: This repository contains the data, analysis scripts and fitted model objects for the manuscript ` Nowhere except under negation? Exceptive constructions in native and heritage grammars '. The .rds files contain the saved model objects, and the model scripts load them instead of refitting when they are present. Participant identifiers in the raw data have been replaced with random codes. The corpus folder contains fig_corpus_licensing.R , which plots the distribution of krome kak across licensing environments from the hand-coded counts of the corpus study. The experiment1_pilot folder contains the pilot comparison of baseline and heritage speakers. The ratings are in data/raw/krome_kak_pilot.xlsx , and 01_prepare_pilot.R converts them to data/pilot_ratings.csv and computes the cell means of the pilot table ( derived/pilot_cell_means.csv ). No models are fitted for the pilot. The experiment2 folder contains the main acceptability experiment. The data/raw folder holds the PCIbex result files for the native group and the two heritage groups, and the background questionnaire ( participants.csv ). 00_import_raw.R reads these files and writes the eligible ratings to data/ , and 01_prepare_data.R applies the exclusions and writes the analysis files to derived/ . 02_fit_models.R fits the graded response model of the heritage-diagnostic items, the ordinal models with the heritageness score (overall and for each grammatical role), and the models in which heritage status is a binary speaker group or the mean diagnostic-item rating. 04_fit_supplementary_models.R fits the by-item variability models for each speaker group and the model of the four attested corpus items. 03_make_figures.R produces the figures in figures/ , and 05_bimodality.R computes the bimodality diagnostics of the participant mean ratings (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test, and one- versus two-component Gaussian mixtures). These scripts are run from inside the experiment2 folder. The heritageness_model folder contains the primary analysis of Experiment 2, in which heritageness is a continuous score estimated from the seven diagnostic items and its uncertainty is carried into the experimental model. 01_prepare_background.py recodes the background questionnaire. 02_fit_measurement_model.R fits the measurement model to the diagnostic items without speaker-group information, stores the posterior draws of the participant scores, and fits the experimental model with posterior-mean scores ( main_plugin.rds ). 03_fit_joint_model.R fits the joint model, in which the diagnostic and experimental ratings inform the score together ( joint.rds ). 04_fit_primary_model.R fits the experimental model separately to 32 posterior draws of the scores ( main_draw_01.rds to main_draw_32.rds ), pools them, and writes the summaries in output/ using summarize.R , additional_summaries.R and helpers.R . The estimates reported for Experiment 2 are in output/main_modular_contrasts.csv and output/joint_contrasts.csv . These scripts are run from the top folder. The analyses use R (brms with the cmdstanr backend, tidyverse, posterior, readxl, moments, diptest, mclust) and Python 3. Package versions are listed in heritageness_model/output/session_info.txt .
title: Nowhere except under negation? Exceptive constructions in native and heritage grammars

NEUROMUSCULAR ELECTRICAL STIMULATION AFTER STROKE AT THE LIMIT F101–F105 | FAMILY 21 | FIVE-FLAGSHIP SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK 33 × STARLI | A companion to the 819-page English research monograph STATUS: prospective nonclinical research design using isolated dummy loads, offline intention-label simulations and synthetic muscle-analog response models. No experiment with patients; no validated therapy, clinical benefit, human stimulation settings, quantum advantage or measured neuroplastic recovery is claimed. A LETTER FROM THE TWENTY-FIRST RESEARCH FAMILY The visible movement of a muscle analog can be a poor witness to the mechanism that produced it. A command may be delivered imperfectly across a changing electrical contact; a trigger may coincide with a learned task cue; a tired load can be driven harder until its output seems ordinary again. A mathematical inverse may confidently assign a unique dose to a nonunique response. Even after a controller reads OFF, a passive mechanism can move. These five ways to be misled are the joint research problem of this family. We therefore begin with independent electrical witnesses, not therapeutic claims. An isolated dummy load, a guarded stimulation-port emulator, an offline BCI cue-replay system and a synthetic force proxy form the minimum environment. By design, no patient evidence is created by this book. Each chapter proposes an explicit competing world, a blind counterfactual and a refusal condition; every result that cannot distinguish those worlds is left unresolved. The research becomes worth inheriting when another laboratory can reproduce an error and improve the question. The companion PDF preserves a fixed 819-page research architecture, 42 recomputable analytic 3D plates, diagrams of the 200 questions and 33 unbuilt Phoenix prototype schematics. The notebook brings the same five distinct mechanisms into readable scientific prose. No internal computation-time target appears in the publication. The five-stage parallel spacetime label names a reasoning workflow rather than a claim about physical parallel universes. I. FOURTEEN RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | When motion is not recovery A motor proxy can contract because a circuit drives it. A person may recover motor function through mechanisms not present in any nonclinical dummy load. This monograph is built around that difference. Its central objective is not to prove rehabilitation efficacy but to design independently testable experiments that isolate electrical input, controller decisions, mechanistic response and attribution of autonomous activity. An example research hinge is closed-loop stimulation. Its proposed mechanism is that measured contact-state feedback can control a load-proxy response without obscuring electrical burden. Its strongest alternative is that a visually stable proxy motion is caused by a fixed sequence or a contact-dependent artifact rather than closed-loop regulation. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to conceal a new contact-impedance trajectory and score measured delivered charge before revealing the programmed waveform. Reporting must include delivered charge [microC], current residual [mA], command-to-load latency [ms], dissipated proxy energy [mJ]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by open-loop constant-sequence replay with equal pulse budget and an instrumented impedance controller. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is electrical overlimit, contact heating surrogate or untraceable charge balance. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model. 02 | Five flags, five distinct modes of failure F101 tests closed-loop measurement of delivered charge under contact change. F102 asks whether triggers align with intention-like events rather than a hidden cue. F103 refuses to purchase apparent output with escalating energy during synthetic fatigue. F104 treats the inverse map from dose to response as potentially nonidentifiable. F105 requires off-state proof and unseen task transfer without interpreting proxy performance as human recovery. An example research hinge is intention-stimulation synchrony. Its proposed mechanism is that an independently timed intention proxy can predict a useful bounded stimulation window without learning task cues. Its strongest alternative is that a cue clock, eye activity or residual EMG, rather than intended action, explains the apparent synchrony. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to hide the cue schedule, alter the decoding delay and compare onset timing against an independent event clock. Reporting must include trigger latency [ms], absolute synchronization error [ms], false trigger rate [count/h], calibration error [1]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by fixed-delay trigger; shuffled-intention trigger; simple threshold decoder with the same recording and compute budget. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is unwarranted triggers when intention evidence is absent or ambiguous. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model. 03 | The isolated circuit is not a person The family platform is an isolated dummy load and muscle-analog simulator with a separated current witness and guarded offline BCI trigger replay. Any waveform here is a synthetic electrical exercise, not an instruction to configure a medical stimulation device. No human tissue, patient dataset, treatment threshold or claimed clinical recovery appears in the experiment results. An example research hinge is fatigue-aware compensation. Its proposed mechanism is that fatigue-state estimation can reduce proxy-output error while respecting energy, contact and thermal safety envelopes. Its strongest alternative is that the controller maintains appearance by increasing energy while true proxy capability deteriorates. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to introduce unseen fatigue-decay trajectories and test whether the controller backs off rather than chasing the original target. Reporting must include proxy-force retention [1], output error [%], electrical energy [mJ], thermal proxy margin [1]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by fixed-gain control; periodic rest schedule; conservative energy-capped rule with identical load histories. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is energy escalation under fatigue, unstable feedback or proxy thermal burden. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model. 04 | Physical quantities and where they live Current is measured at a declared load port in milliamperes; charge is its signed time integral in microcoulombs; time is measured by independent clocks in milliseconds; electrical energy is integrated from synchronized voltage and current in millijoules. Synthetic proxy force and fatigue remain normalized unless separately calibrated. Mixing these categories produces equations with persuasive typography but no trustworthy physical meaning. An example research hinge is dose-response identifiability. Its proposed mechanism is that amplitude, temporal width, impedance and contact distribution can be distinguished by independently witnessed response features. Its strongest alternative is that many different pulses yield the same integrated charge and the apparent dose-response law is underdetermined. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to hold integrated charge fixed, change normalized waveform shape and attempt blinded reconstruction of the hidden pulse family. Reporting must include integrated charge [microC], waveform-width proxy [1], sensitivity rank [count], prediction coverage [%]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by equal-charge pulse-family comparison; impedance-only regression; null Jacobian rank model. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is a nonidentifiable dose parameter used as if it were a causal prescription. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model. 05 | Why three-dimensional geometry can help A 3D surface can expose sensitivity to two controlled sources of error: a contact shift and latency, a cue artifact and trigger delay, fatigue depth and energy reserve, waveform identity and inverse uncertainty, or off-state delay and task novelty. Each plate is synthetic and analytic. The exact grid and standalone recompute script are embedded, while the plot itself cannot substitute for bench calibration or clinical observation. An example research hinge is stimulation-off voluntary capability. Its proposed mechanism is that a genuine capacity gain would persist in untrained, stimulation-off tasks after all powered assistance is demonstrably absent. Its strongest alternative is that passive contraction, practice, hidden actuator work or spontaneous time change produces the visible improvement. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to switch all stimulus outputs off, independently verify zero delivered charge and test a hidden untrained proxy task without feedback. Reporting must include stimulation-off proxy accuracy [%], charge at withdrawal [microC], task-transfer score [1], retest stability [1]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by device-off untrained-task test; equal-time sham schedule; no-output repeated assessment. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is claiming patient recovery from unpowered mechanism or synthetic proxy alone. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model.

summary: The clinical biochemistry laboratories are vital for screening, diagnosis and selection of treatment and monitoring. These results are reliable as a result of reliable quality management carried out during pre-examination, examination and post-examination. Internal quality control (IQC) is used to track the day to day stability of analytical procedures and external quality assessment (EQA) is used to make an independent comparison of the laboratory's performance with assigned values or other laboratories. An unacceptable control result, however, does not, however, mean that the problem has been solved. The nonconformity must be investigated, the direct effects of the nonconformity must be controlled, the root cause (s) of the nonconformity must be identified, the corrective and preventive action (s) must be implemented and effectiveness verified through a structured corrective and preventive action (CAPA) framework. The principles of IQC and EQA in Clinical Biochemistry are reviewed and the contribution of the findings of the two to a CAPA system of Quality Management are assessed. It outlines typical nonconformities that will be found in an analysis, quality control statistical approaches, root cause analysis tools, corrective and preventive actions, documentation requirements and indicators of CAPA effectiveness. Special focus on quality management based on risk and the ISO 15189:2022 requirements. The review also points out that good CAPA go beyond incident reports closing and are evidenced by subsequent data on IQC, EQA, and process performance to show continued improvement. An integrated approach will decrease the chance of analytical failure, improve laboratory competence and promote patient safety.
title: Evaluation of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Framework for Internal and External Quality Control in a Clinical Biochemistry Laboratory

summary: Background: Emphysematous cystitis (EC) is a rare but potentially life-threatening urinary tract infection characterized by gas accumulation within the bladder wall and/or lumen, most commonly associated with gas-producing microorganisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, including empagliflozin, promote urinary glucose excretion, raising questions about a possible association with genitourinary infections. However, the relationship between empagliflozin use and EC remains uncertain, with evidence currently limited to published case reports. Aim: To review the reported cases of emphysematous cystitis (EC) associated with empagliflozin use and to summarize the demographics, clinical features, treatment modalities and outcomes. Methodology: A systematic review was conducted using the databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science from inception until October 2026. The review included published case reports and several patients who developed EC while taking empagliflozin. Patient characteristics, laboratory findings, radiographic findings, management strategies, and clinical outcomes were extracted and qualitatively evaluated. Results: We examined seven patient cases with ages ranging from 62 to 90 (median 76). Two patients received empagliflozin for heart failure, and five patients had type 2 diabetes. Hematuria, dysuria, frequent urination, and suprapubic discomfort were common symptoms that emerged between two weeks and eight months following treatment. Urinary retention, bladder outlet obstruction, chronic renal disease, advanced age, and recent catheterization were among the contributing variables. Klebsiella pneumoniae was the most frequently isolated microorganism, based on microbiological culture results. Computed tomography (CT) was the principal imaging modality used to confirm the diagnosis of emphysematous cystitis. Management generally included discontinuation of empagliflozin, antibiotic therapy, and bladder drainage or decompression when indicated. Five patients recovered, whereas two patients died. Conclusion: Empagliflozin-associated emphysematous cystitis is a rare but serious condition mostly seen in elderly patients with multiple health issues and urinary tract abnormalities. Early detection and treatment are crucial to minimize risks. More research is needed to understand its causes and frequency.
title: Empagliflozin-associated emphysematous cystitis: a systematic review of published case reports

summary: Data and result logs of the PhishVN URL-benchmark study: the three external corpora in the exact rows the study used, and (from version 1.2.0) the study's result logs. External corpora. Class-balanced 1:1 subsamples of PhiUSIIL (20,000 rows, UCI, label polarity converted so that 1 is phishing), ISCX-URL2016 (15,894 rows) and PhishStorm (20,000 rows), the last two in the phishing/legitimate form redistributed with the GramBeddings repository. Each row carries the host the study featurises, 25 lexical features in the CompPhish schema (computed with the public-suffix list of the library version used) and the label. The subsamples were not drawn by a seed, so these files define the transfer experiments. With the PhishVN corpus (Mendeley Data, DOI 10.17632/b97hxbxtpd.4) they are the inputs of the benchmark, protocol, decomposition and transfer tables, which the walkthrough notebook notebooks/url_benchmark/url_benchmark_walkthrough.ipynb in https://github.com/vuthainguyen1602/phishvn recomputes. Cite the original datasets when using the rows (see README.md). Result logs ( results.zip ). One row per model family, protocol and seed for every experiment, the summary files the paper's tables are generated from, and the logs of the analyses added in the first revision (operating points, thresholds carried across corpora, forward cut-offs, the protocol contrast within one phishing feed, label-error scenarios, corpus probe, two-class temporal check, string models, tuning, attribution, cost). results_manifest.csv inside the archive gives every file's size and SHA-256. The files are aggregates and hold no URL, hostname or e-mail address. Version 1.3.0 adds to results.zip the logs of two analyses: a threshold carried across corpora and the protocol contrast with the phishing class drawn from one feed. Version 1.2.0 added results.zip . summary: Tributaries of the middle Rio São Francisco basin, including the Rio Verde Grande, are important nursery habitats for reproduction of migratory fishes and provide water for economic activities such as agriculture, but the characterization of the fish fauna in these areas remains understudied. We document the presence of 53 species across 43 genera within 21 families in the Rio Verde Grande, encompassing the otophysan orders Characiformes (30 species), Gymnotiformes (two species), and Siluriformes (16 species), as well as the percomorph families Cichlidae (two species) and Poeciliidae (three species). Megalamphodus eques and Poecilia reticulata are non-native species and introduced in the Rio Verde Grande and along the São Francisco basin. The sampling site near Jaíba situated at the lowest altitude of 467 m a.s.l. harbored the highest species richness among all sites with 37 species representing 62% of the overall richness and was completely dry in 2019. Analysis of ecological trait factors resulted in assemblage dominated by medium- and large-bodied fishes, prevalence of benthic feeding strategies, and habitat association with lotic environments. This survey represents a baseline for future regional initiatives that require the development of conservation plans focused on the Rio Verde Grande that can thus maintain the unique freshwater species diversity.
title: Ichthyofauna of the Rio Verde Grande, middle São Francisco basin, eastern Brazil (Actinopterygii, Teleostei)

summary: Replication package (paper, code and data) for "Hindsight or Foresight? Alternative Data, Early Warning, and the Measurement of Corporate-Group Failure". It scores eleven families of alternative data on lead time, specificity, Thai accessibility, cost, legal safety and point-in-time integrity; codes 28 failures and turnarounds of firms and business groups by the first public signal in each family; measures hindsight bias on a public panel of 146,045 U.S. firm-years with SEC enforcement labels (Bao et al., 2020), where a gradient-boosting model's ROC AUC falls from 0.833 under random cross-validation to 0.697 under point-in-time evaluation; and runs Monte Carlo simulations of forking paths, alignment artefacts, timeliness versus noise and base rates.
title: hindsight-or-foresight

summary: # Pulsed infrared thermography recordings and reproducibility pipeline for lightning-exposed unidirectional T700/epoxy CFRP panels at 25, 30, and 40 kV **Manuscript**: Sensitivity-Aware Temporal–Spatial Assessment of Thermal-Anomaly Candidate Persistence in Lightning-Exposed T700/Epoxy CFRP Using Pulsed Infrared Thermography. *Sensors*, 2026 (under review). ## Authors Xibin Zhang (corresponding, 202611085025@mail.scut.edu.cn), Lianfang Tian, Bo Peng, Dong Chen, Guozeng Liu. School of Automation Science and Engineering, South China University of Technology, Guangzhou 510640, China. ## Equipment - IR camera: FLIR Silver 480M, 30 Hz nominal, 640×512 sensor. Stored arrays cropped to 500×505×300 (25 kV front), 500×503×300 (30 kV front), 498×501×300 (40 kV front), 350 time samples per recording. - Excitation: two Xenon flash lamps, 5000 J pulse rating, 2–50 ms duration, optical flash thermography. - Specimens: unidirectional T700/epoxy pultruded panels, 100×100×5 mm, impulse-current exposure at nominal 25, 30, and 40 kV. ## Contents - `raw_mat/`: original infrared temperature sequences in MATLAB MAT format. The 35 kV front recording is quarantined as a provenance-duplicate of the excluded 45 kV group (see manuscript Section 3.1). - `temporal_pca_analysis/`: derived TSR residual arrays, candidate masks, sampled-grid PCA outputs, sensitivity tables, adaptive joint-score maps, and the eight-configuration robustness technical report. - `source_code/`: Python reproduction pipeline. Entry points: `reproduce_pipeline.py`, `reproduce_sensitivity.py`, `reproduce_background.py`, `make_summary_figures.py`, `verify_local.py`, `run.py`, `run_all.sh`. - `current_submission/`: V5.2 manuscript, cover letter, title page, highlights, supplementary information, graphical abstract. ## How to reproduce 1. Install Python 3.10+ and packages in `source_code/reproduction_project/requirements.txt`. 2. Place the files under `raw_mat/` with filenames as shipped here. 3. summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . The package contains the seventeen supplementary tables, the analysis and figure code, the recorded software versions, the reconstruction log for the long-read alignments, and a per-read phase-evidence table. What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export. The short-read counts at the two A2143 coordinates are reproduced from the archived alignment, whose header records the exact command and tool versions. What is not. The original NCBI query string and its date were not retained, so the cohort cannot be rebuilt verbatim; per-accession inclusion flags are given instead. The barrnap installation originally used on the analysis machine is missing a Perl module and does not run; the rRNA copy numbers were therefore archived values in earlier versions and are re-derived with barrnap 1.10.5 in this version. The original parameter sets for two of the three long-read procedures were not retained; those procedures were re-run and both original and re-run values are reported side by side and never pooled. One cell of the long-read table reproduces exactly; the others do not, and this is stated in the manuscript. Changes in version 4. The package matches the manuscript. All thirteen supplementary tables are present, including Supplementary Tables S12 and S13, which were absent from the previous version, and Supplementary Table S1 now carries the genome length and assembly level of all 1,483 retained genomes rather than leaving those columns empty. A new Supplementary Table S1b lists the seven excluded genomes that could be recovered from local storage, with their lengths; the genome-length window is 1.5 to 1.7 Mb and this version states the evidence that fixes its bounds. Three new scripts are included: the marker-control experiment (scripts 26 and 27), in which the single copy-differentiating base of the isolate was set to A in both copies, to C in both, to T in both, and exchanged between them, with the reads realigned to each control; and the structural diagnostic of the two 26695 23S copies (script 28), which reports that copy 1 contains no ambiguous base while copy 2 contains one N at genome position 1,475,696. The four control reference sequences are deposited under results/marker_control/. Changes in version 6. This version restores the complete file set. The previous version was published from an incomplete upload, so most of the figures, several of the supplementary tables and part of the analysis code were missing from that record. Zenodo caps a record at 100 files and this package has 134, so the package is now deposited as a single archive, hp23s_copy_assignment_package.zip , which holds every file at the path it occupies in the source repository; this README, the SHA-256 manifest and the archive of rRNA calls and copy sequences are additionally placed loose in the record. From version 10 the manuscript itself is not deposited, in the archive or loose. Every member of the archive is listed in SHA256SUMS.txt with its SHA-256, and that manifest is regenerated here, which corrects the entry for this README (the previous manifest had been computed before the last edit of the file). DOI.txt now lists the version DOIs, and the data-availability sentence in the manuscript names the concept DOI rather than one version, so that it cannot point at a superseded record. Changes in version 7. This version is a manuscript round: the text is rebuilt from the same locked data by the same script, and no reported value changes. Three defects in the supplementary apparatus are correcte
title: Long reads assign a 23S rRNA resistance allele to one of the two copies in Helicobacter pylori; a complete short-read assembly does not

The manuscript reports no patient investigation, no demonstrated therapy benefit, no quantum advantage and no automated clinical decisions. A LETTER FROM THE TWENTY-FOURTH RESEARCH FAMILY What counts as long-term recovery when observation times, severity, intervention exposure and missing outcomes are all changing? A polished recovery curve can be natural history. A scale can saturate while motion quality changes. Daily-life participation can rise because help and opportunity change. An immediate assisted maximum can fade after the device is off. A claim of clinical benefit must never be promoted from the geometry of a synthetic model. The five questions need independent counterfactual witnesses. F116 analyzes change over repeated independent device-off visits while exposing natural history and selective follow-up. F117 compares blinded scale proxies with continuous independent kinematic reference. F118 separates capacity, opportunity and actual participation in synthetic daily tasks. F119 examines what remains after immediate external assistance and familiar cues are withdrawn. F120 applies a predeclared evidence hierarchy to all assigned cases, including missing outcomes, risks and revised endpoint definitions. The common platform is a completely synthetic longitudinal challenge set. No patient data or demonstrated human benefit is reported. The companion PDF preserves the 819-page research architecture with 42 standalone reproducible mathematical grids, 30 candidate equations, 82 chapters of six progressive pages, 200 Research Gates and 33 unbuilt Phoenix concepts. The notebook develops the same research questions in a more continuous scientific prose. The public five-stage parallel spacetime name is a methodology for structured research reasoning, not a claim of real parallel spacetimes. I. FOURTEEN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | A beautiful recovery curve can still be wrong The earliest question is not how quickly a curve rises but which observations exist, which were withheld and whether the curve records unassisted function. Take longitudinal recovery trajectories as a specific case. The candidate says serial unassisted outcome trajectories can be modeled without confusing spontaneous recovery, changing rehabilitation exposure and selective follow-up with an intervention effect. The rival explanation says natural recovery, informative attrition or post-hoc selection of a favorable visit generates the apparent durable recovery curve. A research team should conceal visit times and natural-recovery components, then require predictions of an unrehearsed device-off endpoint at future visits and report unassisted task score [synthetic points], visit gap [weeks], retention contrast [1], follow-up proportion [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is blinded serial device-off task score with a complete visit and attrition record. Compare with visit-matched simple mixed model, prespecified natural-history reference, and no-intervention trajectory with the same measurement resources. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if missing later outcomes labeled as recovered function or model confidence used to replace an unseen visit. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 02 | Five distinct ways evidence may fail F116 separates longitudinal course and natural history; F117 challenges agreement between scales and motion; F118 follows daily activity; F119 contrasts assisted peaks with retention; F120 audits the truthfulness of the claim. Take scale–kinematics agreement as a specific case. The candidate says clinically recognizable scores and independent continuous motion proxies may disagree in ways that depend on scale ceilings, severity and rater calibration. The rival explanation says a scale ceiling, correlated assessor expectation or sensor calibration mismatch produces apparent agreement despite unchanged movement quality. A research team should hold continuous kinematics constant while crossing a scale ceiling, then conceal assessor assignment and test agreement on novel movement profiles and report scale score [synthetic points], joint-angle error [deg], agreement bias [points], ceiling fraction [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is paired independent ordinal-rating and kinematic reference with explicit floor-ceiling behavior. Compare with blind fixed-scale score, reference motion encoder, and simple monotonic calibration with independent floor/ceiling checks. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if a saturated ordinal scale treated as proof of renewed function or an objectively measured movement incorrectly relabeled a validated clinical outcome. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 03 | Anonymized synthetic records before clinical conclusions The common minimal system is a pseudonymous synthetic longitudinal rehabilitation challenge set. No patient datasets are claimed and no medical intervention is proposed. Take daily-life participation and transfer as a specific case. The candidate says independent daily-activity participation must be measured outside rehearsed tasks, with environmental support and opportunities to participate separately recorded. The rival explanation says home assistance, device usage, reduced task opportunity or an observer effect accounts for improvement in recorded daily activity. A research team should transfer a frozen model to simulated unobserved daily-life contexts, manipulate environmental assistance and blind the activity labels and report independent task count [tasks/day], supported-time fraction [1], participation score [synthetic points], missing diary fraction [1]. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 04 | The visit that never happened Missing follow-up cannot be written as recovered ability. Time-to-observation, observation reason and censoring assumptions are scientific variables. Take assistance–retention dissociation as a specific case. The candidate says an immediate assisted performance increment may decay or vanish after device withdrawal and is not exchangeable with durable autonomous capacity. The rival explanation says one exceptional immediate best trial, repeated cue familiarity, powered work or spontaneous time trend exaggerates long-term recovery. summary: This repository contains the de-identified raw datasets supporting the manuscript entitled "Design and Evaluation of a Wearable Vibrotactile Feedback System for Posture Correction in Adolescent Girls with Thoracic Hyperkyphosis: A Three-Arm Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial" submitted to the International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction (IJHCI). Ethical Approval: The experimental protocol was reviewed and approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad (Ethics Code: IR.UM.REC.1405.146). The clinical trial was prospectively registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (Trial ID: IRCT20260725070349N1). Dataset Contents: The provided spreadsheet (Deidentified_Study_Dataset_HIHC_2026_8922.xlsx) contains three distinct worksheets: 1. RCT_Posture_Data: Longitudinal thoracic kyphosis angle measurements across fifteen female adolescents (aged 17-18) randomized into three intervention groups (Device-only, Exercise-only, Combined) measured at baseline (T0), immediately post-intervention (T1, 21 days), and at 2-week unguided follow-up (T2). 2. Validation_BlandAltman: One hundred simultaneous paired posture angle measurements comparing the custom MEMS-based wearable sensor against the clinical reference system (Idiag SpinalMouse®), along with absolute differences and agreement limits. 3. Metadata_Codebook: Detailed codebook describing variable definitions, measurement units, experimental setup, and hardware specifications.
