summary: This record provides the companion experimental data, code, and execution environment for the manuscript “Input Reach versus Oracle Observation: A Systems Engineering Validation Protocol for AI-Reconstructed Components in Legacy System Replacement” by Kigon Park. The artifact includes the frozen experimental protocol and amendment log, library versions and license notices, input sets, reconstruction evidence and outputs, raw execution records, analysis code, re-execution instructions, and a separate Docker container image. The experiments comprise three complementary studies: an equal-budget comparison of input-generation policies on 24 frozen reconstructions; calibration of observation relations using 32 controlled perturbation operators across four APIs; and executable evaluation of 12 fresh reconstructions of cJSON and miniz components. Constructed control violations are distinguished from naturally occurring reconstruction errors. The deposit preserves the experimental release dated 29 October 2026. Some embedded documentation and manuscript-authoring files retain the earlier title, “Input and Observation Adequacy in AI Assisted Binary Reconstruction.” These authoring files correspond to the earlier manuscript rather than the revised MDPI layout. The frozen reconstruction outputs and supplied environment support re-execution of the reported evaluations. Exact reproduction of the model-generation step is limited because an immutable model snapshot and inference sampling seeds were unavailable. Please consult README.txt for the file inventory and re-execution instructions. Third-party components retain their original licenses and notices.
title: Companion Artifact for "Input Reach versus Oracle Observation: A Systems Engineering Validation Protocol for AI-Reconstructed Components in Legacy System Replacement"

summary: A considerable challenge in palaeoanthropology is the handling of fragmented and sensitive human remains, which provide an important source of information about the identity of humans in the past. Virtual reconstructions have facilitated the extraction of these information and can be applied in various fields. By using computed tomography and advanced computer software, the virtual reconstruction of a subadult Neolithic skull from Frankfurt am Main-Fechenheim, Germany, is presented in this study. In combination with a revised age estimation, the reconstruction provides new data for future comparative analyses of one of the oldest preserved human skeletons of Frankfurt city area.
title: A Virtual Cranial Reconstruction of the Oldest Human Remains of Frankfurt am Main-Fechenheim

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: the greedy row-selection rule built into every linear-algebra library, column-pivoted QR, can lose against the best possible choice by a factor of about exp(C√k), with an exact constant C, and never by the 2 k allowed by the textbook guarantee. Context. Many simulation and data methods keep only k of N coordinates of an N×k matrix Q with orthonormal columns (for example the interpolation points of the discrete empirical interpolation method, DEIM). The quality of a choice I is γ = ‖Q(I,:) −1 ‖ 2 , the factor by which interpolation from the chosen coordinates can be worse than the best approximation; some choice always has γ ≤ √(k(N−k+1)). The rule used in practice is column-pivoted QR (QRCP) on Q * , which repeatedly picks the coordinate least explained by those already chosen. Drmač and Gugercin (SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 2016) proved a bound that grows like 2 k . Damle and Kressner asked whether QRCP meets the existence scale on orthonormal rows (Problem 4.3 of Amsel et al., arXiv:2602.05394). Chen, Liu, He and Dong (arXiv:2606.02484) gave the first answer, negative: their examples exceed every polynomial multiple of the existence scale, and their construction already gives growth of order exp(c√k) with a small c. Damle (arXiv:2607.13532) showed that the Bischof–Stewart rule meets the existence scale. Results. Let the coherence μ(Q) be the largest row energy divided by the average. (1) Theorem 2.3: if μ(Q) ≤ H, every legal QRCP selection, with any tie-breaking, has γ ≤ √(e(N−k+1)) exp(C(H)√k), with an explicit constant C(H): C(1) = 2 (equal row energies), C(2) ≈ 2.25, and C(H) 2 /log H → 1. This is the first bound below exponential in k for QRCP on orthonormal rows. (2) The constant is sharp: the worst case satisfies log G k (H) = (C(H)+o(1))√k, with real examples of fewer than 3k 3 rows built from a generalised Kahan matrix; for H > 1 their pivots are unique, and at H = 1 they use the smallest-label tie rule. (3) Corollary 2.6: since μ(Q) ≤ N/k, the bound holds for every input with C(N/k). (4) Theorem 2.7 and Corollary 2.8: without any coherence assumption the worst case is exp(Θ(√(k log(N/k)))) once N ≥ k 2+ε (and log N = o(k)), and exp((1+o(1))√(k log N)) when log N/log k → ∞. (5) Theorem 7.1: an a posteriori bound γ ≤ (√e/d k ) exp(√((k−1)L)) from the observed pivot range L, with an optimal coefficient. At k = 100 the new bound allows about 10 9 to 10 10 where the classical bound allowed about 10 30 ; it is smaller than the classical bound from k = 13 at H = 1. Limits. Exact arithmetic and worst cases only; typical inputs behave far better, and floating-point QRCP is not analysed. Sharpness is on the logarithmic scale: upper and lower bounds still differ by a factor polynomial in k, and the limits are approached slowly. The worst examples need N of order k 3 ; whether growth of order exp(c√k) occurs when N is a fixed multiple of k is open. Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF) and its figure; check scripts with their recorded outputs (verify.py: exact rational Kahan identities, 25 orthonormal inputs, eleven completed examples at k = 16 to 128 factorised by two QRCP implementations, a retained failed candidate as negative control, large-rank core sums against 80-digit evaluations and the endpoint constructions; check_extensions.py: 50-digit checks of C(H), Table 2, the Kahan family for k = 6 to 16 and inequality (7.5) on 779 grid points; fingerprints.py); the figure script; the bibliography; a machine-readable index; a research-gate record; a review summary; a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Checks raise SystemExit and stay active under python -O. Assurance. Written proofs, with finite computational checks. Internal AI-assisted review only: five reviewer roles, an adver
title: How badly can column-pivoted QR choose rows of an orthonormal basis? The sharp stretched-exponential worst case

summary: This dataset provides the numerical results supporting the manuscript entitled  A Topological Selected-Solve Approximation of Inverse Hodge Operators for Explicit DEC/FETD Maxwell Simulations , by A. S. Moura and W. G. Facco. The research investigates sparse approximations of the inverse electric Whitney–Hodge matrix using topologically defined sparsity patterns, with particular emphasis on the radius-three selected-solve approximation (G_{H,3}). The dataset contains 43 CSV files and eight PDF figures documenting the numerical experiments, including: Algebraic validation of topological sparsity patterns and approximation accuracy. Robustness under geometric mesh perturbations and material contrasts. Time-domain Maxwell simulations in two-dimensional perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) cavities. Modal and frequency-domain analyses. Scalability and computational-cost measurements. Comparisons between sparse selected-solve updates, diagonal approximations, and direct LU-based time stepping. CFL stability investigations and electromagnetic energy-drift diagnostics. The archive also includes supporting documentation and SHA-256 checksums for data integrity verification. Source code: https://github.com/alexmoura2024/selected-hodge-dec-fetd The accompanying Python scripts provide the algorithms and procedures required to reproduce the numerical experiments. Runtime measurements may vary with hardware, software versions, and computational environment. This dataset is released to support transparency, verification, and reproducibility in computational electromagnetics and numerical linear algebra.
title: Numerical Datasets for Topological Selected-Solve Approximation of Inverse Hodge Operators in Explicit DEC/FETD Maxwell Simulations

summary: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating yields a MAP mean absolute error of 7.3 mmHg, compared with 9.2 mmHg for random selection at the same coverage. The gated agent achieves 60.0% agreement with recorded actions at 81.0% decision coverage, compared with 55.0% agreement and 99.5% coverage for an ungated ensemble agent. Component ablations show lower factual risk with joint gating than with either gate alone.These results characterize a reliability--coverage trade-off in selective clinical simulation; they do not identify individualized treatment effects or establish improved patient outcomes.
title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support

summary: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.
title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon

summary: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. Observation-to-observation models avoid this dependence, but most omit the recursive filtering cycle that lets DA systems carry a background state through sparse, irregular observations. We introduce WeatherDreamer, a world model that learns this cycle end-to-end from 18 global observing systems, without reanalysis. It infers a latent state from observations, carries it forward hour by hour with learned dynamics, corrects it each hour with new observations, and can predict what any of its observing systems would measure at any location. At held-out stations, its ensembles beat NOAA's Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) for temperature, dew point and wind out to 12 h and are better calibrated than GEFS and the ECMWF ensemble. Precipitation, cloud-top height and solar irradiance, never inputs at inference, are inferred with skill matching or exceeding operational products at short leads. Against the first guess of NOAA's Gridpoint Statistical Interpolation (GSI) DA system, WeatherDreamer's short-range departures are within 10% of GSI's at surface stations and within 25% for moisture-sensitive microwave channels, but up to five times larger for temperature-sounding channels. Never given observation errors, its learned update assumes errors close to known instrument and retrieval errors of microwave sounders and scatterometer winds. WeatherDreamer also separates viewing geometry from atmospheric state, recovering 83-96% of observed limb darkening and producing seamless nadir-view imagery. Producing an hourly global analysis in about 1.5 minutes on one GPU, WeatherDreamer shows that assimilation and forecasting can be learned together directly from observations.
title: WeatherDreamer: Learning a World Model from Multimodal Earth Observations

summary: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process. This gap limits an examiner's ability to analyze the specific behavior of a running large language model (LLM) service that cannot be restarted or modified. We present a method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without requiring prior knowledge of the model's architecture parameters or weights. The approach employs a general six-stage process with platform-specific adapters, utilizing either a PyTorch allocator clock or a kernel-launch clock to identify and read tensor allocations from video memory. We validate this acquisition on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes, demonstrating that the recovered bytes are byte-exact and usable for downstream analysis. As a use case, we apply linear probes trained on standard framework activations to the recovered states, successfully distinguishing refusal from compliance with an AUROC of 0.88 on held-out prompts. This work establishes that live, observational access to intermediate hidden states is feasible on named inference platforms, providing a new source of evidence for examining the operational behavior of deployed AI systems.
title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States

summary: Developing effective forecasting models for diverse time-series domains requires substantial expert knowledge, evidence from scientific literature on the web, and iterative experimentation. However, translating this knowledge and research experience into model designs requires preserving source context and testing applicability under task-specific assumptions. In this paper, we propose NeoResearch, a literature- and experience-guided autonomous research framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) as researchers to discover lightweight, domain-specific forecasting models. Specifically, NeoResearch establishes an expert-inspired dual-loop research workflow, coupling hypothesis-driven architecture exploration with iterative training and hyperparameter optimization through experimental feedback. To enable knowledge-grounded discovery, the agent autonomously mines scientific literature from the Web, extracting modeling mechanisms, empirical evidence, and applicability conditions to formulate task-grounded, testable architecture hypotheses. Furthermore, a hierarchical experience memory links literature findings to experimental outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons, guiding architecture discovery and training optimization while supporting reuse across forecasting tasks. Experiments on ten datasets show competitive performance and support dual loops, literature extraction, and memory reuse. Our code is available.
title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery

summary: Machine learning systems specialize computation to the workload and hardware, but communication remains in generic libraries whose device code and transport decisions are not visible to high-level compilers. We present Obaleth, a compiler that makes GPU-initiated communication part of a kernel's intermediate representation, co-optimizes it alongside computation, and lowers it to specialized transport code. Obaleth plans completions around buffer lifetimes and optimizes memory ordering, synchronization, and batching across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On H100 GPUs, Obaleth sends small messages up to 3.3$\times$ faster, and on 256 GPUs runs all-to-all 1.25$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ faster than NVSHMEM and NCCL GIN, with much smaller memory and register use. In vLLM, it serves Qwen3-235B on 16 B200 GPUs and answers requests up to 1.29$\times$ faster than with DeepEP.
title: Compiling Specialized GPU-Initiated Networking

summary: Coding table underlying Table 5 of the article "Limits and potential of the Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (WEAI): towards a mixed-methods approach in studies on women in traditional communities". Twenty-seven peer-reviewed publications identified in Scopus and Web of Science (descriptors "WEAI", "empowerment", "qualitative") are coded along five methodological dimensions: design and timing of the qualitative component, function of the qualitative component, endogenous indicators, epistemological basis, and what is left out relative to the WEAI+Q proposal. summary: Reproducibility Package — Version 1.1.0 This repository contains the complete computational reproducibility package for the study “Significance-Classification Instability Beyond p-Value Variability: A Monte Carlo Study of Effect Direction and Effect-Estimate Compatibility.” The study investigates statistical-significance classification instability across independent studies generated under the same population mechanism, jointly examining effect-direction agreement, differences in estimated effect magnitude, and direct between-estimate comparisons. Original Simulation Study (Version 1.0.0) The original study comprises 509 unique simulation scenarios, including 486 factorial scenarios and 25 directed transition-region scenarios, with two overlapping conditions. The factorial scenarios used 100,000 paired replications per scenario, while the directed scenarios used 250,000 paired replications. Statistical inference was based on two-sided Welch tests at a significance level of 0.05. The original reproducibility package includes R scripts, simulation functions, scenario definitions, random-number streams, aggregated simulation results, conditional analyses, tables, figures, metadata, and documentation required to reproduce the reported findings. Extensions Introduced in Version 1.1.0 Version 1.1.0 incorporates supplementary mathematical and computational analyses developed in response to the comments and methodological recommendations received during the peer-review process for the manuscript submitted to Mathematics (MDPI) . These extensions were designed to strengthen the methodological robustness, analytical interpretation, and reproducibility of the original findings, particularly regarding significance-classification discordance, effect-direction agreement, heteroscedasticity, statistical power, and direct comparisons between effect estimates. The additional materials are organized in the revision_mayor_2026 directory and include: Supplementary sensitivity analyses covering 24 simulation scenarios. Power-calibrated analyses covering 18 scenarios, targeting approximately 50% statistical power. Additional simulations involving Normal, Student's t, and Gamma distributions, unequal sample sizes, and different standard-deviation ratios. Conditional analyses of significance discordance, effect-direction agreement, and direct between-estimate rejection. Independent computational validation and cross-checks using R and Python. Supplementary numerical results, methodological validation reports, and file-integrity documentation. The supplementary analyses provide additional evidence concerning the robustness and interpretation of the original simulation findings. In particular, conditional rejection frequencies are distinguished from evidence of differences between underlying population effects, and failure to reject a direct between-estimate test is not interpreted as evidence of statistical equivalence. Reproducibility and Version History Version 1.0.0 remains preserved as originally published. Version 1.1.0 extends the computational reproducibility package without replacing or altering the original simulation results. The original and supplementary analyses are maintained separately to ensure transparency, computational traceability, and reproducibility. The accompanying README and CHANGELOG files document the repository structure, the modifications introduced in Version 1.1.0, and the procedures for reproducing the analyses. This version provides an expanded reproducibility resource supporting the scientific revision of the manuscript while preserving the integrity of the original research.
title: Reproducibility Package for "Significance-Classification Instability Beyond p-Value Variability: A Monte Carlo Study of Effect Direction and Effect-Estimate Compatibility"

summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): polyhelper.ai/trends/markets , polyhelper.ai/trends/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24285333 . Orc6, the only non-AAA+ family protein within the origin recognition complex (ORC), has diverged significantly in function, sequence, and structure across eukaryotes, all while remaining necessary for proper genome maintenance and DNA replication in most species. This preprint investigates several differences between human and fruit fly ( Drosophila melanogaster ) Orc6 (HsOrc6 and DmOrc6, respectively), namely the behavior of the conserved C-terminal α-helix that tethers Orc6 to ORC. Here, the authors postulate that the mechanism of Orc6 association varies substantially between the species: in D. melanogaster , the C-terminal α-helix of DmOrc6 forms a high affinity interaction with DmORC reliant on a sulfur-aromatic interaction between M232 and the highly conserved W228. Meanwhile, HsOrc6 has lower affinity for HsORC, but the authors believe this is compensated for by utilizing a strong nuclear localization sequence (NLS) to increase the local concentration of HsOrc6 in the nucleus to allow for binding. The authors utilize several orthogonal methods to evaluate the effects of specific Orc6 mutations and human-fly Orc6 chimeras on ORC-Orc6 association, genome maintenance, and viability. While the general claim the authors make about the differences in nuclear localization and conserved regions of the Orc6 C-terminal α-helix are sensible and backed up by the presented data, there are several points of feedback provided regarding the in vivo experiments and mutant Drosophila lines. These aim to strengthen the scientific rigor of the manuscript and raise alternative explanations for conflicting results in the mutant Orc6 experiments. With these considerations, the manuscript could provide insight into the evolution and differing behavior of Orc6 amongst metazoans. Major comments: 1. MTT assay has appreciably different cell proliferation values between experiments for the same groups (WT, CTR, NA) and appears to use technical triplicates rather than biological replicates (p. 6, 11, Fig. 6B), making it difficult to compare mutants. The authors could carry out additional biological replicates and run all MTT assay trials in the same experiment to account for this and could confirm the authors' statement that the I239M substitution in HsOrc6 is not detrimental. If these replicates cannot be carried out, the authors could comment on their decision to use technical triplicates. 2. No controls were mentioned for rescue protein expression (p. 9-10 "Methods", Fig. 4), and the number of transgenic lines used per mutant was not stated. The cassette randomly integrates into the genome, meaning expression/integration of the Orc6 mutant genes may vary between lines. The authors could state the number of transgenic lines per mutant used and confirm there are multiple transgenic lines for each, then quantify both expression rates and protein concentration using RT-qPCR and total GFP fluorescence, respectively, to allow for better one-to-one comparisons between mutants. 3. Numeric per-genotype rescue counts of Orc6 mutants and ratios are not provided (p. 4-6, 10, Fig. 2-3). Instead, the authors state that rescue efficiency ranged from 10-30% and do not state whether this range is an arbitrary cutoff for being rescued or rather was the range of rescue efficiencies seen throughout all mutants. Providing raw rescue counts and expected number of rescues for each mutant along with a chi-squared test would offer a more robust viability comparison between mutants. 4. Some immunoblots are too washed out to distinguish weak signals from background (Fig. 4A: Orc6HsR237A E241A), several panels appear to be oversaturated (Fig. 4A-4C), and others have large imaging differences between the GFP-Orc6 and Orc5 blots (Fig. 4D, 4E). These irregularities may explain the divergence of the ORC association results amongst
title: PREreview of "Metazoan Orc6 Proteins Evolved Alternative Mechanisms for Association with the ORC Complex: Insights from Drosophila Modeling"

summary: Task-based AI scenarios can map automation into productive capacity, factor shares, wages, and labor reallocation without uniquely determining current expenditure or realized activity when income shifts sharply across households and factors. This paper develops an empirically disciplined closure diagnostic for the 2030 scenarios in Korinek and others (2026). A corrected accounting decomposition shows that, in their Extreme scenario, aggregate labor income is almost unchanged relative to no AI even though cognitive labor income falls sharply, because gains to other workers nearly offset the loss. Using observed ranges for the transmission of persistent income shocks, cash-spending responses, recent corporate payout ratios, Federal Reserve ownership data, and household leverage benchmarks, I report deterministic rather than probabilistic sensitivity sets. The first-round current-consumption response relative to no AI is positive in the Modest scenario but not sign-identified in the Extreme scenario. Holding AI output fixed, however, the shift from labor to capital robustly lowers current consumption within the calibrated envelope. A minimal goods-market closure shows why investment, monetary policy, and external demand are necessary to translate either result into output. The central conclusion is therefore about identification: a task model can identify a production frontier without identifying the macroeconomic path used to reach it. The replication package (code, input tables, outputs, figures) reproduces all reported quantitative results: run python code/01_empirical_closure.py and python code/checks.py.
title: Closing the Loop: Distribution, Consumption, and Macroeconomic Closure under Transformative AI

summary: Toda táctica del manejo integrado de plagas y enfermedades (MIP) cuesta algo cada semana —mano de obra, producto, recorrido del lote— menos una: la que se decidió antes de sembrar. Este artículo examina la resistencia varietal como fundamento del sistema, con las magnitudes medidas en campo y sus condiciones impresas. En Yunnan, China, entre 1998 y 1999, las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes —material convencional, sin modificación transgénica— presentaron una severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor que en monocultivo, a escala de miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios, y los agricultores abandonaron el fungicida contra esa enfermedad (Zhu et al., 2000). Ese caso sostiene el titular: es resistencia disponible, sembrable y medida a escala de paisaje. El contraste opuesto lo aporta el banano frente a la marchitez por *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* raza tropical 4 (Foc TR4): en el ensayo australiano de cinco ciclos, la incidencia acumulada fue de 84 % en el testigo 'Williams' y de 66 % en 'Grand Nain', frente a 2 % en la línea QCAV-4 portadora del gen *MamRGA2* (Harding et al., 2025). Su estatuto es el contrario: QCAV-4 es un banano transgénico aprobado solo en Australia y no es sembrable hoy en Colombia; se cita como evidencia de cuánto puede valer una resistencia cuando existe, no como material disponible para el productor colombiano. Entre ambos extremos, el artículo recorre la durabilidad —que se mide en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva y depende del fondo del paisaje, no de la ficha del cultivar—, el material limpio como decisión separada de la genética, y el injerto como forma de trasplantar la resistencia en tomate. La resistencia es la primera línea porque es la única decisión irreversible dentro del ciclo, y por eso mismo es la que más verificación exige antes de comprar. **Palabras clave:** resistencia varietal; mezclas de cultivares; añublo del arroz; *Magnaporthe oryzae*; Foc TR4; QCAV-4; durabilidad de la resistencia; material limpio; manejo integrado de plagas ## 1. Introducción: la decisión que se toma antes de que exista el problema Hay una decisión de manejo integrado que se toma antes de que el cultivo exista: la elección del material que se siembra. Cuando el productor compra semilla, encarga estacas, aparta tubérculos de su propia cosecha o contrata plántulas de vivero, ya decidió —aunque no lo sepa— qué fracción de la presión de plagas y enfermedades enfrentará el lote durante todo el ciclo. Ninguna aplicación posterior devuelve lo que se perdió por sembrar susceptible en un suelo con historia del patógeno. Esa anterioridad le da una propiedad que ninguna otra táctica tiene en el mismo grado: trabaja gratis toda la temporada, sin recorrido ni aplicación, desde la emergencia hasta la cosecha. Y comparte una segunda propiedad, menos amable: es irreversible dentro del ciclo. Si el monitoreo falla, se corrige la semana siguiente; si el material sembrado era el equivocado, el error dura lo que dura el cultivo —en perennes, años—. La tesis es medible, no retórica: donde se ha comparado material resistente contra susceptible, la diferencia típica es de decenas de puntos porcentuales de incidencia, y a veces equivale a eliminar una línea entera de gasto —el fungicida que deja de aplicarse—. Pero sería deshonesto quedarse en la celebración: el material vegetal es también el terreno de las promesas más frágiles de la sanidad tropical —tolerancias que se quiebran al tercer ciclo, resistencias que el patógeno rodea con razas nuevas, materiales «resistentes» que llegan infectados con otra enfermedad y resistencias enormes que existen únicamente como transgénico aprobado en otro continente—. Las dos caras se imprimen aquí con el mismo tamaño de letra. ## 2. si el material sembrado era el equivocado
el error dura lo que dura el cultivo —en perennes
no retórica: donde se ha comparado material resistente contra susceptible
la diferencia típica es de decenas de puntos porcentuales de incidencia

y a veces equivale a eliminar una línea entera de gasto —el fungicida que deja de aplicarse—. Pero sería deshonesto quedarse en la celebración: el material vegetal es también el terreno de las promesas más frágiles de la sanidad tropical —tolerancias que se quiebran al tercer ciclo
resistencias que el patógeno rodea con razas nuevas

materiales «resistentes» que llegan infectados con otra enfermedad y resistencias enormes que existen únicamente como transgénico aprobado en otro continente—. Las dos caras se imprimen aquí con el mismo tamaño de letra.

## 2. Tres decisiones distintas bajo una misma palabra

En el lenguaje de finca
«buen material» mezcla tres cosas que la evidencia separa

porque cada una falla y se verifica de una manera distinta.

La primera decisión es **genética**: sembrar un genotipo que resiste o tolera al organismo dañino. Resistencia y tolerancia no son sinónimos: la resistencia reduce la infección o el desarrollo del patógeno —o la alimentación y reproducción de la plaga—
la tolerancia permite que el organismo esté presente pero limita el daño en el rendimiento. Un material tolerante puede verse enfermo y rendir bien
y uno con resistencia parcial puede verse limpio en un año de baja presión y colapsar en uno de alta. Importa también distinguir la resistencia de uno o pocos genes de efecto mayor —potente
pero expuesta a que una sola mutación del patógeno la vuelva inútil— de la cuantitativa
repartida en muchos genes de efecto menor
menos espectacular y más duradera. Antes de aceptar la palabra «resistente» hay que preguntar resistente a qué

durante cuántos ciclos y contra qué población del patógeno.

La segunda decisión es **sanitaria**: sembrar material limpio
libre —o tan libre como el sistema permite— de los patógenos que viajan dentro de la semilla
el tubérculo o la plántula. En cultivos de propagación vegetativa —yuca
batata— pesa tanto como la genética
porque el material de siembra es el vehículo principal de virus
bacterias y hongos sistémicos: un genotipo excelente con estacas infectadas es un programa condenado desde el primer día

como demuestra la sección 7.

La tercera decisión es **de arquitectura**: injertar la variedad productiva sobre un portainjerto que aporta la resistencia que la variedad no tiene
típicamente contra patógenos del suelo. El injerto no crea resistencia nueva
y su costo es operativo: vivero capaz

mano de obra entrenada y un portainjerto probado bajo condiciones locales. Las tres decisiones se compran y se verifican por separado.

## 3. Yunnan: la mezcla que llevó el titular

El ensayo de Yunnan sigue siendo la demostración más grande de que la composición genética del lote es una variable de manejo. Las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*

sin. *Pyricularia oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes presentaron una **severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor** que en monocultivo. El efecto no se quedó en parcelas: se mantuvo al escalar a miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios de Yunnan
y su consecuencia práctica fue que los agricultores abandonaron la aplicación de fungicida contra el añublo (Zhu et al.
2000). La fuente es primaria y leída con sus condiciones: es la magnitud mejor sostenida de este artículo

y por eso lleva el titular.

Tres precisiones gobiernan su lectura. La primera es la naturaleza del material: variedades convencionales
obtenidas por mejoramiento clásico y combinadas por diseño de siembra

nada en Yunnan exige aprobación transgénica ni espera regulatoria —la táctica estaba disponible en la misma temporada en que se midió—. La segunda es el mecanismo: la resistencia funcionó mejor repartida en mezcla que concentrada
porque la mezcla reduce a la vez la densidad de tejido susceptible y la velocidad de propagación entre plantas
la unidad de la táctica no fue el gen aislado sino la composición del lote. La tercera es económica: el ahorro no fue un porcentaje de una aplicación
y su comparación correcta es contra la suma de todas las temporadas en que la mezcla siga funcionando —lo que depende de la durabilidad

el tema de la sección 6—.

El caso enseña además qué significa que una resistencia sea «disponible»: que el material existe
que su uso es legal donde se siembra
que el productor puede obtenerlo y que su efecto fue medido en condiciones comparables. Yunnan cumple las cuatro
el banano cumple la última con la mayor magnitud de este artículo

para Colombia— las tres primeras.

## 4. La resistencia a escala de país: el contraste de la roya del café

Entre la parcela y el paisaje hay un punto intermedio: el país. En Colombia
la roya del café (*Hemileia vastatrix*) separa con nitidez los dos mundos de este artículo: **incidencia de 20 % o más en variedades susceptibles frente a 6 % o menos en resistentes**
con pérdidas de 30 a 80 % en las susceptibles cuando el manejo no compensa la susceptibilidad

y más de 84 % del área cafetera nacional sembrada ya con variedades resistentes. La clase de evidencia se imprime con la cifra: es una fuente institucional —la Federación Nacional de Cafeteros de Colombia y Cenicafé—
cuya fuerza es la escala de observación
se lee como balance nacional sostenido
no como comparación experimental entre parcelas

y se cita como magnitud de contexto dentro del tema de la resistencia.

El dato cumple dos funciones: confirma el orden de magnitud —decenas de puntos de incidencia y pérdidas de un tercio a cuatro quintos de la cosecha en el material equivocado— y advierte: la misma fuente reporta seis razas nuevas de roya y nueve variantes más virulentas recientes. La resistencia cafetera colombiana es un éxito en vigilancia permanente

no un problema archivado.

## 5. TR4 del banano: la magnitud mayor y la vía que hoy no está disponible

Frente a la marchitez por *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* raza tropical 4 (Foc TR4)
el ensayo de campo más largo publicado —cinco ciclos
de planta madre a cuarto rebrote

en el Territorio del Norte de Australia— comparó testigos Cavendish susceptibles con líneas portadoras del gen *MamRGA2*. La incidencia acumulada fue de **66 % en el testigo 'Grand Nain' y de 84 % en 'Williams'
frente a un rango de 2 % —la línea QCAV-4— a 36 % en las líneas con el gen** (Harding et al.
2025). La fuente es primaria y abierta
con testigo susceptible en el mismo campo y los mismos ciclos: con testigos en 66 % y 84 %
el 2 % de QCAV-4 es interpretable como lo que es

la separación entre un lote condenado y un lote viable.

Y aquí el marco obligatorio
impreso sin rebaja: **QCAV-4 es un banano genéticamente modificado
aprobado para producción comercial y consumo solo en Australia. No es sembrable hoy en Colombia.** Para el productor colombiano de banano o de plátano

esta resistencia no existe como opción de siembra: no hay material que comprar ni registro que lo ampare. Por eso la arquitectura de este artículo es deliberada: la mitad del titular —la táctica que el lector sí puede ejecutar— la lleva el arroz de Yunnan
con variedad convencional y mezcla de cultivares
la mitad del TR4 se enmarca como lo contrario

la demostración de cuánto vale la vía transgénica y la constatación de que esa vía hoy no está disponible para el productor colombiano. Citar el 2 % como evidencia de la magnitud del efecto «resistencia» es legítimo

## 6. La durabilidad: hectáreas-año

no ficha de cultivar

Si el artículo terminara en la tabla anterior

el lector saldría con una regla simple y falsa: «siembre resistente y el problema queda resuelto». La evidencia obliga a examinar cómo y por qué la resistencia deja de funcionar.

La unidad honesta de la durabilidad no es el año calendario ni la frase «resistencia durable» de un catálogo: es la **hectárea-año de protección efectiva** —cada hectárea sembrada con el material
multiplicada por cada año en que la protección se mantiene bajo presión real—. Leída así
la durabilidad **no es una propiedad de la ficha del cultivar: depende del fondo del paisaje** —de cuánta superficie comparte el mismo genotipo
de cómo se mueve el inóculo entre fincas y regiones—. La mezcla de Yunnan es

una tecnología de durabilidad además de una de control: repartir la resistencia baja la severidad de la temporada y reduce la recompensa que el patógeno obtiene por adaptarse a cualquiera de los genotipos.

El primer mecanismo de quiebre es la **evolución del patógeno**: un genotipo resistente en grandes extensiones ejerce la selección más intensa posible

y sobreviven las variantes capaces de atacarlo. Las seis razas nuevas y las nueve variantes más virulentas de roya reportadas en Colombia son la respuesta esperable del hongo a décadas de resistencia desplegada. La consecuencia de manejo: toda resistencia se siembra junto con su plan de quiebre —diversidad de genotipos

vigilancia de la incidencia en el material «resistente» como alarma temprana y ruta de reemplazo pensada antes de necesitarla—.

El segundo mecanismo no requiere evolución alguna: **la tolerancia anunciada que nunca fue lo que el ensayo corto sugería**. El caso de advertencia permanente es la variante somaclonal GCTCV-218

desplegada en Filipinas como Cavendish tolerante a Foc TR4. Su estatuto de evidencia debe quedar impreso: las cifras favorables que circulan provienen de páginas comerciales y de literatura secundaria
sin fuente primaria abierta que las respalde en la búsqueda verificada del libro fuente
y por tanto no se imprimen aquí como magnitud. Lo que sí está verificado es lo contrario de la promesa: en el ensayo extendido de tres años discutido por Harding et al. (2025)
2025). Había mostrado resistencia moderada en planta madre y primer rebrote

la protección se desvaneció.

La regla de interpretación vale para todo el artículo: **una tolerancia medida en uno o dos ciclos es una compra de tiempo
y debe planearse como tal —monitoreo ciclo a ciclo
el lote tolerante como activo que se deprecia
y sin desmontar las demás capas del programa—. Quien siembra un tolerante sabiendo que compra tiempo decide legítimamente

quien lo siembra creyendo que compró inmunidad ha sido engañado por la propaganda.

El tercer límite no es quiebre sino **ausencia**: frente al rayado pardo de la yuca (CBSD)
la fuente primaria más reciente declara que no existe ninguna variedad con resistencia duradera (Casinga et al.
2025). Donde la genética no ofrece la herramienta
el programa se construye con las demás —material limpio
manejo del vector y roguing—: el hueco declarado orienta el esfuerzo

la resistencia imaginaria lo desperdicia.

## 7. Material limpio: la decisión que la resistencia no reemplaza

En los cultivos de propagación vegetativa
la pregunta «¿de dónde salió este material?» vale tanto como «¿qué genotipo es?»: los virus
las bacterias sistémicas y algunos hongos viajan dentro de la estaca

y el material de siembra es a la vez primera víctima y primer vehículo. La degeneración de la semilla vegetativa —la acumulación de infecciones cuando el productor resiembra su propio material— es el proceso que la estrategia integrada de salud de semilla busca interrumpir con tres componentes que no se sustituyen entre sí: resistencia varietal
manejo en finca y reemplazo estratégico de los lotes (Thomas-Sharma et al.
derrotada por la estaca.** El ensayo de Kabare
en Kivu del Sur (República Democrática del Congo)
sembró dos variedades resistentes al mosaico —'Nabana' (MM 96/4653) y 'Sawasawa' (MM 96/3920)— con estacas sanas y con estacas infectadas por los virus del rayado pardo. Con estacas infectadas
el rendimiento de raíz fresca cayó **44 % a los 9 meses y 86 % a los 12 meses en 'Nabana'
frente a las mismas variedades con estacas sanas
mientras el material sano rindió 5 % más a los 12 meses que a los 9
2025). La resistencia al mosaico era real en ambas parcelas
porque el problema venía dentro de la estaca y era otra enfermedad —una frente a la cual
no existe resistencia duradera: en ese patosistema el material limpio es

casi toda la estrategia disponible—.

**Papa: la selección positiva como tecnología sin laboratorio.** Donde no hay semilla certificada al alcance
la herramienta verificada es marcar en el ciclo anterior las plantas sanas y vigorosas y cosechar de ellas —y solo de ellas— la semilla siguiente. En Uganda
a lo largo de tres generaciones
la selección positiva redujo la incidencia de virus (PVY
PLRV y otros) generación tras generación frente a la selección habitual y la aleatoria
porque al PLRV la literatura le atribuye reducciones de rendimiento de hasta 90 % (*Potato Research*
el análisis por ELISA dio la fotografía complementaria: en los lotes de selección positiva no se detectaron PVY
mientras en los de selección aleatoria se detectaron PVS en 78 %
PLRV en 16 % y PVM en 9 % de los tubérculos (Okeyo et al.
2018). La selección positiva no esteriliza un lote infectado

es frenar la degeneración y ganar ciclos de semilla aceptable.

El criterio práctico es uno solo: **«limpio» y «resistente» se compran por separado y se verifican por separado** —con certificación formal donde existe

renovación periódica y la disciplina de no sembrar jamás material de un lote con síntomas sistémicos visibles—.

## 8. Injertos y portainjertos: trasplantar la resistencia

Hay cultivos en los que la variedad que el mercado quiere no es la que el suelo permite. El injerto separa los dos trabajos: la copa produce lo que se vende y el portainjerto enfrenta lo que el suelo trae. La evidencia tropical más sólida está en tomate contra la marchitez bacteriana (*Ralstonia solanacearum*)

replicada en tres países con el mismo patrón.

En Benín (Abomey-Calavi y Sékou)

el informe técnico del World Vegetable Center comparó la variedad 'Tounvi' autoinjertada —el testigo sin portainjerto resistente— contra la misma variedad sobre dos portainjertos. La incidencia del testigo fue de **65
el rendimiento del injertado fue aproximadamente tres veces el del testigo (Zohoungbogbo et al.
los portainjertos 'EG203' —de berenjena— y 'Hawaii 7796' redujeron la marchitez en **49
0 %** en promedio y mejoraron el rendimiento en **57
injerto con riego reducido llevó la reducción a **76 %** en promedio
6 veces el del testigo (Msabila et al.
el injerto sobre berenjena suprimió la incidencia en más de 20 % y aumentó el rendimiento de dos cultivares en 30 % (*Sustainability*

con menor detalle en la fuente disponible.

Tres lecturas se imponen. La magnitud: pasar de 65–82 % de plantas marchitas a 0–10 % es la diferencia entre un cultivo inviable y uno comercial. La condición: el efecto depende del portainjerto y del sitio —la regla no es «injerte» sino «injerte sobre el portainjerto que haya demostrado resistencia bajo presión comparable a la de su suelo»—. Y el costo oculto: el injerto exige vivero con capacidad técnica y disciplina sanitaria. Queda una advertencia declarada: la rentabilidad comparada del injerto para el pequeño productor no está medida en la literatura abierta
el rendimiento tres veces mayor la sugiere

pero «sugiere» no es «mide».

## 9. Verificar antes de comprar: el interrogatorio del material

Entre la evidencia y la finca hay un mostrador: el del proveedor de semilla

el vivero o el vecino que vende estacas. La mayoría de las decisiones malas de material se toman aceptando en ese mostrador palabras sin precisiones. El interrogatorio que sigue las convierte en preguntas aplicables a cualquier oferta de material «resistente»
exactamente?** La respuesta aceptable nombra el organismo y

es un adjetivo publicitario. Segunda: **¿medido dónde y contra qué testigo?** Una incidencia de 5 % no significa nada sin el testigo susceptible en el mismo ensayo: el dato de TR4 es interpretable porque 'Grand Nain' y 'Williams' marcaron 66 % y 84 % en el mismo campo y los mismos ciclos (Harding et al.
2025). Tercera: **¿durante cuántos ciclos?** Es la pregunta que desarma el caso 'Formosana': en perennes
una resistencia sin al menos tres ciclos bajo presión real es una hipótesis. Cuarta: **¿qué pasa cuando se quiebre?** Genotipos alternos
lo inválido no es el material sino la dependencia exclusiva de él. Y quinta
para material de origen biotecnológico: **¿su uso está aprobado donde yo siembro?** —la pregunta que separa a QCAV-4

de cualquier cultivar convencional—.

Para el material limpio se verifica la procedencia
no el genotipo: ¿de qué lote madre salió —en selección positiva bien hecha
de plantas marcadas como sanas el ciclo anterior—?

¿el lote madre tenía síntomas? —un lote cosechado en un campo con síntomas sistémicos no se «mejora» eligiendo los órganos de mejor aspecto: el ensayo keniano encontró PVS en 78 % de los tubérculos de selección aleatoria (Okeyo et al.
la verificación es del proceso: portainjerto con nombre y respaldo local —'Hawaii7996' y 'Padma F1' en Benín
2024)— y un vivero capaz de mostrar su disciplina sanitaria: sin desinfección

el vivero se convierte en distribuidor del patógeno que el injerto pretendía evitar.

## 10. Conclusiones: la regla de la primera línea

La primera decisión fitosanitaria del programa es el material
antes de sembrar: (1) el genotipo —resistente o tolerante al problema dominante del lote
(2) el estado sanitario —limpio por certificación o por selección positiva verificada—
y (3) la arquitectura —injerto sobre portainjerto demostrado donde un patógeno del suelo limita el cultivo y existe vivero capaz—. Si alguna falla
el programa se rediseña alrededor de ese límite antes de sembrar

no después.

Las magnitudes quedan con sus condiciones y su estatuto. Yunnan —94 % menos severidad
miles de hectáreas en 1998–1999— es evidencia primaria de una táctica convencional y ejecutable. La roya del café —20 % o más frente a 6 % o menos

con fuente institucional— confirma el orden de magnitud y la obligación de vigilar. El TR4 —84 % en 'Williams' y 66 % en 'Grand Nain' frente a 2 % en QCAV-4— mide el techo de una resistencia y delimita la vía transgénica hoy no disponible en Colombia: QCAV-4 está aprobado solo en Australia. Y la durabilidad no se lee en la ficha del cultivar sino en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva sobre el fondo del paisaje.

Tres huecos delimitan la regla: no existe variedad de yuca con resistencia duradera al rayado pardo
las cifras favorables de los somaclonales tipo 'Formosana' carecen de verificación en fuente primaria abierta —solo está verificado su colapso en ensayo largo—
y la rentabilidad del injerto para el pequeño productor no está medida en serie abierta. Los huecos no debilitan la regla: la delimitan
que es lo que distingue una regla de decisión de un eslogan. Sembrar resistente sigue siendo la única táctica que trabaja gratis toda la temporada —siempre que lo sembrado sea

limpio y sembrable donde se siembra—.

summary: Data and code from the second case of a larger study, within the project Disrupting Digital Monolingualism 2 (DDM2), on the state of language metadata in Spanish and Latin American research infrastructures. The study follows language metadata along the Spanish open access aggregation chain: repositories and journals → RECOLECTA, the national aggregator operated by FECYT with REBIUN (225 registered resources) → the Spanish node ( ES ) of LA Referencia (1,478,369 records). It asks where language metadata are declared, transformed and lost, and with what effects on Spain's co-official languages (Catalan/Valencian, Galician, Basque, Aranese) and on Asturian. The deposit includes the RECOLECTA list of resources and endpoints; an OAI-PMH harvest at origin (34,186 records from 111 resources, in oai_dc and oai_openaire ); counts of records with and without language for each of the 96 repositories in the Spanish node, with their language facets; a repository-level contrast between levels; resources absent from LA Referencia; the language facet of the RECOLECTA portal and the provenance of its labels; and tests of selection by resource type. The study is exploratory. Samples were designed for exploration rather than estimation, and the data describe a single snapshot of live systems taken on 11 November 2026. The cases documented illustrate what can happen to language metadata along an aggregation chain; they are not general or causal claims about the infrastructures, institutions or repositories involved. See README.md and codebook.md for sources, method, files and limitations. Data: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.
title: Language metadata in RECOLECTA and the Spanish node of LA Referencia: Snapshot, 11 November 2026

summary: Capital markets open and close windows capriciously, and an issuer who must act once, irreversibly, has a different problem from a trader who may act continuously. This paper formalises an instrument built to decide the first problem: an admission clock that states, at any date, whether the window for placing a new instrument is open, how far open, and what dose that grade permits. The instrument is a conjunction of three gates — internal readiness, market regime, and a veto list — and not a weighted index, a design choice we defend on the ground that averaging allows an open gate to compensate a closed one, which is precisely the error an irreversible act cannot absorb. The regime gate is driven by a latent-factor engine whose identification rests on a point we believe has been underweighted in practice: an index assembled exclusively from indicators endogenous to the crypto market measures a single factor that is itself a transformation of the price level, and therefore carries no information about the future willingness of capital to finance an unseasoned instrument. We show that the primary equity issuance market supplies an exogenous and leading measurement of that same latent variable, and that the relevant measurement is the count and receptivity of small deals rather than aggregate proceeds — a distinction the 2026 data make vivid, with record United States proceeds accompanied by a thirty-four per cent fall in the number of deals priced. The paper's technical core converts the tacit knowledge of a daily operator into testable propositions. We obtain three results worth isolating. First, under a margin buffer set proportionally to the prevailing volatility level, the probability that a carry position breaches its buffer is exactly invariant to the level of volatility and depends, to second order, only on the volatility of volatility; the dependence is strictly increasing when the buffer exceeds √2 standard deviations and reverses below it. This gives the lockability gate a defensible threshold variable and explains why a carry bid withdraws in unstable markets without any change in the mean level of risk. Second, the rotation cascade that carries capital from bitcoin outward to the market's tail is asymmetric in its lag structure, not merely in sign: in expansion it propagates head-to-tail with a positive and tier-increasing lag, which is what makes it exploitable and what gives an issuer warning; in contraction it propagates at lag zero with amplification greater than one, which gives no warning and dries the tail first. Third, the equity of a company holding a leveraged bitcoin treasury is not a levered claim on bitcoin but a levered claim on the regime factor, with elasticity β = λ (1 + ε _m) decomposing into a balance-sheet channel and a premium-elasticity channel, both of which reverse sign together; the accretion identity Δ q/q = ( Δ V/SN)(1 − 1/m) shows the issuance loop inverting exactly at a multiple of one, which the 2025–2026 compression of these multiples and the observable conversion of such companies from net buyers into net sellers appear to bear out. A fourth result was added in this version and is negative. The whole architecture presupposes that the admission window is exogenous — that assent must be obtained from a party the issuer does not control. Where the issuer can operate its own venue, the predicate degenerates into a preference, and three identities follow: in a constant-product pool the marginal price is the ratio of seeded reserves, so the opening price is declared rather than discovered; slippage depends on the fraction of the pool reserve transacted and not on circulating float, so depth decouples from the float arithmetic; and the liquidity position is concave in price, so the issuer who seeds his own pool writes a continuous strip of options on his own instrument — the precise arrangement the dose parameters
title: Timing the Window: A gated regime engine for issuance and rotation in crypto-asset markets — architecture, calibration from operator heuristics, and conditional derivations for cascade rotation and treasury-levered equity exposure

summary: The ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo community benchmark for discriminating physiological from non-physiological protein–protein interfaces (Schweke et al., Proteomics 2023) contains 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 PDB entries. We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The benchmark is described with Bioschemas/schema.org JSON-LD: every interface is annotated with its label, chains, structural features, sequence-cluster assignment, provenance and licence, and linked to the PDB structure files and to snapshots of the RCSB PDB metadata. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the source repository, and the errors found were corrected. A lightweight design removed the need for Git LFS and for duplicated metadata. The post-publication curation of the labels (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces, compared with 836 and 841 in the publication) is documented, and three entries superseded in the PDB are linked to their replacements. A reference machine-learning script with cluster-aware cross-validation is included. Data, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, with full attribution to the original work.
title: FAIRification of the ELIXIR 3D-Bioinfo Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark

summary: SparkEviTune v1.0.1 — SoftwareX Corrective Release SparkEviTune is an evidence-aware, human-controlled software framework for Apache Spark configuration guidance. It combines deterministic configuration rules, Spark event-log analysis, optional machine-learning components subject to data-readiness gates, constrained optimization, and optional explanations. Version 1.0.1 incorporates software corrections prepared during the SoftwareX major revision, including: Improved FastAPI workload input-row handling. Profile Guard validation and associated regression tests. ModelRegistry multiprocessing-related corrections and targeted tests. Updates to dashboard, detection, machine-learning, pipeline, and validation components. Software verification The corrective release passed 61 automated tests under Windows Python 3.12 and Python 3.14. Ruff checks passed in both environments, and dependency consistency checks passed under Python 3.12. These checks establish correctness only within the tested scope and do not demonstrate general multi-worker deployment correctness or unrestricted concurrency safety. Scientific evidence and limitations Historical Spark benchmark results remain associated with their original experimental implementations and execution environments. The historical publication corpus comprises 81 clean runs covering 16 distinct scenarios, below the 20-scenario threshold required for publication-model training. A separate retrospective audit of 90 Learning01 executions found agreement for 90/90 event-log-derived durations, successful completion of 342/342 Spark jobs, and no mismatches across 1,128 shared configuration-property comparisons. Independent duration prediction yielded MAE = 8.9637 s and R² = -0.0621. General predictive accuracy or universal performance improvement is therefore not claimed. Historical Table 3 reconstruction remains incomplete. The A-03 LZ4 provenance and A-04 acceptance-criterion traceability issues remain unresolved. AQE-01 and Lot C experiments are not claimed as validated. SparkEviTune does not automatically apply proposed configurations. Users must review and benchmark recommendations before deployment. Software provenance Version: 1.0.1 Release date: 2026-11-16 Git commit: 65c207197cd75ad095a40555f697e06920bafb24 Repository: https://github.com/morocco-architect/SparkEviTune_v1.0.0 Release: https://github.com/morocco-architect/SparkEviTune_v1.0.0/releases/tag/v1.0.1 License: MIT The historical v1.0.0 release remains unchanged. This archive represents the corrective software version and does not constitute a new experimental benchmark dataset.

summary: The ELIXIR Single Cell Omics community benchmark experiment 1 (BE1; Arigoni et al., Scientific Data 2024) is a 10x Genomics single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset that provides a controlled heterogeneous environment: seven lung cancer cell lines characterised by seven different driver genes, together with a PBMC population, were multiplexed with CellPlex oligonucleotides and sequenced. The data comprise 29,128 cells from the cell lines and 478 PBMC (GEO series GSE243665). We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The experiment is described with the Single Cell Schema (version 0.4), in a machine-readable file that validates against the schema and links the samples, libraries, sequencing and processing steps to the public identifiers of GEO, SRA, BioProject and figshare. A query tool retrieves expression profiles from the public count matrices. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the public records, and the errors found, among them a wrong article DOI, wrong cell counts, an incorrect creator record and unsupported statements, were corrected. Metadata, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub, with full attribution to the original work.

summary: DMDO DMDO (Distributed Multidisciplinary Design Optimization) solves coupled, multidisciplinary engineering design problems by decomposing them into subproblems, one per discipline, and coordinating them with nonhierarchical analytical target cascading (NHATC). Documentation, theory, tutorials and benchmarks:  ahmed-bayoumy.github.io/DMDO Version 2612.0 Why DMDO Design the whole system, let every discipline keep its own tools.  Aircraft, vehicles, turbines and energy systems are designed by teams that each own an analysis: aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, controls, cost. Optimizing them as one monolithic problem needs a multidisciplinary analysis that converges at every design point, one optimizer that suits every discipline, and every code in one process. DMDO needs none of that. No converged multidisciplinary analysis.  Each subproblem keeps its own copies of the variables it shares with the others, and an augmented Lagrangian coordinator drives the copies to agreement. Coupled analyses never have to be iterated to convergence inside the optimizer. Measured on the classic MDO benchmarks.  On the Sellar problem with derivative-free MADS subproblems, DMDO reaches  f = 3.2042, 0.65 % from the best known solution 3.18339  [3], with the disciplines consistent to  1.3 × 10⁻⁶ . In all six recorded benchmark runs (Sellar, Golinski's speed reducer, a geometric program and a basic two-discipline problem), the inconsistency between disciplines falls  below 10⁻³ within 6 to 16 outer iterations . The right optimizer for each discipline.  A subproblem built on a noisy or failing simulation uses derivative-free Mesh Adaptive Direct Search ( OMADS ); a smooth analytical one uses SciPy's SLSQP, in the same run. Any other optimizer plugs in as a small strategy class. Serial, parallel or distributed, with the same answer.  Solve the subproblems one after the other (Gauss–Seidel) or all at once (Jacobi), in-process, in a pool of worker processes, or on remote machines. Jacobi results do not depend on which worker finishes first: the test suite checks that in-process, out-of-order, process-pool and remote runs give bit-identical designs. An API, not just a script.  Build a problem from YAML, a dictionary or Python objects, then  run()  it, drive it one outer iteration at a time with  step() , or solve the subproblems yourself with  ask() / tell() . Observers stream progress, registries and entry points add solvers, executors and analyses, and an optional HTTP service exposes runs to any language. Results you can reproduce.  Runs are seeded; every benchmark run is checked against a recorded history that the code must reproduce bit for bit; interrupted runs resume from their checkpoint to exactly the same result; the test suite runs on Linux, Windows and macOS in continuous integration.   Maximum inconsistency between the copies held by different subproblems, at each outer iteration of the six recorded benchmark runs. Details in the  benchmarking documentation . summary: The PlanckPlay is a 3D-printed representation of the 16 three-dimensional tetrahedra that make up the Planck’s Hexadecachoron—a metamodel (model of models) of physics. Mathematically, a hexadecachoron is the four-dimensional polytope dual to the hypercube, or tesseract. Just as the tetrahedron and cube are three-dimensional Platonic solids, the hexadecachoron and tesseract are their four-dimensional analogues. The hexadecachoron is composed of 16 regular tetrahedra in four-dimensional space. When projected into three dimensions, these tetrahedra appear distorted—much like how the square faces of a cube are distorted in a two-dimensional drawing. PlanckPlay was developed within the Hypercube of Physics (HoP) project, part of the Cluster of Excellence Matters of Activity. In HoP, we explore models that classify physical theories in relation to the four fundamental physical constants: Newton's gravitational constant (G), the inverse speed of light (c -1 ), Planck’s constant (h), and the Boltzmann constant (k B ). In 1899, Max Planck used these constants to define natural units for length, time, mass, and temperature—foundational to modern physics. Within the HoP consortium, we envision PlanckPlay as both a research object and an educational tool, harnessing its gamified structure to make abstract physical concepts tangible and engaging.
title: PlanckPlay - Planck's Hexadecachoron Puzzle

summary: In formal verification, systems engineering, and institutional press releases, authors frequently mask missing causal proofs or physical bottlenecks behind fluent mathematical or technical phrasing—a practice termed semantic smoothing. Evaluating any paper, benchmark, or policy claim at face value wastes cognitive cycles on surface rhetoric (I) before checking whether the underlying physical or logical conservation ledger (C) actually balances.
title: Semantic-Smoothing Tripwires: Pre-Evaluating Proofs, Benchmarks, and Technical Claims

STARLI · MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE FAMILY 09 | PHYSICS OF HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION F041-F045 / Scientific Technical Notebook / Research Working Edition v1.0 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜;讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. THIS NOTEBOOK DOES NOT REPORT HUMAN RESEARCH RESULTS. All figures are deterministic synthetic models; no claim of qigong-specific energy, quantum entanglement, or clinical efficacy is established. Five-flagship genealogy and independent endpoints F041 | Human Infrared Emission Spectra and Skin Temperature at the Limit Native endpoint: infrared spectral radiance residual [W/(m2 sr um)]; strong baseline: rest-matched condition; primary conventional rival: ambient reflection and detector gain. Core physical account: band-resolved Planck radiance with emissivity and reflected apparent temperature. Independent witness: a temperature-stabilized blackbody in the same optical path. The required handoff is to transfer the cavity calibration, spectral response function and radiance covariance matrix. F042 | Pre-Post Qigong Thermal Mapping and Environmental Correction at the Limit Native endpoint: ambient-corrected thermal-map change [K]; strong baseline: movement- and breathing-matched condition; primary conventional rival: airflow, acclimatization and postural shifts. Core physical account: radiative transfer plus convection, evaporation and thermal relaxation. Independent witness: a movement-matched control under the same airflow and camera geometry. The required handoff is to publish raw radiometric frames, registration landmarks and the difference-in-differences estimator. F043 | Human Skin Emissivity and Surface Material Properties at the Limit Native endpoint: skin emissivity residual [dimensionless]; strong baseline: temperature- and moisture-matched reference; primary conventional rival: surface films, humidity and viewing angle. Core physical account: energy conservation at an absorbing, emitting and reflecting boundary. Independent witness: a traceable high-emissivity reference of documented surface treatment. The required handoff is to report bandpass, angular response, film history and covariance between inferred temperature and emissivity. F044 | Palmar Thermal Emission and Local Blood Flow Coupling at the Limit Native endpoint: temperature-perfusion temporal lag [s]; strong baseline: rest and sham-synchronized sensor record; primary conventional rival: probe motion, posture and shared respiratory drive. Core physical account: vascular heat transport convolved with tissue thermal diffusion. Independent witness: a shared-clock perfusion trace plus a motion and respiration record. The required handoff is to release synchronization pulses, surrogate distributions and bilateral negative controls. F045 | Human Thermography and Blinded Image Classification at the Limit Native endpoint: external-site blinded thermography AUC [0-1]; strong baseline: metadata-only and site-heldout classifiers; primary conventional rival: background leakage, identity overlap and domain shift. Core physical account: statistical generalization under a documented distribution shift. Independent witness: an operator- and person-heldout external test with masked class labels. The required handoff is to release split keys, model weights, inference preprocessing, abstention rule and confusion matrices.

summary: This record contains the raw data generated in the computational experiments of the article "EpiBuilder 2.0: A Dockerized and User-Friendly Web Platform for in silico Analysis of Linear B-cell Epitopes" . Source code: https://github.com/labioinfoufsc/EpiBuilder . The data were used to (i) benchmark the processing time of the EpiBuilder 2.0 workflow on CPU and GPU on two different machines, (ii) compare the epitope predictor integrated into EpiBuilder 2.0 (BepiPred v3.0) with an alternative deep-learning predictor (EpiDope v0.3), in processing time and in per-residue concordance, and (iii) carry out the biological evaluation of the predicted linear B-cell epitopes (N-glycosylation filtering, subcellular localization, BLASTp matches against the IEDB and against other proteomes of the same genus). All runs were performed in triplicate . The archive contains only the generated outputs and the shell scripts used to produce them; the input proteomes are public UniProt reference proteomes and are not redistributed. Hardware configurations Machine A (Intel Core i9-14900K @ 6.0 GHz, 80 GB DDR5 6000 MHz): configuration A – CPU only ( machine_A/cpu/ ); A1 – NVIDIA RTX 3080, 10 GB ( machine_A/RTX_3080/ ); A2 – NVIDIA RTX A4500, 20 GB ( machine_A/RTX_A4500/ ). Machine B (Intel Xeon E7-4830 v2 @ 2.20 GHz, 295 GB DDR3 1600 MHz): configuration B – CPU only ( machine_B/cpu/ ). Input proteomes (UniProt, downloaded on 6 November 2026) Influenza B virus B/Lee/1940 – UP000008158 (11 proteins) Zaire ebolavirus – UP000007209 (9 proteins) Borrelia burgdorferi B31 – UP000001807 (1,273 valid proteins) Staphylococcus aureus – UP000008816 (2,888 valid proteins) Candida albicans – UP000000559 (5,977 valid proteins) Software and parameters BepiPred v3.0 (Docker image bioinfoufsc/bepipred3 ), CPU and GPU. EpiDope v0.3 ( flomock/epidope:v0.3 ), CPU only. EpiBuilder 2.0 core workflow in Nextflow ( bioinfoufsc/epibuilder-core ): epitope extraction, physicochemical properties, N-glycosylation, PSORTb v3.0 / WoLF PSORT v0.1, BLASTp v2.17 against the IEDB (~155,279 B-cell epitopes) and reference proteomes of each genus. Parameters: epitope length 10–30 aa; BepiPred v3.0 threshold 0.1512; BLAST minimum identity 90% and minimum query coverage 90%; localization none (viruses), gram_neg ( B. burgdorferi ), gram_pos ( S. aureus ), fungi ( C. albicans ). Contents of EpiBuilder2_experiments.tar.gz scripts/ – experiment_bepipred.sh (BepiPred v3.0, CPU or GPU), experiment_epidope.sh (EpiDope v0.3), experiment.sh (one EpiBuilder 2.0 run) and experiment_triplicate.sh (loop over organisms and replicates). machine_A/ and machine_B/ – one folder per configuration and tool ( bepipred , epidope , epibuilder ), with one subfolder per organism ( INFLUENZA , EBOLA , BORRELIA , STAPHYLOCOCCUS , CANDIDA ) and replicate1 – replicate3 . bepipred/ – FASTA validation output, per-residue scores ( raw_output.csv ), execution logs and wall-clock times ( execution_times.tsv ). epidope/ – per-residue scores ( epidope_scores.csv ), predicted epitopes, per-protein tables and plots, and execution times. epibuilder/ – epitope-level results ( epitope-detail.tsv , epitopes.fasta ), per-protein summary, per-residue scores, subcellular localization, BLASTp hits against the IEDB and each reference proteome, consolidated spreadsheet ( epibuilder.xlsx ) and Nextflow trace, report, timeline and DAG ( reports/ ). Use in the publication CPU vs. GPU processing time of the workflow (configurations A, A1, A2 and B) and comparison between machines: bepipred/*/execution_times.tsv and epibuilder/*/replicateN/reports/trace.txt . BepiPred v3.0 vs. EpiDope v0.3 processing time on CPU: execution_times.tsv of both tools. Per-residue concordance between BepiPred v3.0 and EpiDope v0.3 (Cohen's kappa, Jaccard index, Spearman's rho): raw_output.csv and epidope_scores.csv . Biological evaluation, IEDB matches and cross-species
title: Benchmark data of EpiBuilder 2.0: CPU/GPU performance, BepiPred v3.0 vs. EpiDope v0.3 comparison, and epitope predictions for five pathogen proteomes
