title: River health assessment of the Jacotet River

summary: In PIRLS 2021, fourth-graders in Uzbekistan scored 437 points against a scale centrepoint of 500, and in PISA 2022 only about 14% of fifteen-year-olds reached the baseline level of reading proficiency. These results show that reading literacy has to be built from the primary grades, and the English lesson, which in Uzbekistan begins in Grade 1, is one of the places where this can be done. The article examines explicit reading strategy instruction as a means of developing early reading literacy in English among primary school learners (Grades 2–4). The study combines an integrative review of seven research syntheses on strategy instruction (1994–2021), evidence-based recommendations for comprehension teaching in the primary grades and research on young learners’ strategy use with conceptual modelling. The syntheses report positive effects ranging from very small on standardised tests in whole-class settings (d = 0.19) to large on researcher-developed measures and in second language samples (0.78–0.91); for the primary grades, teaching comprehension strategies through a gradual release of responsibility is supported by strong evidence. On this basis the article proposes a core repertoire of six strategies with child-friendly names and grade-by-grade introduction, a four-phase model of instruction built on picture-supported texts and a “choose – use – check” cycle, and a four-indicator observation rubric for the classroom. Implications for primary English teaching in Uzbekistan and a design for empirical validation are discussed.
tags: early reading literacy; primary school; young EFL learners; explicit strategy instruction; gradual release of responsibility; metacognition; picture-supported reading; classroom assessment
title: DEVELOPING EARLY READING LITERACY IN ENGLISH THROUGH EXPLICIT STRATEGY INSTRUCTION IN PRIMARY SCHOOL

summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.
title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience

summary: Deep-research agents repeatedly decide what to search, read, and verify, often using large cloud-hosted language models for action proposal. However, privacy and local control motivate running agents on users' devices, where limited memory and compute favor smaller models and complicate on-device training. Yet inference-time guidance faces three obstacles: exploring alternatives through real execution adds tool calls, prompted self-evaluation is bounded by the agent's judgment, and model-specific guidance risks repeated adaptation costs. We introduce Seer, an inference-time framework providing local guidance that separates the agent's action proposal from learned consequence prediction and value estimation. From a shared corpus of real research trajectories, we train two models: a tool-response simulator on observed call--response pairs and a value estimator on histories labeled with discounted terminal correctness. The simulator and estimator are trained offline and reused across agents without further training. Moreover, Seer executes only the selected action and adds only real tool responses to the committed history, avoiding tool calls on discarded candidates at additional inference cost. Across multiple deep-research benchmarks, Seer substantially improves agent performance for different language models. For instance, GAIA accuracy rises from 13.6% to 41.7% for Qwen3.5-4B and from 22.3% to 50.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Furthermore, our analyses suggest that broader candidate coverage can compensate for imperfect simulation, while prediction and scoring errors limit the benefits of wider imagined search. These findings highlight the potential of reusable models for prediction and evaluation to strengthen small research agents through extra local computation without the real execution of the discarded candidates.
title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models

summary: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible material state over an unknown number of increments, remain stable when driven recursively by its own predictions, and fit within the memory available at every integration point. Here, a Composites World Model based on a Multi-Modal Spiking Transformer architecture is designed to meet these requirements. The proposed architecture combines a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks the long-term internal state of the material, and transformer blocks that learn the short-term applied strain state. The system is trained in three stages: material architecture encoding, base training on short time windows, and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling to suppress cumulative error drift. The trained model is disassembled at inference and coupled to a non-linear FE solver, enabling structural scale simulation of composites containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experimental results for IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, show that the SNN memory block successfully tracks the material internal state and results in prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.
title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities

summary: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. The benchmark compares predictions with two reference futures from the same prediction initial state, one following the demonstrated rule and the other a common rule, to measure prediction bias toward common dynamics. We further propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which learns how different rules affect object motion, infers the current rule from calibration interactions, and applies it to prediction from a new initial state. RIFT explicitly controls the influence of training frequency on rule inference, allowing sufficiently informative observational evidence to support rare rules. Experiments on TailWorld show that RIFT improves prediction accuracy and physical consistency across varying training imbalances and distribution shifts, with gains in predicting rare dynamics.
title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence

summary: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. They mis-paginate an API, resolve the wrong entity, or answer when no answer was asked. We built a pipeline that lets an agent learn from its own history. It first mines short \emph{lessons} from the agent's own trajectories, one to three per episode. It then consolidates those lessons into a smaller set of \emph{guidelines}, where each guideline records how many lessons it merged. At inference the agent receives either all guidelines or a selected subset. The pipeline ships in the open-source altk-evolve library and is deployed in IBM's CUGA agent and watsonx Orchestrate platform. We report what we learned building, measuring, and productizing it. Our primary instrument is the AppWorld benchmark, across models spanning 40--92\% baseline task completion. The central finding is that the right amount of memory is a property of the model, not the memory. A strong model keeps improving as guidelines are added. DeepSeek-V3.2 gains +9.5 points of task completion and +16.1 points of scenario completion with its full 191-guideline set. A weak model gains less from the same full set than from a small selected subset. gpt-oss-120b starts at 39.9\% task completion. It reaches 51.2\% with all 199 of its guidelines but 55.4\% (mean of two runs) with a selected subset of about 29. Around that result we report what went wrong: a high-support guideline that backfired, provenance silently dropped during consolidation, a swallowed API error that failed every task while producing a plausible log, and a baseline confound that nearly produced a misleading comparison with a prior method. We distill these into recommendations for teams deploying agent memory.
title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents

summary: Irregular multivariate time series forecasting supports healthcare monitoring, environmental analysis, and activity recognition. Channel-independent (CI) approaches capture each variable's temporal patterns but do not explicitly use observations from other variables. Channel-dependent (CD) modeling exploits relationships among variables, yet asynchronous measurements make these relationships difficult to learn. Incorporating cross-variable information while preserving each variable's irregular history therefore remains a key challenge. We propose Temporal-Reference Complementary Forecasting (TRCF), a framework that augments a compact CI forecaster with a complementary CD branch. ANCHOR aggregates observed values and timestamps at shared temporal locations, retaining observation support to form compact CI features. BRIDGE constructs complementary features through history completion. It first estimates each variable's historical values from its own observations, then uses differences between other variables' observed and estimated values at nearby times to correct missing entries. The completed history preserves observed values and is encoded to supply context alongside the direct CI representation. Finally, the two representations are fused, combined with the query-time embedding, and passed to a shallow multilayer perceptron for forecasting. Experiments on four real-world datasets show that TRCF achieves the lowest mean squared error and mean absolute error in the main benchmark comparison, while reducing measured peak inference memory by 17.28% to 87.98% relative to APN.
title: TRCF: Temporal-Reference Complementary Forecasting for Irregular Multivariate Time Series

summary: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with readings grounded in a real laboratory. We introduce TwinLab-Bench, which evaluates AI scientists on self-designed experiments in 52 tasks from laboratories in the physical sciences, the life sciences, and engineering. The benchmark supports more than 100 experimental action types, and the agent's report is scored by comparison with a hidden answer taken from real laboratory records. Each task has its own TwinLab agent, an agent that serves as the environment and executes the experiments that the tested agent designs, reading the raw materials of the laboratory and calling calculators that are built from its records. Compared with a language model that sees only the task description, the TwinLab agent almost eliminates readings that deviate from the real records and inconsistent answers to a repeated request, and closed-book probes control for answers recalled from memory. We find that these tasks remain hard for frontier models: the strongest, Claude Fable 5.2, averages a score of only 45.0, and we conduct an empirical study of where it fails.
title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs

summary: Many useful latent distributions can be sampled but do not have a tractable density. Such distributions may be represented by empirical collections of real-world observations or generated by scientific simulators and black-box generative models. These sample-only priors cannot be used directly in likelihood-based normalizing flows, which require evaluating the prior density. We propose Projected Characteristic-Function matching (PCF), a density-free framework for learning an invertible map between a data distribution and a prior specified only through samples. Our method aligns distributions using projected empirical characteristic functions, eliminating the need for density estimation, adversarial training, or paired observations. To address the non-uniqueness of the transport map, we introduce an optional transport regularizer that selects lower-displacement transformations while preserving endpoint alignment. We benchmark PCF on controlled transports, sample-efficiency studies, and high-dimensional alignment tasks. PCF matches the accuracy of kernel MMD on the controlled benchmark and on raw-pixel MNIST--USPS at a cost linear in the batch size, and it is more sample-efficient, achieving lower endpoint error than MMD in 13 of 15 paired runs across library sizes. By avoiding pairwise kernel evaluation, it reduces discrepancy memory by 29.8% and trains at batch sizes where kernel MMD exceeds GPU memory. These results show that PCF provides accurate and efficient invertible transport, particularly in sample- and memory-limited settings.
title: Invertible Transport Between Sample-Only Distributions via Projected Characteristic Functions

summary: Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations. Gradients are typically computed using adjoint methods, or backpropagation through time (BPTT), whose computational and memory costs grow with the length of the training window. This limits the duration and resolution of hybrid-model training, a major bottleneck for realistic geophysical applications. Approaches like truncated BPTT reduces memory use by discarding sensitivities across truncation boundaries, introducing gradient bias and neglecting long-range dependencies. We propose a class of gradient approximation methods that preserve the adjoint recurrence over the full trajectory while approximating only the pullback operators within it. Exact pullbacks are computed by automatic differentiation at sparse anchor states only. Between anchors, sensitivities propagate either through the identity (Zero-order) or through a reused, frozen pullback (Pullback Reuse). This approximation makes the parameter pullback constant within each chunk, allowing the gradient sum to factorize so that a single evaluation per chunk replaces one per time step. We evaluate both on three systems of increasing complexity, an incomplete Lorenz-63 model, a large-eddy closure for two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic turbulence, and bias correction in a multilayer quasi-geostrophic ocean model. Peak memory falls by up to an order of magnitude and runtime up to fourfold, with Pullback Reuse staying closest to the exact gradient direction. In all three cases, approximate gradients support hybrid-model training at comparable accuracy, showing that effective online learning does not require exact gradients.
title: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models

summary: Reasoning models provide strong multimodal task understanding but struggle with sub-second control because deliberation increases decision latency. Fast decision models can meet the response window, yet prompting and few-shot examples do not readily provide the fine-grained experience required by a new task. Inspired by coached motor learning, this paper presents System-One Recursive Self-Improvement (System-One RSI), which couples two loops. The high-frequency online inner loop is an Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) cycle: a decision model maps each visual observation and task question to structured judgments, and a decision tree converts them into timed actions without invoking a reasoning model. The offline outer loop is a recursive improvement cycle carried out by a team of reasoning agents. The team revises the decision-model prompt and decision tree, captures interaction records, derives supervision from those records, and trains or deploys updated model parameters. The improved system then returns to the environment and generates the experience for the next round, consolidating learned distinctions as external muscle memory. The framework operates with a small number of real episodes, without expert demonstrations, environment modification, sandboxing, or parallel simulation. Experiments in Snake, Zenless Zone Zero, and Black Myth: Wukong use a 27B decision model. Mean Snake score increases from 1.30 to 7.35. In an evaluated scenario of Zenless Zone Zero, median completion time decreases by 8.4%. In an evaluated combat scenario of Black Myth: Wukong, the evasive policy achieves 11 times the mean survival time of a stationary reference, while the offensive policy win rate rises from 0% to 66.7% across the evaluated configurations.
title: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice

summary: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sofilyzia/Fast-JEPA.
title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models

summary: Traffic scenario understanding requires combining fine-grained visual evidence with spatial and temporal reasoning. Tool-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) can use specialized perception tools, but effective collaboration faces two challenges: terminal rewards provide limited guidance for intermediate decisions and error recovery, while repeated planning adds unnecessary cost across similar tasks. Echoing the fast-slow dichotomy of human cognition, we propose StarTV-Agent, which combines policy learning with experience evolution to support adaptive reasoning when needed and efficient reuse of prior experience when possible. During training, Role-Sensitive Process Optimization (RSPO) combines process advantages with terminal advantages, while Weakness-Driven Demonstration Learning (WDL) provides validated teacher demonstrations targeting the student's weak questions. During inference, Lightweight Adaptive Workflow Reuse (LAWR) enables a fast path by selecting suitable workflows and binding task-specific arguments and resource references, while a slow ReAct-based path handles tasks without suitable workflows. We further design label-free feedback based on execution completion, workflow adoption, and cost savings to guide workflow reuse and memory updates. Across three challenging benchmarks, StarTV-Agent achieves up to 8.0% relative performance improvement, while reducing token consumption by up to 52.1%.
title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding

summary: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.
title: Posterior Matching Distillation

summary: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.
title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift

summary: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) provides a bulk magnetic susceptibility estimate per voxel, so contributions from paramagnetic and diamagnetic sources within the same voxel partially cancel. Susceptibility source separation methods identify these compartments by fitting a three-pool complex exponential model to multi-echo gradient-echo (GRE) data. However, conventional voxel-wise fitting with general-purpose constrained solvers requires several hours per whole-brain volume and often fails in high-susceptibility regions. We present CANON-QSM (Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization for QSM), a solver that reformulates the subproblems of the three-pool model and solves them alternately via exact closed-form updates and Newton-type steps, yielding a substantial per-voxel computational speedup. Both in silico and in vivo evaluations demonstrate not only a massive reduction in reconstruction time, completing a whole-brain volume in under two minutes, but also improved accuracy and robustness against artifacts in high-susceptibility regions. Finally, an echo-time analysis of the three-pool model shows that source separation is driven by second-order nonlinearities in signal decay and phase evolution rather than first-order bulk estimates.
title: Susceptibility source separation via Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization

summary: For a power function over a finite field, differential uniformity records only the largest entry of its differential distribution table, whereas the differential spectrum records every multiplicity and its frequency. We determine exact differential spectra for five families of low-uniformity power functions in odd characteristic, including families previously studied primarily through uniformity bounds. Our methods combine spectrum-preserving exponent changes, factorial moments, intersections of injective images, character sums, and point counts on curves over finite fields. For the ternary family of Yuan, Du, Qiao, and Zhou, we give a fixed-cover formula and an explicit Artin factorization for one pair-intersection cover; its odd-degree counts reduce to traces of elliptic and genus-two curves. Inverse-cubic powers yield a conic evaluation in characteristic five and low-genus trace formulas in larger characteristics. Four ternary branches associated with Dobbertin, Mills, Müller, Pott, and Willems share one complete spectrum governed by an elliptic trace. For the Yan--Han family, an Artin--Prym decomposition gives all multiplicity frequencies and exact differential uniformity, including a planar endpoint. For Felke's family, we express extension-field spectra as one-dimensional character sums while identifying the known prime-field cases. A standalone program independently reproduces the finite-field calculations used in the proofs.
title: Exact Differential Spectra for Five Families of Power Functions

summary: In this study, we compare the asymptotic efficiency of three closed-form estimators of the Dirichlet shape parameters. We start by proving that, in the beta distribution, the score-adjusted moment estimator (SA) has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than the usual moment estimator (M1) for both parameters. We then introduce a new moment estimator (M2) that combines the marginal moment equations to obtain a common estimate of the total concentration. M2 coincides with M1 in the beta case and has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances for every positive shape vector in three or more dimensions. We then show that SA is asymptotically more efficient than M2 when all shape parameters are equal; if at least two parameters differ, each estimator has smaller asymptotic variance than the other for some linear combination of the parameters. Furthermore, SA has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than M2 when all shape parameters are at least 1. Finally, we show that this ordering can reverse if a parameter becomes too small, and obtain relevant mathematical and computational bounds. Overall, the study shows that, for the Dirichlet distribution and under a broad range of parameter settings, score-adjusted estimation outperforms the classic moment estimation and identifies the limits of that advantage.
title: Asymptotic efficiency comparison of explicit Dirichlet shape estimators

summary: Many paired image-to-image translation tasks admit multiple valid target appearances, while training provides only one target per source. We propose One-to-Many Flow (O2MFlow), a latent-conditioned Rectified Flow (RF) model for one-to-many generation and backward translation (target$\rightarrow$source) within a single transport framework. Conditioning the RF dynamics on an appearance latent turns transport into a family of latent-indexed bijections: a fixed latent gives a mapping that is inverted by time-reversed integration, and sampled latents produce diverse outputs for the same input. We formalize reusable appearance variations as Shared Latent Transport and show that Kullback--Leibler (KL) regularization directly controls the source--latent distribution gap between training and generation. Across three benchmarks, O2MFlow offers dataset-dependent forward diversity--fidelity trade-offs and the lowest backward LPIPS-Dist among evaluated methods, with the lowest backward FID on two benchmarks.
title: One-to-Many: Diverse and Bidirectional Image-to-Image Translation via Rectified Flow

summary: High-fidelity scene reconstruction with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) requires more than identifying valuable viewpoints: the system must autonomously acquire informative observations and determine task completion under different sensing configurations and limited flight resources. We present AGE-Capture, an autonomous, sensor-adaptive, and efficient active-capture framework for real UAVs. Building on renderability, the framework uses a lightweight online state to evaluate the utility of candidate views, assess task progress, and guide flight execution. By decoupling geometric exploration from reconstruction observations and establishing a unified camera-ray interface, the framework allows different range sensors and RGB camera models to share a reconstruction-driven acquisition pipeline. Reconstruction-frontier viewpoints characterize residual acquisition value for region screening and autonomous termination; dynamics-aware hierarchical planning combined with asynchronous event-driven capture reduces unnecessary inter-region motion, time spent waiting for plans, and repeated observations. Across ten indoor and outdoor simulation scenes, AGE-Capture achieves a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) $3.30$--$3.53\,\mathrm{dB}$ higher than that of the online baselines while using $58.2\%$ of the common mission-time budget on average. Its mean peak GPU memory usage is $91.0\%$--$93.3\%$ lower than that of the same baselines. Experiments with different sensor configurations validate the adaptability of the shared acquisition pipeline, while flights in nine real-world scenes further demonstrate onboard closed-loop operation under practical computational and motion constraints.
title: AGE-Capture: Autonomous, General, and Efficient UAV Capture for High-Fidelity Scene Reconstruction

summary: This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. Equilibrium heights and orientations agree with hydrostatic expectations and published stable configurations, respectively. Two- and three-dimensional wet-bed dam-break simulations reproduce experimental trends in wave elevation and floating-body heave and pitch. Two star-shaped rigid bodies demonstrate applicability to complex geometries without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation. All production strong-coupling simulations satisfy the prescribed relative-residual criterion at every time step before reaching the maximum coupling-iteration count. These results support iterative FD-SPH for lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows.
title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies

summary: We study the recovery of feedforward $\tanh$ networks of fixed architecture with $P$ parameters from finitely many point evaluations. First, we characterize the set of parameters where the differential of the realization map has full rank and show that it coincides with the regular parameters in the sense of Vla{č}i{ć} and B{ö}lcskei (2021). Second, we make use of this characterization to prove that almost every tuple of $2P+1$ sampling points yields uniform-norm Lipschitz stability on compact subsets of this parameter set. Third, we prove that for exact observations, projected gradient descent and projected Gauss--Newton converge locally from sufficiently close feasible initial guesses. The same evaluations also determine the realized function for arbitrary parameters and identify parameters in the characterized set up to permutations and sign changes of hidden neurons. Finally, we develop a general framework for real-analytic networks that highlights the role of full rank in stability and local reconstruction.
title: Full Rank and Stable Sampling of $\tanh$ Networks

summary: This work investigates deep convective self-aggregation in the space of scales, extending the physical-space analysis of Part I. We introduce a novel theoretical framework by examining and deriving a generalized Yaglom equation for the second-order structure function $\langle δh_f^{\prime 2} \rangle$, the scale-dependent variance of Frozen Moist Static Energy (FMSE). Self-aggregation is found to be sustained by an inverse energy cascade driven by boundary-layer production and mediated by mesoscale circulations with horizontal scales $r \sim$(100-250 km). The inverse cascade of energy is found to be realized through a series of shallow and mid-level mesoscale circulations which behave in a self-similar way. Accordingly, the scale-energy variance exhibits an extraordinary collapse across all atmospheric layers onto a robust self-similar power law, $\langle δh_f^{\prime 2} \rangle \sim r^{6/5}$. In contrast, horizontal velocity increments show a degree of self-similarity ($\langle δu_r^{\prime 2} \rangle \sim r^{2/5}$) that retains a residual height dependence. Interestingly, the FMSE scaling breaks down at elevations lower than 750 m and at small local scales below 100 km, allowing us to identify the boundary layer top as a scale-dependent dividing layer where the strong stratification filters the interactions between the surface and free-troposphere, so that small scale dynamics of the low and high atmospheric layers are decoupled while those at large mesoscale are coupled. The derived scaling laws are also used to quantify the moisture-convection feedback via scale-dependent correlation coefficients that show that vertical transport strengthens with scale ($ρ_{mc\perp} \sim r^{2/5}$), while horizontal convergence weakens at the exact inverse rate ($ρ_{mc\parallel} \sim r^{-2/5}$).
title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part II: scale-by-scale budget and mesoscale self-similarity

files.key: Ancestral sequence reconstruction enables functional expression of archaeal thermostable tungsten-containing aldehydeferredoxin oxidoreductases in E. coli.pdf

summary: Tungsten-containing enzymes offer important opportunities in industrial biocatalysis, e.g. to convert carboxylic acids into aldehydes without requiring co-substrates ATP and NADPH. These W-enzymes operate at low reduction potentials compared to the more ubiquitous Moenzymes, enabling unique reactions. Their application is limited by the lack of functional expression in commonly used heterologous host organisms. Here, we show that variants of Pyrococcus furiosus aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PfAOR) obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction can be functionally expressed in E. coli with an activity of 0.86 U/mg towards crotonaldehyde at 60°C, which is a 50-fold higher activity compared to the recombinant extant enzyme. The ancestral enzymes, named ThermoAOR3 and ThermoAOR4, carrying 61 and 84 mutations respectively, were purified using a single-step affinity purification, showed a kcat of 0.95 and 0.86 s-1 at 60 °C, respectively, and have Km values comparable to native PfAOR. ThermoAOR3 contained a redox active [4Fe-4S] cluster like native PfAOR. Furthermore, it contained 10-15% of the expected pterin cofactor, W and Fe, which indicates the enzyme production can still be improved. Altogether, we demonstrate the first heterologous expression of a functionally active W-AOR using a widely used bacterial host, which represents a breakthrough enabling exploration of these enzymes for industrial biocatalysis.
title: Ancestral sequence reconstruction enables functional expression of archaeal thermostable tungsten-containing aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases in E. coli

summary: The concept of d aylight affordance as an ecological factor that is inherent in the remains of built environments can contribute to our understanding of the locations and conditions of domestic activities within ancient dwellings. This paper discusses a general approach to assess ing daylight affordance and presents first results from the case study of House A as part of a broader investigation into Greek residential architecture in ancient Orraon. Because local limestone was used as the main building material, some of the residential dwellings in Orraon , especially House A, have been preserved to such an extent that they allow the best possible reconstruction of their different construction phases, both in terms of building geometry and surface materiality. The proposed method to assess daylight affordance combines a digital reconstruction model with climate-based daylight simulation and task-specific measurement geometries and thresholds for good detail and colour vision. This facilitates the study of domestic activities and their changes throughout the building history of House A, which lasted around 300 years. The analysis of House A demonstrates clearly how activities demanding visual acuity or good colour vision are limited to certain rooms or areas within the building. It further suggests that architectural changes were driven by lighting conditions. These results can be read against the background of scholarly attributions of activities to certain rooms, often based on strictly typological considerations or the distribution of finds. It thus offers a new perspective on the methodologically difficult question of spatial use scenarios in ancient residential buildings. The method of applying the theoretical concept of daylight affordance to ancient architecture is still new. We are currently refining it on the basis of further case studies. Important insights are also expected from experimental archaeological approaches.
title: Daylight affordance as ecological approach to domestic activities in House A in ancient Orraon

summary: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection on the NASA CMAPSS FD001 turbofan dataset. An LSTM autoencoder trained on healthy sliding windows is compared on 20 held-out engines with a cycle-count score, PCA reconstruction, an Isolation Forest and a one-class SVM, with bootstrap intervals over engines, paired comparisons of warning time at equal false-alarm rates and a causal alarm rule. The model is served through a typed FastAPI service and a Streamlit demo in a multi-stage Docker stack.
title: Anomaly Detection API: Autoencoder + FastAPI + Docker

summary: Early interactions can reveal physical properties that later observations no longer show. These properties can still gov- ern the effects of future actions. Inspired by the distinction between retention and selective readout in working mem- ory and cognitive science, we introduce LATER, an action- conditioned world model built on CF-JEPA. LATER stores completed real transitions in partitioned memories that remain fixed during candidate rollouts. A response bridge queries these memories using the current state and candidate action, while multi-cut auxiliary supervision trains the memory writ- ers. On distracted Two-Stage PushT, LATER raises terminal success from 15.5% to 25.0% over reconstructed CF-JEPA. In a separate comparison across six models and two scratch- training seeds, LATER achieves the lowest mean physical readout error in both clean and distracted views, reducing along-push mean absolute error (MAE) under distractors by 20.2% relative to CF-JEPA. Controlled history interventions show that later predictions depend on earlier physical evi- dence even when query observations and actions are fixed, with larger effects during pushing than waiting.
title: LATER: Learning Action-Conditioned Temporal Evidence Retrieval for Predictive World Models

summary: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule definitions, dependencies, and object states in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback in a closed loop. The graph supports joint saving and restoration of rules and world states, while dynamic object binding grounds rule-specified entities in visual instances and uses stored states to constrain generation from their first appearance. We further introduce object attribute state replacement and counterfactual reconstruction training, enabling accurate attribute control and compatible appearance and motion changes while limiting interference with unrelated content. We develop an automated data collection and annotation pipeline using GTA-V and Habitat to construct RuleVerse, a dataset of rule-driven interactions with detailed state and event annotations, including cases where rules take effect before affected objects become visible. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of WorldRuler in preserving rule-state consistency across saving and loading and accurately realizing rule outcomes on designated objects and attributes.
title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules

summary: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.
title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming

summary: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. We present Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS) for set pieces, which treats a corner or a lofted free kick as a distribution over plausible executions and plausible futures instead of a single realised event. From the pre-kick state, MCPS proposes counterfactual deliveries and counterfactual set-ups (where the attackers stand at the kick), plays each out many times in a world model (3D ball physics, a generative model of all 22 players, the keeper's come-or-stay decision and a Player-to-Touch model) and scores every future with a value model. On 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, with every model applied only to matches it never saw, the best available delivery is worth 0.0085 xG more than the one kicked (+28 %), mainly because it reaches an attacker before the keeper. Searching where the attackers stand as well adds +0.0027 xG with the observed ball and +0.0033 on top of the best ball; designing their runs too adds +0.0007 more. We show how to keep such a search honest, and estimate how much more data each component needs before a club could rely on it.
title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces

summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid ($>250\times$ dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension ($d \to d+K$) with $\sqrt{d/(d+K)}$ norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential $(+254,-256)$ tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed $\{+,-,\times\}$ circuits in constant $\mathsf{TC}^0$ depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, $N=1{,}728$; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic ($N=1{,}200$, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, $\le 0.036\%$) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, $\le 0.057\%$) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). A factorized block-sparse sidecar holds A100 memory at 7.89 / 10.65 GiB (4.60 / 8.14 GiB under INT8/INT4 + FP32 sidecar) while passing all 14/14 pre-registered $>2$K-token Tango splits ($N=4{,}392$; 0/11,134 OOD triggers).
title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights

summary: Attention in large language models (LLMs) scores every query against every key with a full dot product. We investigate whether this dot product must be computed completely for attention to be effective. We propose Hidden Sparse Attention (HiSA), which keeps the query and key projections intact but only computes a partial dot product, following a static, parameter-free rule set by the token positions: attention becomes sparse in the hidden (feature) dimension, an axis much less explored than token sparsity, rather than over tokens as in almost all sparse attention methods. Based on the structure of rotary position embeddings (RoPE), we decompose keys and queries into parts which can be omitted when computing attention. By training LLMs from scratch with HiSA, we find that this partial dot product does not hurt but improves performance compared with the complete product while computing only about a third of the query-key products. During inference HiSA improves decoding speed and shrinks memory footprint. We also extend HiSA to FlashAttention-3 kernels for training and inference. Finally, we motivate our approach by showing that dense attention learns to suppress the attention score parts that HiSA drops. Code is available at https://github.com/ambroise-b/hisa.
title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs

summary: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM)-based processing-in-memory (PIM) accelerators offer a highly efficient platform for parallel matrix-vector multiplications (VMM) in neural networks, leveraging analog computation, high density, low leakage, and non-volatility. However, their susceptibility to permanent faults, such as stuck-at-high (\textit{SaH}) and stuck-at-low (\textit{SaL}) resistance states, permanently corrupts the convolutional neural networks (CNNs) weights mapped onto ReRAM cell conductance values, thereby degrading inference accuracy and leading to system unreliability in safety-critical applications. Fault injection is a commonly used technique to assess the vulnerability of neural networks by systematically injecting faults into individual parameters and measuring the resulting accuracy degradation. Although this method is accurate, it is prohibitively time-consuming and computationally expensive, especially for large-scale CNNs. In this paper, we propose a fast, scalable, and analytical framework to quantify the fault vulnerability of convolutional neural networks deployed on ReRAM-based PIM accelerators. This method quantifies vulnerability at different granularities, including weights, kernels, and layers, without the need for exhaustive simulation, enabling the design of fault-tolerant accelerators for edge and safety-critical applications. The comparison between the results of the proposed vulnerability score (VS) metrics with performance metric of CNNs captured with fault injection simulations confirms the effectiveness of our proposed method. Unlike exhaustive fault injection, which requires days or weeks, whereas the proposed approach achieves a speedup of about $10^4\times-10^5\times$, enabling fast and accurate vulnerability analysis for large-scale CNNs within only a few minutes or hours.
title: Scalable fault vulnerability analysis for ReRAM-based process-in-memory CNN accelerators

summary: HeOCR oldprint-v1: Hebrew old and rabbinic print recognition for Tesseract oldprint-v1 is a Tesseract language model ( .traineddata ) for old printed Hebrew in the square script: 19th- and early-20th-century books and rabbinic editions. HeOCR made it by continuing to train HeOCR R7 , itself a fine-tune of Tesseract's own heb model from tessdata_best , for one pass over 76,946 lines: - 22,910 real scanned lines from 4 public-domain books (Internet Archive scans), labelled with the Project Ben-Yehuda transcription of the same edition; - 14,036 real scanned lines from 3 rabbinic editions (Internet Archive scans), labelled with public-domain Sefaria texts and Project Gutenberg ebook #43740; - 40,000 lines rendered from born-digital booklets of Israel's laws and regulations (Reshumot), labelled with the publisher's own text layer, replayed so that modern print is not lost. No label is OCR output. It is the model that HeOCR's evaluation recommends for old print in heocr , the HeOCR document pipeline, beside modern-v1 for modern print. (In the experiment records it is P-hist round v1, arm r7, heb_final .) Performance: not measured on a held-out set of old and rabbinic print yet. HeOCR will score it once in a registered held-out run. That run is the P-hist test (22 held-out books), once its human references exist, against R7 and stock heb ; the result will be added to this card in a new version. The one held-out result so far is a pointed-print test: it does not output niqqud (see Bias, risks and limitations ). summary: HeOCR A1: Hebrew document line reading order (kraken) A1 is a kraken reading-order model. It orders the text lines of a modern Hebrew document page from each line's position and its region type: title, body, stamp, signature, footer, margin, identifier or table cell. HeOCR trained it from scratch on synthetic pages only. A1 is the reading-order step of HeOCR's three-model pipeline: - R4d finds the lines and their regions; - A1 puts them in reading order; - R3h reads them. The three are released together, as separate records that link to each other (see The pipeline ). It is a research baseline. All of its evaluation is on synthetic pages; no reviewed evaluation on real scans exists yet. Performance: not measured on a held-out set yet. HeOCR reports accuracy only on held-out sets, and this model has not yet been scored on one. No held-out score yet; HeOCR will score it once in a registered held-out run. Its result will be added to this card in a new version. How it was chosen: its design (region-type classes, stamp-first tagging) was chosen on hocrgen's fixture batch, and training kept the checkpoint with the best order on its own validation pages (see Training procedure ). It was then compared with kraken's heuristic order on synthetic development batches. These sets were used to choose and compare it, so they are not reported here as its performance. summary: This study examines the relationship between age falsification in the Nigerian public service and youth unemployment, with specific reference to the National Assembly Service Commission from 2004 to 2024. The study adopts an extant review approach, drawing on existing empirical and theoretical literature to explore the prevalence, causes, and implications of age falsification within public institutions. The analysis is anchored on rational choice and anomie perspectives to explain individual motivations and systemic pressures that sustain the practice, while social restorative theory provides a framework for institutional response. Findings reveal that age falsification is widespread and driven by factors such as job insecurity, weak pension systems, poor record keeping, and ineffective enforcement mechanisms. The practice contributes significantly to workforce stagnation by delaying retirement and limiting employment opportunities for younger entrants. Evidence further shows that weak recruitment governance, patronage networks, and fragmented identity verification systems exacerbate the problem. Comparative analysis indicates that while Nigeria struggles with enforcement and verification gaps, countries such as the United Kingdom have reduced incentives for falsification through the removal of rigid retirement structures, Ghana has strengthened identity management through centralized biometric systems, and Rwanda has achieved greater control through early and comprehensive digitization of personnel records. The study concludes that age falsification is not merely an administrative irregularity but a structural governance issue with direct implications for youth employment and public sector efficiency. It recommends comprehensive reforms in verification systems, recruitment processes, and enforcement mechanisms to restore integrity and promote equitable access to public service employment.
tags: Age falsification, youth unemployment, Nigerian public service, National Assembly Service Commission, recruitment governance, identity verification, public sector reform
title: Age Falsification in The Nigerian Public Service and Youth Unemployment: An Extant Review of The National Assembly Service Commission, 2004-2024

summary: Accurate algebraic wall functions for second-moment turbulence statistics are highly sought after in RANS modeling. A natural approach is to express the variance of the inverse hyperbolic sine transformation, \(\langle\phi'^2\rangle\), using only the mean velocity \(U\) and the turbulent kinetic energy \(k\). In this Rapid, we prove that such an approach is fundamentally impossible. We identify an \textit{information barrier}: because \(k\) constrains only the sum of the Reynolds stress components and not their individual partition, any function \(f(U,k)\) is structurally unable to capture the velocity variance in the buffer layer. Using a controlled Gaussian Monte Carlo surrogate parameterized by DNS data at \(Re_\tau = 180, 395, 590\), we demonstrate that varying the anisotropy ratio at fixed \((U,k)\) causes \(\langle\phi'^2\rangle\) to fluctuate by a factor of 4.7. By the triangle inequality, this imposes a strict minimax lower bound on the error of any closed-form function, translating to a relative error strictly greater than \(60\%\). We mathematically trace this barrier to three nonlinear corrections inherent to the concavity of \(\operatorname{arcsinh}\): mean shift, skewness, and non-Gaussianity. Finally, we show that bypassing this barrier requires abandoning the \((U,k)\) restriction in favor of explicit Reynolds-stress inputs.
title: The Information Barrier of Algebraic Wall Functions: Why \(U\) and \(k\) Cannot Determine the Arcsinh-Transformed Velocity Variance

summary: In 1513 the Castilian Crown began directing its conquistadors to read aloud the Requerimiento, a legal demand that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas submit at once to the authority of the Pope and the Spanish monarch. Composed by the jurist Juan López de Palacios Rubios, it was recited in Spanish or Latin, often out of earshot and to communities with no means of grasping its terms, and yet refusal, or the mere inability to consent, was treated as lawful grounds for war and enslavement. For the Taíno of the Caribbean it was the purest instrument of weaponized information asymmetry: a choice demanded under conditions that made informed choice impossible. This article formalizes the structural inverse of that instrument. It proposes a formal model of a peer-recognition currency in which the unit of account is perceived contribution value, issuance is fully endogenous, no sovereign intermediary exists, and the exchange space is structured by context-tagged domains rather than a flat signal architecture. The model's central claim is that when a boundedly rational agent simultaneously optimizes for accumulation, because a high balance signals competence and influence, and for expenditure, because high spending signals piety, humility, and reciprocal embeddedness, the resulting equilibrium is altruistic in the behavioral sense, not because altruism is designed into the incentive structure but because it is the only stable solution to the dual-motive optimization problem in a peer network with an observable ledger. A novel institutional role is defined: the epistemic witness, which informs without judging and without suggesting, preserving full independent agency while eliminating the information asymmetry between a participant and their own recognized contribution record. Where the Requerimiento compelled assent to terms that could not be read, the witness makes the terms of recognition fully legible to the participant before they act. The model is situated within the intersecting literatures of mechanism design, social epistemology, signaling theory, gift economy, commons governance, social compact theory, and cognitive behavioral economics. A candidate validation architecture is identified in which the model's predictions are falsifiable, and a formal appendix establishes the equilibrium result as a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium under perfect public monitoring. The paper concludes that the architecture described represents a distinct class of social exchange institution whose properties cannot be derived from any existing system and whose emergence of altruism as a structural rather than moral outcome has implications beyond the design of digital platforms.
title: E-Karma: A Formal Model of Peer-Recognition Currency, Dual-Motive Optimization, and the Structural Emergence of Altruism

summary: Erman and Sam asked whether every integral point on a pure ray of the Boij-Söderberg cone is the Betti table of a finite length module over k[x,y,z] or over the enveloping algebra U of the Heisenberg Lie algebra; Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu answered negatively. We study the point (1,2,2,1) on (0,e,3e,4e), excluded over k[x,y,z] and passing their test over U. It is realized by U/U(x^e,y^e) if and only if char k = 0 or char k >= 2e, and in characteristic 2 no module with at most one more relation than generators has finite length over U. In odd characteristic p we prove a criterion for pairs of forms with a central commutator, with explicit pure pairs for e = 0 or 1 modulo p, and pull-backs along endomorphisms of U. For the pairs x^e + alpha y^t, y^e + beta x^t we prove that coprimality conditions, two congruences and one scalar condition give the pure Hilbert function when p >= 2t, and the pure pair when one more coprimality holds; explicit short pairs are pure for p = 2e - 1 (every prime p >= 5) and for p = 2e - 3 (the primes below 2,000,000). Searches in weight-class strata, lists of forms, the filter for every exponent and the members fixed by the exchange of x and y settle the other pairs. The point is realized in every characteristic other than 2 for 2 <= e <= 16 except e = 11, where characteristic 3 is open. A census of the 220 rays with d_3 <= 12 over k[x,y,z] realizes the primitive point on 193 and excludes it on 12; in characteristic 0 the least counterexample has d_3 = 10. Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (branch develop). The paper does not claim a negative answer to Question 6.1 of Erman and Sam, which is due to Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu, and claims no priority for any other result.
title: Primitive Betti points over k[x,y,z] and the Heisenberg enveloping algebra: the point (1,2,2,1) on (0,e,3e,4e) fails only in characteristic 2 for 2 <= e <= 16 with e != 11, is realized whenever an odd prime p divides e(e-1) or equals 2e-1, and a census for d_3 <= 12

summary: Extending Spezia's determinant result (2018), we prove his two conjectures in OEIS A322844, Comments, the two statements in the conjectures block (revision 68, August 23, 2025): the absolute second exterior trace of the serpentine matrix is the stated quartic quasipolynomial, and every exterior trace of order greater than two vanishes. The matrix has rank exactly two for every size at least two. A factorization through a two-dimensional space gives its characteristic polynomial, including the sign of the second exterior trace. Corollaries give a minimal polynomial, a permanent formula, diagonal sums, generating functions and reciprocal sums. We distinguish the exponential generating function from a shifted-factorial expression in the source.
title: Rank-two extensions of Spezia's 2018 determinant result: the two conjectures in OEIS A322844, Comments (revision 68)

summary: Purpose: This study aims to examine the temporal structure of naval platform procurement rivalry between Türkiye and Greece during 1990–2025. By analysing the reciprocal relationships between naval platform deliveries and international orders in both countries, it investigates the lags at which procurement activities become most pronounced and the role of major naval procurement programmes in shaping these relationships. Method: Annual naval platform delivery and international order series compiled from SIPRI for 1990–2025 were analysed using ordinary least squares (OLS) models with 0–3-year lags and Newey–West standard errors. The findings were assessed through common-sample, full first-difference, distributed-lag, military expenditure control, order-date sensitivity, and period-window analyses, complemented by changes in fleet tonnage from the Power at Sea 2.0 dataset. Findings: In the baseline models, Greek deliveries are positively associated with Turkish deliveries two years later (β = 0.427) and Turkish orders one year later (β = 0.636), while Turkish deliveries are positively associated with Greek orders three years later (β = 0.395; BH-adjusted p < 0.05). All three selected coefficients remained positive after controlling for military expenditure, although their statistical support weakened following BH adjustment. Excluding the period corresponding to the MEKO-200 delivery window reduced the H1 coefficient to 0.102. In the full first-difference models, the H1 relationship persisted, whereas the order-related relationships were sensitive to the transformation. Conclusion: The strongest lagged association in Turkish–Greek naval procurement was observed between Greek ship deliveries and subsequent Turkish orders. This finding is consistent with Richardson’s action–reaction approach and Jervis’s security dilemma framework, which underpin the study’s theoretical perspective. The study demonstrates that naval procurement rivalry between the two countries exhibits asymmetric relationships in terms of direction and timing, particularly across the order and delivery stages.
title: The Temporal Structure of Turkish–Greek Naval Procurement Rivalry: Orders and Deliveries (1990–2025)

summary: On 20 November 2026 L. Alpöge posted a four-page note and a Lean 4 archive claiming a derivation of Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis: 175,187 files, 17.4 million lines, the three standard axioms, no human-readable proof. We read the archive against the one-bit normal form of the Riemann Hypothesis, public in our git repository since October 2026 in Lean and since August 2026 in prose. The headline is Mathlib's own statement. Its last step is the band reduction our Lean record states as one face of the normal form. Everything in it except one proposition was in our public Lean record first, and that proposition is the bit our record isolated and printed as its only premise. Its premise is the definition of ζ, which a law of logic proved in our file classifies as strictly stronger than the value, so the derivation is a tautology of that premise. A second Lean test shows the standard axioms cannot carry the bit: if the archive stands, the bit came out of ζ, through a window estimate on Tate–Shafarevich lengths that holds every program-generated proof in the archive. Both seals build silently in core Lean 4.19.0 and are printed whole. We close with a provenance ledger and a critique of the artifact as published.
title: The Bit in the Definition: A Lean Derivation of the Riemann Hypothesis, Its Tautology, and the Public Record It Lands In

summary: Action-Research Lessons Learned from a Dis|mis Administrative Incident This book is an action-research study of lessons learned from a dis|mis administrative incident . It uses the incident as a situated case through which to examine how administrative uncertainty, informational asymmetry, technological mediation, institutional inertia, and contested interpretation can affect cognition, expression, dignity, and public trust. The project is guided by the attached work’s progression from “Fundamental Rights At Risk” and “On Partiality” to “On Liberty of Thinking,” “On Inner Peace & Recensions,” “Introducing CogOps,” “On Cognitive Health,” and the case studies on judicial impartiality, private affiliations, oath conflict, and SIS–Schengen transparency. The table of contents therefore provides the project’s conceptual route: from rights and institutional balance, through cognition and inner life, towards administrative, technological, and governance risks. The research does not present the personal account as conclusive proof of intentional wrongdoing. Rather, it treats the incident as a source of lessons learned, research questions, provisional concepts, and methodological warnings . The purpose is to distinguish observed events from interpretation, allegation, metaphor, and hypothesis while asking how comparable vulnerabilities might arise in other administrative environments. From rights to cognition The first part of the research begins with fundamental rights and institutional impartiality. In the chapter “On Partiality,” the attached work states: “It is also relational: whenever you are judged, a relationship is involved.” This proposition provides an important starting point for action research. An administrative decision is not only a technical act; it occurs within a relationship involving a citizen, a public agent, an institution, a body of law, and a surrounding informational environment. A failure of communication, an absence of reasons, a delay, or an inability to challenge a decision can therefore produce effects extending beyond the immediate administrative matter. The same chapter gives a second guiding image: “We are all equal under gravity.” Here, the balance functions as a non-technical symbol of equality, impartiality, and the need to prevent power from becoming detached from rights. Within the proposed research, this image is translated into questions about procedural fairness, equal access to information, the visibility of relevant affiliations, and the ability of affected persons to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning them. Liberty of thinking The chapter “On Liberty of Thinking” provides the closest conceptual foundation for the study of inner ecology. It describes writing and symbolic expression as a means of creating distance from an overwhelming or difficult experience: “Being able to formulate, express, and work on things symbolically helps us create emotional distance.” This observation is central to the action-research design. Recension, writing, drawing, multilingual expression, and documentary reconstruction are not treated merely as literary devices. They are used as practical research instruments through which an individual experience can be reviewed, organised, questioned, and made accessible to others. The chapter also describes expression as a form of shelter: “It was therefore a genuine shelter to be able to express ourselves through this ‘way of the pencil.’” Adapted to a CERREV-oriented research programme, this becomes a question about the conditions under which citizens and public agents can formulate disagreement without escalation. The research therefore examines whether accessible forms of expression can reduce informational dissonance, support self-correction, and create a more reliable basis
title: THE ASYLUM : From Soft Corruption to Disruptive Cognitive Operations: Reaching Inner Peace

summary: This publication specifies and documents a researcher-directed methodology for AI-assisted mathematical discovery, developed within the independent mathematical research program of Structural Stability Science (SSS). The methodology exhibits continuity with, but remains distinct from, the originating Structural Identification Method (SIM; Tonucci, 2026). It integrates scientific identification and continuing research direction, AI-assisted scientific interlocution, mathematical formalization and analytical development, computational implementation, dependency-preserving adjudication, and source-specific contribution provenance. Scientific interlocution consists of sustained technical exchange through which mathematical questions, interpretations, hypotheses, dependencies, counterexamples, proposed constructions, and candidate proof routes are examined. Researcher-directed decisions concerning problem selection, investigative objectives, mathematical evaluation, and research-program continuity remain distinguishable from AI-generated mathematical proposals, calculations, arguments, critiques, and technical representations. Both retain identifiable contributions under their documented source conditions. The methodology specifies two complementary records. The mathematical claim record preserves originating questions, hypotheses, conclusion scope, dependencies, supporting evidence, and verification findings. The source-to-contribution record preserves originating research-state continuity, earlier research artifacts, prompt-visible AI operations, researcher-directed decisions, branch reconciliation, attribution correction, and publication outcomes. These records retain distinct evidentiary functions. A prompt-response transcript documents operations expressed within an interaction; it does not independently establish the complete originating research state or the provenance of the continuing investigation. The originating mathematical investigation concerned order preservation under real extension, admissibility, counterexamples, and mathematical continuation. The documented research sequence subsequently encompassed adjoint observation gain, analytical extensions, exact reference-state rank, restricted Fourier observability, conditional Gramian transfer, time-dependent observability, high-frequency obstruction, nonlinear terminal-target correction, and Navier–Stokes continuation questions, together with the organization of Adjoint Gain Theory. These investigations retain their individual mathematical claims, source identities, verification conditions, and unresolved proof obligations. The scientific contribution is the specification and documented application of a researcher-directed methodology that preserves mathematical claim identity and research-process provenance while distinguishing scientific origination from substantive AI-assisted mathematical production. The publication does not independently certify the mathematical results of cited sources or amend the originating scientific identities, definitions, or conditions of SIM, SSS, or Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT).
